title: 出身奴隸:布克·華盛頓自傳
author: Booker T. Washington 布克·T·華盛頓
description: 《Up from Slavery》(1901)。布克·T·華盛頓講述自己生於奴隸、赤手空拳求學、創辦塔斯基吉學院,以及1895年亞特蘭大博覽會演說嘅傳奇人生。附沃爾特·佩奇導言。英文原文對照廣東話/普通話翻譯。

passages.original: This volume is the outgrowth of a series of articles, dealing with incidents in my life, which were published consecutively in the Outlook. While they were appearing in that magazine I was constantly surprised at the number of requests which came to me from all parts of the country, asking that the articles be permanently preserved in book form. I am most grateful to the Outlook for permission to gratify these requests.
passages.vernacular: 呢本書源自一系列講述我人生事件嘅文章,佢哋曾經連續刊登喺《展望》雜誌。文章喺該雜誌連載期間,我不斷驚訝地收到來自全國各地嘅大量要求,希望文章可以永久保存成書。我非常感謝《展望》准許我滿足呢啲要求。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這本書源自一系列講述我人生事件的文章,它們曾經連續刊登在《展望》雜誌。文章在該雜誌連載期間,我不斷驚訝地收到來自全國各地的大量要求,希望文章可以永久保存成書。我非常感謝《展望》准許我滿足這些要求。

passages.original: I have tried to tell a simple, straightforward story, with no attempt at embellishment. My regret is that what I have attempted to do has been done so imperfectly. The greater part of my time and strength is required for the executive work connected with the Tuskegee Normal and Industrial Institute, and in securing the money necessary for the support of the institution. Much of what I have said has been written on board trains, or at hotels or railroad stations while I have been waiting for trains, or during the moments that I could spare from my work while at Tuskegee. Without the painstaking and generous assistance of Mr. Max Bennett Thrasher I could not have succeeded in any satisfactory degree.
passages.vernacular: 我嘗試講一個簡單、直接嘅故事,冇半點修飾。我嘅遺憾係,我所嘗試做嘅,做得好不完美。我大部分時間同精力,都要用喺塔斯基吉師範及工業學院嘅行政工作,同籌集維持學院所需嘅款項上面。我所講嘅好多內容,係喺火車上、酒店或者火車站等車時,或者喺塔斯基吉工作中可以抽出嘅片刻寫成。冇馬克斯·貝內特·思拉舍先生細心而慷慨嘅協助,我冇可能達到任何令人滿意嘅程度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我嘗試講一個簡單、直接的故事,沒有半點修飾。我的遺憾是,我所嘗試做的,做得很不完美。我大部分時間和精力,都要用在塔斯基吉師範及工業學院的行政工作,和籌集維持學院所需的款項上面。我所說的很多內容,是在火車上、酒店或火車站等車時,或在塔斯基吉工作中可以抽出的片刻寫成。沒有馬克斯·貝內特·思拉舍先生細心而慷慨的協助,我不可能達到任何令人滿意的程度。

chapters.title: Introduction by Walter H. Page 沃爾特·佩奇導言

passages.original: The details of Mr. Washington’s early life, as frankly set down in “Up from Slavery,” do not give quite a whole view of his education. He had the training that a coloured youth receives at Hampton, which, indeed, the autobiography does explain. But the reader does not get his intellectual pedigree, for Mr. Washington himself, perhaps, does not as clearly understand it as another man might. The truth is he had a training during the most impressionable period of his life that was very extraordinary, such a training as few men of his generation have had. To see its full meaning one must start in the Hawaiian Islands half a century or more ago.* There Samuel Armstrong, a youth of missionary parents, earned enough money to pay his expenses at an American college. Equipped with this small sum and the earnestness that the undertaking implied, he came to Williams College when Dr. Mark Hopkins was president. Williams College had many good things for youth in that day, as it has in this, but the greatest was the strong personality of its famous president. Every student does not profit by a great teacher; but perhaps no young man ever came under the influence of Dr. Hopkins, whose whole nature was so ripe for profit by such an experience as young Armstrong. He lived in the family of President Hopkins, and thus had a training that was wholly out of the common; and this training had much to do with the development of his own strong character, whose originality and force we are only beginning to appreciate.
passages.vernacular: 華盛頓先生早年生活嘅細節,正如《出身奴隸》坦率寫低,並冇完整呈現佢嘅教育全貌。佢接受過有色人種青年喺漢普頓所受嘅訓練,呢點自傳確實有交代。不過讀者得不到佢嘅思想淵源,因為華盛頓先生自己,也許,冇其他人咁清楚了解。事實係,佢喺一生最容易受影響嘅時期,接受咗非常特別嘅訓練,同代人當中少有人有過咁嘅訓練。要了解其全部意義,必須由半個世紀或者更早前嘅夏威夷群島開始。*嗰度,傳教士父母嘅兒子塞繆爾·阿姆斯特朗,賺到足夠錢支付喺一間美國學院讀書嘅費用。佢帶住呢筆小錢,同呢項事業所蘊含嘅誠摯,嚟到馬克·霍普金斯博士做校長時嘅威廉姆斯學院。威廉姆斯學院喺當時對青年有好多好處,今日亦然,不過最大嘅好處,係佢著名校長嘅強烈個人魅力。並非每個學生都能從偉大嘅老師身上得益;不過也許從來冇一個年輕人,像年輕嘅阿姆斯特朗咁,整個天性咁成熟,可以從霍普金斯博士嘅影響中得益。佢住喺霍普金斯校長嘅家庭,因此接受完全不同尋常嘅訓練;呢種訓練對佢自己強烈品格嘅發展有好大關係,佢品格嘅獨創性同力量,我哋而家才剛開始領會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 華盛頓先生早年生活的細節,正如《出身奴隸》坦率寫下,並沒有完整呈現他的教育全貌。他接受過有色人種青年在漢普頓所受的訓練,這一點自傳確實有交代。不過讀者得不到他的思想淵源,因為華盛頓先生自己,也許,沒有其他人那麼清楚了解。事實是,他在一生最容易受影響的時期,接受了非常特別的訓練,同代人當中少有人有過這樣的訓練。要了解其全部意義,必須由半個世紀或更早前的夏威夷群島開始。*那裡,傳教士父母的兒子塞繆爾·阿姆斯特朗,賺到足夠錢支付在一間美國學院讀書的費用。他帶著這筆小錢,和這項事業所蘊含的誠摯,來到馬克·霍普金斯博士做校長時的威廉斯學院。威廉斯學院在當時對青年有許多好處,今日亦然,不過最大的好處,是它著名校長的強烈個人魅力。並非每個學生都能從偉大的老師身上得益;不過也許從來沒有一個年輕人,像年輕的阿姆斯特朗那樣,整個天性那麼成熟,可以從霍普金斯博士的影響中得益。他住在霍普金斯校長的家庭,因此接受完全不同尋常的訓練;這種訓練對他自己強烈品格的發展有很大關係,他品格的獨創性和力量,我們現在才剛開始領會。

passages.original: * For this interesting view of Mr. Washington’s education, I am indebted to Robert C. Ogden, Esq., Chairman of the Board of Trustees of Hampton Institute and the intimate friend of General Armstrong during the whole period of his educational work.
passages.vernacular: *對於華盛頓先生教育嘅呢個有趣看法,我要感謝羅伯特·C·奧格登先生,佢係漢普頓學院董事會主席,亦係阿姆斯特朗將軍整個教育工作期間嘅摯友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: *對於華盛頓先生教育的這個有趣看法,我要感謝羅伯特·C·奧格登先生,他是漢普頓學院董事會主席,也是阿姆斯特朗將軍整個教育工作期間的摯友。

passages.original: In turn, Samuel Armstrong, the founder of Hampton Institute, took up his work as a trainer of youth. He had very raw material, and doubtless most of his pupils failed to get the greatest lessons from him; but, as he had been a peculiarly receptive pupil of Dr. Hopkins, so Booker Washington became a peculiarly receptive pupil of his. To the formation of Mr. Washington’s character, then, went the missionary zeal of New England, influenced by one of the strongest personalities in modern education, and the wide-reaching moral earnestness of General Armstrong himself. These influences are easily recognizable in Mr. Washington to-day by men who knew Dr. Hopkins and General Armstrong.
passages.vernacular: 之後,漢普頓學院創辦人塞繆爾·阿姆斯特朗,承擔起培訓青年嘅工作。佢嘅材料好粗糙,大部分學生大概都冇從佢身上學到最重要嘅功課;不過正如佢自己曾經係霍普金斯博士特別肯接受教導嘅學生,布克·華盛頓亦成為佢特別肯接受教導嘅學生。所以,華盛頓先生品格嘅形成,包含新英格蘭嘅傳教熱忱(受現代教育中最強烈嘅個性之一影響),以及阿姆斯特朗將軍自己影響深遠嘅道德誠摯。呢啲影響,認識霍普金斯博士同阿姆斯特朗將軍嘅人,今日喺華盛頓先生身上好容易辨認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 之後,漢普頓學院創辦人塞繆爾·阿姆斯特朗,承擔起培訓青年的工作。他的材料很粗糙,大部分學生大概都沒從他身上學到最重要的功課;不過正如他自己曾經是霍普金斯博士特別肯接受教導的學生,布克·華盛頓也成為他特別肯接受教導的學生。所以,華盛頓先生品格的形成,包含新英格蘭的傳教熱忱(受現代教育中最強烈的個性之一影響),以及阿姆斯特朗將軍自己影響深遠的道德誠摯。這些影響,認識霍普金斯博士和阿姆斯特朗將軍的人,今日在華盛頓先生身上很容易辨認。

passages.original: I got the cue to Mr. Washington’s character from a very simple incident many years ago. I had never seen him, and I knew little about him, except that he was the head of a school at Tuskegee, Alabama. I had occasion to write to him, and I addressed him as “The Rev. Booker T. Washington.” In his reply there was no mention of my addressing him as a clergyman. But when I had occasion to write to him again, and persisted in making him a preacher, his second letter brought a postscript: “I have no claim to ‘Rev.’” I knew most of the coloured men who at that time had become prominent as leaders of their race, but I had not then known one who was neither a politician nor a preacher; and I had not heard of the head of an important coloured school who was not a preacher. “A new kind of man in the coloured world,” I said to myself—“a new kind of man surely if he looks upon his task as an economic one instead of a theological one.” I wrote him an apology for mistaking him for a preacher.
passages.vernacular: 我從多年前一個好簡單嘅小事,領悟到華盛頓先生品格嘅線索。我從未見過佢,對佢所知好少,只知佢係阿拉巴馬州塔斯基吉一間學校嘅校長。我有事要寫信畀佢,稱呼佢「布克·T·華盛頓牧師」。佢嘅回信冇提到我稱呼佢做牧師。不過我有事再次寫信畀佢,仍然堅持將佢當成傳道人,佢嘅第二封信附有一句附言:「我冇資格稱『牧師』。」我認識當時已成為其種族領袖而知名嘅大部分有色人種男士,但我當時未認識一位既唔係政客亦唔係傳道人嘅;我亦未聽過一間重要有色人種學校嘅校長唔係傳道人。我同自己講:「有色人種世界嘅新一類人,」「如果佢視自己嘅任務為經濟性而唔係神學性,肯定係新一類人。」我寫咗封道歉信畀佢,為誤以為佢係傳道人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從多年前一個很簡單的小事,領悟到華盛頓先生品格的線索。我從未見過他,對他所知很少,只知他是阿拉巴馬州塔斯基吉一間學校的校長。我有事要寫信給他,稱呼他「布克·T·華盛頓牧師」。他的回信沒提到我稱呼他做牧師。不過我有事再次寫信給他,仍然堅持將他當成傳道人,他的第二封信附有一句附言:「我沒資格稱『牧師』。」我認識當時已成為其種族領袖而知名的大部分有色人種男士,但我當時未認識一位既不是政客也不是傳道人的;我也未聽過一間重要有色人種學校的校長不是傳道人。我對自己說:「有色人種世界的新一類人,」「如果他視自己的任務為經濟性而不是神學性,肯定是新一類人。」我寫了封道歉信給他,為誤以為他是傳道人。

passages.original: The first time that I went to Tuskegee I was asked to make an address to the school on Sunday evening. I sat upon the platform of the large chapel and looked forth on a thousand coloured faces, and the choir of a hundred or more behind me sang a familiar religious melody, and the whole company joined in the chorus with unction. I was the only white man under the roof, and the scene and the songs made an impression on me that I shall never forget. Mr. Washington arose and asked them to sing one after another of the old melodies that I had heard all my life; but I had never before heard them sung by a thousand voices nor by the voices of educated Negroes. I had associated them with the Negro of the past, not with the Negro who was struggling upward. They brought to my mind the plantation, the cabin, the slave, not the freedman in quest of education. But on the plantation and in the cabin they had never been sung as these thousand students sang them. I saw again all the old plantations that I had ever seen; the whole history of the Negro ran through my mind; and the inexpressible pathos of his life found expression in these songs as I had never before felt it.
passages.vernacular: 我第一次去塔斯基吉,被請喺星期日晚向學校發表演說。我坐喺大禮拜堂嘅講台上,望住一千張有色人種面孔,我後面一百幾人嘅詩班唱一首熟悉嘅宗教旋律,全場一齊熱情咁合唱副歌。我係屋頂下唯一嘅白人,呢個場景同歌聲令我留下永不忘記嘅印象。華盛頓先生站起,請佢哋一首接一首咁唱我一生都聽過嘅舊旋律;不過我從未聽過一千把聲音咁唱,亦從未聽過受過教育嘅黑人嘅聲音咁唱。我之前將佢哋同過去嘅黑人聯繫,而唔係同奮力向上嘅黑人聯繫。佢哋令我想起種植園、小屋、奴隸,而唔係追求教育嘅自由人。不過喺種植園同小屋裡面,佢哋從未被唱得似呢一千個學生咁唱。我再次見到我見過嘅所有舊種植園;黑人嘅整個歷史喺我腦海中掠過;佢生活嘅難以言喻嘅悲愴,喺呢啲歌曲中表達出嚟,我從未咁深切地感受過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我第一次去塔斯基吉,被請在星期日晚向學校發表演說。我坐在大禮拜堂的講台上,望著一千張有色人種面孔,我後面一百多人的詩班唱一首熟悉的宗教旋律,全場一起熱情地合唱副歌。我是屋頂下唯一的白人,這個場景和歌聲使我留下永不忘記的印象。華盛頓先生站起,請他們一首接一首地唱我一生都聽過的舊旋律;不過我從未聽過一千個聲音這樣唱,也從未聽過受過教育的黑人的聲音這樣唱。我之前將它們與過去的黑人聯繫,而不是與奮力向上的黑人聯繫。它們使我想起種植園、小屋、奴隸,而不是追求教育的自由人。不過在種植園和小屋裡,它們從未被唱得像這一千個學生那樣唱。我再次見到我見過的所有舊種植園;黑人的整個歷史在我腦海中掠過;他生活的難以言喻的悲愴,在這些歌曲中表達出來,我從未那麼深切地感受過。

passages.original: And the future? These were the ambitious youths of the race, at work with an earnestness that put to shame the conventional student life of most educational institutions. Another song rolled up along the rafters. And as soon as silence came, I found myself in front of this extraordinary mass of faces, thinking not of them, but of that long and unhappy chapter in our country’s history which followed the one great structural mistake of the Fathers of the Republic; thinking of the one continuous great problem that generations of statesmen had wrangled over, and a million men fought about, and that had so dwarfed the mass of English men in the Southern States as to hold them back a hundred years behind their fellows in every other part of the world—in England, in Australia, and in the Northern and Western States; I was thinking of this dark shadow that had oppressed every large-minded statesman from Jefferson to Lincoln. These thousand young men and women about me were victims of it. I, too, was an innocent victim of it. The whole Republic was a victim of that fundamental error of importing Africa into America. I held firmly to the first article of my faith that the Republic must stand fast by the principle of a fair ballot; but I recalled the wretched mess that Reconstruction had made of it; I recalled the low level of public life in all the “black” States. Every effort of philanthropy seemed to have miscarried, every effort at correcting abuses seemed of doubtful value, and the race friction seemed to become severer. Here was the century-old problem in all its pathos seated singing before me. Who were the more to be pitied—these innocent victims of an ancient wrong, or I and men like me, who had inherited the problem? I had long ago thrown aside illusions and theories, and was willing to meet the facts face to face, and to do whatever in God’s name a man might do towards saving the next generation from such a burden. But I felt the weight of twenty well-nigh hopeless years of thought and reading and observation; for the old difficulties remained and new ones had sprung up. Then I saw clearly that the way out of a century of blunders had been made by this man who stood beside me and was introducing me to this audience. Before me was the material he had used. All about me was the indisputable evidence that he had found the natural line of development. He had shown the way. Time and patience and encouragement and work would do the rest.
passages.vernacular: 而未來呢?呢啲係種族嘅有抱負嘅青年,以一種令大部分教育機構嘅傳統學生生活相形見絀嘅認真工作。另一首歌沿住椽子升起。一靜下嚟,我發現自己企喺呢大群非凡嘅面孔前面,唔係諗佢哋,而係諗我國歷史中跟隨共和國開國者一個巨大結構性錯誤嘅漫長不幸篇章;諗佢一個持續嘅巨大問題,幾代政治家為此爭吵,百萬人為此作戰,令南部各州嘅英國人大眾受壓抑,比世界其他地方嘅同胞落後一百年——英格蘭、澳洲,以及北部同西部各州;我諗緊呢個壓迫每一位胸襟廣闊嘅政治家(由傑佛遜到林肯)嘅黑暗陰影。我周圍呢一千個青年男女係佢嘅受害者。我亦係佢嘅無辜受害者。整個共和國都係「將非洲輸入美洲」呢個根本錯誤嘅受害者。我堅守我信仰第一條:共和國必須堅持公平投票嘅原則;不過我記起重建時期搞出嘅一團糟;我記起所有「黑人」州公共生活嘅低水平。每個慈善努力似乎都失敗,每個糾正弊端嘅努力似乎價值成疑,種族摩擦似乎變得更嚴重。呢個世紀之久嘅問題,連同佢全部悲愴,就坐喺我面前唱歌。誰更值得同情——呢啲古老不公嘅無辜受害者,抑或我同似我嘅人,繼承咗呢個問題?我好耐之前已經拋開幻想同理論,願意直面事實,並且以上帝之名,盡人所能令下一代免受呢個重擔。不過我感受到二十年幾乎絕望嘅思考、閱讀同觀察嘅重量;因為舊困難仍然存在,新困難又冒起。然後我清楚見到,走出一個世紀錯誤嘅道路,係由企喺我身旁、向呢班聽眾介紹我嘅呢個人開闢嘅。我面前就係佢所用嘅材料。我周圍都係無可爭辯嘅證據,證明佢搵到咗自然嘅發展路線。佢指出咗道路。時間、耐性、鼓勵同工作會做完其餘嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而未來呢?這些是種族的有抱負的青年,以一種使大部分教育機構的傳統學生生活相形見絀的認真工作。另一首歌沿著椽子升起。一靜下來,我發現自己站在這大群非凡的面孔前面,不是想他們,而是想我國歷史中跟隨共和國開國者一個巨大結構性錯誤的漫長不幸篇章;想它一個持續的巨大問題,幾代政治家為此爭吵,百萬人為此作戰,使南部各州的英國人大眾受壓抑,比世界其他地方的同胞落後一百年——英格蘭、澳洲,以及北部和西部各州;我想著這個壓迫每一位胸襟廣闊的政治家(由傑佛遜到林肯)的黑暗陰影。我周圍這一千個青年男女是它的受害者。我也是它的無辜受害者。整個共和國都是「將非洲輸入美洲」這個根本錯誤的受害者。我堅守我信仰第一條:共和國必須堅持公平投票的原則;不過我記起重建時期搞出的一團糟;我記起所有「黑人」州公共生活的低水平。每個慈善努力似乎都失敗,每個糾正弊端的努力似乎價值成疑,種族摩擦似乎變得更嚴重。這個世紀之久的問題,連同它全部悲愴,就坐在我面前唱歌。誰更值得同情——這些古老不公的無辜受害者,抑或我和像我的人,繼承了這個問題?我很久之前已經拋開幻想和理論,願意直面事實,並且以上帝之名,盡人所能使下一代免受這個重擔。不過我感受到二十年幾乎絕望的思考、閱讀和觀察的重量;因為舊困難仍然存在,新困難又冒起。然後我清楚看到,走出一個世紀錯誤的道路,是由站在我身旁、向這班聽眾介紹我的這個人開闢的。我面前就是他所用的材料。我周圍都是無可爭辯的證據,證明他找到了自然的發展路線。他指出了道路。時間、耐性、鼓勵和工作會做完其餘的。

passages.original: It was then more clearly than ever before that I understood the patriotic significance of Mr. Washington’s work. It is this conception of it and of him that I have ever since carried with me. It is on this that his claim to our gratitude rests.
passages.vernacular: 正係嗰時,我比以往任何時候都更清楚咁明白華盛頓先生工作嘅愛國意義。我從此一直帶住對佢同佢工作嘅呢個概念。佢要求我哋感激嘅基礎就在於此。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 正是那時,我比以往任何時候都更清楚地明白華盛頓先生工作的愛國意義。我從此一直帶著對他和他工作的這個概念。他要求我們感激的基礎就在於此。

passages.original: To teach the Negro to read, whether English, or Greek, or Hebrew, butters no parsnips. To make the Negro work, that is what his master did in one way and hunger has done in another; yet both these left Southern life where they found it. But to teach the Negro to do skilful work, as men of all the races that have risen have worked,—responsible work, which IS education and character; and most of all when Negroes so teach Negroes to do this that they will teach others with a missionary zeal that puts all ordinary philanthropic efforts to shame,—this is to change the whole economic basis of life and the whole character of a people.
passages.vernacular: 教黑人讀書,無論英文、希臘文或希伯來文,都「無補於事」。令黑人工作,呢個就係佢嘅主人用一種方式、飢餓用另一種方式做過嘅;但兩者都令南方生活停留喺佢哋發現嘅地方。但係教黑人做熟練嘅工作,正如所有崛起嘅種族嘅人所做嘅工作——負責任嘅工作,即係教育同品格;尤其當黑人咁教黑人做,令佢哋以傳教般嘅熱忱教導他人,令所有普通慈善努力相形見絀——呢個就係改變生活嘅整個經濟基礎同一個民族嘅整個品格。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 教黑人讀書,無論英文、希臘文或希伯來文,都「無補於事」。使黑人工作,這就是他的主人用一種方式、飢餓用另一種方式做過的;但兩者都使南方生活停留在它們發現的地方。但是教黑人做熟練的工作,正如所有崛起的種族的人所做的工作——負責任的工作,即教育和品格;尤其當黑人這樣教黑人做,使他們以傳教般的熱忱教導他人,使所有普通慈善努力相形見絀——這就是改變生活的整個經濟基礎和一個民族的整個品格。

passages.original: The plan itself is not a new one. It was worked out at Hampton Institute, but it was done at Hampton by white men. The plan had, in fact, been many times theoretically laid down by thoughtful students of Southern life. Handicrafts were taught in the days of slavery on most well-managed plantations. But Tuskegee is, nevertheless, a brand-new chapter in the history of the Negro, and in the history of the knottiest problem we have ever faced. It not only makes “a carpenter of a man; it makes a man of a carpenter.” In one sense, therefore, it is of greater value than any other institution for the training of men and women that we have, from Cambridge to Palo Alto. It is almost the only one of which it may be said that it points the way to a new epoch in a large area of our national life.
passages.vernacular: 呢個計劃本身並唔新。佢喺漢普頓學院實踐,不過喺漢普頓係由白人做嘅。計劃事實上已經被南方生活嘅深思學者理論性咁提出過好多次。奴隸制時期,大部分管理良好嘅種植園都教授手工藝。不過塔斯基吉仍然係黑人歷史、亦係我哋面對過最棘手問題嘅歷史中嘅嶄新篇章。佢唔單止「令一個人成為木匠;佢令一個木匠成為人」。所以,某種意義上,佢比我哋從劍橋到帕洛阿爾托嘅任何其他培訓男女嘅機構更有價值。佢幾乎係唯一一間可以話佢為我國生活嘅一大片領域指向新時代嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個計劃本身並不新。它在漢普頓學院實踐,不過在漢普頓是由白人做的。計劃事實上已經被南方生活的深思學者理論性地提出過很多次。奴隸制時期,大部分管理良好的種植園都教授手工藝。不過塔斯基吉仍然是黑人歷史、也是我們面對過最棘手問題的歷史中的嶄新篇章。它不僅「使一個人成為木匠;它使一個木匠成為人」。所以,某種意義上,它比我們從劍橋到帕洛阿爾托的任何其他培訓男女的機構更有價值。它幾乎是唯一一間可以說它為我國生活的一大片領域指向新時代的。

passages.original: To work out the plan on paper, or at a distance—that is one thing. For a white man to work it out—that too, is an easy thing. For a coloured man to work it out in the South, where, in its constructive period, he was necessarily misunderstood by his own people as well as by the whites, and where he had to adjust it at every step to the strained race relations—that is so very different and more difficult a thing that the man who did it put the country under lasting obligations to him.
passages.vernacular: 喺紙上或者遠處實踐呢個計劃,係一回事。由一個白人實踐——都係容易嘅事。由一個有色人種喺南方實踐,喺佢建設時期,必然被自己人民同白人誤解,而且每一步都要適應緊張嘅種族關係——就困難同不同得多,做到嘅人令國家永遠欠佢一份恩情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在紙上或遠處實踐這個計劃,是一回事。由一個白人實踐——也是容易的事。由一個有色人種在南方實踐,在他建設時期,必然被自己人民和白人誤解,而且每一步都要適應緊張的種族關係——就困難和不同得多,做到的人使國家永遠欠他一份恩情。

passages.original: It was not and is not a mere educational task. Anybody could teach boys trades and give them an elementary education. Such tasks have been done since the beginning of civilization. But this task had to be done with the rawest of raw material, done within the civilization of the dominant race, and so done as not to run across race lines and social lines that are the strongest forces in the community. It had to be done for the benefit of the whole community. It had to be done, moreover, without local help, in the face of the direst poverty, done by begging, and done in spite of the ignorance of one race and the prejudice of the other.
passages.vernacular: 佢過去唔係、而家亦唔係單純嘅教育任務。任何人都可以教男孩手藝,畀佢哋基本教育。此類任務自文明開始以來都做過。不過呢個任務要用最粗糙嘅原材料去做,喺主導種族嘅文明之內做,而且要做到唔越過社區中最強大力量嘅種族界線同社會界線。佢必須為整個社區嘅利益而做。而且佢必須在冇本地幫助、面對最嚴重貧困之下做,靠乞討做,儘管一個種族無知同另一個種族偏見都要做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它過去不是、現在也不是單純的教育任務。任何人都可以教男孩手藝,給他們基本教育。此類任務自文明開始以來都做過。不過這個任務要用最粗糙的原材料去做,在主導種族的文明之內做,而且要做到不越過社區中最強大力量的種族界線和社會界線。它必須為整個社區的利益而做。而且它必須在沒有本地幫助、面對最嚴重貧困之下做,靠乞討做,儘管一個種族無知和另一個種族偏見都要做。

passages.original: No man living had a harder task, and a task that called for more wisdom to do it right. The true measure of Mr. Washington’s success is, then, not his teaching the pupils of Tuskegee, nor even gaining the support of philanthropic persons at a distance, but this—that every Southern white man of character and of wisdom has been won to a cordial recognition of the value of the work, even men who held and still hold to the conviction that a mere book education for the Southern blacks under present conditions is a positive evil. This is a demonstration of the efficiency of the Hampton-Tuskegee idea that stands like the demonstration of the value of democratic institutions themselves—a demonstration made so clear in spite of the greatest odds that it is no longer open to argument.
passages.vernacular: 冇活人有更艱難嘅任務,亦冇任務需要更多智慧去做好。所以,衡量華盛頓先生成功嘅真正標準,唔係佢教塔斯基吉嘅學生,甚至唔係贏得遠方慈善人士嘅支持,而係呢點——每一位有品格同智慧嘅南方白人,都被爭取到誠懇認可呢項工作嘅價值,甚至包括曾經、而且仍然堅信在當前情況下單純書本教育對南方黑人係絕對有害嘅人。呢個係漢普頓—塔斯基吉理念成效嘅證明,就好似證明民主制度本身價值嘅證明一樣——儘管面對最大困難,仍然證明得如此清楚,已經不容爭論。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有活人有更艱難的任務,也沒有任務需要更多智慧去做好。所以,衡量華盛頓先生成功的真正標準,不是他教塔斯基吉的學生,甚至不是贏得遠方慈善人士的支持,而是這一點——每一位有品格和智慧的南方白人,都被爭取到誠懇認可這項工作的價值,甚至包括曾經、而且仍然堅信在當前情況下單純書本教育對南方黑人是絕對有害的人。這是漢普頓—塔斯基吉理念成效的證明,就像證明民主制度本身價值的證明一樣——儘管面對最大困難,仍然證明得如此清楚,已經不容爭論。

passages.original: Consider the change that has come in twenty years in the discussion of the Negro problem. Two or three decades ago social philosophers and statisticians and well-meaning philanthropists were still talking and writing about the deportation of the Negroes, or about their settlement within some restricted area, or about their settling in all parts of the Union, or about their decline through their neglect of their children, or about their rapid multiplication till they should expel the whites from the South—of every sort of nonsense under heaven. All this has given place to the simple plan of an indefinite extension among the neglected classes of both races of the Hampton-Tuskegee system of training. The “problem” in one sense has disappeared. The future will have for the South swift or slow development of its masses and of its soil in proportion to the swift or slow development of this kind of training. This change of view is a true measure of Mr. Washington’s work.
passages.vernacular: 想想二十年來黑人問題討論嘅變化。二三十年前,社會哲學家、統計學家同善意嘅慈善家仍然在談論同寫作關於驅逐黑人、將佢哋安置喺某個受限區域、令佢哋分散喺聯邦各地、佢哋因忽視子女而衰落,或者佢哋快速繁殖直到將白人逐出南方——天底下各種胡說八道。所有呢啲已經讓位畀一個簡單計劃:將漢普頓—塔斯基吉培訓制度無限擴展到兩個種族被忽視嘅階層。某種意義上,「問題」已經消失。南方嘅未來,其大眾同土地發展嘅快慢,將與此類培訓發展嘅快慢成比例。呢種觀點嘅轉變,係衡量華盛頓先生工作嘅真正尺度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想想二十年來黑人問題討論的變化。二三十年前,社會哲學家、統計學家和善意的慈善家仍然在談論和寫作關於驅逐黑人、將他們安置在某個受限區域、使他們分散在聯邦各地、他們因忽視子女而衰落,或者他們快速繁殖直到將白人逐出南方——天底下各種胡說八道。所有這些已經讓位給一個簡單計劃:將漢普頓—塔斯基吉培訓制度無限擴展到兩個種族被忽視的階層。某種意義上,「問題」已經消失。南方的未來,其大眾和土地發展的快慢,將與此類培訓發展的快慢成比例。這種觀點的轉變,是衡量華盛頓先生工作的真正尺度。

passages.original: The literature of the Negro in America is colossal, from political oratory through abolitionism to “Uncle Tom’s Cabin” and “Cotton is King”—a vast mass of books which many men have read to the waste of good years (and I among them); but the only books that I have read a second time or ever care again to read in the whole list (most of them by tiresome and unbalanced “reformers”) are “Uncle Remus” and “Up from Slavery”; for these are the great literature of the subject. One has all the best of the past, the other foreshadows a better future; and the men who wrote them are the only men who have written of the subject with that perfect frankness and perfect knowledge and perfect poise whose other name is genius.
passages.vernacular: 美國黑人嘅文獻浩如煙海,由政治演說經廢奴主義到《湯姆叔叔的小屋》同《棉花為王》——大量書籍,好多人讀過而浪費咗好年華(我亦在其中);不過我喺全部書單中讀過第二次、或者想再讀嘅書(大部分係由煩人、失衡嘅「改革者」寫),只有《雷穆斯叔叔》同《出身奴隸》;因為呢兩本係關於此主題嘅偉大文學。一本載有過去所有最好嘅,另一本預示更好嘅未來;而寫呢兩本書嘅人,係僅有以完美坦率、完美知識同完美平衡(佢另一個名字就係天才)寫此主題嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 美國黑人的文獻浩如煙海,由政治演說經廢奴主義到《湯姆叔叔的小屋》和《棉花為王》——大量書籍,很多人讀過而浪費了好年華(我也在其中);不過我在全部書單中讀過第二次、或想再讀的書(大部分是由煩人、失衡的「改革者」寫),只有《雷穆斯叔叔》和《出身奴隸》;因為這兩本是關於此主題的偉大文學。一本載有過去所有最好的,另一本預示更好的未來;而寫這兩本書的人,是僅有以完美坦率、完美知識和完美平衡(它另一個名字就是天才)寫此主題的人。

passages.original: Mr. Washington has won a world-wide fame at an early age. His story of his own life already has the distinction of translation into more languages, I think, than any other American book; and I suppose that he has as large a personal acquaintance among men of influence as any private citizen now living.
passages.vernacular: 華盛頓先生年紀輕輕就贏得世界性嘅名聲。佢自己人生嘅故事,已經有被翻譯成比任何其他美國書籍更多語言嘅榮譽,我諗;而我估計佢同有影響力人士嘅私人交往,同任何現存私人公民一樣廣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 華盛頓先生年紀輕輕就贏得世界性的名聲。他自己人生的故事,已經有被翻譯成比任何其他美國書籍更多語言的榮譽,我想;而我猜他與有影響力人士的私人交往,和任何現存私人公民一樣廣。

passages.original: His own teaching at Tuskegee is unique. He lectures to his advanced students on the art of right living, not out of text-books, but straight out of life. Then he sends them into the country to visit Negro families. Such a student will come back with a minute report of the way in which the family that he has seen lives, what their earnings are, what they do well and what they do ill; and he will explain how they might live better. He constructs a definite plan for the betterment of that particular family out of the resources that they have. Such a student, if he be bright, will profit more by an experience like this than he could profit by all the books on sociology and economics that ever were written. I talked with a boy at Tuskegee who had made such a study as this, and I could not keep from contrasting his knowledge and enthusiasm with what I heard in a class room at a Negro university in one of the Southern cities, which is conducted on the idea that a college course will save the soul. Here the class was reciting a lesson from an abstruse text-book on economics, reciting it by rote, with so obvious a failure to assimilate it that the waste of labour was pitiful.
passages.vernacular: 佢自己喺塔斯基吉嘅教學獨一無二。佢向高年級學生講授正確生活嘅藝術,唔係從教科書,而係直接從生活。然後佢派佢哋去鄉村探訪黑人家庭。呢種學生會帶住詳細報告返嚟,講佢所見嘅家庭點樣生活、收入幾多、佢哋做得好咩、做得差咩;佢會解釋佢哋可以點樣生活得更好。佢憑佢哋擁有嘅資源,為嗰個家庭改善制定一個具體計劃。如果呢種學生聰明,佢從呢種經驗得到嘅益處,多過從所有寫過嘅社會學同經濟學書籍得到嘅。我同塔斯基吉一個做過呢種研究嘅男孩傾過,我忍不住將佢嘅知識同熱情,同我喺南方一個城市黑人大學課室裡面聽到嘅比較,嗰度按「大學課程會拯救靈魂」嘅想法進行。嗰度班級正背誦一本艱深經濟學教科書嘅功課,死記硬背,明顯冇消化,勞力浪費得令人可憐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他自己在塔斯基吉的教學獨一無二。他向高年級學生講授正確生活的藝術,不是從教科書,而是直接從生活。然後他派他們去鄉村探訪黑人家庭。這種學生會帶著詳細報告回來,講他所見的家庭怎樣生活、收入多少、他們做得好什麼、做得差什麼;他會解釋他們可以怎樣生活得更好。他憑他們擁有的資源,為那個家庭改善制定一個具體計劃。如果這種學生聰明,他從這種經驗得到的益處,多過從所有寫過的社會學和經濟學書籍得到的。我與塔斯基吉一個做過這種研究的男孩談過,我忍不住將他的知識和熱情,與我在南方一個城市黑人大學課室裡聽到的比較,那裡按「大學課程會拯救靈魂」的想法進行。那裡班級正背誦一本艱深經濟學教科書的功課,死記硬背,明顯沒消化,勞力浪費得令人可憐。

passages.original: I asked Mr. Washington years ago what he regarded as the most important result of his work, and he replied:
passages.vernacular: 我多年前問華盛頓先生,佢認為佢工作最重要嘅成果係咩,佢答:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我多年前問華盛頓先生,他認為他工作最重要的成果是什麼,他答:

passages.original: “I do not know which to put first, the effect of Tuskegee’s work on the Negro, or the effect on the attitude of the white man to the Negro.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知先放邊個,係塔斯基吉工作對黑人嘅影響,定係對白人對黑人態度嘅影響。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道先放哪個,是塔斯基吉工作對黑人的影響,還是對白人對黑人態度的影響。」

passages.original: The race divergence under the system of miseducation was fast getting wider. Under the influence of the Hampton-Tuskegee idea the races are coming into a closer sympathy and into an honourable and helpful relation. As the Negro becomes economically independent, he becomes a responsible part of the Southern life; and the whites so recognize him. And this must be so from the nature of things. There is nothing artificial about it. It is development in a perfectly natural way. And the Southern whites not only so recognize it, but they are imitating it in the teaching of the neglected masses of their own race. It has thus come about that the school is taking a more direct and helpful hold on life in the South than anywhere else in the country. Education is not a thing apart from life—not a “system,” nor a philosophy; it is direct teaching how to live and how to work.
passages.vernacular: 喺錯誤教育制度下,種族分歧迅速擴大。喺漢普頓—塔斯基吉理念嘅影響下,種族正走向更緊密嘅同情,以及光榮而有益嘅關係。隨黑人經濟獨立,佢成為南方生活負責任嘅一部分;而白人亦咁承認佢。而呢點從事物性質嚟講必然如此。冇半點人為。係以完全自然嘅方式發展。而南方白人不單咁承認,而且喺教導自己種族被忽視嘅大眾時模仿佢。所以學校喺南方比喺國內任何其他地方,更直接、更有益咁把握生活。教育唔係獨立於生活嘅事物——唔係「制度」,唔係哲學;而係直接教授點樣生活同點樣工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在錯誤教育制度下,種族分歧迅速擴大。在漢普頓—塔斯基吉理念的影響下,種族正走向更緊密的同情,以及光榮而有益的關係。隨黑人經濟獨立,他成為南方生活負責任的一部分;而白人也這樣承認他。而這一點從事物性質來說必然如此。沒有半點人為。是以完全自然的方式發展。而南方白人不僅這樣承認,而且在教導自己種族被忽視的大眾時模仿它。所以學校在南方比在國內任何其他地方,更直接、更有益地把握生活。教育不是獨立於生活的事物——不是「制度」,不是哲學;而是直接教授怎樣生活和怎樣工作。

passages.original: To say that Mr. Washington has won the gratitude of all thoughtful Southern white men, is to say that he has worked with the highest practical wisdom at a large constructive task; for no plan for the up-building of the freedman could succeed that ran counter to Southern opinion. To win the support of Southern opinion and to shape it was a necessary part of the task; and in this he has so well succeeded that the South has a sincere and high regard for him. He once said to me that he recalled the day, and remembered it thankfully, when he grew large enough to regard a Southern white man as he regarded a Northern one. It is well for our common country that the day is come when he and his work are regarded as highly in the South as in any other part of the Union. I think that no man of our generation has a more noteworthy achievement to his credit than this; and it is an achievement of moral earnestness of the strong character of a man who has done a great national service.
passages.vernacular: 講華盛頓先生贏得所有深思熟慮嘅南方白人嘅感激,就係講佢以最高嘅實用智慧處理一項大型建設性任務;因為任何違反南方輿論嘅解放黑奴重建計劃都唔會成功。贏得南方輿論嘅支持並塑造佢,係任務必要嘅一部分;而佢做得咁好,令南方對佢有真誠而崇高嘅尊重。佢曾經同我講,佢記得、並感激地記得,佢長大到可以像看待北方白人一樣看待南方白人嗰日。對我哋共同嘅國家好彩,而家佢同佢嘅工作喺南方受到同聯邦其他任何地方一樣高嘅尊重。我認為我哋呢一代冇人有比呢個更值得注意嘅成就;而且係一個強者品格嘅道德誠摯嘅成就,佢為國家作出咗偉大嘅服務。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說華盛頓先生贏得所有深思熟慮的南方白人的感激,就是說他以最高的實用智慧處理一項大型建設性任務;因為任何違反南方輿論的解放黑奴重建計劃都不會成功。贏得南方輿論的支持並塑造它,是任務必要的一部分;而他做得這麼好,使南方對他有真誠而崇高的尊重。他曾經對我說,他記得、並感激地記得,他長大到可以像看待北方白人一樣看待南方白人那一天。對我們共同的國家幸運,現在他和他的工作在南方受到和聯邦其他任何地方一樣高的尊重。我認為我們這一代沒有人有比這個更值得注意的成就;而且是一個強者品格的道德誠摯的成就,他為國家作出了偉大的服務。

passages.original: Walter H. Page.
passages.vernacular: 沃爾特·H·佩奇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沃爾特·H·佩奇。

chapters.title: A Slave Among Slaves 奴隸之中的奴隸

passages.original: I was born a slave on a plantation in Franklin County, Virginia. I am not quite sure of the exact place or exact date of my birth, but at any rate I suspect I must have been born somewhere and at some time. As nearly as I have been able to learn, I was born near a cross-roads post-office called Hale’s Ford, and the year was 1858 or 1859. I do not know the month or the day. The earliest impressions I can now recall are of the plantation and the slave quarters—the latter being the part of the plantation where the slaves had their cabins.
passages.vernacular: 我係喺弗吉尼亞州富蘭克林縣一個種植園出世嘅奴隸。我唔太肯定自己出世嘅確切地點同確切日期,不過無論如何,我估計我一定係喺某處、某個時候出世嘅。據我所能了解,我係喺一個叫黑爾渡口嘅十字路口郵局附近出世,年份係1858年或者1859年。月份同日子我唔知道。我而家能夠回憶最早嘅印象,係種植園同奴隸住處——後者係種植園內奴隸住小屋嘅部分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是在弗吉尼亞州富蘭克林縣一個種植園出生的奴隸。我不太肯定自己出生的確切地點和確切日期,不過無論如何,我猜我一定是在某處、某個時候出生的。據我所能了解,我是在一個叫黑爾渡口的十字路口郵局附近出生,年份是1858年或1859年。月份和日子我不知道。我現在能夠回憶最早的印象,是種植園和奴隸住處——後者是種植園內奴隸住小屋的部分。

passages.original: My life had its beginning in the midst of the most miserable, desolate, and discouraging surroundings. This was so, however, not because my owners were especially cruel, for they were not, as compared with many others. I was born in a typical log cabin, about fourteen by sixteen feet square. In this cabin I lived with my mother and a brother and sister till after the Civil War, when we were all declared free.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅生命喺最悲慘、荒涼、令人氣餒嘅環境中開始。不過,呢個並唔係因為我嘅主人特別殘酷,因為同好多其他人比較,佢哋並唔係。我喺一間典型嘅木屋出世,大約十四呎乘十六呎見方。我同我媽媽、一個哥哥同一個妹妹住喺呢間屋,直到內戰之後,我哋全部被宣布自由。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的生命在最悲慘、荒涼、令人氣餒的環境中開始。不過,這並不是因為我的主人特別殘酷,因為與很多其他人比較,他們並不是。我在一間典型的木屋出生,大約十四呎乘十六呎見方。我與我母親、一個哥哥和一個妹妹住在這間屋子,直到內戰之後,我們全部被宣布自由。

passages.original: Of my ancestry I know almost nothing. In the slave quarters, and even later, I heard whispered conversations among the coloured people of the tortures which the slaves, including, no doubt, my ancestors on my mother’s side, suffered in the middle passage of the slave ship while being conveyed from Africa to America. I have been unsuccessful in securing any information that would throw any accurate light upon the history of my family beyond my mother. She, I remember, had a half-brother and a half-sister. In the days of slavery not very much attention was given to family history and family records—that is, black family records. My mother, I suppose, attracted the attention of a purchaser who was afterward my owner and hers. Her addition to the slave family attracted about as much attention as the purchase of a new horse or cow. Of my father I know even less than of my mother. I do not even know his name. I have heard reports to the effect that he was a white man who lived on one of the near-by plantations. Whoever he was, I never heard of his taking the least interest in me or providing in any way for my rearing. But I do not find especial fault with him. He was simply another unfortunate victim of the institution which the Nation unhappily had engrafted upon it at that time.
passages.vernacular: 關於我嘅祖先,我幾乎一無所知。喺奴隸住處,甚至之後,我聽到有色人種之間低聲談論奴隸喺從非洲運往美洲嘅奴隸船「中間航程」所受嘅酷刑,無疑包括我母親一方嘅祖先。我冇成功取得任何資料,可以準確說明我母親以外我家族嘅歷史。我記得,佢有一個同父異母嘅哥哥同一個同父異母嘅姐姐。喺奴隸制時代,冇太多人留意家族歷史同家族記錄——即係黑人嘅家族記錄。我估計,我媽媽引起咗一位買家嘅注意,佢之後成為我同佢嘅主人。佢加入奴隸家庭引起嘅注意,大約同買一匹新馬或者新牛差唔多。關於我爸爸,我知道得比我媽媽更少。我甚至唔知道佢嘅名。我聽過傳聞,話佢係住喺附近一個種植園嘅白人。無論佢係邊個,我從未聽過佢對我有半點興趣,或者以任何方式供養我成長。不過我並唔特別責怪佢。佢只係另一個不幸嘅受害者,受害於國家當時不幸嫁接上嘅制度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 關於我的祖先,我幾乎一無所知。在奴隸住處,甚至之後,我聽到有色人種之間低聲談論奴隸在從非洲運往美洲的奴隸船「中間航程」所受的酷刑,無疑包括我母親一方的祖先。我沒成功取得任何資料,可以準確說明我母親以外我家族的歷史。我記得,她有一個同父異母的哥哥和一個同父異母的姐姐。在奴隸制時代,沒太多人留意家族歷史和家族記錄——即黑人的家族記錄。我猜,我母親引起了一位買家的注意,他之後成為我和她的主人。她加入奴隸家庭引起的注意,大約與買一匹新馬或新牛差不多。關於我父親,我知道得比我母親更少。我甚至不知道他的名字。我聽過傳聞,說他是住在附近一個種植園的白人。無論他是誰,我從未聽過他對我有半點興趣,或以任何方式供養我成長。不過我並不特別責怪他。他只是另一個不幸的受害者,受害於國家當時不幸嫁接上的制度。

passages.original: The cabin was not only our living-place, but was also used as the kitchen for the plantation. My mother was the plantation cook. The cabin was without glass windows; it had only openings in the side which let in the light, and also the cold, chilly air of winter. There was a door to the cabin—that is, something that was called a door—but the uncertain hinges by which it was hung, and the large cracks in it, to say nothing of the fact that it was too small, made the room a very uncomfortable one. In addition to these openings there was, in the lower right-hand corner of the room, the “cat-hole,”—a contrivance which almost every mansion or cabin in Virginia possessed during the ante-bellum period. The “cat-hole” was a square opening, about seven by eight inches, provided for the purpose of letting the cat pass in and out of the house at will during the night. In the case of our particular cabin I could never understand the necessity for this convenience, since there were at least a half-dozen other places in the cabin that would have accommodated the cats. There was no wooden floor in our cabin, the naked earth being used as a floor. In the centre of the earthen floor there was a large, deep opening covered with boards, which was used as a place in which to store sweet potatoes during the winter. An impression of this potato-hole is very distinctly engraved upon my memory, because I recall that during the process of putting the potatoes in or taking them out I would often come into possession of one or two, which I roasted and thoroughly enjoyed. There was no cooking-stove on our plantation, and all the cooking for the whites and slaves my mother had to do over an open fireplace, mostly in pots and “skillets.” While the poorly built cabin caused us to suffer with cold in the winter, the heat from the open fireplace in summer was equally trying.
passages.vernacular: 呢間屋唔單止係我哋嘅居所,亦係種植園嘅廚房。我媽媽係種植園嘅廚師。屋冇玻璃窗;只有側面嘅開口,讓光線進入,同時亦讓冬天嘅冷風進入。屋有一道門——即係被稱為門嘅嘢——不過佢嘅鉸鏈不牢固,門上有大裂縫,更不用講佢太細,令房間好不舒服。除咗呢啲開口之外,房間右下角有個「貓洞」——內戰前時期弗吉尼亞幾乎每間大宅或小屋都有嘅設計。「貓洞」係一個大約七吋乘八吋嘅方形開口,用嚟讓貓喺夜晚隨意出入屋。對於我哋呢間小屋,我從來唔明白點解需要呢個設施,因為小屋至少有六個其他地方可以讓貓進出。我哋屋冇木地板,赤裸嘅泥土就係地板。泥土地板中間有個大而深嘅開口,蓋住木板,冬天用嚟儲存番薯。呢個薯洞嘅印象非常清晰咁刻在我記憶裡面,因為我記得在放入或者拿出番薯嘅過程中,我經常拎到一兩個,烤熟之後津津有味咁食。我哋種植園冇煮食爐,我媽媽要為白人同奴隸煮所有嘅嘢,都喺敞開嘅壁爐上,大多用鍋同「長柄煎鍋」。建得差嘅小屋令我哋冬天挨凍,而夏天敞開壁爐嘅熱度同樣難受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這間屋子不僅是我們的居所,也是種植園的廚房。我母親是種植園的廚師。屋子沒有玻璃窗;只有側面的開口,讓光線進入,同時也讓冬天的冷風進入。屋子有一道門——即被稱為門的東西——不過它的鉸鏈不牢固,門上有大裂縫,更不用說它太小,使房間很不舒服。除了這些開口之外,房間右下角有個「貓洞」——內戰前時期弗吉尼亞幾乎每間大宅或小屋都有的設計。「貓洞」是一個大約七吋乘八吋的方形開口,用來讓貓在夜晚隨意出入屋子。對於我們這間小屋,我從來不明白為什麼需要這個設施,因為小屋至少有六個其他地方可以讓貓進出。我們屋子沒木地板,赤裸的泥土就是地板。泥土地板中間有個大而深的開口,蓋著木板,冬天用來儲存番薯。這個薯洞的印象非常清晰地刻在我記憶裡,因為我記得在放入或拿出番薯的過程中,我經常拿到一兩個,烤熟之後津津有味地吃。我們種植園沒煮食爐,我母親要為白人和奴隸煮所有的東西,都在敞開的壁爐上,多數用鍋和「長柄煎鍋」。建得差的小屋使我們冬天挨凍,而夏天敞開壁爐的熱度同樣難受。

passages.original: The early years of my life, which were spent in the little cabin, were not very different from those of thousands of other slaves. My mother, of course, had little time in which to give attention to the training of her children during the day. She snatched a few moments for our care in the early morning before her work began, and at night after the day’s work was done. One of my earliest recollections is that of my mother cooking a chicken late at night, and awakening her children for the purpose of feeding them. How or where she got it I do not know. I presume, however, it was procured from our owner’s farm. Some people may call this theft. If such a thing were to happen now, I should condemn it as theft myself. But taking place at the time it did, and for the reason that it did, no one could ever make me believe that my mother was guilty of thieving. She was simply a victim of the system of slavery. I cannot remember having slept in a bed until after our family was declared free by the Emancipation Proclamation. Three children—John, my older brother, Amanda, my sister, and myself—had a pallet on the dirt floor, or, to be more correct, we slept in and on a bundle of filthy rags laid upon the dirt floor.
passages.vernacular: 我喺細小屋度度過嘅早年生活,同成千上萬其他奴隸嘅冇好大分別。我媽媽日間當然冇太多時間關心子女嘅教養。佢喺一大清早開工之前,同夜晚一日工作完成之後,抽幾分鐘照顧我哋。我最早嘅記憶之一,係我媽媽喺深夜煮一隻雞,叫醒佢啲子女食。佢點樣、喺邊度攞到,我唔知道。不過我估計係從我哋主人嘅農場攞嘅。有人可能稱呢種做偷竊。如果呢種事而家發生,我自己都會譴責佢係偷竊。不過當時發生,而且出於當時嗰個原因,冇人可以令我相信我媽媽有偷竊罪。佢只係奴隸制度嘅受害者。我記不起在我哋家庭因《解放宣言》被宣布自由之前,我睡過床。三個孩子——我哥哥約翰、我妹妹阿曼達同我——喺泥地上有一張草墊,或者更準確咁講,我哋睡喺一堆鋪喺泥地上嘅污糟破布入面同上面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在細小屋度過的早年生活,與成千上萬其他奴隸的沒有很大分別。我母親白天當然沒太多時間關心子女的教養。她在一大清早開工之前,和夜晚一天工作完成之後,抽幾分鐘照顧我們。我最早的記憶之一,是我母親在深夜煮一隻雞,叫醒她的子女吃。她怎樣、在哪裡拿到,我不知道。不過我猜是從我們主人的農場拿的。有人可能稱這種做偷竊。如果這種事現在發生,我自己也會譴責它是偷竊。不過當時發生,而且出於當時那個原因,沒有人可以使我相信我母親有偷竊罪。她只是奴隸制度的受害者。我記不起在我們家庭因《解放宣言》被宣布自由之前,我睡過床。三個孩子——我哥哥約翰、我妹妹阿曼達和我——在泥地上有一張草墊,或者更準確地說,我們睡在一堆鋪在泥地上的骯髒破布裡面和上面。

passages.original: I was asked not long ago to tell something about the sports and pastimes that I engaged in during my youth. Until that question was asked it had never occurred to me that there was no period of my life that was devoted to play. From the time that I can remember anything, almost every day of my life had been occupied in some kind of labour; though I think I would now be a more useful man if I had had time for sports. During the period that I spent in slavery I was not large enough to be of much service, still I was occupied most of the time in cleaning the yards, carrying water to the men in the fields, or going to the mill to which I used to take the corn, once a week, to be ground. The mill was about three miles from the plantation. This work I always dreaded. The heavy bag of corn would be thrown across the back of the horse, and the corn divided about evenly on each side; but in some way, almost without exception, on these trips, the corn would so shift as to become unbalanced and would fall off the horse, and often I would fall with it. As I was not strong enough to reload the corn upon the horse, I would have to wait, sometimes for many hours, till a chance passer-by came along who would help me out of my trouble. The hours while waiting for some one were usually spent in crying. The time consumed in this way made me late in reaching the mill, and by the time I got my corn ground and reached home it would be far into the night. The road was a lonely one, and often led through dense forests. I was always frightened. The woods were said to be full of soldiers who had deserted from the army, and I had been told that the first thing a deserter did to a Negro boy when he found him alone was to cut off his ears. Besides, when I was late in getting home I knew I would always get a severe scolding or a flogging.
passages.vernacular: 前不久有人要我講下我年輕時參與過嘅運動同消遣。喺被問到之前,我從未想過我人生冇一段時間係用嚟玩嘅。從我記得任何嘢開始,我人生幾乎每日都忙於某種勞動;雖然我諗如果我有時間玩運動,我而家可能係個更有用嘅人。我做奴隸嘅時期,我唔夠大做好多事,不過我大部分時間都忙於清潔院子、擔水畀田裡嘅男人,或者去磨坊,我習慣每星期一次帶玉米去磨。磨坊距離種植園大約三英里。呢份工作我一直好驚。沉重嘅玉米袋會被放喺馬背上,玉米大致平均分喺兩邊;不過幾乎毫無例外,喺呢啲旅程中,玉米會以某種方式移位變得失衡,從馬上跌落,而我經常同佢一齊跌落。因為我唔夠力將玉米重新放返上馬,我要等,有時好幾個鐘,直到有路過嘅人幫我脫困。等人嘅時間,通常用嚟喊。咁樣消耗嘅時間令我遲到磨坊,到我磨好玉米返到屋企,已經深夜。路荒涼,經常穿過茂密森林。我一直好驚。據講樹林裡面滿係逃兵,有人話我知,逃兵遇到獨自一人嘅黑人男孩,第一件事就係割佢耳仔。此外,我遲返屋企時,我知道總會捱一頓嚴厲責罵或者鞭打。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 前不久有人要我講講我年輕時參與過的運動和消遣。在被問到之前,我從未想過我人生沒有一段時間是用來玩的。從我記得任何東西開始,我人生幾乎每天都忙於某種勞動;雖然我想如果我有時間玩運動,我現在可能是個更有用的人。我做奴隸的時期,我不夠大做很多事,不過我大部分時間都忙於清潔院子、擔水給田裡的男人,或去磨坊,我習慣每星期一次帶玉米去磨。磨坊距離種植園大約三英里。這份工作我一直很怕。沉重的玉米袋會被放在馬背上,玉米大致平均分在兩邊;不過幾乎毫無例外,在這些旅程中,玉米會以某種方式移位變得失衡,從馬上跌落,而我經常與它一起跌落。因為我不夠力將玉米重新放回馬上,我要等,有時好幾個小時,直到有路過的人幫我脫困。等人的時間,通常用來哭。這樣消耗的時間使我遲到磨坊,到我磨好玉米回到家,已經深夜。路荒涼,經常穿過茂密森林。我一直很怕。據說樹林裡滿是逃兵,有人告訴我,逃兵遇到獨自一人的黑人男孩,第一件事就是割他耳朵。此外,我晚回家時,我知道總會挨一頓嚴厲責罵或鞭打。

passages.original: I had no schooling whatever while I was a slave, though I remember on several occasions I went as far as the schoolhouse door with one of my young mistresses to carry her books. The picture of several dozen boys and girls in a schoolroom engaged in study made a deep impression upon me, and I had the feeling that to get into a schoolhouse and study in this way would be about the same as getting into paradise.
passages.vernacular: 我做奴隸時完全冇上過學,雖然我記得有幾次,我陪一位年輕小姐去到學校門口,幫佢拎書。幾十個男孩女孩喺課室裡面學習嘅畫面,令我留下深刻印象,我覺得入學校讀書,就同入天堂差唔多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我做奴隸時完全沒上過學,雖然我記得有幾次,我陪一位年輕小姐去到學校門口,幫她拿書。幾十個男孩女孩在課室裡學習的畫面,使我留下深刻印象,我覺得入學校讀書,就與入天堂差不多。

passages.original: So far as I can now recall, the first knowledge that I got of the fact that we were slaves, and that freedom of the slaves was being discussed, was early one morning before day, when I was awakened by my mother kneeling over her children and fervently praying that Lincoln and his armies might be successful, and that one day she and her children might be free. In this connection I have never been able to understand how the slaves throughout the South, completely ignorant as were the masses so far as books or newspapers were concerned, were able to keep themselves so accurately and completely informed about the great National questions that were agitating the country. From the time that Garrison, Lovejoy, and others began to agitate for freedom, the slaves throughout the South kept in close touch with the progress of the movement. Though I was a mere child during the preparation for the Civil War and during the war itself, I now recall the many late-at-night whispered discussions that I heard my mother and the other slaves on the plantation indulge in. These discussions showed that they understood the situation, and that they kept themselves informed of events by what was termed the “grape-vine” telegraph.
passages.vernacular: 就我而家所能記得,我第一次知道我哋係奴隸、而且奴隸嘅自由正被討論,係一個清晨天未亮,我被我媽媽喚醒,佢跪喺子女上面,熱切祈禱林肯同佢軍隊成功,有一日佢同子女可以自由。就此而言,我從來唔明白,點解南方各地嘅奴隸,對書本或報紙完全無知,居然能夠咁準確全面咁了解當時震動國家嘅國家大問題。自從加里森、洛夫喬伊同其他人開始鼓吹自由,南方各地嘅奴隸都同運動嘅進展保持密切聯繫。雖然內戰準備期間同戰爭期間我只係個小孩,我而家記得我聽到我媽媽同種植園其他奴隸深夜低聲討論嘅許多情景。呢啲討論顯示佢哋明白形勢,並透過所謂「葡萄藤」電報令自己了解事件。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就我現在所能記得,我第一次知道我們是奴隸、而且奴隸的自由正被討論,是一個清晨天未亮,我被我母親喚醒,她跪在子女上面,熱切祈禱林肯和他軍隊成功,有一天她和子女可以自由。就此而言,我從來不明白,為什麼南方各地的奴隸,對書本或報紙完全無知,居然能夠這麼準確全面地了解當時震動國家的國家大問題。自從加里森、洛夫喬伊和其他人開始鼓吹自由,南方各地的奴隸都與運動的進展保持密切聯繫。雖然內戰準備期間和戰爭期間我只是個小孩,我現在記得我聽到我母親和種植園其他奴隸深夜低聲討論的許多情景。這些討論顯示他們明白形勢,並透過所謂「葡萄藤」電報使自己了解事件。

passages.original: During the campaign when Lincoln was first a candidate for the Presidency, the slaves on our far-off plantation, miles from any railroad or large city or daily newspaper, knew what the issues involved were. When war was begun between the North and the South, every slave on our plantation felt and knew that, though other issues were discussed, the primal one was that of slavery. Even the most ignorant members of my race on the remote plantations felt in their hearts, with a certainty that admitted of no doubt, that the freedom of the slaves would be the one great result of the war, if the Northern armies conquered. Every success of the Federal armies and every defeat of the Confederate forces was watched with the keenest and most intense interest. Often the slaves got knowledge of the results of great battles before the white people received it. This news was usually gotten from the coloured man who was sent to the post-office for the mail. In our case the post-office was about three miles from the plantation, and the mail came once or twice a week. The man who was sent to the office would linger about the place long enough to get the drift of the conversation from the group of white people who naturally congregated there, after receiving their mail, to discuss the latest news. The mail-carrier on his way back to our master’s house would as naturally retail the news that he had secured among the slaves, and in this way they often heard of important events before the white people at the “big house,” as the master’s house was called.
passages.vernacular: 林肯首次做總統候選人嘅競選期間,我哋偏遠種植園嘅奴隸,距離任何鐵路、大城市或日報幾英里,知道涉及嘅議題係咩。當南北開戰時,我哋種植園每個奴隸都感覺同知道,雖然其他議題被討論,最主要嘅係奴隸制度。即使喺偏遠種植園我嘅種族當中最無知嘅成員,心裡面都毫無疑問地感覺到,如果北軍征服,奴隸嘅自由會係戰爭嘅一個大結果。聯邦軍隊每次成功、同盟軍每次失敗,都被最敏銳、最強烈嘅興趣追蹤。奴隸們經常比白人更早得知大戰役嘅結果。呢啲消息通常係從被派去郵局拎信嘅有色人種男人度得到。就我哋嘅情況,郵局距離種植園大約三英里,信件每星期一兩次到。被派去郵局嘅人會喺嗰度逗留足夠長時間,從自然聚集喺嗰度、收完信之後討論最新消息嘅白人群組入面,聽取談話嘅大意。取信人返主人屋嘅途中,自然會將所得消息傳畀奴隸,咁樣佢哋經常比被稱為「大屋」嘅主人屋裡面嘅白人更早聽到重要事件。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 林肯首次做總統候選人的競選期間,我們偏遠種植園的奴隸,距離任何鐵路、大城市或日報幾英里,知道涉及的議題是什麼。當南北開戰時,我們種植園每個奴隸都感覺和知道,雖然其他議題被討論,最主要的是奴隸制度。即使在偏遠種植園我的種族當中最無知的成員,心裡都毫無疑問地感覺到,如果北軍征服,奴隸的自由會是戰爭的一個大結果。聯邦軍隊每次成功、同盟軍每次失敗,都被最敏銳、最強烈的興趣追蹤。奴隸們經常比白人更早得知大戰役的結果。這些消息通常是從被派去郵局拿信的有色人種男人那裡得到。就我們的情況,郵局距離種植園大約三英里,信件每星期一兩次到。被派去郵局的人會在那裡逗留足夠長時間,從自然聚集在那裡、收完信之後討論最新消息的白人群組中,聽取談話的大意。取信人回主人屋的途中,自然會將所得消息傳給奴隸,這樣他們經常比被稱為「大屋」的主人屋裡的白人更早聽到重要事件。

passages.original: I cannot remember a single instance during my childhood or early boyhood when our entire family sat down to the table together, and God’s blessing was asked, and the family ate a meal in a civilized manner. On the plantation in Virginia, and even later, meals were gotten by the children very much as dumb animals get theirs. It was a piece of bread here and a scrap of meat there. It was a cup of milk at one time and some potatoes at another. Sometimes a portion of our family would eat out of the skillet or pot, while some one else would eat from a tin plate held on the knees, and often using nothing but the hands with which to hold the food. When I had grown to sufficient size, I was required to go to the “big house” at meal-times to fan the flies from the table by means of a large set of paper fans operated by a pulley. Naturally much of the conversation of the white people turned upon the subject of freedom and the war, and I absorbed a good deal of it. I remember that at one time I saw two of my young mistresses and some lady visitors eating ginger-cakes, in the yard. At that time those cakes seemed to me to be absolutely the most tempting and desirable things that I had ever seen; and I then and there resolved that, if I ever got free, the height of my ambition would be reached if I could get to the point where I could secure and eat ginger-cakes in the way that I saw those ladies doing.
passages.vernacular: 我記不起在我童年或者早期少年時期,有過一次我哋全家一齊坐喺枱邊、請求上帝祝福、全家以文明方式食一餐飯。喺弗吉尼亞嘅種植園,甚至之後,孩子哋攞食物嘅方式同啞巴動物攞食物差唔多。呢度一塊麵包,嗰度一小塊肉。有時一杯牛奶,有時一啲薯仔。有時我哋家人當中一部分人從長柄煎鍋或者鍋食,另一人從放喺膝上嘅錫碟食,經常除咗雙手冇其他工具拿住食物。我長到夠大之後,要求喺用餐時間去「大屋」,用一套大型紙扇(以滑輪操作)為枱扇走蒼蠅。自然地,白人好多談話都圍繞自由同戰爭,我吸收咗好多。我記得有一次,我喺院子裡面見到我兩位年輕小姐同一些女士訪客喺度食薑餅。當時嗰啲餅對我嚟講絕對係我見過最誘人、最想要嘅嘢;我就喺嗰度下定決心,如果我有自由,我最大嘅抱負就係可以搵到、並以我見到嗰啲女士咁嘅方式食薑餅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我記不起在我童年或早期少年時期,有過一次我們全家一起坐在桌邊、請求上帝祝福、全家以文明方式吃一頓飯。在弗吉尼亞的種植園,甚至之後,孩子們拿食物的方式與啞巴動物拿食物差不多。這裡一塊麵包,那裡一小塊肉。有時一杯牛奶,有時一些馬鈴薯。有時我們家人當中一部分人從長柄煎鍋或鍋吃,另一人從放在膝上的錫碟吃,經常除了雙手沒其他工具拿著食物。我長到夠大之後,要求在用餐時間去「大屋」,用一套大型紙扇(以滑輪操作)為桌子扇走蒼蠅。自然地,白人很多談話都圍繞自由和戰爭,我吸收了很多。我記得有一次,我在院子裡看到我兩位年輕小姐和一些女士訪客在吃薑餅。當時那些餅對我來說絕對是我見過最誘人、最想要的東西;我就在那裡下定決心,如果我有自由,我最大的抱負就是可以找到、並以我看到那些女士那樣的方式吃薑餅。

passages.original: Of course as the war was prolonged the white people, in many cases, often found it difficult to secure food for themselves. I think the slaves felt the deprivation less than the whites, because the usual diet for slaves was corn bread and pork, and these could be raised on the plantation; but coffee, tea, sugar, and other articles which the whites had been accustomed to use could not be raised on the plantation, and the conditions brought about by the war frequently made it impossible to secure these things. The whites were often in great straits. Parched corn was used for coffee, and a kind of black molasses was used instead of sugar. Many times nothing was used to sweeten the so-called tea and coffee.
passages.vernacular: 當然隨戰爭持續,白人好多時發現自己都難以搵到食物。我認為奴隸對匱乏嘅感受比白人少,因為奴隸通常嘅飲食係粟米麵包同豬肉,呢啲可以喺種植園種;但咖啡、茶、糖同其他白人習慣使用嘅物品,唔能夠喺種植園種,戰爭造成嘅情況經常令搵到呢啲嘢變成不可能。白人經常陷入極大困境。烘乾嘅玉米被用嚟代替咖啡,一種黑糖蜜用嚟代替糖。好多時所謂嘅茶同咖啡冇用任何嘢加甜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然隨戰爭持續,白人很多時候發現自己也難以找到食物。我認為奴隸對匱乏的感受比白人少,因為奴隸通常的飲食是玉米麵包和豬肉,這些可以在種植園種;但咖啡、茶、糖和其他白人習慣使用的物品,不能夠在種植園種,戰爭造成的情況經常使找到這些東西變成不可能。白人經常陷入極大困境。烘乾的玉米被用來代替咖啡,一種黑糖蜜用來代替糖。很多時所謂的茶和咖啡沒用任何東西加甜。

passages.original: The first pair of shoes that I recall wearing were wooden ones. They had rough leather on the top, but the bottoms, which were about an inch thick, were of wood. When I walked they made a fearful noise, and besides this they were very inconvenient, since there was no yielding to the natural pressure of the foot. In wearing them one presented an exceedingly awkward appearance. The most trying ordeal that I was forced to endure as a slave boy, however, was the wearing of a flax shirt. In the portion of Virginia where I lived it was common to use flax as part of the clothing for the slaves. That part of the flax from which our clothing was made was largely the refuse, which of course was the cheapest and roughest part. I can scarcely imagine any torture, except, perhaps, the pulling of a tooth, that is equal to that caused by putting on a new flax shirt for the first time. It is almost equal to the feeling that one would experience if he had a dozen or more chestnut burrs, or a hundred small pin-points, in contact with his flesh. Even to this day I can recall accurately the tortures that I underwent when putting on one of these garments. The fact that my flesh was soft and tender added to the pain. But I had no choice. I had to wear the flax shirt or none; and had it been left to me to choose, I should have chosen to wear no covering. In connection with the flax shirt, my brother John, who is several years older than I am, performed one of the most generous acts that I ever heard of one slave relative doing for another. On several occasions when I was being forced to wear a new flax shirt, he generously agreed to put it on in my stead and wear it for several days, till it was “broken in.” Until I had grown to be quite a youth this single garment was all that I wore.
passages.vernacular: 我記得穿過嘅第一對鞋係木鞋。佢哋鞋面係粗皮革,但鞋底大約一吋厚,係木頭。我行路時佢哋發出可怕嘅聲音,而且非常不便,因為對腳嘅自然壓力冇半點讓步。穿佢哋時樣子極其笨拙。不過,我做奴隸男孩時被迫忍受最難受嘅考驗,係穿亞麻衫。喺我住嘅弗吉尼亞地區,用亞麻做奴隸衣服一部分好普遍。用嚟做我哋衣服嘅亞麻部分,大多係廢料,當然係最平、最粗糙嘅部分。我幾乎想像唔到有任何酷刑,除咗拔牙,可以同第一次穿新亞麻衫造成嘅痛苦相比。佢幾乎等於一個人有十幾個或更多栗子刺殼,或者一百個細針尖,接觸皮膚嘅感覺。即使到今日,我仍然可以準確回憶我穿其中一件衣服時所受嘅酷刑。我嘅皮膚柔軟嬌嫩,增加咗痛苦。不過我冇選擇。我要穿亞麻衫,否則冇衫穿;如果由我選擇,我會選擇冇衫穿。關於亞麻衫,我哥哥約翰(佢比我大幾歲),做咗我聽過一個奴隸親人為另一個做過最慷慨嘅事之一。有幾次我被迫穿新亞麻衫,佢慷慨咁答應代我穿,穿幾日,直到佢「穿軟」。直到我長成相當大嘅少年,呢件單衣就係我穿嘅全部。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我記得穿過的第一雙鞋是木鞋。它們鞋面是粗皮革,但鞋底大約一吋厚,是木頭。我走路時它們發出可怕的聲音,而且非常不便,因為對腳的自然壓力沒半點讓步。穿它們時樣子極其笨拙。不過,我做奴隸男孩時被迫忍受最難受的考驗,是穿亞麻衫。在我住的弗吉尼亞地區,用亞麻做奴隸衣服一部分很普遍。用來做我們衣服的亞麻部分,多數是廢料,當然是最便宜、最粗糙的部分。我幾乎想像不到有任何酷刑,除了拔牙,可以與第一次穿新亞麻衫造成的痛苦相比。它幾乎等於一個人有十幾個或更多栗子刺殼,或一百個細針尖,接觸皮膚的感覺。即使到今日,我仍然可以準確回憶我穿其中一件衣服時所受的酷刑。我的皮膚柔軟嬌嫩,增加了痛苦。不過我沒選擇。我要穿亞麻衫,否則沒衣服穿;如果由我選擇,我會選擇沒衣服穿。關於亞麻衫,我哥哥約翰(他比我大幾歲),做了我聽過一個奴隸親人為另一個做過最慷慨的事之一。有幾次我被迫穿新亞麻衫,他慷慨地答應代我穿,穿幾天,直到它「穿軟」。直到我長成相當大的少年,這件單衣就是我穿的全部。

passages.original: One may get the idea, from what I have said, that there was bitter feeling toward the white people on the part of my race, because of the fact that most of the white population was away fighting in a war which would result in keeping the Negro in slavery if the South was successful. In the case of the slaves on our place this was not true, and it was not true of any large portion of the slave population in the South where the Negro was treated with anything like decency. During the Civil War one of my young masters was killed, and two were severely wounded. I recall the feeling of sorrow which existed among the slaves when they heard of the death of “Mars’ Billy.” It was no sham sorrow, but real. Some of the slaves had nursed “Mars’ Billy”; others had played with him when he was a child. “Mars’ Billy” had begged for mercy in the case of others when the overseer or master was thrashing them. The sorrow in the slave quarter was only second to that in the “big house.” When the two young masters were brought home wounded, the sympathy of the slaves was shown in many ways. They were just as anxious to assist in the nursing as the family relatives of the wounded. Some of the slaves would even beg for the privilege of sitting up at night to nurse their wounded masters. This tenderness and sympathy on the part of those held in bondage was a result of their kindly and generous nature. In order to defend and protect the women and children who were left on the plantations when the white males went to war, the slaves would have laid down their lives. The slave who was selected to sleep in the “big house” during the absence of the males was considered to have the place of honour. Any one attempting to harm “young Mistress” or “old Mistress” during the night would have had to cross the dead body of the slave to do so. I do not know how many have noticed it, but I think that it will be found to be true that there are few instances, either in slavery or freedom, in which a member of my race has been known to betray a specific trust.
passages.vernacular: 從我所講嘅,人們可能以為我嘅種族對白人有怨恨,因為大部分白人都離開咗去打一場如果南方成功就會令黑人繼續做奴隸嘅戰爭。就我哋農場嘅奴隸而言,並唔係咁;南方奴隸人口大部分(黑人受到起碼體面對待嘅地方)亦唔係咁。內戰期間,我其中一位年輕少爺被殺,兩位重傷。我記得奴隸們聽到「比利少爺」死訊時嘅悲傷。唔係假悲傷,係真嘅。有些奴隸照顧過「比利少爺」;其他人曾喺佢細時同佢玩。當監工或主人鞭打其他人時,「比利少爺」曾為佢哋求情。奴隸住處嘅悲傷,僅次於「大屋」。當兩位年輕少爺受傷被帶返屋,奴隸嘅同情以多種方式顯示。佢哋同傷者嘅家庭親屬一樣渴望參與照顧。有些奴隸甚至乞求准許夜晚守夜照顧受傷嘅少爺。呢種被奴役者嘅溫柔同情,係佢哋善良慷慨天性嘅結果。為咗保衛同保護白人男性上戰場後留喺種植園嘅婦女同孩子,奴隸們會獻出生命。男性不在期間被挑選睡喺「大屋」嘅奴隸,被視為擁有榮譽職位。任何人夜晚想傷害「少奶奶」或「老太太」,都必須跨過呢位奴隸嘅屍體。我唔知有幾多人留意到,不過我認為會發現確實如此:無論喺奴隸制或自由中,我嘅種族成員被知道背叛特定信任嘅例子好少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從我所說的,人們可能以為我的種族對白人有怨恨,因為大部分白人都離開了去打一場如果南方成功就會使黑人繼續做奴隸的戰爭。就我們農場的奴隸而言,並不是這樣;南方奴隸人口大部分(黑人受到起碼體面對待的地方)也不是這樣。內戰期間,我其中一位年輕少爺被殺,兩位重傷。我記得奴隸們聽到「比利少爺」死訊時的悲傷。不是假悲傷,是真的。有些奴隸照顧過「比利少爺」;其他人曾在他小時與他玩。當監工或主人鞭打其他人時,「比利少爺」曾為他們求情。奴隸住處的悲傷,僅次於「大屋」。當兩位年輕少爺受傷被帶回家,奴隸的同情以多種方式顯示。他們與傷者的家庭親屬一樣渴望參與照顧。有些奴隸甚至乞求准許夜晚守夜照顧受傷的少爺。這種被奴役者的溫柔同情,是他們善良慷慨天性的結果。為了保衛和保護白人男性上戰場後留在種植園的婦女和孩子,奴隸們會獻出生命。男性不在期間被挑選睡在「大屋」的奴隸,被視為擁有榮譽職位。任何人夜晚想傷害「少奶奶」或「老太太」,都必須跨過這位奴隸的屍體。我不知有多少人留意到,不過我認為會發現確實如此:無論在奴隸制或自由中,我的種族成員被知道背叛特定信任的例子很少。

passages.original: As a rule, not only did the members of my race entertain no feelings of bitterness against the whites before and during the war, but there are many instances of Negroes tenderly caring for their former masters and mistresses who for some reason have become poor and dependent since the war. I know of instances where the former masters of slaves have for years been supplied with money by their former slaves to keep them from suffering. I have known of still other cases in which the former slaves have assisted in the education of the descendants of their former owners. I know of a case on a large plantation in the South in which a young white man, the son of the former owner of the estate, has become so reduced in purse and self-control by reason of drink that he is a pitiable creature; and yet, notwithstanding the poverty of the coloured people themselves on this plantation, they have for years supplied this young white man with the necessities of life. One sends him a little coffee or sugar, another a little meat, and so on. Nothing that the coloured people possess is too good for the son of “old Mars’ Tom,” who will perhaps never be permitted to suffer while any remain on the place who knew directly or indirectly of “old Mars’ Tom.”
passages.vernacular: 通常,我嘅種族成員喺戰前同戰時,不單對白人冇怨恨,而且有好多例子,黑人溫柔照顧因某些原因戰後變得貧窮同依賴嘅前主人同前女主人。我知道有例子,奴隸嘅前主人多年來由佢哋嘅前奴隸提供金錢,令佢哋免於受苦。我亦知道其他例子,前奴隸協助教育佢哋前主人嘅後代。我知道南方一個大種植園嘅例子,一位年輕白人(前莊園主嘅兒子)因飲酒而錢財同自制力大幅衰退,成為可憐嘅人;然而,儘管呢個種植園有色人種自己貧窮,佢哋多年來一直為呢位年輕白人提供生活必需品。一人送佢少少咖啡或者糖,另一人送少少肉,如此類推。有色人種擁有嘅任何嘢,都唔會好過畀「老湯姆少爺」嘅兒子,只要種植園還有人直接或間接認識「老湯姆少爺」,佢也許永遠唔會被容許受苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 通常,我的種族成員在戰前和戰時,不僅對白人沒怨恨,而且有很多例子,黑人溫柔照顧因某些原因戰後變得貧窮和依賴的前主人和前女主人。我知道有例子,奴隸的前主人多年來由他們的前奴隸提供金錢,使他們免於受苦。我也知道其他例子,前奴隸協助教育他們前主人的後代。我知道南方一個大種植園的例子,一位年輕白人(前莊園主的兒子)因飲酒而錢財和自制力大幅衰退,成為可憐的人;然而,儘管這個種植園有色人種自己貧窮,他們多年來一直為這位年輕白人提供生活必需品。一人送他一點咖啡或糖,另一人送一點肉,如此類推。有色人種擁有的任何東西,都不會好過給「老湯姆少爺」的兒子,只要種植園還有人直接或間接認識「老湯姆少爺」,他也許永遠不會被容許受苦。

passages.original: I have said that there are few instances of a member of my race betraying a specific trust. One of the best illustrations of this which I know of is in the case of an ex-slave from Virginia whom I met not long ago in a little town in the state of Ohio. I found that this man had made a contract with his master, two or three years previous to the Emancipation Proclamation, to the effect that the slave was to be permitted to buy himself, by paying so much per year for his body; and while he was paying for himself, he was to be permitted to labour where and for whom he pleased. Finding that he could secure better wages in Ohio, he went there. When freedom came, he was still in debt to his master some three hundred dollars. Notwithstanding that the Emancipation Proclamation freed him from any obligation to his master, this black man walked the greater portion of the distance back to where his old master lived in Virginia, and placed the last dollar, with interest, in his hands. In talking to me about this, the man told me that he knew that he did not have to pay the debt, but that he had given his word to the master, and his word he had never broken. He felt that he could not enjoy his freedom till he had fulfilled his promise.
passages.vernacular: 我話過,我嘅種族成員背叛特定信任嘅例子好少。我知道其中一個最好嘅說明,係一位來自弗吉尼亞嘅前奴隸,我不久前喺俄亥俄州一個小鎮遇到。我發現呢個人喺《解放宣言》之前兩三年同佢主人訂過合約,內容係准許該奴隸買斷自己,每年付若干作為身體嘅價錢;而佢為自己付款期間,准許佢喺邊度、為邊個勞動,隨佢喜歡。發現可以喺俄亥俄賺更好工資,佢就去咗嗰度。自由到來時,佢仍然欠主人大約三百美元。儘管《解放宣言》令佢免於對主人嘅任何責任,呢位黑人步行咗大部分路程返去佢舊主人喺弗吉尼亞居住嘅地方,將最後一個美元連利息放喺佢手上。同我談及呢件事時,佢話佢知道自己唔需要還債,但佢向主人承諾過,而佢從未食言。佢覺得,履行承諾之前,佢冇辦法享受自由。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說過,我的種族成員背叛特定信任的例子很少。我知道其中一個最好的說明,是一位來自弗吉尼亞的前奴隸,我不久前在俄亥俄州一個小鎮遇到。我發現這個人在《解放宣言》之前兩三年與他主人訂過合約,內容是准許該奴隸買斷自己,每年付若干作為身體的價錢;而他為自己付款期間,准許他在哪裡、為誰勞動,隨他喜歡。發現可以在俄亥俄賺更好工資,他就去了那裡。自由到來時,他仍然欠主人大約三百美元。儘管《解放宣言》使他免於對主人的任何責任,這位黑人步行了大部分路程回去他舊主人在弗吉尼亞居住的地方,將最後一個美元連利息放在他手上。與我談及這件事時,他說他知道自己不需要還債,但他向主人承諾過,而他從未食言。他覺得,履行承諾之前,他沒辦法享受自由。

passages.original: From some things that I have said one may get the idea that some of the slaves did not want freedom. This is not true. I have never seen one who did not want to be free, or one who would return to slavery.
passages.vernacular: 從我所講嘅一些嘢,人們可能以為有些奴隸唔想要自由。並唔係咁。我從未見過一個唔想自由、或者會返去做奴隸嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從我所說的一些話,人們可能以為有些奴隸不想要自由。並不是這樣。我從未見過一個不想自由、或會回去做奴隸的人。

passages.original: I pity from the bottom of my heart any nation or body of people that is so unfortunate as to get entangled in the net of slavery. I have long since ceased to cherish any spirit of bitterness against the Southern white people on account of the enslavement of my race. No one section of our country was wholly responsible for its introduction, and, besides, it was recognized and protected for years by the General Government. Having once got its tentacles fastened on to the economic and social life of the Republic, it was no easy matter for the country to relieve itself of the institution. Then, when we rid ourselves of prejudice, or racial feeling, and look facts in the face, we must acknowledge that, notwithstanding the cruelty and moral wrong of slavery, the ten million Negroes inhabiting this country, who themselves or whose ancestors went through the school of American slavery, are in a stronger and more hopeful condition, materially, intellectually, morally, and religiously, than is true of an equal number of black people in any other portion of the globe. This is so to such an extent that Negroes in this country, who themselves or whose forefathers went through the school of slavery, are constantly returning to Africa as missionaries to enlighten those who remained in the fatherland. This I say, not to justify slavery—on the other hand, I condemn it as an institution, as we all know that in America it was established for selfish and financial reasons, and not from a missionary motive—but to call attention to a fact, and to show how Providence so often uses men and institutions to accomplish a purpose. When persons ask me in these days how, in the midst of what sometimes seem hopelessly discouraging conditions, I can have such faith in the future of my race in this country, I remind them of the wilderness through which and out of which, a good Providence has already led us.
passages.vernacular: 我由衷同情任何不幸被奴隸制網羅纏住嘅國家或群體。我好耐之前已經唔再對南方白人因為我種族被奴役而懷有怨恨嘅心態。我國冇任何一個地區要為佢嘅引入完全負責,而且,聯邦政府多年來都承認同保護佢。一旦佢嘅觸手固定喺共和國嘅經濟同社會生活上,國家要擺脫呢個制度並唔容易。然後,當我哋擺脫偏見或種族感情,直面事實,我哋必須承認,儘管奴隸制殘酷同道德上錯誤,居住喺呢個國家、自己或者祖先經歷過美國奴隸制學校嘅一千萬黑人,在物質、智力、道德同宗教上,比地球任何其他地方同等數量嘅黑人,都處於更強同更有希望嘅狀況。程度如此,以致呢個國家嘅黑人(自己或祖先經歷過奴隸制學校),不斷返去非洲做傳教士,啟蒙留喺祖國嘅人。我講呢啲唔係為奴隸制辯護——相反,我譴責佢作為一種制度,因為我哋都知道佢喺美洲係出於自私同金錢理由而建立,唔係出於傳教動機——而係為咗引起大家注意一個事實,並顯示天意點樣經常使用人同制度去完成一個目的。當今天有人問我,喺有時似乎毫無希望地令人氣餒嘅情況之中,我點樣對我種族喺呢個國家嘅未來有咁大信心,我提醒佢哋,仁慈嘅天意已經帶領我哋穿過、走出嘅荒野。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我由衷同情任何不幸被奴隸制網羅纏住的國家或群體。我很久之前已經不再對南方白人因為我種族被奴役而懷有怨恨的心態。我國沒有任何一個地區要為它的引入完全負責,而且,聯邦政府多年來都承認和保護它。一旦它的觸手固定在共和國的經濟和社會生活上,國家要擺脫這個制度並不容易。然後,當我們擺脫偏見或種族感情,直面事實,我們必須承認,儘管奴隸制殘酷和道德上錯誤,居住在這個國家、自己或祖先經歷過美國奴隸制學校的一千萬黑人,在物質、智力、道德和宗教上,比地球任何其他地方同等數量的黑人,都處於更強和更有希望的狀況。程度如此,以致這個國家的黑人(自己或祖先經歷過奴隸制學校),不斷回去非洲做傳教士,啟蒙留在祖國的人。我說這些不是為奴隸制辯護——相反,我譴責它作為一種制度,因為我們都知道它在美洲是出於自私和金錢理由而建立,不是出於傳教動機——而是為了引起大家注意一個事實,並顯示天意怎樣經常使用人和制度去完成一個目的。當今天有人問我,在有時似乎毫無希望地令人氣餒的情況之中,我怎樣對我種族在這個國家的未來有那麼大信心,我提醒他們,仁慈的天意已經帶領我們穿過、走出的荒野。

passages.original: Ever since I have been old enough to think for myself, I have entertained the idea that, notwithstanding the cruel wrongs inflicted upon us, the black man got nearly as much out of slavery as the white man did. The hurtful influences of the institution were not by any means confined to the Negro. This was fully illustrated by the life upon our own plantation. The whole machinery of slavery was so constructed as to cause labour, as a rule, to be looked upon as a badge of degradation, of inferiority. Hence labour was something that both races on the slave plantation sought to escape. The slave system on our place, in a large measure, took the spirit of self-reliance and self-help out of the white people. My old master had many boys and girls, but not one, so far as I know, ever mastered a single trade or special line of productive industry. The girls were not taught to cook, sew, or to take care of the house. All of this was left to the slaves. The slaves, of course, had little personal interest in the life of the plantation, and their ignorance prevented them from learning how to do things in the most improved and thorough manner. As a result of the system, fences were out of repair, gates were hanging half off the hinges, doors creaked, window-panes were out, plastering had fallen but was not replaced, weeds grew in the yard. As a rule, there was food for whites and blacks, but inside the house, and on the dining-room table, there was wanting that delicacy and refinement of touch and finish which can make a home the most convenient, comfortable, and attractive place in the world. Withal there was a waste of food and other materials which was sad. When freedom came, the slaves were almost as well fitted to begin life anew as the master, except in the matter of book-learning and ownership of property. The slave owner and his sons had mastered no special industry. They unconsciously had imbibed the feeling that manual labour was not the proper thing for them. On the other hand, the slaves, in many cases, had mastered some handicraft, and none were ashamed, and few unwilling, to labour.
passages.vernacular: 自從我年紀夠大可以自己思考,我就一直有個想法:儘管我哋受到殘酷嘅不公對待,黑人從奴隸制得到嘅,幾乎同白人一樣多。呢個制度嘅有害影響絕不限於黑人。我哋自己種植園嘅生活充分說明咗呢點。奴隸制嘅整個機制,被建構成令勞動通常被視為墮落同低等嘅標誌。所以,勞動係奴隸種植園上兩個種族都試圖逃避嘅嘢。我哋農場嘅奴隸制度,很大程度上奪走咗白人嘅自力更生同自助精神。我舊主人有好多兒女,但就我所知,冇一個掌握過一門手藝或者任何特定生產行業。女孩冇被教煮食、縫紉或者照顧房子。所有呢啲都留畀奴隸。奴隸當然對種植園生活冇太大個人興趣,佢哋嘅無知又令佢哋無法學習以最改良、最徹底嘅方式做事。制度嘅結果係:籬笆失修,門半吊喺鉸鏈上,門吱吱作響,窗玻璃冇咗,灰泥跌咗冇補,院子長滿雜草。通常,白人同黑人都有食物,不過屋裡面同飯廳枱上,缺乏嗰種可以令家成為世上最方便、舒適、有吸引力嘅地方嘅精緻同優雅嘅修飾。此外,食物同其他材料嘅浪費令人難過。自由到來時,除咗書本學問同財產擁有權之外,奴隸幾乎同主人一樣適合重新開始人生。奴隸主同佢兒子冇掌握任何特定行業。佢哋無意中吸收咗一種感覺:體力勞動唔適合佢哋。另一方面,奴隸喺好多情況下掌握咗某種手藝,冇一個覺得羞恥,亦少有不願意勞動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從我年紀夠大可以自己思考,我就一直有個想法:儘管我們受到殘酷的不公對待,黑人從奴隸制得到的,幾乎與白人一樣多。這個制度的有害影響絕不限於黑人。我們自己種植園的生活充分說明了這一點。奴隸制的整個機制,被建構成使勞動通常被視為墮落和低等的標誌。所以,勞動是奴隸種植園上兩個種族都試圖逃避的東西。我們農場的奴隸制度,很大程度上奪走了白人的自力更生和自助精神。我舊主人有很多兒女,但就我所知,沒有一個掌握過一門手藝或任何特定生產行業。女孩沒被教煮食、縫紉或照顧房子。所有這些都留給奴隸。奴隸當然對種植園生活沒太大個人興趣,他們的無知又使他們無法學習以最改良、最徹底的方式做事。制度的結果是:籬笆失修,門半吊在鉸鏈上,門吱吱作響,窗玻璃沒了,灰泥掉了沒補,院子長滿雜草。通常,白人和黑人都有食物,不過屋裡和飯廳桌上,缺乏那種可以使家成為世上最方便、舒適、有吸引力的地方的精緻和優雅的修飾。此外,食物和其他材料的浪費令人難過。自由到來時,除了書本學問和財產擁有權之外,奴隸幾乎與主人一樣適合重新開始人生。奴隸主和他兒子沒掌握任何特定行業。他們無意中吸收了一種感覺:體力勞動不適合他們。另一方面,奴隸在很多情況下掌握了某種手藝,沒有一個覺得羞恥,也少有不願意勞動。

passages.original: Finally the war closed, and the day of freedom came. It was a momentous and eventful day to all upon our plantation. We had been expecting it. Freedom was in the air, and had been for months. Deserting soldiers returning to their homes were to be seen every day. Others who had been discharged, or whose regiments had been paroled, were constantly passing near our place. The “grape-vine telegraph” was kept busy night and day. The news and mutterings of great events were swiftly carried from one plantation to another. In the fear of “Yankee” invasions, the silverware and other valuables were taken from the “big house,” buried in the woods, and guarded by trusted slaves. Woe be to any one who would have attempted to disturb the buried treasure. The slaves would give the Yankee soldiers food, drink, clothing—anything but that which had been specifically intrusted to their care and honour. As the great day drew nearer, there was more singing in the slave quarters than usual. It was bolder, had more ring, and lasted later into the night. Most of the verses of the plantation songs had some reference to freedom. True, they had sung those same verses before, but they had been careful to explain that the “freedom” in these songs referred to the next world, and had no connection with life in this world. Now they gradually threw off the mask, and were not afraid to let it be known that the “freedom” in their songs meant freedom of the body in this world. The night before the eventful day, word was sent to the slave quarters to the effect that something unusual was going to take place at the “big house” the next morning. There was little, if any, sleep that night. All as excitement and expectancy. Early the next morning word was sent to all the slaves, old and young, to gather at the house. In company with my mother, brother, and sister, and a large number of other slaves, I went to the master’s house. All of our master’s family were either standing or seated on the veranda of the house, where they could see what was to take place and hear what was said. There was a feeling of deep interest, or perhaps sadness, on their faces, but not bitterness. As I now recall the impression they made upon me, they did not at the moment seem to be sad because of the loss of property, but rather because of parting with those whom they had reared and who were in many ways very close to them. The most distinct thing that I now recall in connection with the scene was that some man who seemed to be a stranger (a United States officer, I presume) made a little speech and then read a rather long paper—the Emancipation Proclamation, I think. After the reading we were told that we were all free, and could go when and where we pleased. My mother, who was standing by my side, leaned over and kissed her children, while tears of joy ran down her cheeks. She explained to us what it all meant, that this was the day for which she had been so long praying, but fearing that she would never live to see.
passages.vernacular: 終於戰爭結束,自由嘅日子到來。對我哋種植園上所有人嚟講,呢日係重大而多事嘅一日。我哋一直都預期。自由喺空氣中,已經好幾個月。每日都可以見到逃兵返屋企。其他被解散、或者所屬團被假釋嘅人,不斷經過我哋附近。「葡萄藤電報」日夜忙碌。大事嘅消息同低語迅速從一個種植園傳到另一個。因為害怕「洋基」入侵,銀器同其他貴重物品被從「大屋」拎出,埋喺樹林,由可信賴嘅奴隸看守。任何人如果試圖騷擾埋藏嘅寶藏就有禍了。奴隸會畀洋基士兵食物、飲品、衣服——任何嘢,除咗被明確託付畀佢哋照顧同榮譽嘅嘢。隨大日子接近,奴隸住處嘅歌聲比平時更多。歌聲更大膽,更響亮,持續到更夜。種植園歌曲大部分歌詞都同自由有關。確實,佢哋以前唱過同樣歌詞,不過佢哋小心解釋,歌中嘅「自由」係指來世,同今世生活冇關係。而家佢哋逐漸摘下面具,不怕讓人知道佢哋歌中嘅「自由」意思係今世身體嘅自由。重大日子前一晚,消息傳到奴隸住處,話第二朝「大屋」會發生一些不尋常嘅事。嗰晚幾乎冇瞓過,如果有嘅話。一切都係興奮同期待。第二日一大清早,消息傳畀所有奴隸,不論老幼,到屋集合。我同我媽媽、哥哥、妹妹,以及大批其他奴隸,一齊去咗主人屋。我哋主人全家,不是企著就是坐喺屋嘅走廊上,可以睇到將發生嘅事、聽到所講嘅話。佢哋臉上有種深切關注,或者也許悲傷嘅感覺,但冇怨恨。我而家記起佢哋畀我嘅印象:佢哋當時似乎唔係因為失去財產而悲傷,而係因為同自己養大、而且喺好多方面非常親近嘅人分離。我而家記得同呢個場景有關最清楚嘅,係一個似乎係陌生人嘅男人(我估係美國軍官)發表咗簡短演說,然後讀咗一份相當長嘅文件——我諗係《解放宣言》。讀完之後,我哋被告知全部都自由,可以喺自己喜歡嘅時間去自己喜歡嘅地方。我媽媽企喺我身旁,俯身吻佢啲子女,喜悅嘅眼淚沿住佢臉頰流落。佢向我哋解釋呢一切係咩意思:呢日係佢祈禱咗咁耐、卻擔心自己活唔到見到嘅日子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 終於戰爭結束,自由的日子到來。對我們種植園上所有人來說,這一天是重大而多事的一天。我們一直都預期。自由在空氣中,已經好幾個月。每天都可以看到逃兵回家。其他被解散、或所屬團被假釋的人,不斷經過我們附近。「葡萄藤電報」日夜忙碌。大事的消息和低語迅速從一個種植園傳到另一個。因為害怕「洋基」入侵,銀器和其他貴重物品被從「大屋」拿出,埋在樹林,由可信賴的奴隸看守。任何人如果試圖騷擾埋藏的寶藏就有禍了。奴隸會給洋基士兵食物、飲品、衣服——任何東西,除了被明確託付給他們照顧和榮譽的東西。隨大日子接近,奴隸住處的歌聲比平時更多。歌聲更大膽,更響亮,持續到更夜。種植園歌曲大部分歌詞都與自由有關。確實,他們以前唱過同樣歌詞,不過他們小心解釋,歌中的「自由」是指來世,與今世生活沒關係。現在他們逐漸摘下面具,不怕讓人知道他們歌中的「自由」意思是今世身體的自由。重大日子前一晚,消息傳到奴隸住處,說第二天早上「大屋」會發生一些不尋常的事。那晚幾乎沒睡過,如果有的話。一切都是興奮和期待。第二天一大清早,消息傳給所有奴隸,無論老幼,到屋子集合。我與我母親、哥哥、妹妹,以及大批其他奴隸,一起去了主人屋。我們主人全家,不是站著就是坐在屋子的走廊上,可以看到將發生的事、聽到所說的話。他們臉上有種深切關注,或許悲傷的感覺,但沒怨恨。我現在記起他們給我的印象:他們當時似乎不是因為失去財產而悲傷,而是因為與自己養大、而且在很多方面非常親近的人分離。我現在記得與這個場景有關最清楚的,是一個似乎是陌生人的男人(我猜是美國軍官)發表了簡短演說,然後讀了一份相當長的文件——我想是《解放宣言》。讀完之後,我們被告知全部都自由,可以在自己喜歡的時間去自己喜歡的地方。我母親站在我身旁,俯身吻她的子女,喜悅的眼淚沿著她臉頰流下。她向我們解釋這一切是什麼意思:這天是她祈禱了那麼久、卻擔心自己活不到看到的日子。

passages.original: For some minutes there was great rejoicing, and thanksgiving, and wild scenes of ecstasy. But there was no feeling of bitterness. In fact, there was pity among the slaves for our former owners. The wild rejoicing on the part of the emancipated coloured people lasted but for a brief period, for I noticed that by the time they returned to their cabins there was a change in their feelings. The great responsibility of being free, of having charge of themselves, of having to think and plan for themselves and their children, seemed to take possession of them. It was very much like suddenly turning a youth of ten or twelve years out into the world to provide for himself. In a few hours the great questions with which the Anglo-Saxon race had been grappling for centuries had been thrown upon these people to be solved. These were the questions of a home, a living, the rearing of children, education, citizenship, and the establishment and support of churches. Was it any wonder that within a few hours the wild rejoicing ceased and a feeling of deep gloom seemed to pervade the slave quarters? To some it seemed that, now that they were in actual possession of it, freedom was a more serious thing than they had expected to find it. Some of the slaves were seventy or eighty years old; their best days were gone. They had no strength with which to earn a living in a strange place and among strange people, even if they had been sure where to find a new place of abode. To this class the problem seemed especially hard. Besides, deep down in their hearts there was a strange and peculiar attachment to “old Marster” and “old Missus,” and to their children, which they found it hard to think of breaking off. With these they had spent in some cases nearly a half-century, and it was no light thing to think of parting. Gradually, one by one, stealthily at first, the older slaves began to wander from the slave quarters back to the “big house” to have a whispered conversation with their former owners as to the future.
passages.vernacular: 有幾分鐘,場面極度歡欣、感恩,同狂喜嘅景象。不過冇怨恨。事實上,奴隸對我哋以前嘅主人有同情。獲得解放嘅有色人種嘅狂喜只持續咗好短時間,因為我留意到,佢哋返到小屋時,感覺已經有變化。自由嘅巨大責任,要自己負責自己、要為自己同子女思考同計劃,似乎佔據咗佢哋。就好似突然將一個十歲或者十二歲嘅少年拋出世界自己謀生一樣。幾個鐘之內,盎格魯-撒克遜種族幾個世紀以來一直搏鬥嘅大問題,就拋畀呢啲人去解決。呢啲係家、生計、養育子女、教育、公民身份,以及建立同維持教會嘅問題。難怪幾個鐘之內,狂喜停止,一種深深嘅陰鬱感似乎瀰漫奴隸住處?對有些人嚟講,似乎自由一旦真正擁有,比佢哋預期嘅更嚴肅。有些奴隸七八十歲;最好嘅日子已經過去。佢哋冇力氣喺陌生地方、陌生人當中謀生,即使佢哋肯定去邊度搵新住處。對呢類人嚟講,問題似乎特別困難。此外,佢哋內心深處,對「老主人」同「老太太」,以及佢哋嘅子女,有一種奇怪而特殊嘅依戀,佢哋覺得難以想像斷絕。喺某些情況下,佢哋同佢哋度過近半個世紀,想到分離並唔輕鬆。逐漸,一個接一個,起初偷偷咁,年紀大嘅奴隸開始從奴隸住處游蕩返「大屋」,同佢哋以前嘅主人低聲討論將來。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有幾分鐘,場面極度歡欣、感恩,和狂喜的景象。不過沒怨恨。事實上,奴隸對我們以前的主人有同情。獲得解放的有色人種的狂喜只持續了很短時間,因為我留意到,他們回到小屋時,感覺已經有變化。自由的巨大責任,要自己負責自己、要為自己和子女思考和計劃,似乎佔據了他們。就像突然將一個十歲或十二歲的少年拋出世界自己謀生一樣。幾個小時之內,盎格魯-撒克遜種族幾個世紀以來一直搏鬥的大問題,就拋給這些人去解決。這些是家、生計、養育子女、教育、公民身分,以及建立和維持教會的問題。難怪幾個小時之內,狂喜停止,一種深深的陰鬱感似乎瀰漫奴隸住處?對有些人來說,似乎自由一旦真正擁有,比他們預期的更嚴肅。有些奴隸七八十歲;最好的日子已經過去。他們沒力氣在陌生地方、陌生人當中謀生,即使他們肯定去哪裡找新住處。對這類人來說,問題似乎特別困難。此外,他們內心深處,對「老主人」和「老太太」,以及他們的子女,有一種奇怪而特殊的依戀,他們覺得難以想像斷絕。在某些情況下,他們與他們度過近半個世紀,想到分離並不輕鬆。逐漸,一個接一個,起初偷偷地,年紀大的奴隸開始從奴隸住處遊蕩回「大屋」,與他們以前的主人低聲討論將來。

passages.original: After the coming of freedom there were two points upon which practically all the people on our place were agreed, and I found that this was generally true throughout the South: that they must change their names, and that they must leave the old plantation for at least a few days or weeks in order that they might really feel sure that they were free.
passages.vernacular: 自由到來之後,我哋種植園上幾乎所有人都同意兩點,而我發現呢點喺整個南方普遍如此:佢哋必須改名,同時必須離開舊種植園至少幾日或幾個星期,先可以真正覺得肯定自己係自由嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自由到來之後,我們種植園上幾乎所有人都同意兩點,而我發現這一點在整個南方普遍如此:他們必須改名,同時必須離開舊種植園至少幾天或幾個星期,才可以真正覺得肯定自己是自由的。

passages.original: In some way a feeling got among the coloured people that it was far from proper for them to bear the surname of their former owners, and a great many of them took other surnames. This was one of the first signs of freedom. When they were slaves, a coloured person was simply called “John” or “Susan.” There was seldom occasion for more than the use of the one name. If “John” or “Susan” belonged to a white man by the name of “Hatcher,” sometimes he was called “John Hatcher,” or as often “Hatcher’s John.” But there was a feeling that “John Hatcher” or “Hatcher’s John” was not the proper title by which to denote a freeman; and so in many cases “John Hatcher” was changed to “John S. Lincoln” or “John S. Sherman,” the initial “S” standing for no name, it being simply a part of what the coloured man proudly called his “entitles.”
passages.vernacular: 有色人種之間不知點解形成一種感覺,認為佢哋用前主人嘅姓氏係好不恰當,好多人就改用其他姓氏。呢個係自由嘅最早跡象之一。佢哋做奴隸時,有色人種只係被叫做「約翰」或者「蘇珊」。好少有場合需要用多過一個名。如果「約翰」或者「蘇珊」屬於一位姓「哈切爾」嘅白人,有時佢被叫做「約翰·哈切爾」,或者同樣常被叫做「哈切爾嘅約翰」。不過有種感覺,認為「約翰·哈切爾」或者「哈切爾嘅約翰」唔係稱呼自由人嘅適當稱號;所以好多情況下「約翰·哈切爾」改為「約翰·S·林肯」或者「約翰·S·謝爾曼」,首字母「S」唔代表任何名字,只係有色人種驕傲地稱為佢「頭銜」嘅一部分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有色人種之間不知怎的形成一種感覺,認為他們用前主人的姓氏是很不恰當,很多人就改用其他姓氏。這是自由的最早跡象之一。他們做奴隸時,有色人種只是被叫做「約翰」或「蘇珊」。很少有場合需要用多過一個名字。如果「約翰」或「蘇珊」屬於一位姓「哈切爾」的白人,有時他被叫做「約翰·哈切爾」,或同樣常被叫做「哈切爾的約翰」。不過有種感覺,認為「約翰·哈切爾」或「哈切爾的約翰」不是稱呼自由人的適當稱號;所以很多情況下「約翰·哈切爾」改為「約翰·S·林肯」或「約翰·S·謝爾曼」,首字母「S」不代表任何名字,只是有色人種驕傲地稱為他「頭銜」的一部分。

passages.original: As I have stated, most of the coloured people left the old plantation for a short while at least, so as to be sure, it seemed, that they could leave and try their freedom on to see how it felt. After they had remained away for a while, many of the older slaves, especially, returned to their old homes and made some kind of contract with their former owners by which they remained on the estate.
passages.vernacular: 正如我所講,大部分有色人種至少短時間離開舊種植園,似乎係為咗肯定佢哋可以離開、試試自由嘅滋味。離開一段時間之後,好多老年奴隸尤其返去佢哋舊家,同前主人訂立某種合約,留喺莊園。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 正如我所說,大部分有色人種至少短時間離開舊種植園,似乎是為了肯定他們可以離開、試試自由的滋味。離開一段時間之後,很多老年奴隸尤其回去他們舊家,與前主人訂立某種合約,留在莊園。

passages.original: My mother’s husband, who was the stepfather of my brother John and myself, did not belong to the same owners as did my mother. In fact, he seldom came to our plantation. I remember seeing him there perhaps once a year, that being about Christmas time. In some way, during the war, by running away and following the Federal soldiers, it seems, he found his way into the new state of West Virginia. As soon as freedom was declared, he sent for my mother to come to the Kanawha Valley, in West Virginia. At that time a journey from Virginia over the mountains to West Virginia was rather a tedious and in some cases a painful undertaking. What little clothing and few household goods we had were placed in a cart, but the children walked the greater portion of the distance, which was several hundred miles.
passages.vernacular: 我媽媽嘅丈夫,即係我哥哥約翰同我嘅繼父,同我媽媽唔屬於同一批主人。事實上,佢好少嚟我哋種植園。我記得見過佢喺嗰度,大概一年一次,大約聖誕節。戰爭期間,似乎佢逃走並跟隨聯邦士兵,不知點樣去咗新成立嘅西弗吉尼亞州。一宣布自由,佢就派人叫我媽媽去西弗吉尼亞嘅卡諾瓦山谷。當時由弗吉尼亞翻山去西弗吉尼亞係相當沉悶、有時痛苦嘅旅程。我哋有嘅少少衣服同幾件家什放喺一輛車上,不過孩子哋要步行大部分路程,幾百英里。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我母親的丈夫,即我哥哥約翰和我的繼父,與我母親不屬於同一批主人。事實上,他很少來我們種植園。我記得見過他在那裡,大概一年一次,大約聖誕節。戰爭期間,似乎他逃走並跟隨聯邦士兵,不知怎樣去了新成立的西弗吉尼亞州。一宣布自由,他就派人叫我母親去西弗吉尼亞的卡諾瓦山谷。當時由弗吉尼亞翻山去西弗吉尼亞是相當沉悶、有時痛苦的旅程。我們有的一點衣服和幾件家什放在一輛車上,不過孩子們要步行大部分路程,幾百英里。

passages.original: I do not think any of us ever had been very far from the plantation, and the taking of a long journey into another state was quite an event. The parting from our former owners and the members of our own race on the plantation was a serious occasion. From the time of our parting till their death we kept up a correspondence with the older members of the family, and in later years we have kept in touch with those who were the younger members. We were several weeks making the trip, and most of the time we slept in the open air and did our cooking over a log fire out-of-doors. One night I recall that we camped near an abandoned log cabin, and my mother decided to build a fire in that for cooking, and afterward to make a “pallet” on the floor for our sleeping. Just as the fire had gotten well started a large black snake fully a yard and a half long dropped down the chimney and ran out on the floor. Of course we at once abandoned that cabin. Finally we reached our destination—a little town called Malden, which is about five miles from Charleston, the present capital of the state.
passages.vernacular: 我諗我哋當中冇人去過離種植園好遠嘅地方,去另一個州長途旅行係相當大嘅事。同前主人同種植園上我哋種族嘅成員告別,係嚴肅嘅場合。從分別嗰時起直到佢哋去世,我哋同家庭嘅年長成員保持通信,後來幾年亦同年輕成員保持聯繫。我哋花咗幾個星期行程,大部分時間睡喺露天,用戶外嘅原木火煮食。我記得有一晚我哋喺一間廢棄木屋附近紮營,我媽媽決定喺度生火煮食,之後喺地上做個「草墊」睡覺。火剛好生起,一條至少一碼半長嘅大黑蛇從煙囪掉落,跑出地板。我哋當然立即放棄嗰間小屋。最後我哋到達目的地——一個叫馬爾登嘅小鎮,距離州現時首府查爾斯頓大約五英里。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我們當中沒有人去過離種植園很遠的地方,去另一個州長途旅行是相當大的事。與前主人和種植園上我們種族的成員告別,是嚴肅的場合。從分別那時起直到他們去世,我們與家庭的年長成員保持通信,後來幾年也與年輕成員保持聯繫。我們花了幾個星期行程,大部分時間睡在露天,用戶外的原木火煮食。我記得有一晚我們在一間廢棄木屋附近紮營,我母親決定在那裡生火煮食,之後在地上做個「草墊」睡覺。火剛好生起,一條至少一碼半長的大黑蛇從煙囪掉落,跑出地板。我們當然立即放棄那間小屋。最後我們到達目的地——一個叫馬爾登的小鎮,距離州現時首府查爾斯頓大約五英里。

passages.original: At that time salt-mining was the great industry in that part of West Virginia, and the little town of Malden was right in the midst of the salt-furnaces. My stepfather had already secured a job at a salt-furnace, and he had also secured a little cabin for us to live in. Our new house was no better than the one we had left on the old plantation in Virginia. In fact, in one respect it was worse. Notwithstanding the poor condition of our plantation cabin, we were at all times sure of pure air. Our new home was in the midst of a cluster of cabins crowded closely together, and as there were no sanitary regulations, the filth about the cabins was often intolerable. Some of our neighbours were coloured people, and some were the poorest and most ignorant and degraded white people. It was a motley mixture. Drinking, gambling, quarrels, fights, and shockingly immoral practices were frequent. All who lived in the little town were in one way or another connected with the salt business. Though I was a mere child, my stepfather put me and my brother at work in one of the furnaces. Often I began work as early as four o’clock in the morning.
passages.vernacular: 當時採鹽係西弗吉尼亞嗰個地區嘅主要行業,馬爾登小鎮就喺鹽爐中間。我繼父已經喺一個鹽爐搵到工作,亦搵到一間細小屋畀我哋住。我哋嘅新屋並唔比喺弗吉尼亞舊種植園離開嗰間好。事實上,有一方面更差。儘管種植園小屋狀況差,我哋始終確定有清新空氣。我哋新家喺一群擠得好密嘅小屋中間,因為冇衛生規定,小屋周圍嘅污穢經常難以忍受。我哋一些鄰居係有色人種,一些係最窮、最無知、最墮落嘅白人。係一個混雜嘅群體。飲酒、賭博、爭吵、打鬥同令人震驚嘅不道德行為好常見。住喺小鎮嘅所有人,都以某種方式同鹽業有關。雖然我只係個小孩,我繼父就叫我同我哥哥去其中一個鹽爐做工。我經常早喺凌晨四點就開工。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當時採鹽是西弗吉尼亞那個地區的主要行業,馬爾登小鎮就在鹽爐中間。我繼父已經在一個鹽爐找到工作,也找到一間小屋給我們住。我們的新屋並不比在弗吉尼亞舊種植園離開那間好。事實上,有一方面更差。儘管種植園小屋狀況差,我們始終確定有清新空氣。我們新家在一群擠得很密的小屋中間,因為沒有衛生規定,小屋周圍的污穢經常難以忍受。我們一些鄰居是有色人種,一些是最窮、最無知、最墮落的白人。是一個混雜的群體。飲酒、賭博、爭吵、打鬥和令人震驚的不道德行為很常見。住在小鎮的所有人,都以某種方式與鹽業有關。雖然我只是個小孩,我繼父就叫我和我哥哥去其中一個鹽爐做工。我經常早在凌晨四點就開工。

passages.original: The first thing I ever learned in the way of book knowledge was while working in this salt-furnace. Each salt-packer had his barrels marked with a certain number. The number allotted to my stepfather was “18.” At the close of the day’s work the boss of the packers would come around and put “18” on each of our barrels, and I soon learned to recognize that figure wherever I saw it, and after a while got to the point where I could make that figure, though I knew nothing about any other figures or letters.
passages.vernacular: 我學到嘅第一樣書本知識,係喺呢個鹽爐做工時。每位裝鹽工人嘅桶都標有某個號碼。分配畀我繼父嘅號碼係「18」。一日工作結束時,裝鹽工人嘅老闆會過嚟,喺我哋每個桶上寫上「18」,我好快學會認出呢個數字,喺邊度見到都認得,過咗一陣子甚至可以寫呢個數字,雖然我對其他數字或者字母一無所知。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我學到的第一樣書本知識,是在這個鹽爐做工時。每位裝鹽工人的桶都標有某個號碼。分配給我繼父的號碼是「18」。一天工作結束時,裝鹽工人的老闆會過來,在我們每個桶上寫上「18」,我很快學會認出這個數字,在哪裡看到都認得,過了一陣子甚至可以寫這個數字,雖然我對其他數字或字母一無所知。
