Mistakes I knew would be made, but these mistakes would teach us valuable lessons for the future.
passages.vernacular: 我又話畀懷疑呢個計劃智慧嘅人聽,我哋大部分學生貧窮咁嚟,來自南方棉花、糖同稻米種植園嘅小屋,雖然我知道即刻畀佢哋住精美建築會令學生好高興,不過我覺得教佢哋點樣興建自己嘅建築,會係遵循更自然嘅發展過程。我知道會犯錯,不過呢啲錯誤會教我哋寶貴嘅將來功課。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我又告訴懷疑這個計劃智慧的人,我們大部分學生貧窮地來,來自南方棉花、糖和稻米種植園的小屋,雖然我知道立刻給他們住精美建築會使學生很高興,不過我覺得教他們怎樣興建自己的建築,會是遵循更自然的發展過程。我知道會犯錯,不過這些錯誤會教我們寶貴的將來功課。

passages.original: During the now nineteen years’ existence of the Tuskegee school, the plan of having the buildings erected by student labour has been adhered to. In this time forty buildings, counting small and large, have been built, and all except four are almost wholly the product of student labour. As an additional result, hundreds of men are now scattered throughout the South who received their knowledge of mechanics while being taught how to erect these buildings. Skill and knowledge are now handed down from one set of students to another in this way, until at the present time a building of any description or size can be constructed wholly by our instructors and students, from the drawing of the plans to the putting in of the electric fixtures, without going off the grounds for a single workman.
passages.vernacular: 塔斯基吉學校而家存在咗十九年,用學生勞動興建建築嘅計劃一直堅持。呢段時間,四十座建築(連大細)已經興建,除咗四座之外,幾乎全部係學生勞動嘅成果。作為額外成果,幾百個男人而家散佈南方各地,佢哋喺學習點樣興建呢啲建築時得到機械知識。技能同知識而家咁從一批學生傳給另一批,以致而家任何類型同大小嘅建築,都可以完全由我哋嘅導師同學生興建,由畫圖則到安裝電器設備,唔使離開校園搵一個工人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 塔斯基吉學校現在存在了十九年,用學生勞動興建建築的計劃一直堅持。這段時間,四十座建築(連大小)已經興建,除了四座之外,幾乎全部是學生勞動的成果。作為額外成果,幾百個男人現在散佈南方各地,他們在學習怎樣興建這些建築時得到機械知識。技能和知識現在這樣從一批學生傳給另一批,以致現在任何類型和大小的建築,都可以完全由我們的導師和學生興建,由畫圖則到安裝電器設備,不用離開校園找一個工人。

passages.original: Not a few times, when a new student has been led into the temptation of marring the looks of some building by leadpencil marks or by the cuts of a jack-knife, I have heard an old student remind him: “Don’t do that. That is our building. I helped put it up.”
passages.vernacular: 不止幾次,當新學生被引誘用鉛筆或者小刀刻痕破壞某座建築嘅外觀,我聽到老學生提醒佢:「唔好咁做。呢個係我哋嘅建築。我幫手起嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不止幾次,當新學生被引誘用鉛筆或小刀刻痕破壞某座建築的外觀,我聽到老學生提醒他:「不要這樣做。這是我們的建築。我幫忙起的。」

passages.original: In the early days of the school I think my most trying experience was in the matter of brickmaking. As soon as we got the farm work reasonably well started, we directed our next efforts toward the industry of making bricks. We needed these for use in connection with the erection of our own buildings; but there was also another reason for establishing this industry. There was no brickyard in the town, and in addition to our own needs there was a demand for bricks in the general market.
passages.vernacular: 學校早期,我諗我最艱難嘅經歷係燒磚。農場工作一合理開始,我哋就將下一個努力轉向造磚行業。我哋需要磚來興建自己嘅建築;不過開辦呢個行業亦有另一個原因。鎮上冇磚場,除咗我哋自己嘅需要,一般市場亦有磚嘅需求。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 學校早期,我想我最艱難的經歷是燒磚。農場工作一合理開始,我們就將下一個努力轉向造磚行業。我們需要磚來興建自己的建築;不過開辦這個行業也有另一個原因。鎮上沒磚場,除了我們自己的需要,一般市場也有磚的需求。

passages.original: I had always sympathized with the “Children of Israel,” in their task of “making bricks without straw,” but ours was the task of making bricks with no money and no experience.
passages.vernacular: 我一直同情「以色列人」做「冇稻草造磚」嘅任務,不過我哋嘅任務係冇錢冇經驗造磚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一直同情「以色列人」做「沒稻草造磚」的任務,不過我們的任務是沒錢沒經驗造磚。

passages.original: In the first place, the work was hard and dirty, and it was difficult to get the students to help. When it came to brickmaking, their distaste for manual labour in connection with book education became especially manifest. It was not a pleasant task for one to stand in the mud-pit for hours, with the mud up to his knees. More than one man became disgusted and left the school.
passages.vernacular: 首先,工作辛苦污糟,難以令學生幫手。到造磚時,佢哋對書本教育之外嘅體力勞動嘅厭惡特別明顯。站喺泥坑幾個鐘,泥到膝蓋,並唔係愉快嘅任務。不止一個人感到厭惡而離開學校。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 首先,工作辛苦骯髒,難以使學生幫手。到造磚時,他們對書本教育之外的體力勞動的厭惡特別明顯。站在泥坑幾個小時,泥到膝蓋,並不是愉快的任務。不止一個人感到厭惡而離開學校。

passages.original: We tried several locations before we opened up a pit that furnished brick clay. I had always supposed that brickmaking was very simple, but I soon found out by bitter experience that it required special skill and knowledge, particularly in the burning of the bricks. After a good deal of effort we moulded about twenty-five thousand bricks, and put them into a kiln to be burned. This kiln turned out to be a failure, because it was not properly constructed or properly burned. We began at once, however, on a second kiln. This, for some reason, also proved a failure. The failure of this kiln made it still more difficult to get the students to take part in the work. Several of the teachers, however, who had been trained in the industries at Hampton, volunteered their services, and in some way we succeeded in getting a third kiln ready for burning. The burning of a kiln required about a week. Toward the latter part of the week, when it seemed as if we were going to have a good many thousand bricks in a few hours, in the middle of the night the kiln fell. For the third time we had failed.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘗試咗幾個地點,先開咗一個提供磚土嘅坑。我一直以為造磚好簡單,不過我好快從痛苦經驗發現,佢需要特別技能同知識,尤其係燒磚。經過好多努力,我哋造咗大約二萬五千塊磚,放入窯燒。呢個窯證明係失敗,因為建造得唔正確,燒得唔正確。不過我哋即刻開始第二個窯。呢個不知點解亦證明失敗。呢個窯嘅失敗,令更難令學生參與工作。不過,幾位喺漢普頓受過行業訓練嘅老師自願提供服務,我哋不知點樣成功準備好第三個窯燒。燒一個窯需要大約一個星期。星期後期,似乎我哋幾個鐘內會得到好幾千塊磚時,半夜窯塌咗。第三次我哋失敗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們嘗試了幾個地點,才開了一個提供磚土的坑。我一直以為造磚很簡單,不過我很快從痛苦經驗發現,它需要特別技能和知識,尤其是燒磚。經過很多努力,我們造了大約二萬五千塊磚,放入窯燒。這個窯證明是失敗,因為建造得不正確,燒得不正確。不過我們立刻開始第二個窯。這個不知為什麼也證明失敗。這個窯的失敗,使更難使學生參與工作。不過,幾位在漢普頓受過行業訓練的老師自願提供服務,我們不知怎樣成功準備好第三個窯燒。燒一個窯需要大約一個星期。星期後期,似乎我們幾個小時內會得到好幾千塊磚時,半夜窯塌了。第三次我們失敗。

passages.original: The failure of this last kiln left me without a single dollar with which to make another experiment. Most of the teachers advised the abandoning of the effort to make bricks. In the midst of my troubles I thought of a watch which had come into my possession years before. I took the watch to the city of Montgomery, which was not far distant, and placed it in a pawn-shop. I secured cash upon it to the amount of fifteen dollars, with which to renew the brickmaking experiment. I returned to Tuskegee, and, with the help of the fifteen dollars, rallied our rather demoralized and discouraged forces and began a fourth attempt to make bricks. This time, I am glad to say, we were successful. Before I got hold of any money, the time-limit on my watch had expired, and I have never seen it since; but I have never regretted the loss of it.
passages.vernacular: 最後呢個窯嘅失敗,令我連一美元都冇,用嚟做另一個實驗。大部分老師建議放棄造磚嘅努力。喺我嘅煩惱之中,我想起多年前落入我手嘅一隻錶。我拎錶去咗距離唔遠嘅蒙哥馬利市,放入當舖。我憑佢得到十五美元現金,用嚟重新做造磚實驗。我返到塔斯基吉,憑十五美元,召集我哋相當沮喪氣餒嘅力量,開始第四次造磚嘗試。今次,我好高興咁講,我哋成功。我未拎到任何錢之前,我隻錶嘅期限已過,我從此冇再見過;不過我從未後悔失去佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後這個窯的失敗,使我連一美元都沒有,用來做另一個實驗。大部分老師建議放棄造磚的努力。在我的煩惱之中,我想起多年前落入我手的一隻錶。我拿錶去了距離不遠的蒙哥馬利市,放入當舖。我憑它得到十五美元現金,用來重新做造磚實驗。我回到塔斯基吉,憑十五美元,召集我們相當沮喪氣餒的力量,開始第四次造磚嘗試。這次,我很高興地說,我們成功。我未拿到任何錢之前,我那隻錶的期限已過,我從此沒再見過;不過我從未後悔失去它。

passages.original: Brickmaking has now become such an important industry at the school that last season our students manufactured twelve hundred thousand of first-class bricks, of a quality suitable to be sold in any market. Aside from this, scores of young men have mastered the brickmaking trade—both the making of bricks by hand and by machinery—and are now engaged in this industry in many parts of the South.
passages.vernacular: 造磚而家成為學校一個咁重要嘅行業,上個季節我哋學生生產咗一百二十萬塊頭等磚,質量適合喺任何市場出售。除此之外,幾十個年輕男子已經掌握造磚手藝——手工造磚同機器造磚——而家喺南方好多地方從事呢個行業。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 造磚現在成為學校一個這麼重要的行業,上個季節我們學生生產了一百二十萬塊頭等磚,質量適合在任何市場出售。除此之外,幾十個年輕男子已經掌握造磚手藝——手工造磚和機器造磚——現在在南方很多地方從事這個行業。

passages.original: The making of these bricks taught me an important lesson in regard to the relations of the two races in the South. Many white people who had had no contact with the school, and perhaps no sympathy with it, came to us to buy bricks because they found out that ours were good bricks. They discovered that we were supplying a real want in the community. The making of these bricks caused many of the white residents of the neighbourhood to begin to feel that the education of the Negro was not making him worthless, but that in educating our students we were adding something to the wealth and comfort of the community. As the people of the neighbourhood came to us to buy bricks, we got acquainted with them; they traded with us and we with them. Our business interests became intermingled. We had something which they wanted; they had something which we wanted. This, in a large measure, helped to lay the foundation for the pleasant relations that have continued to exist between us and the white people in that section, and which now extend throughout the South.
passages.vernacular: 造呢啲磚教咗我一個關於南方兩個種族關係嘅重要功課。好多同學校冇接觸、也許冇同情嘅白人,來我哋度買磚,因為佢哋發現我哋嘅磚好。佢哋發現我哋正為社區提供真正需要。造呢啲磚令好多鄰近白人居民開始覺得,黑人教育並唔令佢變得冇用,而係我哋教育學生為社區嘅財富同舒適增添咗嘢。隨鄰近人民來我哋度買磚,我哋同佢哋熟識;佢哋同我哋交易,我哋同佢哋交易。我哋嘅商業利益交織起來。我哋有佢哋想要嘅嘢;佢哋有我哋想要嘅嘢。呢個好大程度上,幫助奠定咗我哋同嗰個地區白人之間愉快關係嘅基礎,呢種關係持續存在,而家延伸到整個南方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 造這些磚教了我一個關於南方兩個種族關係的重要功課。很多與學校沒接觸、也許沒同情的白人,來我們這裡買磚,因為他們發現我們的磚好。他們發現我們正為社區提供真正需要。造這些磚使很多鄰近白人居民開始覺得,黑人教育並不使他變得沒用,而是我們教育學生為社區的財富和舒適增添了東西。隨鄰近人民來我們這裡買磚,我們與他們熟識;他們與我們交易,我們與他們交易。我們的商業利益交織起來。我們有他們想要的東西;他們有我們想要的東西。這很大程度上,幫助奠定了我們與那個地區白人之間愉快關係的基礎,這種關係持續存在,現在延伸到整個南方。

passages.original: Wherever one of our brickmakers has gone in the South, we find that he has something to contribute to the well-being of the community into which he has gone; something that has made the community feel that, in a degree, it is indebted to him, and perhaps, to a certain extent, dependent upon him. In this way pleasant relations between the races have been stimulated.
passages.vernacular: 無論我哋其中一位磚匠去到南方邊度,我哋發現佢有些嘢可以貢獻畀佢去到嘅社區嘅福祉;令社區覺得某程度上欠佢,也許某種程度上倚靠佢。咁樣促進咗兩個種族之間嘅愉快關係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論我們其中一位磚匠去到南方哪裡,我們發現他有些東西可以貢獻給他去到的社區的福祉;使社區覺得某種程度上欠他,也許某種程度上倚靠他。這樣促進了兩個種族之間的愉快關係。

passages.original: My experience is that there is something in human nature which always makes an individual recognize and reward merit, no matter under what colour of skin merit is found. I have found, too, that it is the visible, the tangible, that goes a long ways in softening prejudices. The actual sight of a first-class house that a Negro has built is ten times more potent than pages of discussion about a house that he ought to build, or perhaps could build.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅經驗係,人性中有些嘢總係令個人認可同獎賞價值,無論價值係喺咩膚色下發現。我亦發現,可見嘅、有形嘅,對緩和偏見有好大幫助。親眼見到黑人建造嘅一流房屋,比關於佢應該或者可能建造嘅房屋嘅幾頁討論有力十倍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的經驗是,人性中有些東西總是使個人認可和獎賞價值,無論價值是在什麼膚色下發現。我也發現,可見的、有形的,對緩和偏見有很大幫助。親眼看到黑人建造的一流房屋,比關於他應該或可能建造的房屋的幾頁討論有力十倍。

passages.original: The same principle of industrial education has been carried out in the building of our own wagons, carts, and buggies, from the first. We now own and use on our farm and about the school dozens of these vehicles, and every one of them has been built by the hands of the students. Aside from this, we help supply the local market with these vehicles. The supplying of them to the people in the community has had the same effect as the supplying of bricks, and the man who learns at Tuskegee to build and repair wagons and carts is regarded as a benefactor by both races in the community where he goes. The people with whom he lives and works are going to think twice before they part with such a man.
passages.vernacular: 同樣嘅工業教育原則,從一開始就實行於我哋自己貨車、手推車同輕便馬車嘅建造。我哋而家擁有並喺農場同校園周圍使用幾十輛呢類車輛,每一輛都由學生雙手建造。除此之外,我哋幫助為當地市場供應呢啲車輛。向社區人民供應佢哋,同供應磚有同樣效果,喺塔斯基吉學會建造同修理貨車同手推車嘅人,被佢去到嘅社區兩個種族都視為恩人。同佢生活同工作嘅人,會三思先離開咁嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同樣的工業教育原則,從一開始就實行於我們自己貨車、手推車和輕便馬車的建造。我們現在擁有並在農場和校園周圍使用幾十輛這類車輛,每一輛都由學生雙手建造。除此之外,我們幫助為當地市場供應這些車輛。向社區人民供應它們,與供應磚有同樣效果,在塔斯基吉學會建造和修理貨車和手推車的人,被他去到的社區兩個種族都視為恩人。與他生活和工作的人,會三思才離開這樣的人。

passages.original: The individual who can do something that the world wants done will, in the end, make his way regardless of race. One man may go into a community prepared to supply the people there with an analysis of Greek sentences. The community may not at the time be prepared for, or feel the need of, Greek analysis, but it may feel its need of bricks and houses and wagons. If the man can supply the need for those, then, it will lead eventually to a demand for the first product, and with the demand will come the ability to appreciate it and to profit by it.
passages.vernacular: 可以做世界需要做嘅事嘅人,最終無論種族都會出人頭地。一個人可能去到一個社區,準備好為人民提供希臘文句子嘅分析。社區當時可能未準備好、或者感覺唔需要希臘文分析,不過可能感覺需要磚、房屋同貨車。如果佢可以提供呢啲需要,最終會帶來對第一種產品嘅需求,而隨需求,就會有欣賞同從中得益嘅能力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可以做世界需要做的事的人,最終無論種族都會出人頭地。一個人可能去到一個社區,準備好為人民提供希臘文句子的分析。社區當時可能未準備好、或感覺不需要希臘文分析,不過可能感覺需要磚、房屋和貨車。如果他可以提供這些需要,最終會帶來對第一種產品的需求,而隨需求,就會有欣賞和從中得益的能力。

passages.original: About the time that we succeeded in burning our first kiln of bricks we began facing in an emphasized form the objection of the students to being taught to work. By this time it had gotten to be pretty well advertised throughout the state that every student who came to Tuskegee, no matter what his financial ability might be, must learn some industry. Quite a number of letters came from parents protesting against their children engaging in labour while they were in the school. Other parents came to the school to protest in person. Most of the new students brought a written or a verbal request from their parents to the effect that they wanted their children taught nothing but books. The more books, the larger they were, and the longer the titles printed upon them, the better pleased the students and their parents seemed to be.
passages.vernacular: 大約我哋成功燒第一窯磚嘅時候,我哋開始以強調嘅形式面對學生對被教導工作嘅反對。到嗰時,全州相當廣泛咁宣傳,每個來塔斯基吉嘅學生,無論財力如何,都必須學一門行業。好多家長寫信來抗議佢哋嘅孩子在學校時從事勞動。其他家長親自來學校抗議。大部分新學生帶住家長嘅書面或口頭要求,話佢哋想子女只學書本。書越多、越大、印喺上面嘅標題越長,學生同家長似乎越滿意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大約我們成功燒第一窯磚的時候,我們開始以強調的形式面對學生對被教導工作的反對。到那時,全州相當廣泛地宣傳,每個來塔斯基吉的學生,無論財力如何,都必須學一門行業。很多家長寫信來抗議他們的孩子在學校時從事勞動。其他家長親自來學校抗議。大部分新學生帶著家長的書面或口頭要求,說他們想子女只學書本。書越多、越大、印在上面的標題越長,學生和家長似乎越滿意。

passages.original: I gave little heed to these protests, except that I lost no opportunity to go into as many parts of the state as I could, for the purpose of speaking to the parents, and showing them the value of industrial education. Besides, I talked to the students constantly on the subject. Notwithstanding the unpopularity of industrial work, the school continued to increase in numbers to such an extent that by the middle of the second year there was an attendance of about one hundred and fifty, representing almost all parts of the state of Alabama, and including a few from other states.
passages.vernacular: 我對呢啲抗議冇太理會,只係我不放過任何機會去全州盡可能多嘅地方,向家長演講,向佢哋展示工業教育嘅價值。此外,我不斷就此題目同學生傾偈。儘管工業工作不受歡迎,學校人數繼續增加,到第二年中間,出席人數約一百五十,代表阿拉巴馬州幾乎各地,並包括一些來自其他州嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我對這些抗議沒太理會,只是我不放過任何機會去全州盡可能多的地方,向家長演講,向他們展示工業教育的價值。此外,我不斷就此題目與學生交談。儘管工業工作不受歡迎,學校人數繼續增加,到第二年中間,出席人數約一百五十,代表阿拉巴馬州幾乎各地,並包括一些來自其他州的人。

passages.original: In the summer of 1882 Miss Davidson and I both went North and engaged in the work of raising funds for the completion of our new building. On my way North I stopped in New York to try to get a letter of recommendation from an officer of a missionary organization who had become somewhat acquainted with me a few years previous. This man not only refused to give me the letter, but advised me most earnestly to go back home at once, and not make any attempt to get money, for he was quite sure that I would never get more than enough to pay my travelling expenses. I thanked him for his advice, and proceeded on my journey.
passages.vernacular: 1882年夏天,戴維森小姐同我都去咗北方,從事為完成我哋新建築籌款嘅工作。我去北方途中喺紐約停低,嘗試從一位幾年前同我有些認識嘅傳教組織官員度得到推薦信。呢個人唔單止拒絕畀我信,還最認真咁勸我即刻返屋企,唔好嘗試籌錢,因為佢相當肯定我所得到嘅唔會超過支付旅費。我多謝佢嘅意見,繼續我嘅旅程。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 1882年夏天,戴維森小姐和我都去了北方,從事為完成我們新建築籌款的工作。我去北方途中在紐約停下,嘗試從一位幾年前與我有些認識的傳教組織官員那裡得到推薦信。這個人不僅拒絕給我信,還最認真地勸我立刻回家,不要嘗試籌錢,因為他相當肯定我所得到的不會超過支付旅費。我感謝他的意見,繼續我的旅程。

passages.original: The first place I went to in the North, was Northampton, Mass., where I spent nearly a half-day in looking for a coloured family with whom I could board, never dreaming that any hotel would admit me. I was greatly surprised when I found that I would have no trouble in being accommodated at a hotel.
passages.vernacular: 我喺北方第一個去嘅地方係麻薩諸塞州北安普頓,我喺嗰度花咗差唔多半日搵一個有色人種家庭寄宿,從未夢想有酒店會收我。我發現可以輕易喺酒店得到安排,令我好驚訝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在北方第一個去的地方是麻薩諸塞州北安普頓,我在那裡花了差不多半天找一個有色人種家庭寄宿,從未夢想有酒店會收我。我發現可以輕易在酒店得到安排,使我很驚訝。

passages.original: We were successful in getting money enough so that on Thanksgiving Day of that year we held our first service in the chapel of Porter Hall, although the building was not completed.
passages.vernacular: 我哋成功籌到足夠錢,令嗰年感恩節,我哋雖然建築未完成,喺波特樓禮拜堂舉行第一次禮拜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們成功籌到足夠錢,使那年感恩節,我們雖然建築未完成,在波特樓禮拜堂舉行第一次禮拜。

passages.original: In looking about for some one to preach the Thanksgiving sermon, I found one of the rarest men that it has ever been my privilege to know. This was the Rev. Robert C. Bedford, a white man from Wisconsin, who was then pastor of a little coloured Congregational church in Montgomery, Ala. Before going to Montgomery to look for some one to preach this sermon I had never heard of Mr. Bedford. He had never heard of me. He gladly consented to come to Tuskegee and hold the Thanksgiving service. It was the first service of the kind that the coloured people there had ever observed, and what a deep interest they manifested in it! The sight of the new building made it a day of Thanksgiving for them never to be forgotten.
passages.vernacular: 喺搵人講感恩節講道時,我搵到我有幸認識過最罕見嘅人之一。佢係羅伯特·C·貝德福德牧師,來自威斯康星嘅白人,當時係阿拉巴馬蒙哥馬利一間細有色人種公理會教堂嘅牧師。我去蒙哥馬利搵人講道之前,我從未聽過貝德福德先生。佢從未聽過我。佢欣然同意來塔斯基吉舉行感恩節禮拜。呢個係嗰度有色人種舉行過嘅第一次同類禮拜,佢哋表現咗幾深嘅興趣!見到新建築,令佢哋嗰日成為難忘嘅感恩節。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在找人講感恩節講道時,我找到我有幸認識過最罕見的人之一。他是羅伯特·C·貝德福德牧師,來自威斯康星的白人,當時是阿拉巴馬蒙哥馬利一間小有色人種公理會教堂的牧師。我去蒙哥馬利找人講道之前,我從未聽過貝德福德先生。他從未聽過我。他欣然同意來塔斯基吉舉行感恩節禮拜。這是那裡有色人種舉行過的第一次同類禮拜,他們表現了多深的興趣!看到新建築,使他們那天成為難忘的感恩節。

passages.original: Mr. Bedford consented to become one of the trustees of the school, and in that capacity, and as a worker for it, he has been connected with it for eighteen years. During this time he has borne the school upon his heart night and day, and is never so happy as when he is performing some service, no matter how humble, for it. He completely obliterates himself in everything, and looks only for permission to serve where service is most disagreeable, and where others would not be attracted. In all my relations with him he has seemed to me to approach as nearly to the spirit of the Master as almost any man I ever met.
passages.vernacular: 貝德福德先生同意成為學校嘅受託人之一,以呢個身份,同作為為學校工作嘅人,佢已經同學校聯繫十八年。呢段時間,佢日夜將學校放喺心上,從來冇咁快樂,除非為佢做某種服務,無論幾卑微。佢喺一切事上完全忘我,只尋求准許喺最不愉快、其他人唔會被吸引嘅地方服務。我同佢所有關係中,佢對我嚟講似乎幾乎最接近主嘅精神,同我遇過嘅幾乎任何人一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝德福德先生同意成為學校的受託人之一,以這個身分,和作為為學校工作的人,他已經與學校聯繫十八年。這段時間,他日夜將學校放在心上,從來沒那麼快樂,除非為它做某種服務,無論多卑微。他在一切事上完全忘我,只尋求准許在最不愉快、其他人不會被吸引的地方服務。我與他所有關係中,他對我來說似乎幾乎最接近主的精神,和我遇過的幾乎任何人一樣。

passages.original: A little later there came into the service of the school another man, quite young at the time, and fresh from Hampton, without whose service the school never could have become what it is. This was Mr. Warren Logan, who now for seventeen years has been the treasurer of the Institute, and the acting principal during my absence. He has always shown a degree of unselfishness and an amount of business tact, coupled with a clear judgment, that has kept the school in good condition no matter how long I have been absent from it. During all the financial stress through which the school has passed, his patience and faith in our ultimate success have not left him.
passages.vernacular: 不久之後,另一個人加入學校服務,當時好年輕,剛從漢普頓出來,冇佢嘅服務,學校永遠唔可能成為而家嘅樣子。係沃倫·洛根先生,佢而家十七年來一直係學院嘅財務主管,同我不在期間嘅署理校長。佢一直表現出一種無私程度,同一定程度嘅商業機智,加上清晰判斷,令學校無論我離開幾耐都保持良好狀況。學校經歷嘅所有財政壓力期間,佢嘅耐性同對我哋最終成功嘅信心從未離開佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久之後,另一個人加入學校服務,當時很年輕,剛從漢普頓出來,沒他的服務,學校永遠不可能成為現在的樣子。是沃倫·洛根先生,他現在十七年來一直是學院的財務主管,和我不在期間的署理校長。他一直表現出一種無私程度,和一定程度的商業機智,加上清晰判斷,使學校無論我離開多久都保持良好狀況。學校經歷的所有財政壓力期間,他的耐性和對我們最終成功的信心從未離開他。

passages.original: As soon as our first building was near enough to completion so that we could occupy a portion of it—which was near the middle of the second year of the school—we opened a boarding department. Students had begun coming from quite a distance, and in such increasing numbers that we felt more and more that we were merely skimming over the surface, in that we were not getting hold of the students in their home life.
passages.vernacular: 我哋第一座建築一接近完成,足以令我哋佔用其中一部分——大約係學校第二年中間——我哋開設咗寄宿部門。學生開始從相當遠嘅地方來,而且人數不斷增加,令我哋越來越覺得我哋只係掠過表面,因為我哋冇接觸到學生嘅家庭生活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們第一座建築一接近完成,足以使我們佔用其中一部分——大約是學校第二年中間——我們開設了寄宿部門。學生開始從相當遠的地方來,而且人數不斷增加,使我們越來越覺得我們只是掠過表面,因為我們沒接觸到學生的家庭生活。

passages.original: We had nothing but the students and their appetites with which to begin a boarding department. No provision had been made in the new building for a kitchen and dining room; but we discovered that by digging out a large amount of earth from under the building we could make a partially lighted basement room that could be used for a kitchen and dining room. Again I called on the students to volunteer for work, this time to assist in digging out the basement. This they did, and in a few weeks we had a place to cook and eat in, although it was very rough and uncomfortable. Any one seeing the place now would never believe that it was once used for a dining room.
passages.vernacular: 我哋開始寄宿部門時,除咗學生同佢哋嘅胃口,咩都冇。新建築冇為廚房同飯廳作準備;不過我哋發現,從建築下面挖出大量泥土,可以做一個部分有光嘅地庫房間,用作廚房同飯廳。我再次叫學生自願工作,今次協助挖地庫。佢哋做咗,幾個星期內我哋有咗煮食同食飯嘅地方,雖然好粗糙不舒服。任何人而家見到嗰個地方,都唔會相信佢曾經用作飯廳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們開始寄宿部門時,除了學生和他們的胃口,什麼都沒有。新建築沒為廚房和飯廳作準備;不過我們發現,從建築下面挖出大量泥土,可以做一個部分有光的地庫房間,用作廚房和飯廳。我再次叫學生自願工作,這次協助挖地庫。他們做了,幾個星期內我們有了煮食和吃飯的地方,雖然很粗糙不舒服。任何人現在看到那個地方,都不會相信它曾經用作飯廳。

passages.original: The most serious problem, though, was to get the boarding department started off in running order, with nothing to do with in the way of furniture, and with no money with which to buy anything. The merchants in the town would let us have what food we wanted on credit. In fact, in those earlier years I was constantly embarrassed because people seemed to have more faith in me than I had in myself. It was pretty hard to cook, however, without stoves, and awkward to eat without dishes. At first the cooking was done out-of-doors, in the old-fashioned, primitive style, in pots and skillets placed over a fire. Some of the carpenters’ benches that had been used in the construction of the building were utilized for tables. As for dishes, there were too few to make it worth while to spend time in describing them.
passages.vernacular: 不過最嚴重嘅問題,係令寄宿部門以運作秩序開始,冇傢俬可用,亦冇錢買任何嘢。鎮上商人容許我哋賒賬買想要嘅食物。事實上,早期那幾年,我不斷感到尷尬,因為人們似乎對我嘅信心比我對自己嘅更多。不過,冇爐煮食好難,冇碟食飯好尷尬。起初煮食係喺戶外,以舊式原始方法,用鍋同長柄煎鍋放喺火上。一些建築時用過嘅木匠工作台被用作枱。至於碟,太少,唔值得花時間描述。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過最嚴重的問題,是使寄宿部門以運作秩序開始,沒傢俱可用,也沒錢買任何東西。鎮上商人容許我們賒賬買想要的食物。事實上,早期那幾年,我不斷感到尷尬,因為人們似乎對我的信心比我對自己的更多。不過,沒爐煮食很難,沒碟吃飯很尷尬。起初煮食是在戶外,以舊式原始方法,用鍋和長柄煎鍋放在火上。一些建築時用過的木匠工作台被用作桌子。至於碟子,太少,不值得花時間描述。

passages.original: No one connected with the boarding department seemed to have any idea that meals must be served at certain fixed and regular hours, and this was a source of great worry. Everything was so out of joint and so inconvenient that I feel safe in saying that for the first two weeks something was wrong at every meal. Either the meat was not done or had been burnt, or the salt had been left out of the bread, or the tea had been forgotten.
passages.vernacular: 寄宿部門嘅人似乎冇人有任何想法,餐點必須喺固定、定時嘅時間供應,呢點係好大憂慮嘅來源。一切都咁亂同不便,我可以穩妥咁講,頭兩個星期每餐都出問題。要麼肉冇煮熟或者燒焦,要麼麵包冇放鹽,要麼忘記咗茶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 寄宿部門的人似乎沒人有任何想法,餐點必須在固定、定時的時間供應,這點是很大憂慮的來源。一切都那麼亂和不便,我可以穩妥地說,頭兩個星期每餐都出問題。要麼肉沒煮熟或燒焦,要麼麵包沒放鹽,要麼忘記了茶。

passages.original: Early one morning I was standing near the dining-room door listening to the complaints of the students. The complaints that morning were especially emphatic and numerous, because the whole breakfast had been a failure. One of the girls who had failed to get any breakfast came out and went to the well to draw some water to drink and take the place of the breakfast which she had not been able to get. When she reached the well, she found that the rope was broken and that she could get no water. She turned from the well and said, in the most discouraged tone, not knowing that I was where I could hear her, “We can’t even get water to drink at this school.” I think no one remark ever came so near discouraging me as that one.
passages.vernacular: 有一朝早,我企喺飯廳門附近,聽學生嘅投訴。嗰朝嘅投訴特別強烈同多,因為整個早餐都失敗。其中一個冇食到早餐嘅女孩出嚟,去井邊打水飲,代替佢冇得到嘅早餐。佢去到井邊,發現繩斷咗,打唔到水。佢轉身離開口井,以最氣餒嘅語氣講,唔知我喺聽得到嘅地方:「我哋喺呢間學校連水都飲唔到。」我諗冇一句說話比嗰句更接近令我氣餒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天早上,我站在飯廳門附近,聽學生的投訴。那天早上的投訴特別強烈和多,因為整個早餐都失敗。其中一個沒吃到早餐的女孩出來,去井邊打水喝,代替她沒得到的早餐。她到了井邊,發現繩子斷了,打不到水。她轉身離開那口井,以最氣餒的語氣說,不知我在聽得到的地方:「我們在這間學校連水都喝不到。」我想沒有一句話比那句更接近使我氣餒。

passages.original: At another time, when Mr. Bedford—whom I have already spoken of as one of our trustees, and a devoted friend of the institution—was visiting the school, he was given a bedroom immediately over the dining room. Early in the morning he was awakened by a rather animated discussion between two boys in the dining room below. The discussion was over the question as to whose turn it was to use the coffee-cup that morning. One boy won the case by proving that for three mornings he had not had an opportunity to use the cup at all.
passages.vernacular: 另一次,貝德福德先生(我提過係我哋受託人之一、同學院嘅忠實朋友)探訪學校時,佢被安排住喺飯廳正上面嘅臥室。朝早,佢被下面飯廳兩個男孩相當熱烈嘅討論吵醒。討論嘅係嗰朝輪到邊個用咖啡杯。其中一個男孩證明佢三個早上都完全冇機會用杯而贏咗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 另一次,貝德福德先生(我提過是我們受託人之一、和學院的忠實朋友)探訪學校時,他被安排住在飯廳正上面的臥室。早上,他被下面飯廳兩個男孩相當熱烈的討論吵醒。討論的是那天早上輪到誰用咖啡杯。其中一個男孩證明他三個早上都完全沒機會用杯而贏了。

passages.original: But gradually, with patience and hard work, we brought order out of chaos, just as will be true of any problem if we stick to it with patience and wisdom and earnest effort.
passages.vernacular: 不過逐漸,憑耐性同努力,我哋將混亂變成秩序,就好似任何問題,只要我哋以耐性、智慧同認真努力堅持,都會如此。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過逐漸,憑耐性和努力,我們將混亂變成秩序,就像任何問題,只要我們以耐性、智慧和認真努力堅持,都會如此。

passages.original: As I look back now over that part of our struggle, I am glad to see that we had it. I am glad that we endured all those discomforts and inconveniences. I am glad that our students had to dig out the place for their kitchen and dining room. I am glad that our first boarding-place was in the dismal, ill-lighted, and damp basement. Had we started in a fine, attractive, convenient room, I fear we would have “lost our heads” and become “stuck up.” It means a great deal, I think, to start off on a foundation which one has made for one’s self.
passages.vernacular: 我而家回顧我哋奮鬥嘅呢個部分,好高興我哋有過。我好高興我哋忍受過所有呢啲不適同不便。我好高興我哋嘅學生要自己為佢哋嘅廚房同飯廳挖地方。我好高興我哋第一個寄宿地方係喺陰沉、光線差、潮濕嘅地庫。如果我哋喺一間精美、吸引、方便嘅房間開始,我恐怕我哋會「失去理智」而變得「自大」。我諗,從一個自己建立嘅基礎開始,有好大意義。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在回顧我們奮鬥的這個部分,很高興我們有過。我很高興我們忍受過所有這些不適和不便。我很高興我們的學生要自己為他們的廚房和飯廳挖地方。我很高興我們第一個寄宿地方是在陰沉、光線差、潮濕的地庫。如果我們在一間精美、吸引、方便的房間開始,我恐怕我們會「失去理智」而變得「自大」。我想,從一個自己建立的基礎開始,有很大意義。

passages.original: When our old students return to Tuskegee now, as they often do, and go into our large, beautiful, well-ventilated, and well-lighted dining room, and see tempting, well-cooked food—largely grown by the students themselves—and see tables, neat tablecloths and napkins, and vases of flowers upon the tables, and hear singing birds, and note that each meal is served exactly upon the minute, with no disorder, and with almost no complaint coming from the hundreds that now fill our dining room, they, too, often say to me that they are glad that we started as we did, and built ourselves up year by year, by a slow and natural process of growth.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅老學生而家經常返塔斯基吉,入我哋嘅大、漂亮、通風、光猛嘅飯廳,見到誘人煮得好嘅食物——大部分由學生自己種——見到枱、整潔嘅枱布同餐巾、枱上嘅花瓶,聽到雀鳥唱歌,留意到每餐準時供應,冇混亂,而家填滿我哋飯廳嘅幾百人幾乎冇投訴,佢哋亦經常話畀我知,佢哋好高興我哋咁開始,一年一年透過緩慢自然嘅成長過程建立自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的老學生現在經常回塔斯基吉,進我們的大、漂亮、通風、光線充足的飯廳,看到誘人煮得好的食物——大部分由學生自己種——看到桌子、整潔的桌布和餐巾、桌上的花瓶,聽到雀鳥唱歌,留意到每餐準時供應,沒混亂,現在填滿我們飯廳的幾百人幾乎沒投訴,他們也經常告訴我,他們很高興我們這樣開始,一年一年透過緩慢自然的成長過程建立自己。

chapters.title: Making Their Beds Before They Could Lie On Them 先造床才能躺下

passages.original: A little later in the history of the school we had a visit from General J.F.B. Marshall, the Treasurer of the Hampton Institute, who had had faith enough to lend us the first two hundred and fifty dollars with which to make a payment down on the farm. He remained with us a week, and made a careful inspection of everything. He seemed well pleased with our progress, and wrote back interesting and encouraging reports to Hampton. A little later Miss Mary F. Mackie, the teacher who had given me the “sweeping” examination when I entered Hampton, came to see us, and still later General Armstrong himself came.
passages.vernacular: 學校歷史稍後,漢普頓學院出納員J·F·B·馬歇爾將軍來探訪我哋,佢曾經有足夠信心借畀我哋第一筆二百五十美元,用嚟支付農場首期。佢同我哋住咗一個星期,仔細檢查一切。佢似乎對我哋嘅進步好滿意,寫咗有趣而鼓勵嘅報告返漢普頓。稍後,我入漢普頓時畀我「掃地」考試嘅老師瑪麗·F·麥基小姐來探我哋,再之後阿姆斯特朗將軍自己亦嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 學校歷史稍後,漢普頓學院出納員J·F·B·馬歇爾將軍來探訪我們,他曾經有足夠信心借給我們第一筆二百五十美元,用來支付農場首期。他和我們住了一個星期,仔細檢查一切。他似乎對我們的進步很滿意,寫了有趣而鼓勵的報告回漢普頓。稍後,我進漢普頓時給我「掃地」考試的老師瑪麗·F·麥基小姐來探我們,再之後阿姆斯特朗將軍自己也來。

passages.original: At the time of the visits of these Hampton friends the number of teachers at Tuskegee had increased considerably, and the most of the new teachers were graduates of the Hampton Institute. We gave our Hampton friends, especially General Armstrong, a cordial welcome. They were all surprised and pleased at the rapid progress that the school had made within so short a time. The coloured people from miles around came to the school to get a look at General Armstrong, about whom they had heard so much. The General was not only welcomed by the members of my own race, but by the Southern white people as well.
passages.vernacular: 漢普頓朋友探訪時,塔斯基吉嘅老師人數已經大大增加,大部分新老師係漢普頓學院嘅畢業生。我哋熱情歡迎漢普頓朋友,尤其係阿姆斯特朗將軍。佢哋全部都對學校喺咁短時間內取得嘅快速進步感到驚訝同高興。方圓幾英里嘅有色人種來學校睇阿姆斯特朗將軍,佢哋聽過好多關於佢嘅事。將軍唔單止受到我種族成員歡迎,南方白人亦歡迎佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 漢普頓朋友探訪時,塔斯基吉的老師人數已經大大增加,大部分新老師是漢普頓學院的畢業生。我們熱情歡迎漢普頓朋友,尤其是阿姆斯特朗將軍。他們全部都對學校在這麼短時間內取得的快速進步感到驚訝和高興。方圓幾英里的有色人種來學校看阿姆斯特朗將軍,他們聽過很多關於他的事。將軍不僅受到我種族成員歡迎,南方白人也歡迎他。

passages.original: This first visit which General Armstrong made to Tuskegee gave me an opportunity to get an insight into his character such as I had not before had. I refer to his interest in the Southern white people. Before this I had had the thought that General Armstrong, having fought the Southern white man, rather cherished a feeling of bitterness toward the white South, and was interested in helping only the coloured man there. But this visit convinced me that I did not know the greatness and the generosity of the man. I soon learned, by his visits to the Southern white people, and from his conversations with them, that he was as anxious about the prosperity and the happiness of the white race as the black. He cherished no bitterness against the South, and was happy when an opportunity offered for manifesting his sympathy. In all my acquaintance with General Armstrong I never heard him speak, in public or in private, a single bitter word against the white man in the South. From his example in this respect I learned the lesson that great men cultivate love, and that only little men cherish a spirit of hatred. I learned that assistance given to the weak makes the one who gives it strong; and that oppression of the unfortunate makes one weak.
passages.vernacular: 阿姆斯特朗將軍呢次第一次探訪塔斯基吉,畀我機會了解佢品格嘅一面,係我之前未有嘅。我係指佢對南方白人嘅關心。喺此之前,我一直覺得阿姆斯特朗將軍曾同南方白人作戰,似乎對白人南方抱持怨恨,只有興趣幫助嗰度嘅有色人種。不過呢次探訪令我相信,我唔知道呢個人嘅偉大同慷慨。我好快從佢探訪南方白人同同佢哋傾偈中了解到,佢同樣關心白人種族嘅繁榮同快樂,同關心黑人一樣。佢對南方冇半點怨恨,有機會表達同情時好高興。我認識阿姆斯特朗將軍期間,我從未聽過佢喺公開或私下講任何一句對南方白人嘅怨言。從佢呢方面嘅榜樣,我學到功課:偉人培養愛,只有小人懷抱仇恨精神。我學到,對弱者提供援助令提供者變得強大;而壓迫不幸者令人變得軟弱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 阿姆斯特朗將軍這次第一次探訪塔斯基吉,給我機會了解他品格的一面,是我之前未有的。我是指他對南方白人的關心。在此之前,我一直覺得阿姆斯特朗將軍曾與南方白人作戰,似乎對白人南方抱持怨恨,只有興趣幫助那裡的有色人種。不過這次探訪使我相信,我不知道這個人的偉大和慷慨。我很快從他探訪南方白人和與他們交談中了解到,他同樣關心白人種族的繁榮和快樂,和關心黑人一樣。他對南方沒半點怨恨,有機會表達同情時很高興。我認識阿姆斯特朗將軍期間,我從未聽過他在公開或私下說任何一句對南方白人的怨言。從他這方面的榜樣,我學到功課:偉人培養愛,只有小人懷抱仇恨精神。我學到,對弱者提供援助使提供者變得強大;而壓迫不幸者使人變得軟弱。

passages.original: It is now long ago that I learned this lesson from General Armstrong, and resolved that I would permit no man, no matter what his colour might be, to narrow and degrade my soul by making me hate him. With God’s help, I believe that I have completely rid myself of any ill feeling toward the Southern white man for any wrong that he may have inflicted upon my race. I am made to feel just as happy now when I am rendering service to Southern white men as when the service is rendered to a member of my own race. I pity from the bottom of my heart any individual who is so unfortunate as to get into the habit of holding race prejudice.
passages.vernacular: 我從阿姆斯特朗將軍度學到呢個功課已經好耐,並決心我唔畀任何人,無論佢膚色如何,令我憎恨佢而令我嘅靈魂變窄、變墮落。憑上帝嘅幫助,我相信我已經完全擺脫對南方白人嘅任何惡感,不論佢可能對我種族造成嘅任何錯。我而家為南方白人提供服務時,同為我自己種族成員提供服務時一樣快樂。我由衷同情任何不幸養成種族偏見習慣嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從阿姆斯特朗將軍那裡學到這個功課已經很久,並決心我不讓任何人,無論他膚色如何,使我憎恨他而使我的靈魂變窄、變墮落。憑上帝的幫助,我相信我已經完全擺脫對南方白人的任何惡感,不論他可能對我種族造成的任何錯。我現在為南方白人提供服務時,與為我自己種族成員提供服務時一樣快樂。我由衷同情任何不幸養成種族偏見習慣的人。

passages.original: The more I consider the subject, the more strongly I am convinced that the most harmful effect of the practice to which the people in certain sections of the South have felt themselves compelled to resort, in order to get rid of the force of the Negroes’ ballot, is not wholly in the wrong done to the Negro, but in the permanent injury to the morals of the white man. The wrong to the Negro is temporary, but to the morals of the white man the injury is permanent. I have noted time and time again that when an individual perjures himself in order to break the force of the black man’s ballot, he soon learns to practise dishonesty in other relations of life, not only where the Negro is concerned, but equally so where a white man is concerned. The white man who begins by cheating a Negro usually ends by cheating a white man. The white man who begins to break the law by lynching a Negro soon yields to the temptation to lynch a white man. All this, it seems to me, makes it important that the whole Nation lend a hand in trying to lift the burden of ignorance from the South.
passages.vernacular: 我越考慮呢個題目,就越堅信,南方某些地區人民覺得被迫採用嘅、用嚟擺脫黑人選票力量嘅做法,最有害嘅效果,並唔完全係對黑人嘅錯,而係對白人道德嘅永久損害。對黑人嘅錯係暫時嘅,不過對白人道德嘅損害係永久嘅。我一次又一次留意到,當一個人作偽證以破壞黑人選票嘅力量,佢好快學會喺生活其他關係中實行不誠實,不單涉及黑人,涉及白人時亦同樣。由欺騙黑人開始嘅白人,通常以欺騙白人結束。由私刑殺害黑人而開始違法嘅白人,好快屈服於私刑殺害白人嘅誘惑。所有呢啲,依我睇,令全國伸出援手,嘗試消除南方嘅無知負擔,變得重要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我越考慮這個題目,就越堅信,南方某些地區人民覺得被迫採用的、用來擺脫黑人選票力量的做法,最有害的效果,並不完全是對黑人的錯,而是對白人道德的永久損害。對黑人的錯是暫時的,不過對白人道德的損害是永久的。我一次又一次留意到,當一個人作偽證以破壞黑人選票的力量,他很快學會在生活其他關係中實行不誠實,不僅涉及黑人,涉及白人時也同樣。由欺騙黑人開始的白人,通常以欺騙白人結束。由私刑殺害黑人而開始違法的白人,很快屈服於私刑殺害白人的誘惑。所有這些,依我看,使全國伸出援手,嘗試消除南方的無知負擔,變得重要。

passages.original: Another thing that is becoming more apparent each year in the development of education in the South is the influence of General Armstrong’s idea of education; and this not upon the blacks alone, but upon the whites also. At the present time there is almost no Southern state that is not putting forth efforts in the direction of securing industrial education for its white boys and girls, and in most cases it is easy to trace the history of these efforts back to General Armstrong.
passages.vernacular: 南方教育發展中另一件每年越來越明顯嘅事,係阿姆斯特朗將軍教育理念嘅影響;而且唔單止對黑人,對白人亦然。而家南方幾乎冇一個州唔在努力為其白人男女孩子爭取工業教育,大部分情況下好容易追溯呢啲努力嘅歷史到阿姆斯特朗將軍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南方教育發展中另一件每年越來越明顯的事,是阿姆斯特朗將軍教育理念的影響;而且不僅對黑人,對白人也然。現在南方幾乎沒一個州不在努力為其白人男女孩子爭取工業教育,大部分情況下很容易追溯這些努力的歷史到阿姆斯特朗將軍。

passages.original: Soon after the opening of our humble boarding department students began coming to us in still larger numbers. For weeks we not only had to contend with the difficulty of providing board, with no money, but also with that of providing sleeping accommodations. For this purpose we rented a number of cabins near the school. These cabins were in a dilapidated condition, and during the winter months the students who occupied them necessarily suffered from the cold. We charge the students eight dollars a month—all they were able to pay—for their board. This included, besides board, room, fuel, and washing. We also gave the students credit on their board bills for all the work which they did for the school which was of any value to the institution. The cost of tuition, which was fifty dollars a year for each student, we had to secure then, as now, wherever we could.
passages.vernacular: 我哋簡陋嘅寄宿部門開設後不久,學生開始以更大數量來到。好幾個星期,我哋唔單止要同冇錢提供膳食嘅困難搏鬥,仲要同提供睡眠地方嘅困難搏鬥。為此我哋租咗學校附近好幾間小屋。呢啲小屋破舊,冬天佔用佢哋嘅學生必然受凍。我哋向學生收每月八美元——佢哋所能支付嘅全部——作為膳食費。除咗膳食,仲包括房間、燃料同洗衣。我哋亦按學生為學校做嘅對學院有價值嘅所有工作,記入佢哋膳食賬單。學費係每個學生每年五十美元,當時同現在一樣,我哋要喺任何可以搵到嘅地方籌集。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們簡陋的寄宿部門開設後不久,學生開始以更大數量來到。好幾個星期,我們不僅要與沒錢提供膳食的困難搏鬥,還要與提供睡眠地方的困難搏鬥。為此我們租了學校附近好幾間小屋。這些小屋破舊,冬天佔用它們的學生必然受凍。我們向學生收每月八美元——他們所能支付的全部——作為膳食費。除了膳食,還包括房間、燃料和洗衣。我們也按學生為學校做的對學院有價值的所有工作,記入他們膳食賬單。學費是每個學生每年五十美元,當時和現在一樣,我們要在任何可以找到的地方籌集。

passages.original: This small charge in cash gave us no capital with which to start a boarding department. The weather during the second winter of our work was very cold. We were not able to provide enough bed-clothes to keep the students warm. In fact, for some time we were not able to provide, except in a few cases, bedsteads and mattresses of any kind. During the coldest nights I was so troubled about the discomfort of the students that I could not sleep myself. I recall that on several occasions I went in the middle of the night to the shanties occupied by the young men, for the purpose of confronting them. Often I found some of them sitting huddled around a fire, with the one blanket which we had been able to provide wrapped around them, trying in this way to keep warm. During the whole night some of them did not attempt to lie down. One morning, when the night previous had been unusually cold, I asked those of the students in the chapel who thought that they had been frostbitten during the night to raise their hands. Three hands went up. Notwithstanding these experiences, there was almost no complaining on the part of the students. They knew that we were doing the best that we could for them. They were happy in the privilege of being permitted to enjoy any kind of opportunity that would enable them to improve their condition. They were constantly asking what they might do to lighten the burdens of the teachers.
passages.vernacular: 呢筆少少現金收費畀唔到我哋資本開始寄宿部門。我哋工作第二個冬天天氣好冷。我哋無法提供足夠被褥令學生保暖。事實上,有一段時間,除少數情況,我哋無法提供任何床架同褥。最冷嘅夜晚,我為學生嘅不適擔心到自己都瞓唔著。我記得有幾次我半夜去年輕男子住嘅棚屋,去面對佢哋。我經常發現佢哋有些人縮成一團圍住火坐,裹住我哋能夠提供嘅一張毯,以此保暖。整晚佢哋有些人冇嘗試躺低。有一朝早,前一晚特別冷,我問禮拜堂裡面覺得自己前一晚凍傷咗嘅學生舉手。三隻手舉起。儘管有呢啲經歷,學生幾乎冇抱怨。佢哋知道我哋正盡力為佢哋做。佢哋為能夠享受任何可以令佢哋改善處境嘅機會而快樂。佢哋不斷問可以做咩減輕老師負擔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這筆小小現金收費給不到我們資本開始寄宿部門。我們工作第二個冬天天氣很冷。我們無法提供足夠被褥使學生保暖。事實上,有一段時間,除少數情況,我們無法提供任何床架和褥子。最冷的夜晚,我為學生的不適擔心到自己都睡不著。我記得有幾次我半夜去年輕男子住的棚屋,去面對他們。我經常發現他們有些人縮成一團圍著火坐,裹著我們能夠提供的一張毯子,以此保暖。整晚他們有些人沒嘗試躺下。有一天早上,前一晚特別冷,我問禮拜堂裡覺得自己前一晚凍傷了的學生舉手。三隻手舉起。儘管有這些經歷,學生幾乎沒抱怨。他們知道我們正盡力為他們做。他們為能夠享受任何可以使他們改善處境的機會而快樂。他們不斷問可以做什麼減輕老師負擔。

passages.original: I have heard it stated more than once, both in the North and in the South, that coloured people would not obey and respect each other when one member of the race is placed in a position of authority over others. In regard to this general belief and these statements, I can say that during the nineteen years of my experience at Tuskegee I never, either by word or act, have been treated with disrespect by any student or officer connected with the institution. On the other hand, I am constantly embarrassed by the many acts of thoughtful kindness. The students do not seem to want to see me carry a large book or a satchel or any kind of a burden through the grounds. In such cases more than one always offers to relieve me. I almost never go out of my office when the rain is falling that some student does not come to my side with an umbrella and ask to be allowed to hold it over me.
passages.vernacular: 我不止一次聽過,無論喺北方或者南方,話有色人種唔會服從同尊重彼此,當種族一個成員被置於其他人之上嘅權威位置時。關於呢個普遍相信同呢啲說法,我可以講,我喺塔斯基吉十九年經驗期間,從未被任何學生或學院職員以言語或行為不尊重地對待。相反,我不斷被許多體貼好意嘅行為弄到尷尬。學生似乎唔想見到我拎大書、手提包或任何負擔經過校園。咁嘅情況下,總係多過一個提出減輕我嘅負擔。我落雨時幾乎從不離開辦公室,而冇學生行到我身邊,帶住遮,要求准許為我撐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不止一次聽過,無論在北方或南方,說有色人種不會服從和尊重彼此,當種族一個成員被置於其他人之上的權威位置時。關於這個普遍相信和這些說法,我可以說,我在塔斯基吉十九年經驗期間,從未被任何學生或學院職員以言語或行為不尊重地對待。相反,我不斷被許多體貼好意的行為弄到尷尬。學生似乎不想看到我拿大書、手提包或任何負擔經過校園。這樣的情況下,總是多過一個提出減輕我的負擔。我下雨時幾乎從不離開辦公室,而沒學生走到我身邊,帶著傘,要求准許為我撐。

passages.original: While writing upon this subject, it is a pleasure for me to add that in all my contact with the white people of the South I have never received a single personal insult. The white people in and near Tuskegee, to an especial degree, seem to count it as a privilege to show me all the respect within their power, and often go out of their way to do this.
passages.vernacular: 寫呢個題目時,我好高興補充,我同南方白人所有接觸中,從未受到過一次個人侮辱。塔斯基吉及附近嘅白人,尤其似乎視盡其所能向我表示一切尊重為特權,經常特地咁做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 寫這個題目時,我很高興補充,我與南方白人所有接觸中,從未受到過一次個人侮辱。塔斯基吉及附近的白人,尤其似乎視盡其所能向我表示一切尊重為特權,經常特地這樣做。

passages.original: Not very long ago I was making a journey between Dallas (Texas) and Houston. In some way it became known in advance that I was on the train. At nearly every station at which the train stopped, numbers of white people, including in most cases of the officials of the town, came aboard and introduced themselves and thanked me heartily for the work that I was trying to do for the South.
passages.vernacular: 不久前,我喺達拉斯(德克薩斯)同休斯頓之間旅行。不知點樣,事先被知道我喺火車上。火車停低嘅幾乎每個車站,都有好多白人(大部分情況包括鎮上官員)上車,介紹自己,衷心多謝我為南方所做嘅工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久前,我在達拉斯(德克薩斯)和休斯頓之間旅行。不知怎樣,事先被知道我在火車上。火車停下的幾乎每個車站,都有很多白人(大部分情況包括鎮上官員)上車,介紹自己,衷心感謝我為南方所做的工作。

passages.original: On another occasion, when I was making a trip from Augusta, Georgia, to Atlanta, being rather tired from much travel, I rode in a Pullman sleeper. When I went into the car, I found there two ladies from Boston whom I knew well. These good ladies were perfectly ignorant, it seems, of the customs of the South, and in the goodness of their hearts insisted that I take a seat with them in their section. After some hesitation I consented. I had been there but a few minutes when one of them, without my knowledge, ordered supper to be served for the three of us. This embarrassed me still further. The car was full of Southern white men, most of whom had their eyes on our party. When I found that supper had been ordered, I tried to contrive some excuse that would permit me to leave the section, but the ladies insisted that I must eat with them. I finally settled back in my seat with a sigh, and said to myself, “I am in for it now, sure.”
passages.vernacular: 另一次,我由佐治亞州奧古斯塔去亞特蘭大旅行,因為長途旅行相當疲倦,我坐普爾曼臥車。我入車廂時,發現有兩位我熟識嘅波士頓女士。呢兩位好女士似乎完全唔知道南方習俗,好心地堅持要我同佢哋坐喺佢哋嘅分隔座位。猶豫之後,我同意。我坐咗冇幾分鐘,其中一位冇通知我就叫咗晚餐畀我哋三個人。呢個令我更加尷尬。車廂全部係南方白人,大部分人嘅眼睛都望住我哋嘅小組。當我發現晚餐已經點咗,我試圖搵個藉口離開座位,不過女士堅持我必須同佢哋一齊食。我最終歎一口氣靠喺座位,對自己講:「我而家肯定死定。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 另一次,我由喬治亞州奧古斯塔去亞特蘭大旅行,因為長途旅行相當疲倦,我坐普爾曼臥車。我入車廂時,發現有兩位我熟識的波士頓女士。這兩位好女士似乎完全不知道南方習俗,好心地堅持要我與她們坐在她們的分隔座位。猶豫之後,我同意。我坐了沒幾分鐘,其中一位沒通知我就叫了晚餐給我們三個人。這使我更加尷尬。車廂全部是南方白人,大部分人的眼睛都望著我們的小組。當我發現晚餐已經點了,我試圖找個藉口離開座位,不過女士堅持我必須與她們一起吃。我最終歎一口氣靠在座位,對自己說:「我現在肯定死定。」

passages.original: To add further to the embarrassment of the situation, soon after the supper was placed on the table one of the ladies remembered that she had in her satchel a special kind of tea which she wished served, and as she said she felt quite sure the porter did not know how to brew it properly, she insisted upon getting up and preparing and serving it herself. At last the meal was over; and it seemed the longest one that I had ever eaten. When we were through, I decided to get myself out of the embarrassing situation and go to the smoking-room, where most of the men were by that time, to see how the land lay. In the meantime, however, it had become known in some way throughout the car who I was. When I went into the smoking-room I was never more surprised in my life than when each man, nearly every one of them a citizen of Georgia, came up and introduced himself to me and thanked me earnestly for the work that I was trying to do for the whole South. This was not flattery, because each one of these individuals knew that he had nothing to gain by trying to flatter me.
passages.vernacular: 令情況更加尷尬嘅係,晚餐放上枱後不久,其中一位女士記起佢手提包有一種佢想供應嘅特別茶,佢話佢相當肯定侍者唔識正確沖,堅持自己起身準備同供應。終於食完飯;似乎係我食過最長嘅一餐。食完之後,我決定擺脫尷尬局面,去吸煙室,大部分男人嗰時都喺嗰度,睇下情況如何。不過同時,整個車廂不知點樣已經知道我係邊個。我入吸煙室時,我一生從未咁驚訝:每個男人,幾乎全部係佐治亞公民,走過嚟介紹自己,認真多謝我為整個南方所做嘅工作。呢個唔係奉承,因為每個人都知道試圖奉承我佢冇任何嘢可得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 使情況更加尷尬的是,晚餐放上桌後不久,其中一位女士記起她手提包有一種她想供應的特別茶,她說她相當肯定侍者不會正確沖,堅持自己起身準備和供應。終於吃完飯;似乎是我吃過最長的一頓。吃完之後,我決定擺脫尷尬局面,去吸煙室,大部分男人那時都在那裡,看看情況如何。不過同時,整個車廂不知怎樣已經知道我是誰。我入吸煙室時,我一生從未那麼驚訝:每個男人,幾乎全部是喬治亞公民,走過來介紹自己,認真感謝我為整個南方所做的工作。這不是奉承,因為每個人都知道試圖奉承我他沒任何東西可得。

passages.original: From the first I have sought to impress the students with the idea that Tuskegee is not my institution, or that of the officers, but that it is their institution, and that they have as much interest in it as any of the trustees or instructors. I have further sought to have them feel that I am at the institution as their friend and adviser, and not as their overseer. It has been my aim to have them speak with directness and frankness about anything that concerns the life of the school. Two or three times a year I ask the students to write me a letter criticising or making complaints or suggestions about anything connected with the institution. When this is not done, I have them meet me in the chapel for a heart-to-heart talk about the conduct of the school. There are no meetings with our students that I enjoy more than these, and none are more helpful to me in planning for the future. These meetings, it seems to me, enable me to get at the very heart of all that concerns the school. Few things help an individual more than to place responsibility upon him, and to let him know that you trust him. When I have read of labour troubles between employers and employees, I have often thought that many strikes and similar disturbances might be avoided if the employers would cultivate the habit of getting nearer to their employees, of consulting and advising with them, and letting them feel that the interests of the two are the same. Every individual responds to confidence, and this is not more true of any race than of the Negroes. Let them once understand that you are unselfishly interested in them, and you can lead them to any extent.
passages.vernacular: 從一開始,我就試圖令學生印象深刻,塔斯基吉唔係我嘅學院,亦唔係職員嘅,而係佢哋嘅學院,佢哋對佢嘅興趣同任何受託人或導師一樣多。我進一步試圖令佢哋覺得,我喺學院係作為佢哋嘅朋友同顧問,而唔係佢哋嘅監工。我嘅目標係令佢哋對任何關乎學校生活嘅事直接坦率咁講。每年兩三次,我要求學生寫信畀我,批評或投訴或者建議任何關於學院嘅事。冇做嘅時候,我叫佢哋喺禮拜堂同我見面,就學校嘅運作推心置腹傾談。冇比呢啲同學生嘅聚會更令我享受,亦冇比呢啲更有助我計劃將來。呢啲聚會,依我睇,令我可以了解所有關於學校嘅核心。冇多少事比畀一個人責任、令佢知道你信任佢更有助佢。我讀到勞資雙方嘅勞工糾紛時,經常諗,如果僱主培養更接近僱員、同佢哋商量同徵求意見、令佢哋覺得雙方利益相同嘅習慣,好多罷工同類似騷亂可以避免。每個人都對信任有回應,黑人亦不比任何種族少。只要佢哋明白你無私咁關心佢哋,你就可以帶領佢哋到任何程度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從一開始,我就試圖使學生印象深刻,塔斯基吉不是我的學院,也不是職員的,而是他們的學院,他們對它的興趣和任何受託人或導師一樣多。我進一步試圖使他們覺得,我在學院是作為他們的朋友和顧問,而不是他們的監工。我的目標是使他們對任何關乎學校生活的事直接坦率地講。每年兩三次,我要求學生寫信給我,批評或投訴或建議任何關於學院的事。沒做的時候,我叫他們在禮拜堂與我見面,就學校的運作推心置腹交談。沒有比這些與學生的聚會更使我享受,也沒有比這些更有助我計劃將來。這些聚會,依我看,使我可以了解所有關於學校的核心。沒多少事比給一個人責任、使他知道你信任他更有助他。我讀到勞資雙方的勞工糾紛時,經常想,如果僱主培養更接近僱員、與他們商量和徵求意見、使他們覺得雙方利益相同的習慣,很多罷工和類似騷亂可以避免。每個人都對信任有回應,黑人也不比任何種族少。只要他們明白你無私地關心他們,你就可以帶領他們到任何程度。

passages.original: It was my aim from the first at Tuskegee to not only have the buildings erected by the students themselves, but to have them make their own furniture as far as was possible. I now marvel at the patience of the students while sleeping upon the floor while waiting for some kind of a bedstead to be constructed, or at their sleeping without any kind of a mattress while waiting for something that looked like a mattress to be made.
passages.vernacular: 我喺塔斯基吉從一開始嘅目標,唔單止令建築由學生自己興建,仲要令佢哋盡可能製作自己嘅傢俬。我而家驚嘆學生嘅耐性:等待某種床架建造時瞓喺地板,或者等待造出似褥嘅嘢時冇任何褥子瞓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在塔斯基吉從一開始的目標,不僅使建築由學生自己興建,還要使他們盡可能製作自己的傢俱。我現在驚嘆學生的耐性:等待某種床架建造時睡在地板,或等待造出像褥子的東西時沒任何褥子睡。

passages.original: In the early days we had very few students who had been used to handling carpenters’ tools, and the bedsteads made by the students then were very rough and very weak. Not unfrequently when I went into the students’ rooms in the morning I would find at least two bedsteads lying about on the floor. The problem of providing mattresses was a difficult one to solve. We finally mastered this, however, by getting some cheap cloth and sewing pieces of this together as to make large bags. These bags we filled with the pine straw—or, as it is sometimes called, pine needles—which we secured from the forests near by. I am glad to say that the industry of mattress-making has grown steadily since then, and has been improved to such an extent that at the present time it is an important branch of the work which is taught systematically to a number of our girls, and that the mattresses that now come out of the mattress-shop at Tuskegee are about as good as those bought in the average store. For some time after the opening of the boarding department we had no chairs in the students’ bedrooms or in the dining rooms. Instead of chairs we used stools which the students constructed by nailing together three pieces of rough board. As a rule, the furniture in the students’ rooms during the early days of the school consisted of a bed, some stools, and sometimes a rough table made by the students. The plan of having the students make the furniture is still followed, but the number of pieces in a room has been increased, and the workmanship has so improved that little fault can be found with the articles now. One thing that I have always insisted upon at Tuskegee is that everywhere there should be absolute cleanliness. Over and over again the students were reminded in those first years—and are reminded now—that people would excuse us for our poverty, for our lack of comforts and conveniences, but that they would not excuse us for dirt.
passages.vernacular: 早期我哋好少學生慣用木匠工具,當時學生製作嘅床架好粗糙好脆弱。朝早我入學生嘅房間,經常發現至少兩張床架躺喺地板。提供褥子係難以解決嘅問題。不過我哋最終解決咗,搵到廉價布,縫埋一齊做成大袋。我哋用從附近森林得到嘅松針(或者有時叫松葉)填滿呢啲袋。我好高興咁講,褥子製作行業從此穩定增長,並改進到而家係系統教授畀我哋好多女孩嘅重要工作分支,而家塔斯基吉褥子工場出嚟嘅褥子,大約同普通舖頭買嘅一樣好。寄宿部門開設後一段時間,學生臥室同飯廳都冇椅。我哋用學生用三塊粗木板釘埋做成嘅凳,代替椅。學校早期,學生房間嘅傢俬通常包括一張床、一些凳,有時係學生做嘅粗糙枱。由學生製作傢俬嘅計劃仍然遵循,不過房間裡面嘅件數增加,工藝改進到而家嘅物品幾乎冇毛病可挑。我喺塔斯基吉一直堅持嘅一件事,係到處要絕對清潔。頭幾年反覆提醒學生——現在亦在提醒——人們會原諒我哋貧窮、缺乏舒適同便利,但唔會原諒污穢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早期我們很少學生慣用木匠工具,當時學生製作的床架很粗糙很脆弱。早上我入學生的房間,經常發現至少兩張床架躺在地板。提供褥子是難以解決的問題。不過我們最終解決了,找到廉價布,縫在一起做成大袋。我們用從附近森林得到的松針(或有時叫松葉)填滿這些袋。我很高興地說,褥子製作行業從此穩定增長,並改進到現在是系統教授給我們很多女孩的重要工作分支,現在塔斯基吉褥子工場出來的褥子,大約和普通店鋪買的一樣好。寄宿部門開設後一段時間,學生臥室和飯廳都沒椅子。我們用學生用三塊粗木板釘在一起做成的凳子,代替椅子。學校早期,學生房間的傢俱通常包括一張床、一些凳子,有時是學生做的粗糙桌子。由學生製作傢俱的計劃仍然遵循,不過房間裡的件數增加,工藝改進到現在的物品幾乎沒毛病可挑。我在塔斯基吉一直堅持的一件事,是到處要絕對清潔。頭幾年反覆提醒學生——現在也在提醒——人們會原諒我們貧窮、缺乏舒適和便利,但不會原諒污穢。

passages.original: Another thing that has been insisted upon at the school is the use of the tooth-brush. “The gospel of the tooth-brush,” as General Armstrong used to call it, is part of our creed at Tuskegee. No student is permitted to retain who does not keep and use a tooth-brush. Several times, in recent years, students have come to us who brought with them almost no other article except a tooth-brush. They had heard from the lips of other students about our insisting upon the use of this, and so, to make a good impression, they brought at least a tooth-brush with them. I remember that one morning, not long ago, I went with the lady principal on her usual morning tour of inspection of the girls’ rooms. We found one room that contained three girls who had recently arrived at the school. When I asked them if they had tooth-brushes, one of the girls replied, pointing to a brush: “Yes, sir. That is our brush. We bought it together, yesterday.” It did not take them long to learn a different lesson.
passages.vernacular: 學校堅持嘅另一件事,係使用牙刷。「牙刷福音」(阿姆斯特朗將軍以前咁稱呼)係我哋塔斯基吉信條嘅一部分。冇保存同使用牙刷嘅學生,唔獲准留低。近年幾次,學生來到我哋度,除咗牙刷,幾乎冇帶任何其他物品。佢哋從其他學生口中聽到我哋堅持使用牙刷,所以為咗畀好印象,至少帶咗一支牙刷。我記得不久前一個早晨,我同女主任一齊進行佢通常嘅早晨女孩房間巡視。我哋發現一間房有三個最近到學校嘅女孩。當我問佢哋有冇牙刷,其中一個女孩指住一支牙刷答:「有,先生。嗰支係我哋嘅牙刷。我哋昨日一齊買嘅。」佢哋冇幾耐就學到唔同嘅功課。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 學校堅持的另一件事,是使用牙刷。「牙刷福音」(阿姆斯特朗將軍以前這樣稱呼)是我們塔斯基吉信條的一部分。沒保存和使用牙刷的學生,不獲准留下。近年幾次,學生來到我們這裡,除了牙刷,幾乎沒帶任何其他物品。他們從其他學生口中聽到我們堅持使用牙刷,所以為了給好印象,至少帶了一支牙刷。我記得不久前一個早晨,我和女主任一起進行她通常的早晨女孩房間巡視。我們發現一間房有三個最近到學校的女孩。當我問她們有沒有牙刷,其中一個女孩指著一支牙刷答:「有,先生。那支是我們的牙刷。我們昨天一起買的。」她們沒多久就學到不同的功課。

passages.original: It has been interesting to note the effect that the use of the tooth-brush has had in bringing about a higher degree of civilization among the students. With few exceptions, I have noticed that, if we can get a student to the point where, when the first or second tooth-brush disappears, he of his own motion buys another, I have not been disappointed in the future of that individual. Absolute cleanliness of the body has been insisted upon from the first. The students have been taught to bathe as regularly as to take their meals. This lesson we began teaching before we had anything in the shape of a bath-house. Most of the students came from plantation districts, and often we had to teach them how to sleep at night; that is, whether between the two sheets—after we got to the point where we could provide them two sheets—or under both of them. Naturally I found it difficult to teach them to sleep between two sheets when we were able to supply but one. The importance of the use of the night-gown received the same attention.
passages.vernacular: 留意牙刷使用,對促使學生更高程度文明嘅效果,好有趣。除少數例外,我留意到,如果我哋可以令一個學生去到,當第一支或第二支牙刷不見,佢自己主動買另一支,我對嗰個人嘅將來就冇失望過。從一開始就堅持身體絕對清潔。學生被教導洗澡同食飯一樣定時。呢個功課我哋喺有任何浴室形式之前就開始教。大部分學生來自種植園地區,我哋經常要教佢哋夜晚點樣瞓;即係,瞓喺兩張床單之間——當我哋可以提供兩張床單之後——定係喺兩張下面。自然地,當我哋只能供應一張時,我覺得好難教佢哋瞓喺兩張床單之間。使用睡衣嘅重要性受到同樣注意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 留意牙刷使用,對促使學生更高程度文明的效果,很有趣。除少數例外,我留意到,如果我們可以使一個學生去到,當第一支或第二支牙刷不見,他自己主動買另一支,我對那個人的將來就沒失望過。從一開始就堅持身體絕對清潔。學生被教導洗澡和吃飯一樣定時。這個功課我們在有任何浴室形式之前就開始教。大部分學生來自種植園地區,我們經常要教他們夜晚怎樣睡;即,睡在兩張床單之間——當我們可以提供兩張床單之後——還是在兩張下面。自然地,當我們只能供應一張時,我覺得很難教他們睡在兩張床單之間。使用睡衣的重要性受到同樣注意。

passages.original: For a long time one of the most difficult tasks was to teach the students that all the buttons were to be kept on their clothes, and that there must be no torn places or grease-spots. This lesson, I am pleased to be able to say, has been so thoroughly learned and so faithfully handed down from year to year by one set of students to another that often at the present time, when the students march out of the chapel in the evening and their dress is inspected, as it is every night, not one button is found to be missing.
passages.vernacular: 好長時間,最困難嘅任務之一,係教學生所有鈕扣都要保持喺衣服上,唔可以有破洞或者油漬。呢個功課,我好高興可以講,已經被學生一批一批咁徹底學到、忠實地傳下去,以致而家學生晚間行出禮拜堂、衣著被檢查(每晚都檢查)時,經常冇一粒鈕扣不見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很長時間,最困難的任務之一,是教學生所有鈕扣都要保持在衣服上,不可以有破洞或油漬。這個功課,我很高興可以說,已經被學生一批一批地徹底學到、忠實地傳下去,以致現在學生晚間走出禮拜堂、衣著被檢查(每晚都檢查)時,經常沒一粒鈕扣不見。

passages.original: When we opened our boarding department, we provided rooms in the attic of Porter Hall, our first building, for a number of girls. But the number of students, of both sexes, continued to increase. We could find rooms outside the school grounds for many of the young men, but the girls we did not care to expose in this way. Very soon the problem of providing more rooms for the girls, as well as a larger boarding department for all the students, grew serious. As a result, we finally decided to undertake the construction of a still larger building—a building that would contain rooms for the girls and boarding accommodations for all.
passages.vernacular: 我哋開設寄宿部門時,喺第一座建築波特樓嘅閣樓,為一批女孩提供房間。不過男女學生人數繼續增加。我哋可以喺校園外為好多年輕男子搵到房間,不過女孩我哋唔想咁樣暴露。好快,為女孩提供更多房間,以及為全體學生提供更大寄宿部門嘅問題變得嚴重。結果,我哋最終決定承擔興建一座更大建築——一座載有女孩房間同全體寄宿設施嘅建築。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們開設寄宿部門時,在第一座建築波特樓的閣樓,為一批女孩提供房間。不過男女學生人數繼續增加。我們可以在校園外為很多年輕男子找到房間,不過女孩我們不想這樣暴露。很快,為女孩提供更多房間,以及為全體學生提供更大寄宿部門的問題變得嚴重。結果,我們最終決定承擔興建一座更大建築——一座載有女孩房間和全體寄宿設施的建築。

passages.original: After having had a preliminary sketch of the needed building made, we found that it would cost about ten thousand dollars. We had no money whatever with which to begin; still we decided to give the needed building a name. We knew we could name it, even though we were in doubt about our ability to secure the means for its construction. We decided to call the proposed building Alabama Hall, in honour of the state in which we were labouring. Again Miss Davidson began making efforts to enlist the interest and help of the coloured and white people in and near Tuskegee. They responded willingly, in proportion to their means. The students, as in the case of our first building, Porter Hall, began digging out the dirt in order to allow the laying of the foundations.
passages.vernacular: 所需建築嘅初步草圖畫好之後,我哋發現造價大約一萬美元。我哋完全冇錢開始;但我哋仍然決定為所需建築命名。我哋知道可以命名,雖然我哋懷疑自己有冇能力得到興建嘅資金。我哋決定將擬建嘅建築命名為阿拉巴馬樓,以紀念我哋工作嘅州。戴維森小姐再次開始努力爭取塔斯基吉及附近嘅有色人種同白人嘅興趣同幫助。佢哋樂意按佢哋能力回應。學生,同我哋第一座建築波特樓嘅情況一樣,開始挖土,令可以打地基。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所需建築的初步草圖畫好之後,我們發現造價大約一萬美元。我們完全沒錢開始;但我們仍然決定為所需建築命名。我們知道可以命名,雖然我們懷疑自己有沒有能力得到興建的資金。我們決定將擬建的建築命名為阿拉巴馬樓,以紀念我們工作的州。戴維森小姐再次開始努力爭取塔斯基吉及附近的有色人種和白人的興趣和幫助。他們樂意按他們能力回應。學生,與我們第一座建築波特樓的情況一樣,開始挖土,使可以打地基。

passages.original: When we seemed at the end of our resources, so far as securing money was concerned, something occurred which showed the greatness of General Armstrong—something which proved how far he was above the ordinary individual. When we were in the midst of great anxiety as to where and how we were to get funds for the new building, I received a telegram from General Armstrong asking me if I could spend a month travelling with him through the North, and asking me, if I could do so, to come to Hampton at once. Of course I accepted General Armstrong’s invitation, and went to Hampton immediately. On arriving there I found that the General had decided to take a quartette of singers through the North, and hold meetings for a month in important cities, at which meetings he and I were to speak. Imagine my surprise when the General told me, further, that these meetings were to be held, not in the interests of Hampton, but in the interests of Tuskegee, and that the Hampton Institute was to be responsible for all the expenses.
passages.vernacular: 就籌款而言,當我哋似乎已經用盡資源時,發生咗一件事,顯示阿姆斯特朗將軍嘅偉大——證明佢高過普通人幾遠。當我哋身處極大焦慮,唔知邊度、點樣為新建築得到資金,我收到阿姆斯特朗將軍一封電報,問我可唔可以花一個月同佢穿越北方旅行,並問我如果可以,即刻去漢普頓。我當然接受阿姆斯特朗將軍嘅邀請,即刻去漢普頓。我到嗰度發現將軍決定帶一個四重唱歌手穿越北方,喺重要城市舉行一個月嘅聚會,聚會上佢同我演講。想像我嘅驚訝,當將軍進一步話畀我知,呢啲聚會唔係為漢普頓嘅利益而開,而係為塔斯基吉嘅利益,而漢普頓學院要負責所有開支。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就籌款而言,當我們似乎已經用盡資源時,發生了一件事,顯示阿姆斯特朗將軍的偉大——證明他高過普通人多遠。當我們身處極大焦慮,不知在哪裡、怎樣為新建築得到資金,我收到阿姆斯特朗將軍一封電報,問我可不可以花一個月與他穿越北方旅行,並問我如果可以,立刻去漢普頓。我當然接受阿姆斯特朗將軍的邀請,立刻去漢普頓。我到那裡發現將軍決定帶一個四重唱歌手穿越北方,在重要城市舉行一個月的聚會,聚會上他和我演講。想像我的驚訝,當將軍進一步告訴我,這些聚會不是為漢普頓的利益而開,而是為塔斯基吉的利益,而漢普頓學院要負責所有開支。

passages.original: Although he never told me so in so many words, I found that General Armstrong took this method of introducing me to the people of the North, as well as for the sake of securing some immediate funds to be used in the erection of Alabama Hall. A weak and narrow man would have reasoned that all the money which came to Tuskegee in this way would be just so much taken from the Hampton Institute; but none of these selfish or short-sighted feelings ever entered the breast of General Armstrong. He was too big to be little, too good to be mean. He knew that the people in the North who gave money gave it for the purpose of helping the whole cause of Negro civilization, and not merely for the advancement of any one school. The General knew, too, that the way to strengthen Hampton was to make it a centre of unselfish power in the working out of the whole Southern problem.
passages.vernacular: 雖然佢從未咁直接話畀我知,我發現阿姆斯特朗將軍採用呢個方法,既係為咗將我介紹畀北方嘅人民,亦為咗得到一些即時資金,用於興建阿拉巴馬樓。一個軟弱狹隘嘅人會推論,以呢種方式來到塔斯基吉嘅所有錢,都係從漢普頓學院拿走嘅;不過冇一個呢種自私或短視嘅感覺曾經進入阿姆斯特朗將軍嘅胸懷。佢太偉大,唔會渺小;太善良,唔會刻薄。佢知道北方捐錢嘅人,係為咗幫助整個黑人文明事業,而唔單單為咗推進任何一間學校。將軍亦知道,加強漢普頓嘅方法,係令佢成為解決整個南方問題嘅無私力量中心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然他從未這樣直接告訴我,我發現阿姆斯特朗將軍採用這個方法,既是為了將我介紹給北方的人民,也為了得到一些即時資金,用於興建阿拉巴馬樓。一個軟弱狹隘的人會推論,以這種方式來到塔斯基吉的所有錢,都是從漢普頓學院拿走的;不過沒一個這種自私或短視的感覺曾經進入阿姆斯特朗將軍的胸懷。他太偉大,不會渺小;太善良,不會刻薄。他知道北方捐錢的人,是為了幫助整個黑人文明事業,而不單單為了推進任何一間學校。將軍也知道,加強漢普頓的方法,是使它成為解決整個南方問題的無私力量中心。

passages.original: In regard to the addresses which I was to make in the North, I recall just one piece of advice which the General gave me. He said: “Give them an idea for every word.” I think it would be hard to improve upon this advice; and it might be made to apply to all public speaking. From that time to the present I have always tried to keep his advice in mind.
passages.vernacular: 關於我要喺北方發表嘅演說,我只記得將軍畀我嘅一個忠告。佢講:「每個字畀佢哋一個想法。」我諗好難改進呢個忠告;佢可以適用於所有公眾演說。從嗰時到而家,我一直嘗試記住佢嘅忠告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 關於我要在北方發表的演說,我只記得將軍給我的一個忠告。他說:「每個字給他們一個想法。」我想很難改進這個忠告;它可以適用於所有公眾演說。從那時到現在,我一直嘗試記住他的忠告。

passages.original: Meetings were held in New York, Brooklyn, Boston, Philadelphia, and other large cities, and at all of these meetings General Armstrong pleaded, together with myself, for help, not for Hampton, but for Tuskegee. At these meetings an especial effort was made to secure help for the building of Alabama Hall, as well as to introduce the school to the attention of the general public. In both these respects the meetings proved successful.
passages.vernacular: 聚會喺紐約、布魯克林、波士頓、費城同其他大城市舉行,所有呢啲聚會上,阿姆斯特朗將軍連同我,懇求幫助,唔係為漢普頓,而係為塔斯基吉。喺呢啲聚會,特別努力為興建阿拉巴馬樓爭取幫助,同時向一般公眾介紹學校。喺呢兩方面,聚會證明都成功。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聚會在紐約、布魯克林、波士頓、費城和其他大城市舉行,所有這些聚會上,阿姆斯特朗將軍連同我,懇求幫助,不是為漢普頓,而是為塔斯基吉。在這些聚會,特別努力為興建阿拉巴馬樓爭取幫助,同時向一般公眾介紹學校。在這兩方面,聚會證明都成功。

passages.original: After that kindly introduction I began going North alone to secure funds. During the last fifteen years I have been compelled to spend a large proportion of my time away from the school, in an effort to secure money to provide for the growing needs of the institution. In my efforts to get funds I have had some experiences that may be of interest to my readers. Time and time again I have been asked, by people who are trying to secure money for philanthropic purposes, what rule or rules I followed to secure the interest and help of people who were able to contribute money to worthy objects. As far as the science of what is called begging can be reduced to rules, I would say that I have had but two rules. First, always to do my whole duty regarding making our work known to individuals and organizations; and, second, not to worry about the results. This second rule has been the hardest for me to live up to. When bills are on the eve of falling due, with not a dollar in hand with which to meet them, it is pretty difficult to learn not to worry, although I think I am learning more and more each year that all worry simply consumes, and to no purpose, just so much physical and mental strength that might otherwise be given to effective work. After considerable experience in coming into contact with wealthy and noted men, I have observed that those who have accomplished the greatest results are those who “keep under the body”; are those who never grow excited or lose self-control, but are always calm, self-possessed, patient, and polite. I think that President William McKinley is the best example of a man of this class that I have ever seen.
passages.vernacular: 經過嗰次友善嘅介紹,我開始獨自去北方籌款。過去十五年,我被迫花大部分時間離開學校,努力籌錢為學院日益增長嘅需要提供。我努力籌款期間,有些經歷也許讀者會有興趣。一次又一次,試圖為慈善目的籌錢嘅人問我,我遵循咩規則爭取有能力為值得目標捐錢嘅人嘅興趣同幫助。只要所謂乞求嘅科學可以歸納為規則,我會話我只有兩條規則。第一,始終盡我全部責任,向個人同組織介紹我哋嘅工作;第二,唔為結果擔心。呢第二條規則對我最難遵守。當賬單即將到期,手上冇一美元應付時,好難學會唔擔心,雖然我認為我每年越來越學到,所有擔心都白白消耗本來可以用於有效工作嘅體力同精神。經過大量接觸富有同著名人士嘅經驗,我觀察到,取得最大成果嘅人,係「克制身體」嘅人;係從不激動或失去自制,始終冷靜、沉著、耐心、有禮嘅人。我諗威廉·麥金萊總統係我見過呢類人嘅最佳榜樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 經過那次友善的介紹,我開始獨自去北方籌款。過去十五年,我被迫花大部分時間離開學校,努力籌錢為學院日益增長的需要提供。我努力籌款期間,有些經歷也許讀者會有興趣。一次又一次,試圖為慈善目的籌錢的人問我,我遵循什麼規則爭取有能力為值得目標捐錢的人的興趣和幫助。只要所謂乞求的科學可以歸納為規則,我會說我只有兩條規則。第一,始終盡我全部責任,向個人和組織介紹我們的工作;第二,不為結果擔心。這第二條規則對我最難遵守。當賬單即將到期,手上沒一美元應付時,很難學會不擔心,雖然我認為我每年越來越學到,所有擔心都白白消耗本來可以用於有效工作的體力和精神。經過大量接觸富有和著名人士的經驗,我觀察到,取得最大成果的人,是「克制身體」的人;是從不激動或失去自制,始終冷靜、沉著、耐心、有禮的人。我想威廉·麥金萊總統是我見過這類人的最佳榜樣。

passages.original: In order to be successful in any kind of undertaking, I think the main thing is for one to grow to the point where he completely forgets himself; that is, to lose himself in a great cause. In proportion as one loses himself in the way, in the same degree does he get the highest happiness out of his work.
passages.vernacular: 為咗喺任何事業成功,我諗主要係一個人要成長到完全忘我嘅程度;即係,為一個偉大事業而忘記自己。一個人喺途中忘記自己越多,從工作中得到嘅最高快樂就越多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了在任何事業成功,我想主要是一個人要成長到完全忘我的程度;即,為一個偉大事業而忘記自己。一個人在途中忘記自己越多,從工作中得到的最高快樂就越多。

passages.original: My experience in getting money for Tuskegee has taught me to have no patience with those people who are always condemning the rich because they are rich, and because they do not give more to objects of charity. In the first place, those who are guilty of such sweeping criticisms do not know how many people would be made poor, and how much suffering would result, if wealthy people were to part all at once with any large proportion of their wealth in a way to disorganize and cripple great business enterprises. Then very few persons have any idea of the large number of applications for help that rich people are constantly being flooded with. I know wealthy people who receive as much as twenty calls a day for help. More than once when I have gone into the offices of rich men, I have found half a dozen persons waiting to see them, and all come for the same purpose, that of securing money. And all these calls in person, to say nothing of the applications received through the mails. Very few people have any idea of the amount of money given away by persons who never permit their names to be known. I have often heard persons condemned for not giving away money, who, to my own knowledge, were giving away thousands of dollars every year so quietly that the world knew nothing about it.
passages.vernacular: 我為塔斯基吉籌錢嘅經驗,令我對成日譴責富人因為佢哋富有、因為佢哋冇向慈善對象捐更多嘅人冇耐性。首先,犯呢種籠統批評嘅人,唔知道如果富人以擾亂同削弱大型商業事業嘅方式一次過放棄大部分財富,會令多少人變窮,造成幾多苦難。其次,好少人知道富人不斷被淹沒嘅求助申請數量之多。我認識有富人每日收到多達二十個求助。不止一次我入富人嘅辦公室,發現有六個人等候見佢,全部為同一個目的來,即籌錢。而所有呢啲係親自拜訪,更不用講郵寄收到嘅申請。好少人知道從不讓自己名字被知道嘅人捐出嘅錢數目。我經常聽到人們因為冇捐錢而被譴責,而據我自己所知,佢哋每年默默捐出幾千美元,世界冇人知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我為塔斯基吉籌錢的經驗,使我對整天譴責富人因為他們富有、因為他們沒向慈善對象捐更多的人沒耐性。首先,犯這種籠統批評的人,不知道如果富人以擾亂和削弱大型商業事業的方式一次過放棄大部分財富,會使多少人變窮,造成多少苦難。其次,很少人知道富人不斷被淹沒的求助申請數量之多。我認識有富人每天收到多達二十個求助。不止一次我入富人的辦公室,發現有六個人等候見他,全部為同一個目的來,即籌錢。而所有這些是親自拜訪,更不用說郵寄收到的申請。很少人知道從不讓自己名字被知道的人捐出的錢數目。我經常聽到人們因為沒捐錢而被譴責,而據我自己所知,他們每年默默捐出幾千美元,世界沒人知道。

passages.original: As an example of this, there are two ladies in New York, whose names rarely appear in print, but who, in a quiet way, have given us the means with which to erect three large and important buildings during the last eight years. Besides the gift of these buildings, they have made other generous donations to the school. And they not only help Tuskegee, but they are constantly seeking opportunities to help other worthy causes.
passages.vernacular: 作為例子,紐約有兩位女士,名字好少見報,不過過去八年,佢哋默默咁畀我哋資金,興建三座大而重要嘅建築。除咗捐贈呢啲建築,佢哋亦對學校作出其他慷慨捐贈。佢哋唔單止幫助塔斯基吉,仲不斷尋找機會幫助其他值得嘅事業。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 作為例子,紐約有兩位女士,名字很少見報,不過過去八年,她們默默地給我們資金,興建三座大而重要的建築。除了捐贈這些建築,她們也對學校作出其他慷慨捐贈。她們不僅幫助塔斯基吉,還不斷尋找機會幫助其他值得的事業。

passages.original: Although it has been my privilege to be the medium through which a good many hundred thousand dollars have been received for the work at Tuskegee, I have always avoided what the world calls “begging.” I often tell people that I have never “begged” any money, and that I am not a “beggar.” My experience and observation have convinced me that persistent asking outright for money from the rich does not, as a rule, secure help. I have usually proceeded on the principle that persons who possess sense enough to earn money have sense enough to know how to give it away, and that the mere making known of the facts regarding Tuskegee, and especially the facts regarding the work of the graduates, has been more effective than outright begging. I think that the presentation of facts, on a high, dignified plane, is all the begging that most rich people care for.
passages.vernacular: 雖然我有幸成為一個媒介,透過佢為塔斯基吉嘅工作收到好幾十萬美元,我一直避免世人所謂嘅「乞求」。我經常話畀人知,我從未「乞求」過任何錢,我唔係「乞丐」。我嘅經驗同觀察令我相信,持續向富人直接要錢,通常並唔會得到幫助。我通常按呢個原則進行:有足夠頭腦賺錢嘅人,有足夠頭腦知道點樣捐錢,而單單說明關於塔斯基吉嘅事實,尤其係關於畢業生工作嘅事實,比直接乞求更有效。我諗以高尚、有尊嚴嘅層面陳述事實,就係大部分富人願意接受嘅全部乞求。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然我有幸成為一個媒介,透過它為塔斯基吉的工作收到好幾十萬美元,我一直避免世人所謂的「乞求」。我經常告訴人,我從未「乞求」過任何錢,我不是「乞丐」。我的經驗和觀察使我相信,持續向富人直接要錢,通常並不會得到幫助。我通常按這個原則進行:有足夠頭腦賺錢的人,有足夠頭腦知道怎樣捐錢,而單單說明關於塔斯基吉的事實,尤其是關於畢業生工作的事實,比直接乞求更有效。我想以高尚、有尊嚴的層面陳述事實,就是大部分富人願意接受的全部乞求。

passages.original: While the work of going from door to door and from office to office is hard, disagreeable, and costly in bodily strength, yet it has some compensations. Such work gives one a rare opportunity to study human nature. It also has its compensations in giving one an opportunity to meet some of the best people in the world—to be more correct, I think I should say the best people in the world. When one takes a broad survey of the country, he will find that the most useful and influential people in it are those who take the deepest interest in institutions that exist for the purpose of making the world better.
passages.vernacular: 雖然逐家逐戶、逐間辦公室工作辛苦、令人不快、損耗體力,不過亦有些補償。呢種工作畀人一個罕見嘅機會研究人性。亦有補償,畀人機會結識世上一些最好嘅人——更準確咁講,我認為應該話世上最好嘅人。當一個人廣泛審視國家,會發現國內最有用、最有影響力嘅人,係對為令世界更好而存在嘅機構最感興趣嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然逐家逐戶、逐間辦公室工作辛苦、令人不快、損耗體力,不過也有些補償。這種工作給人一個罕見的機會研究人性。也有補償,給人機會結識世上一些最好的人——更準確地說,我認為應該說世上最好的人。當一個人廣泛審視國家,會發現國內最有用、最有影響力的人,是對為使世界更好而存在的機構最感興趣的人。

passages.original: At one time, when I was in Boston, I called at the door of a rather wealthy lady, and was admitted to the vestibule and sent up my card. While I was waiting for an answer, her husband came in, and asked me in the most abrupt manner what I wanted. When I tried to explain the object of my call, he became still more ungentlemanly in his words and manner, and finally grew so excited that I left the house without waiting for a reply from the lady. A few blocks from that house I called to see a gentleman who received me in the most cordial manner. He wrote me his check for a generous sum, and then, before I had had an opportunity to thank him, said: “I am so grateful to you, Mr. Washington, for giving me the opportunity to help a good cause. It is a privilege to have a share in it. We in Boston are constantly indebted to you for doing our work.” My experience in securing money convinces me that the first type of man is growing more rare all the time, and that the latter type is increasing; that is, that, more and more, rich people are coming to regard men and women who apply to them for help for worthy objects, not as beggars, but as agents for doing their work.
passages.vernacular: 有一次我喺波士頓,去敲一位相當富有嘅女士嘅門,獲准入玄關,遞上名片。等回覆期間,佢丈夫入嚟,以最唐突嘅方式問我想要咩。當我試圖解釋來意,佢嘅言語同態度變得更加冇禮貌,最終變得咁激動,我冇等女士回覆就離開咗屋。離嗰間屋幾條街,我去見一位紳士,佢以最熱情嘅方式接待我。佢寫咗張慷慨金額嘅支票畀我,然後,我未有機會多謝佢,佢就講:「華盛頓先生,我非常感激你畀我機會幫助一個好事業。能夠參與係一種特權。我哋波士頓人不斷欠你,因為你為我哋做我哋嘅工作。」我籌錢嘅經驗令我相信,第一種人越來越罕見,後一種正在增加;即係,越來越多富人開始視為值得目標而申請幫助嘅男女,唔係乞丐,而係為佢哋做工作嘅代理人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一次我在波士頓,去敲一位相當富有的女士的門,獲准入玄關,遞上名片。等回覆期間,她丈夫進來,以最唐突的方式問我想要什麼。當我試圖解釋來意,他的言語和態度變得更加沒禮貌,最終變得那麼激動,我沒等女士回覆就離開了屋子。離那間屋子幾條街,我去見一位紳士,他以最熱情的方式接待我。他寫了張慷慨金額的支票給我,然後,我未有機會感謝他,他就說:「華盛頓先生,我非常感激你給我機會幫助一個好事業。能夠參與是一種特權。我們波士頓人不斷欠你,因為你為我們做我們的工作。」我籌錢的經驗使我相信,第一種人越來越罕見,後一種正在增加;即,越來越多富人開始視為值得目標而申請幫助的男女,不是乞丐,而是為他們做工作的代理人。

passages.original: In the city of Boston I have rarely called upon an individual for funds that I have not been thanked for calling, usually before I could get an opportunity to thank the donor for the money. In that city the donors seem to feel, in a large degree, that an honour is being conferred upon them in their being permitted to give. Nowhere else have I met with, in so large a measure, this fine and Christlike spirit as in the city of Boston, although there are many notable instances of it outside that city. I repeat my belief that the world is growing in the direction of giving. I repeat that the main rule by which I have been guided in collecting money is to do my full duty in regard to giving people who have money an opportunity for help.
passages.vernacular: 喺波士頓市,我好少向一個人籌款而冇被多謝佢嘅來訪,通常係我未有機會多謝捐款人嘅錢之前。喺嗰個城市,捐款人似乎好大程度覺得被准許捐款係獲得榮譽。我喺其他地方冇遇到過咁大程度嘅呢種美好基督般精神,喺波士頓市,雖然城外亦有許多顯著例子。我重複我相信世界正朝向給予嘅方向發展。我重複,我籌款所遵循嘅主要規則,係盡我全部責任,畀有錢人一個幫助嘅機會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在波士頓市,我很少向一個人籌款而沒被感謝他的來訪,通常是我未有機會感謝捐款人的錢之前。在那個城市,捐款人似乎很大程度覺得被准許捐款是獲得榮譽。我在其他地方沒遇到過那麼大程度的這種美好基督般精神,在波士頓市,雖然城外也有許多顯著例子。我重複我相信世界正朝向給予的方向發展。我重複,我籌款所遵循的主要規則,是盡我全部責任,給有錢人一個幫助的機會。

passages.original: In the early years of the Tuskegee school I walked the streets or travelled country roads in the North for days and days without receiving a dollar. Often as it happened, when during the week I had been disappointed in not getting a cent from the very individuals from whom I most expected help, and when I was almost broken down and discouraged, that generous help has come from some one who I had had little idea would give at all.
passages.vernacular: 塔斯基吉學校早年,我喺北方街道行,或者喺鄉村道路旅行,好多日冇收到一美元。經常正係,當我一個星期對正我最期望幫助嘅人冇得到一分錢而失望,幾乎崩潰氣餒時,慷慨幫助來自我幾乎冇想過會畀嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 塔斯基吉學校早年,我在北方街道走,或在鄉村道路旅行,很多天沒收到一美元。經常正是,當我一個星期對正我最期望幫助的人沒得到一分錢而失望,幾乎崩潰氣餒時,慷慨幫助來自我幾乎沒想過會給的人。

passages.original: I recall that on one occasion I obtained information that led me to believe that a gentleman who lived about two miles out in the country from Stamford, Conn., might become interested in our efforts at Tuskegee if our conditions and needs were presented to him. On an unusually cold and stormy day I walked the two miles to see him. After some difficulty I succeeded in securing an interview with him. He listened with some degree of interest to what I had to say, but did not give me anything. I could not help having the feeling that, in a measure, the three hours that I had spent in seeing him had been thrown away. Still, I had followed my usual rule of doing my duty. If I had not seen him, I should have felt unhappy over neglect of duty.
passages.vernacular: 我記得有一次我得到資訊,令我相信一位住喺康涅狄格州斯坦福德鄉下大約兩英里外嘅紳士,如果向佢介紹我哋嘅情況同需要,可能對我哋塔斯基吉嘅努力感興趣。喺一個異常寒冷多風暴嘅日子,我步行兩英里去見佢。經過一些困難,我成功得到同佢面談。佢以某程度嘅興趣聽我講,但冇畀我任何嘢。我忍不住覺得,我花喺見佢嘅三個鐘,某程度上係白費。不過,我遵循咗我通常嘅盡責規則。如果我冇見佢,我會因為疏忽職責而不快樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我記得有一次我得到資訊,使我相信一位住在康涅狄格州斯坦福德鄉下大約兩英里外的紳士,如果向他介紹我們的情況和需要,可能對我們塔斯基吉的努力感興趣。在一個異常寒冷多風暴的日子,我步行兩英里去見他。經過一些困難,我成功得到與他面談。他以某種程度的興趣聽我講,但沒給我任何東西。我忍不住覺得,我花在見他的三個小時,某種程度上是白費。不過,我遵循了我通常的盡責規則。如果我沒見他,我會因為疏忽職責而不快樂。

passages.original: Two years after this visit a letter came to Tuskegee from this man, which read like this: “Enclosed I send you a New York draft for ten thousand dollars, to be used in furtherance of your work. I had placed this sum in my will for your school, but deem it wiser to give it to you while I live. I recall with pleasure your visit to me two years ago.”
passages.vernacular: 呢次探訪兩年後,一封信從呢個人來到塔斯基吉,內容大致如下:「隨函附上一張一萬美元嘅紐約匯票,用於推進你嘅工作。我原本已將呢筆錢放入我嘅遺囑畀你嘅學校,不過認為喺生時畀你更明智。我愉快咁記得兩年前你嘅探訪。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這次探訪兩年後,一封信從這個人來到塔斯基吉,內容大致如下:「隨函附上一張一萬美元的紐約匯票,用於推進你的工作。我原本已將這筆錢放入我的遺囑給你的學校,不過認為在生時給你更明智。我愉快地記得兩年前你的探訪。」

passages.original: I can hardly imagine any occurrence which could have given me more genuine satisfaction than the receipt of this draft. It was by far the largest single donation which up to that time the school had ever received. It came at a time when an unusually long period had passed since we had received any money. We were in great distress because of lack of funds, and the nervous strain was tremendous. It is difficult for me to think of any situation that is more trying on the nerves than that of conducting a large institution, with heavy obligations to meet, without knowing where the money is to come from to meet these obligations from month to month.
passages.vernacular: 我幾乎想像唔到有任何事件,可以比收到呢張匯票畀我更真誠嘅滿足。佢係學校到當時為止收過嘅最大單筆捐款。佢喺我哋收到任何錢之後異常長時間過去嘅時候來到。我哋因缺乏資金而非常困苦,神經壓力巨大。我好難想到有任何情況比經營一間大型機構、承擔沉重責任、卻唔知每月責任嘅錢從邊度來更磨損神經。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我幾乎想像不到有任何事件,可以比收到這張匯票給我更真誠的滿足。它是學校到當時為止收過的最大單筆捐款。它在我們收到任何錢之後異常長時間過去的時候來到。我們因缺乏資金而非常困苦,神經壓力巨大。我很難想到有任何情況比經營一間大型機構、承擔沉重責任、卻不知每月責任的錢從哪裡來更磨損神經。

passages.original: In our case I felt a double responsibility, and this made the anxiety all the more intense. If the institution had been officered by white persons, and had failed, it would have injured the cause of Negro education; but I knew that the failure of our institution, officered by Negroes, would not only mean the loss of a school, but would cause people, in a large degree, to lose faith in the ability of the entire race. The receipt of this draft for ten thousand dollars, under all these circumstances, partially lifted a burden that had been pressing down upon me for days.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅情況,我感到雙重責任,令焦慮更加強烈。如果機構由白人管理而失敗,會損害黑人教育事業;不過我知道,由黑人管理嘅我哋機構失敗,唔單止意味失去一間學校,而且會令人們好大程度對整個種族嘅能力失去信心。喺所有呢啲情況下,收到呢張一萬美元匯票,部分減輕咗壓住我多日嘅負擔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的情況,我感到雙重責任,使焦慮更加強烈。如果機構由白人管理而失敗,會損害黑人教育事業;不過我知道,由黑人管理的我們機構失敗,不僅意味失去一間學校,而且會使人們很大程度對整個種族的能力失去信心。在所有這些情況下,收到這張一萬美元匯票,部分減輕了壓著我多天的負擔。

passages.original: From the beginning of our work to the present I have always had the feeling, and lose no opportunity to impress our teachers with the same idea, that the school will always be supported in proportion as the inside of the institution is kept clean and pure and wholesome.
passages.vernacular: 從我哋工作開始到現在,我一直有個感覺,並不放過任何機會向老師們灌輸同樣想法:學校得到嘅支持,永遠同機構內部保持清潔、純淨、健康嘅程度成比例。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從我們工作開始到現在,我一直有個感覺,並不放過任何機會向老師們灌輸同樣想法:學校得到的支持,永遠與機構內部保持清潔、純淨、健康的程度成比例。

passages.original: The first time I ever saw the late Collis P. Huntington, the great railroad man, he gave me two dollars for our school. The last time I saw him, which was a few months before he died, he gave me fifty thousand dollars toward our endowment fund. Between these two gifts there were others of generous proportions which came every year from both Mr. and Mrs. Huntington.
passages.vernacular: 我第一次見已故嘅科利斯·P·亨廷頓(偉大嘅鐵路人),佢畀咗兩美元我哋學校。我最後一次見佢,係佢去世前幾個月,佢畀咗五萬美元我哋嘅基金。喺呢兩份捐贈之間,亨廷頓先生同太太每年都有其他慷慨金額。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我第一次見已故的科利斯·P·亨廷頓(偉大的鐵路人),他給了兩美元我們學校。我最後一次見他,是他去世前幾個月,他給了五萬美元我們的基金。在這兩份捐贈之間,亨廷頓先生和太太每年都有其他慷慨金額。

passages.original: Some people may say that it was Tuskegee’s good luck that brought to us this gift of fifty thousand dollars. No, it was not luck. It was hard work. Nothing ever comes to me, that is worth having, except as the result of hard work. When Mr. Huntington gave me the first two dollars, I did not blame him for not giving me more, but made up my mind that I was going to convince him by tangible results that we were worthy of larger gifts. For a dozen years I made a strong effort to convince Mr. Huntington of the value of our work. I noted that just in proportion as the usefulness of the school grew, his donations increased. Never did I meet an individual who took a more kindly and sympathetic interest in our school than did Mr. Huntington. He not only gave money to us, but took time in which to advise me, as a father would a son, about the general conduct of the school.
passages.vernacular: 有人可能話係塔斯基吉嘅好運帶嚟呢份五萬美元嘅捐贈。唔係,唔係運氣。係辛勤工作。任何值得擁有嘅嘢,除咗辛勤工作嘅結果,從來唔會到我身上。當亨廷頓先生畀我第一筆兩美元,我冇怪佢冇畀更多,而係下定決心,我要用有形成果說服佢,我哋值得更大嘅捐贈。十二年間,我努力說服亨廷頓先生,我哋工作嘅價值。我留意到,隨學校用處增長,佢嘅捐贈成比例增加。我從未遇到過一個比亨廷頓先生對我哋學校更友善同同情嘅人。佢唔單止捐錢畀我哋,仲花時間好似父親對兒子咁勸告我學校嘅一般管理。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有人可能說是塔斯基吉的好運帶來這份五萬美元的捐贈。不是,不是運氣。是辛勤工作。任何值得擁有的東西,除了辛勤工作的結果,從來不會到我身上。當亨廷頓先生給我第一筆兩美元,我沒怪他沒給更多,而是下定決心,我要用有形成果說服他,我們值得更大的捐贈。十二年間,我努力說服亨廷頓先生,我們工作的價值。我留意到,隨學校用處增長,他的捐贈成比例增加。我從未遇到過一個比亨廷頓先生對我們學校更友善和同情的人。他不僅捐錢給我們,還花時間像父親對兒子那樣勸告我學校的一般管理。

passages.original: More than once I have found myself in some pretty tight places while collecting money in the North. The following incident I have never related but once before, for the reason that I feared that people would not believe it. One morning I found myself in Providence, Rhode Island, without a cent of money with which to buy breakfast. In crossing the street to see a lady from whom I hoped to get some money, I found a bright new twenty-five-cent piece in the middle of the street track. I not only had this twenty-five cents for my breakfast, but within a few minutes I had a donation from the lady on whom I had started to call.
passages.vernacular: 不止一次,我喺北方籌錢時發現自己處於相當窘迫嘅境地。以下呢件事我只講過一次,因為我擔心人們唔相信。有一朝,我喺羅得島普羅維登斯,冇一分錢買早餐。橫過街道去見一位我希望從佢度得到一些錢嘅女士,我喺街道電車軌中間發現一個閃亮嶄新嘅二十五美分硬幣。我唔單止有呢二十五美分食早餐,幾分鐘內,我仲從我開始探訪嘅女士得到捐款。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不止一次,我在北方籌錢時發現自己處於相當窘迫的境地。以下這件事我只講過一次,因為我擔心人們不相信。有一天早上,我在羅得島普羅維登斯,沒一分錢買早餐。橫過街道去見一位我希望從她那裡得到一些錢的女士,我在街道電車軌中間發現一個閃亮嶄新的二十五美分硬幣。我不僅有這二十五美分吃早餐,幾分鐘內,我還從我開始探訪的女士得到捐款。

passages.original: At one of our Commencements I was bold enough to invite the Rev. E. Winchester Donald, D.D., rector of Trinity Church, Boston, to preach the Commencement sermon.
