passages.vernacularMandarin: 克利夫蘭先生不僅以多種個人方式向我表示友誼,也一直同意為我們學校做我要求他做的任何事。他做到,無論是個人捐款,或運用影響力爭取他人捐款。從我與克利夫蘭先生的個人相識判斷,我不相信他意識到自己有任何膚色偏見。他太偉大,不會這樣。我與人接觸中發現,通常只有細小、狹隘、為自己而活、從不讀好書、不旅行、從不以容許自己與其他靈魂——偉大外部世界——接觸的方式打開心靈的人。沒一個視野被膚色所限的人,可以接觸世上最高最好的東西。我在很多地方與人見面,發現最快樂的人是為他人做最多的人;最痛苦的是做最少的人。我也發現,很少事物(如果有)比種族偏見更能使人盲目和狹隘。我在星期日晚在禮拜堂向我們學生講話時,經常告訴他們,我生活越久、對世界經驗越多,就越相信,畢竟最值得為之而活——如有需要,為之而死——的一件事,是使別人更快樂、更有用的機會。

passages.original: The coloured people and the coloured newspapers at first seemed to be greatly pleased with the character of my Atlanta address, as well as with its reception. But after the first burst of enthusiasm began to die away, and the coloured people began reading the speech in cold type, some of them seemed to feel that they had been hypnotized. They seemed to feel that I had been too liberal in my remarks toward the Southern whites, and that I had not spoken out strongly enough for what they termed the “rights” of my race. For a while there was a reaction, so far as a certain element of my own race was concerned, but later these reactionary ones seemed to have been won over to my way of believing and acting.
passages.vernacular: 有色人種同有色人種報紙起初似乎對我亞特蘭大演說嘅品格,以及佢受到嘅歡迎,好滿意。不過,第一陣熱情開始消退,有色人種開始用冷靜嘅鉛字睇演說,有些人似乎覺得自己被催眠。佢哋似乎覺得,我對南方白人嘅言論太寬容,冇為佢哋所謂我種族嘅「權利」足夠強烈發聲。有一段時間,就我自己種族某部分人而言有反彈,不過後來呢啲反對者似乎被爭取到我嘅信念同行為。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有色人種和有色人種報紙起初似乎對我亞特蘭大演說的品格,以及它受到的歡迎,很滿意。不過,第一陣熱情開始消退,有色人種開始用冷靜的鉛字看演說,有些人似乎覺得自己被催眠。他們似乎覺得,我對南方白人的言論太寬容,沒為他們所謂我種族的「權利」足夠強烈發聲。有一段時間,就我自己種族某部分人而言有反彈,不過後來這些反對者似乎被爭取到我的信念和行為。

passages.original: While speaking of changes in public sentiment, I recall that about ten years after the school at Tuskegee was established, I had an experience that I shall never forget. Dr. Lyman Abbott, then the pastor of Plymouth Church, and also editor of the Outlook (then the Christian Union), asked me to write a letter for his paper giving my opinion of the exact condition, mental and moral, of the coloured ministers in the South, as based upon my observations. I wrote the letter, giving the exact facts as I conceived them to be. The picture painted was a rather black one—or, since I am black, shall I say “white”? It could not be otherwise with a race but a few years out of slavery, a race which had not had time or opportunity to produce a competent ministry.
passages.vernacular: 講到公眾情緒嘅變化,我記得塔斯基吉學校成立大約十年後,我有過一次永不忘記嘅經歷。當時普利茅斯教堂牧師同《展望》(當時叫《基督教聯合》)編輯萊曼·阿博特博士,請我為佢報紙寫封信,根據我嘅觀察,講我對南方有色人種牧師心智同道德確切狀況嘅意見。我寫咗信,畀出我認為嘅確切事實。畫出嘅圖畫相當黑——或者,因為我係黑人,應該話「白」?對一個離開奴隸制只有幾年、冇時間或機會培養稱職牧師隊伍嘅種族,不可能有其他情況。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 講到公眾情緒的變化,我記得塔斯基吉學校成立大約十年後,我有過一次永不忘記的經歷。當時普利茅斯教堂牧師和《展望》(當時叫《基督教聯合》)編輯萊曼·阿博特博士,請我為他報紙寫封信,根據我的觀察,講我對南方有色人種牧師心智和道德確切狀況的意見。我寫了信,給出我認為的確切事實。畫出的圖畫相當黑——或者,因為我是黑人,應該說「白」?對一個離開奴隸制只有幾年、沒時間或機會培養稱職牧師隊伍的種族,不可能有其他情況。

passages.original: What I said soon reached every Negro minister in the country, I think, and the letters of condemnation which I received from them were not few. I think that for a year after the publication of this article every association and every conference or religious body of any kind, of my race, that met, did not fail before adjourning to pass a resolution condemning me, or calling upon me to retract or modify what I had said. Many of these organizations went so far in their resolutions as to advise parents to cease sending their children to Tuskegee. One association even appointed a “missionary” whose duty it was to warn the people against sending their children to Tuskegee. This missionary had a son in the school, and I noticed that, whatever the “missionary” might have said or done with regard to others, he was careful not to take his son away from the institution. Many of the coloured papers, especially those that were the organs of religious bodies, joined in the general chorus of condemnation or demands for retraction.
passages.vernacular: 我所講嘅好快傳到全國每位黑人牧師,我收到嘅譴責信不少。我諗呢篇文章發表後一年,我種族每個召開會議嘅協會、會議或任何宗教團體,休會前都冇失責通過決議譴責我,或者要求我撤回或修改所講嘅。好多呢類組織嘅決議甚至建議家長停止送子女去塔斯基吉。一個協會甚至任命一位「傳教士」,職責係警告人民唔好送子女去塔斯基吉。呢位傳教士有個兒子喺學校,我留意到,無論「傳教士」對其他人講過或做過咩,佢小心唔將兒子從學院帶走。好多有色人種報紙,尤其係宗教團體嘅機關報,加入譴責或要求撤回嘅大合唱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我所說的很快傳到全國每位黑人牧師,我收到的譴責信不少。我想這篇文章發表後一年,我種族每個召開會議的協會、會議或任何宗教團體,休會前都沒失責通過決議譴責我,或要求我撤回或修改所說的。很多這類組織的決議甚至建議家長停止送子女去塔斯基吉。一個協會甚至任命一位「傳教士」,職責是警告人民不要送子女去塔斯基吉。這位傳教士有個兒子在學校,我留意到,無論「傳教士」對其他人說過或做過什麼,他小心不將兒子從學院帶走。很多有色人種報紙,尤其是宗教團體的機關報,加入譴責或要求撤回的大合唱。

passages.original: During the whole time of the excitement, and through all the criticism, I did not utter a word of explanation or retraction. I knew that I was right, and that time and the sober second thought of the people would vindicate me. It was not long before the bishops and other church leaders began to make careful investigation of the conditions of the ministry, and they found out that I was right. In fact, the oldest and most influential bishop in one branch of the Methodist Church said that my words were far too mild. Very soon public sentiment began making itself felt, in demanding a purifying of the ministry. While this is not yet complete by any means, I think I may say, without egotism, and I have been told by many of our most influential ministers, that my words had much to do with starting a demand for the placing of a higher type of men in the pulpit. I have had the satisfaction of having many who once condemned me thank me heartily for my frank words.
passages.vernacular: 整個激動期間,以及所有批評期間,我冇講一個字解釋或撤回。我知道我係啱嘅,時間同人民冷靜嘅再三思考會證明我。冇耐,主教同其他教會領袖開始仔細調查牧師隊伍嘅情況,發現我係啱嘅。事實上,衛理公會一個分支最年長、最有影響力嘅主教話,我嘅說話太溫和。好快,公眾情緒開始要求淨化牧師隊伍。雖然呢個仍然遠未完成,我諗我可以冇自負咁講,我亦被我哋好多最有影響力嘅牧師告知,我嘅說話對開始要求將更高類型嘅人放上講壇有好大關係。我得到咗滿足:好多曾經譴責我嘅人,衷心多謝我嘅坦率說話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整個激動期間,以及所有批評期間,我沒說一個字解釋或撤回。我知道我是對的,時間和人民冷靜的再三思考會證明我。沒多久,主教和其他教會領袖開始仔細調查牧師隊伍的情況,發現我是對的。事實上,衛理公會一個分支最年長、最有影響力的主教說,我的話太溫和。很快,公眾情緒開始要求淨化牧師隊伍。雖然這個仍然遠未完成,我想我可以沒自負地說,我也被我們很多最有影響力的牧師告知,我的話對開始要求將更高類型的人放上講壇有很大關係。我得到了滿足:很多曾經譴責我的人,衷心感謝我的坦率說話。

passages.original: The change of the attitude of the Negro ministry, so far as regards myself, is so complete that at the present time I have no warmer friends among any class than I have among the clergymen. The improvement in the character and life of the Negro ministers is one of the most gratifying evidences of the progress of the race. My experience with them, as well as other events in my life, convince me that the thing to do, when one feels sure that he has said or done the right thing, and is condemned, is to stand still and keep quiet. If he is right, time will show it.
passages.vernacular: 黑人牧師隊伍對我態度嘅改變咁徹底,以致而家我喺任何階層都冇比喺牧師當中更熱情嘅朋友。黑人牧師品格同生活嘅改善,係種族進步最令人滿意嘅證據之一。我同佢哋嘅經驗,以及我人生其他事件,令我相信,當一個人肯定自己講過或者做過正確嘅事而被譴責,要做嘅就係站穩保持安靜。如果佢係啱嘅,時間會證明。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 黑人牧師隊伍對我態度的改變那麼徹底,以致現在我在任何階層都沒比在牧師當中更熱情的朋友。黑人牧師品格和生活的改善,是種族進步最令人滿意的證據之一。我與他們的經驗,以及我人生其他事件,使我相信,當一個人肯定自己說過或做過正確的事而被譴責,要做的就是站穩保持安靜。如果他是對的,時間會證明。

passages.original: In the midst of the discussion which was going on concerning my Atlanta speech, I received the letter which I give below, from Dr. Gilman, the President of Johns Hopkins University, who had been made chairman of the judges of award in connection with the Atlanta Exposition:—

passages.original: President’s Office, September 30, 1895.
passages.vernacular: 校長辦公室,1895年9月30日。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 校長辦公室,1895年9月30日。

passages.original: Dear Mr. Washington: Would it be agreeable to you to be one of the Judges of Award in the Department of Education at Atlanta? If so, I shall be glad to place your name upon the list. A line by telegraph will be welcomed.
passages.vernacular: 親愛嘅華盛頓先生:你可唔可以接受做亞特蘭大教育部門嘅評審之一?如果可以,我會樂意將你嘅名放入名單。用電報回幾個字我就多謝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 親愛的華盛頓先生:你可不可以接受做亞特蘭大教育部門的評審之一?如果可以,我會樂意將你的名字放入名單。用電報回幾個字我就感謝。

passages.original: Yours very truly,
passages.vernacular: 你非常真誠嘅,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你非常真誠的,

passages.original: D.C. Gilman
passages.vernacular: D·C·吉爾曼
passages.vernacularMandarin: D·C·吉爾曼

passages.original: I think I was even more surprised to receive this invitation than I had been to receive the invitation to speak at the opening of the Exposition. It was to be a part of my duty, as one of the jurors, to pass not only upon the exhibits of the coloured schools, but also upon those of the white schools. I accepted the position, and spent a month in Atlanta in performance of the duties which it entailed. The board of jurors was a large one, containing in all of sixty members. It was about equally divided between Southern white people and Northern white people. Among them were college presidents, leading scientists and men of letters, and specialists in many subjects. When the group of jurors to which I was assigned met for organization, Mr. Thomas Nelson Page, who was one of the number, moved that I be made secretary of that division, and the motion was unanimously adopted. Nearly half of our division were Southern people. In performing my duties in the inspection of the exhibits of white schools I was in every case treated with respect, and at the close of our labours I parted from my associates with regret.
passages.vernacular: 我諗我收到呢個邀請,比收到邀請喺博覽會開幕演說更驚訝。作為評審團成員之一,我嘅職責一部分,係唔單止評審有色人種學校嘅展覽,亦評審白人學校嘅。我接受咗職位,喺亞特蘭大花咗一個月履行職責。評審團係一個大團體,總共六十位成員。大致平均分為南方白人同北方白人。其中有學院校長、主要科學家同文人,同多個科目嘅專家。我被分配嘅評審小組開會組織時,其中一人托馬斯·納爾遜·佩奇先生動議我成為該部門秘書,動議一致通過。我哋部門差唔多一半係南方人。我履行檢查白人學校展覽嘅職責時,每個情況下都被尊重對待,我哋工作結束時,我同同事分開時有些不捨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我收到這個邀請,比收到邀請在博覽會開幕演說更驚訝。作為評審團成員之一,我的職責一部分,是不僅評審有色人種學校的展覽,也評審白人學校的。我接受了職位,在亞特蘭大花了一個月履行職責。評審團是一個大團體,總共六十位成員。大致平均分為南方白人和北方白人。其中有學院校長、主要科學家和文人,和多個科目的專家。我被分配的評審小組開會組織時,其中一人托馬斯·納爾遜·佩奇先生動議我成為該部門秘書,動議一致通過。我們部門差不多一半是南方人。我履行檢查白人學校展覽的職責時,每個情況下都被尊重對待,我們工作結束時,我與同事分開時有些不捨。

passages.original: I am often asked to express myself more freely than I do upon the political condition and the political future of my race. These recollections of my experience in Atlanta give me the opportunity to do so briefly. My own belief is, although I have never before said so in so many words, that the time will come when the Negro in the South will be accorded all the political rights which his ability, character, and material possessions entitle him to. I think, though, that the opportunity to freely exercise such political rights will not come in any large degree through outside or artificial forcing, but will be accorded to the Negro by the Southern white people themselves, and that they will protect him in the exercise of those rights. Just as soon as the South gets over the old feeling that it is being forced by “foreigners,” or “aliens,” to do something which it does not want to do, I believe that the change in the direction that I have indicated is going to begin. In fact, there are indications that it is already beginning in a slight degree.
passages.vernacular: 我經常被要求,比我而家更自由咁表達關於我種族嘅政治狀況同政治未來。呢啲我喺亞特蘭大經歷嘅回憶,畀我機會簡短咁做。我自己嘅信念(雖然我之前從未咁直接講過)係,終有一日,南方嘅黑人會得到佢嘅能力、品格同物質財產所應得嘅所有政治權利。不過我諗,自由行使呢類政治權利嘅機會,唔會好大程度透過外來或人為強迫來到,而係由南方白人自己畀黑人,佢哋亦會保護佢行使呢啲權利。一旦南方擺脫被「外國人」或「外來者」強迫做佢唔想做嘅事嘅舊感覺,我相信我所指方向嘅改變就會開始。事實上,有跡象顯示,佢已經某程度開始。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我經常被要求,比我現在更自由地表達關於我種族的政治狀況和政治未來。這些我在亞特蘭大經歷的回憶,給我機會簡短地做。我自己的信念(雖然我之前從未這樣直接說過)是,終有一天,南方的黑人會得到他的能力、品格和物質財產所應得的所有政治權利。不過我想,自由行使這類政治權利的機會,不會很大程度透過外來或人為強迫來到,而是由南方白人自己給黑人,他們也會保護他行使這些權利。一旦南方擺脫被「外國人」或「外來者」強迫做它不想做的事的舊感覺,我相信我所指方向的改變就會開始。事實上,有跡象顯示,它已經某種程度開始。

passages.original: Let me illustrate my meaning. Suppose that some months before the opening of the Atlanta Exposition there had been a general demand from the press and public platform outside the South that a Negro be given a place on the opening programme, and that a Negro be placed upon the board of jurors of award. Would any such recognition of the race have taken place? I do not think so. The Atlanta officials went as far as they did because they felt it to be a pleasure, as well as a duty, to reward what they considered merit in the Negro race. Say what we will, there is something in human nature which we cannot blot out, which makes one man, in the end, recognize and reward merit in another, regardless of colour or race.
passages.vernacular: 讓我說明我嘅意思。假設亞特蘭大博覽會開幕前幾個月,南方以外嘅報界同公眾講台普遍要求,黑人喺開幕節目中有一個位置,黑人被放入評審團。會有任何對種族嘅此類認可嗎?我唔認為。亞特蘭大官員做到呢個地步,係因為佢哋覺得獎賞佢哋認為黑人種族嘅價值,係樂事同責任。無論我哋講咩,人性中有些嘢我哋無法抹去,令一個人最終認可同獎賞另一個人嘅價值,無論膚色或種族。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我說明我的意思。假設亞特蘭大博覽會開幕前幾個月,南方以外的報界和公眾講台普遍要求,黑人在開幕節目中有一個位置,黑人被放入評審團。會有任何對種族的此類認可嗎?我不認為。亞特蘭大官員做到這個地步,是因為他們覺得獎賞他們認為黑人種族的價值,是樂事和責任。無論我們說什麼,人性中有些東西我們無法抹去,使一個人最終認可和獎賞另一個人的價值,無論膚色或種族。

passages.original: I believe it is the duty of the Negro—as the greater part of the race is already doing—to deport himself modestly in regard to political claims, depending upon the slow but sure influences that proceed from the possession of property, intelligence, and high character for the full recognition of his political rights. I think that the according of the full exercise of political rights is going to be a matter of natural, slow growth, not an over-night, gourd-vine affair. I do not believe that the Negro should cease voting, for a man cannot learn the exercise of self-government by ceasing to vote, any more than a boy can learn to swim by keeping out of the water, but I do believe that in his voting he should more and more be influenced by those of intelligence and character who are his next-door neighbours.
passages.vernacular: 我相信黑人嘅責任(如大部分種族已經做到)係,就政治要求謙遜地舉止,倚靠擁有財產、智慧同高尚品格而來嘅緩慢但確實嘅影響,爭取其政治權利得到充分認可。我認為,充分行使政治權利將係自然緩慢成長嘅事,唔係一夜之間嘅瓜藤事。我唔相信黑人應該停止投票,因為一個人唔可以靠停止投票學會行使自治,正如男孩唔可以靠避開水學會游水,不過我相信,佢投票時應越來越受佢隔離鄰居中有智慧同品格嘅人影響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我相信黑人的責任(如大部分種族已經做到)是,就政治要求謙遜地舉止,倚靠擁有財產、智慧和高尚品格而來的緩慢但確實的影響,爭取其政治權利得到充分認可。我認為,充分行使政治權利將是自然緩慢成長的事,不是一夜之間的瓜藤事。我不相信黑人應該停止投票,因為一個人不可以靠停止投票學會行使自治,正如男孩不可以靠避開水學會游泳,不過我相信,他投票時應越來越受他隔壁鄰居中有智慧和品格的人影響。

passages.original: I know coloured men who, through the encouragement, help, and advice of Southern white people, have accumulated thousands of dollars’ worth of property, but who, at the same time, would never think of going to those same persons for advice concerning the casting of their ballots. This, it seems to me, is unwise and unreasonable, and should cease. In saying this I do not mean that the Negro should truckle, or not vote from principle, for the instant he ceases to vote from principle he loses the confidence and respect of the Southern white man even.
passages.vernacular: 我認識一些有色人種男人,憑南方白人嘅鼓勵、幫助同勸告,累積咗幾千美元財產,但同時,佢哋從來唔會諗到去搵同一批人,就投票徵求意見。依我睇,呢個係不明智不合理,應該停止。我咁講,唔係指黑人應該諂媚,或者唔出於原則投票,因為佢一唔出於原則投票,連南方白人都會失去對佢嘅信任同尊重。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我認識一些有色人種男人,憑南方白人的鼓勵、幫助和勸告,累積了幾千美元財產,但同時,他們從來不會想到去找同一批人,就投票徵求意見。依我看,這是不明智不合理,應該停止。我這樣說,不是指黑人應該諂媚,或不出於原則投票,因為他一不出於原則投票,連南方白人都會失去對他的信任和尊重。

passages.original: I do not believe that any state should make a law that permits an ignorant and poverty-stricken white man to vote, and prevents a black man in the same condition from voting. Such a law is not only unjust, but it will react, as all unjust laws do, in time; for the effect of such a law is to encourage the Negro to secure education and property, and at the same time it encourages the white man to remain in ignorance and poverty. I believe that in time, through the operation of intelligence and friendly race relations, all cheating at the ballot-box in the South will cease. It will become apparent that the white man who begins by cheating a Negro out of his ballot soon learns to cheat a white man out of his, and that the man who does this ends his career of dishonesty by the theft of property or by some equally serious crime. In my opinion, the time will come when the South will encourage all of its citizens to vote. It will see that it pays better, from every standpoint, to have healthy, vigorous life than to have that political stagnation which always results when one-half of the population has no share and no interest in the Government.
passages.vernacular: 我唔相信任何州應制定法律,容許無知貧窮嘅白人投票,而阻止處於同樣狀況嘅黑人投票。呢種法律唔單止不公,而且會好似所有不公法律一樣,最終產生反作用;因為呢種法律嘅效果,係鼓勵黑人得到教育同財產,同時鼓勵白人留喺無知同貧窮。我相信,隨時間,透過智慧同友好種族關係嘅運作,南方所有票箱舞弊都會停止。會變得明顯,由欺騙黑人選票開始嘅白人,好快學會欺騙白人嘅選票,而咁做嘅人以盜竊財產或其他同樣嚴重嘅罪行結束佢嘅不誠實生涯。依我意見,終有一日南方會鼓勵所有市民投票。佢會見到,從各個角度,有健康、有活力嘅生活,比人口一半冇份、冇興趣於政府時必然出現嘅政治停滯更有利。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不相信任何州應制定法律,容許無知貧窮的白人投票,而阻止處於同樣狀況的黑人投票。這種法律不僅不公,而且會像所有不公法律一樣,最終產生反作用;因為這種法律的效果,是鼓勵黑人得到教育和財產,同時鼓勵白人留在無知和貧窮。我相信,隨時間,透過智慧和友好種族關係的運作,南方所有票箱舞弊都會停止。會變得明顯,由欺騙黑人選票開始的白人,很快學會欺騙白人的選票,而這樣做的人以盜竊財產或其他同樣嚴重的罪行結束他的不誠實生涯。依我意見,終有一天南方會鼓勵所有市民投票。它會看到,從各個角度,有健康、有活力的生活,比人口一半沒份、沒興趣於政府時必然出現的政治停滯更有利。

passages.original: As a rule, I believe in universal, free suffrage, but I believe that in the South we are confronted with peculiar conditions that justify the protection of the ballot in many of the states, for a while at least, either by an education test, a property test, or by both combined; but whatever tests are required, they should be made to apply with equal and exact justice to both races.
passages.vernacular: 通常我相信普遍自由選舉權,不過我相信,南方面對特殊情況,足以證明喺好多州,至少一段時間,以教育測試、財產測試或兩者結合保護選票係合理,不過無論需要咩測試,都應該令佢哋以同等準確嘅公正適用於兩個種族。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 通常我相信普遍自由選舉權,不過我相信,南方面對特殊情況,足以證明在很多州,至少一段時間,以教育測試、財產測試或兩者結合保護選票是合理,不過無論需要什麼測試,都應該使它們以同等準確的公正適用於兩個種族。

chapters.title: The Secret of Success in Public Speaking 公眾演說的成功秘訣

passages.original: As to how my address at Atlanta was received by the audience in the Exposition building, I think I prefer to let Mr. James Creelman, the noted war correspondent, tell. Mr. Creelman was present, and telegraphed the following account to the New York World:—
passages.vernacular: 我嘅亞特蘭大演說喺博覽會大樓受到聽眾點樣歡迎,我想我寧願畀著名戰地記者詹姆斯·克里爾曼先生講。克里爾曼先生在場,並電報以下記述畀《紐約世界報》:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的亞特蘭大演說在博覽會大樓受到聽眾怎樣歡迎,我想我寧願讓著名戰地記者詹姆斯·克里爾曼先生講。克里爾曼先生在場,並電報以下記述給《紐約世界報》:

passages.original: Atlanta, September 18.
passages.vernacular: 亞特蘭大,9月18日。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 亞特蘭大,9月18日。

passages.original: While President Cleveland was waiting at Gray Gables to-day, to send the electric spark that started the machinery of the Atlanta Exposition, a Negro Moses stood before a great audience of white people and delivered an oration that marks a new epoch in the history of the South; and a body of Negro troops marched in a procession with the citizen soldiery of Georgia and Louisiana. The whole city is thrilling to-night with a realization of the extraordinary significance of these two unprecedented events. Nothing has happened since Henry Grady’s immortal speech before the New England society in New York that indicates so profoundly the spirit of the New South, except, perhaps, the opening of the Exposition itself.
passages.vernacular: 克利夫蘭總統今日喺灰色山牆等待,發出啟動亞特蘭大博覽會機器嘅電火花時,一位黑人摩西企喺一大批白人聽眾面前,發表一篇標誌南方歷史新紀元嘅演說;而一隊黑人軍隊同佐治亞同路易斯安那嘅公民士兵一齊喺遊行中行軍。整個城市今晚因為意識到呢兩件史無前例事件嘅非凡意義而激動。自從亨利·格雷迪喺紐約新英格蘭協會嘅不朽演說以來,冇任何事比呢件事更深刻咁顯示新南方嘅精神,除咗也許博覽會開幕本身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 克利夫蘭總統今日在灰色山牆等待,發出啟動亞特蘭大博覽會機器的電火花時,一位黑人摩西站在一大批白人聽眾面前,發表一篇標誌南方歷史新紀元的演說;而一隊黑人軍隊和喬治亞和路易斯安那的公民士兵一起在遊行中行軍。整個城市今晚因為意識到這兩件史無前例事件的非凡意義而激動。自從亨利·格雷迪在紐約新英格蘭協會的不朽演說以來,沒任何事比這件事更深刻地顯示新南方的精神,除了也許博覽會開幕本身。

passages.original: When Professor Booker T. Washington, Principal of an industrial school for coloured people in Tuskegee, Ala. stood on the platform of the Auditorium, with the sun shining over the heads of his auditors into his eyes, and with his whole face lit up with the fire of prophecy, Clark Howell, the successor of Henry Grady, said to me, “That man’s speech is the beginning of a moral revolution in America.”
passages.vernacular: 當阿拉巴馬塔斯基吉一間有色人種工業學校校長布克·T·華盛頓教授企喺禮堂講台上,陽光從聽眾頭頂照入佢眼睛,佢整個面孔被預言之火照亮,亨利·格雷迪嘅繼任者克拉克·豪厄爾對我講:「嗰個人嘅演說係美國一場道德革命嘅開始。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當阿拉巴馬塔斯基吉一間有色人種工業學校校長布克·T·華盛頓教授站在禮堂講台上,陽光從聽眾頭頂照入他眼睛,他整個臉孔被預言之火照亮,亨利·格雷迪的繼任者克拉克·豪厄爾對我說:「那個人的演說是美國一場道德革命的開始。」

passages.original: It is the first time that a Negro has made a speech in the South on any important occasion before an audience composed of white men and women. It electrified the audience, and the response was as if it had come from the throat of a whirlwind.
passages.vernacular: 係黑人第一次喺南方任何重要場合,向白人男女聽眾發表演說。佢令聽眾觸電,回應好似來自旋風嘅喉嚨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是黑人第一次在南方任何重要場合,向白人男女聽眾發表演說。它使聽眾觸電,回應好像來自旋風的喉嚨。

passages.original: Mrs. Thompson had hardly taken her seat when all eyes were turned on a tall tawny Negro sitting in the front row of the platform. It was Professor Booker T. Washington, President of the Tuskegee (Alabama) Normal and Industrial Institute, who must rank from this time forth as the foremost man of his race in America. Gilmore’s Band played the “Star-Spangled Banner,” and the audience cheered. The tune changed to “Dixie” and the audience roared with shrill “hi-yis.” Again the music changed, this time to “Yankee Doodle,” and the clamour lessened.
passages.vernacular: 湯普森夫人剛坐低,所有眼睛就轉向坐喺講台前排一個高大黃褐色皮膚嘅黑人。係阿拉巴馬塔斯基吉師範及工業學院校長布克·T·華盛頓教授,從此刻起必須被視為美國佢種族嘅首要人物。吉爾莫樂隊奏《星條旗》,聽眾歡呼。曲調轉做《迪克西》,聽眾以尖銳嘅「嗨呀」大叫。音樂再變,今次係《洋基歌》,喧鬧減弱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯普森夫人剛坐下,所有眼睛就轉向坐在講台前排一個高大黃褐色皮膚的黑人。是阿拉巴馬塔斯基吉師範及工業學院校長布克·T·華盛頓教授,從此刻起必須被視為美國他種族的首要人物。吉爾莫樂隊奏《星條旗》,聽眾歡呼。曲調轉為《迪克西》,聽眾以尖銳的「嗨呀」大叫。音樂再變,這次是《洋基歌》,喧鬧減弱。

passages.original: All this time the eyes of the thousands present looked straight at the Negro orator. A strange thing was to happen. A black man was to speak for his people, with none to interrupt him. As Professor Washington strode to the edge of the stage, the low, descending sun shot fiery rays through the windows into his face. A great shout greeted him. He turned his head to avoid the blinding light, and moved about the platform for relief. Then he turned his wonderful countenance to the sun without a blink of the eyelids, and began to talk.
passages.vernacular: 呢段時間,在場幾千人嘅眼睛直接望住黑人演說家。一件奇怪嘅事即將發生。一個黑人將為佢嘅人民發言,冇人打斷佢。華盛頓教授大步走到舞台邊緣,低垂下沉嘅太陽透過窗射出火般嘅光線照入佢面。一陣大喊歡迎佢。佢轉頭避開刺眼嘅光,喺講台上走動求舒緩。然後佢將佢非凡嘅面容轉向太陽,眼睛眨都冇眨,開始講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這段時間,在場幾千人的眼睛直接望著黑人演說家。一件奇怪的事即將發生。一個黑人將為他的人民發言,沒人打斷他。華盛頓教授大步走到舞台邊緣,低垂下沉的太陽透過窗射出火般的光線照入他臉。一陣大喊歡迎他。他轉頭避開刺眼的光,在講台上走動求舒緩。然後他將他非凡的面容轉向太陽,眼睛眨都沒眨,開始說。

passages.original: There was a remarkable figure; tall, bony, straight as a Sioux chief, high forehead, straight nose, heavy jaws, and strong, determined mouth, with big white teeth, piercing eyes, and a commanding manner. The sinews stood out on his bronzed neck, and his muscular right arm swung high in the air, with a lead-pencil grasped in the clinched brown fist. His big feet were planted squarely, with the heels together and the toes turned out. His voice range out clear and true, and he paused impressively as he made each point. Within ten minutes the multitude was in an uproar of enthusiasm—handkerchiefs were waved, canes were flourished, hats were tossed in the air. The fairest women of Georgia stood up and cheered. It was as if the orator had bewitched them.
passages.vernacular: 真係一個非凡嘅人物;高、瘦、似蘇族酋長般挺直,高額、直鼻、厚顎,強而堅定嘅嘴,大白牙齒,銳利嘅眼睛,有威嚴嘅舉止。青銅色頸項上嘅筋腱凸起,佢強壯嘅右臂高高揮向空中,握緊嘅棕色拳頭拿住一支鉛筆。佢嘅大腳平穩地放住,腳跟靠埋、腳趾向外。佢嘅聲音清晰真實咁響起,每講一點就令人印象深刻地停頓。十分鐘內,人群熱情激昂——手帕揮動,手杖舞動,帽拋向空中。佐治亞最美麗嘅女士站起歡呼。好似演說家迷住咗佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真是一個非凡的人物;高、瘦、像蘇族酋長般挺直,高額、直鼻、厚顎,強而堅定的嘴,大白牙齒,銳利的眼睛,有威嚴的舉止。青銅色頸項上的筋腱凸起,他強壯的右臂高高揮向空中,握緊的棕色拳頭拿著一支鉛筆。他的大腳平穩地放著,腳跟靠在一起、腳趾向外。他的聲音清晰真實地響起,每說一點就令人印象深刻地停頓。十分鐘內,人群熱情激昂——手帕揮動,手杖舞動,帽子拋向空中。喬治亞最美麗的女士站起歡呼。好像演說家迷住了她們。

passages.original: And when he held his dusky hand high above his head, with the fingers stretched wide apart, and said to the white people of the South on behalf of his race, “In all things that are purely social we can be as separate as the fingers, yet one as the hand in all things essential to mutual progress,” the great wave of sound dashed itself against the walls, and the whole audience was on its feet in a delirium of applause, and I thought at that moment of the night when Henry Grady stood among the curling wreaths of tobacco-smoke in Delmonico’s banquet-hall and said, “I am a Cavalier among Roundheads.”
passages.vernacular: 當佢將深色嘅手高舉過頭,手指大大張開,代表佢嘅種族對南方白人講:「喺所有純社交嘅事情上,我哋可以似手指咁分開,不過喺所有互相進步所必需嘅事情上,似手掌咁係一體」,巨大嘅聲浪衝擊牆壁,全場聽眾站起,瘋狂喝彩,我當時想起亨利·格雷迪企喺德爾莫尼科宴會廳盤旋嘅煙圈之中,講:「我係圓顱黨人當中嘅騎士。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當他將深色的手高舉過頭,手指大大張開,代表他的種族對南方白人說:「在所有純社交的事情上,我們可以像手指那樣分開,不過在所有互相進步所必需的事情上,像手掌那樣是一體」,巨大的聲浪衝擊牆壁,全場聽眾站起,瘋狂喝彩,我當時想起亨利·格雷迪站在德爾莫尼科宴會廳盤旋的煙圈之中,說:「我是圓顱黨人當中的騎士。」

passages.original: I have heard the great orators of many countries, but not even Gladstone himself could have pleased a cause with most consummate power than did this angular Negro, standing in a nimbus of sunshine, surrounded by the men who once fought to keep his race in bondage. The roar might swell ever so high, but the expression of his earnest face never changed.
passages.vernacular: 我聽過好多國家嘅偉大演說家,不過連格萊斯頓自己都無法以比呢個棱角分明嘅黑人更完美嘅力量為一個事業辯護,佢企喺陽光光環中,被曾經為保持佢種族奴役而戰嘅人包圍。吼聲無論幾高,佢認真嘅面孔嘅表情從未改變。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽過很多國家的偉大演說家,不過連格萊斯頓自己都無法以比這個棱角分明的黑人更完美的力量為一個事業辯護,他站在陽光光環中,被曾經為保持他種族奴役而戰的人包圍。吼聲無論多高,他認真的臉孔的表情從未改變。

passages.original: A ragged, ebony giant, squatted on the floor in one of the aisles, watched the orator with burning eyes and tremulous face until the supreme burst of applause came, and then the tears ran down his face. Most of the Negroes in the audience were crying, perhaps without knowing just why.
passages.vernacular: 一個衣衫襤褸嘅烏木巨人,蹲喺走道其中一條地板,用燃燒嘅眼睛同顫抖嘅面孔望住演說家,直到最高潮嘅掌聲來到,然後眼淚沿住佢嘅面流落。聽眾中大部分黑人都喺喊,也許唔知點解。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個衣衫襤褸的烏木巨人,蹲在走道其中一條地板,用燃燒的眼睛和顫抖的臉孔望著演說家,直到最高潮的掌聲來到,然後眼淚沿著他的臉流下。聽眾中大部分黑人都在哭,也許不知為什麼。

passages.original: At the close of the speech Governor Bullock rushed across the stage and seized the orator’s hand. Another shout greeted this demonstration, and for a few minutes the two men stood facing each other, hand in hand.
passages.vernacular: 演說結束時,布洛克州長衝過舞台,握住演說家嘅手。另一陣歡呼迎接呢個示範,有幾分鐘兩個人面對面,手拉手企住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 演說結束時,布洛克州長衝過舞台,握住演說家的手。另一陣歡呼迎接這個示範,有幾分鐘兩個人面對面,手拉手站著。

passages.original: So far as I could spare the time from the immediate work at Tuskegee, after my Atlanta address, I accepted some of the invitations to speak in public which came to me, especially those that would take me into territory where I thought it would pay to plead the cause of my race, but I always did this with the understanding that I was to be free to talk about my life-work and the needs of my people. I also had it understood that I was not to speak in the capacity of a professional lecturer, or for mere commercial gain.
passages.vernacular: 我亞特蘭大演說之後,只要我可以從塔斯基吉當前工作騰出時間,我接受咗一些公眾演講邀請,尤其係會帶我去我認為值得為我種族申辯嘅地區,不過我總係以我可以自由講我嘅終身事業同我人民嘅需要為諒解。我亦令人明白,我唔會以專業演講者身份,或者單純為商業利益演講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我亞特蘭大演說之後,只要我可以從塔斯基吉當前工作騰出時間,我接受了一些公眾演講邀請,尤其是會帶我去我認為值得為我種族申辯的地區,不過我總是以我可以自由講我的終身事業和我人民的需要為諒解。我也使人明白,我不會以專業演講者身分,或單純為商業利益演講。

passages.original: In my efforts on the public platform I never have been able to understand why people come to hear me speak. This question I never can rid myself of. Time and time again, as I have stood in the street in front of a building and have seen men and women passing in large numbers into the audience room where I was to speak, I have felt ashamed that I should be the cause of people—as it seemed to me—wasting a valuable hour of their time. Some years ago I was to deliver an address before a literary society in Madison, Wis. An hour before the time set for me to speak, a fierce snow-storm began, and continued for several hours. I made up my mind that there would be no audience, and that I should not have to speak, but, as a matter of duty, I went to the church, and found it packed with people. The surprise gave me a shock that I did not recover from during the whole evening.
passages.vernacular: 我喺公眾講台上嘅努力,我從來唔明白點解人們來聽我演講。呢個問題我永遠無法擺脫。一次又一次,我企喺建築前面街道,見到男女大批大批咁入我要演講嘅聽眾廳,我感到羞愧,我居然成為令人(依我睇)浪費寶貴一個鐘嘅原因。幾年前,我要喺威斯康星麥迪遜一個文學會發表演說。我定咗演講時間前一個鐘,一場猛烈暴風雪開始,持續幾個鐘。我決定唔會有聽眾,我唔使演講,不過出於責任,我去咗教堂,發現擠滿人。呢個驚訝令我震驚,成晚都冇恢復。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在公眾講台上的努力,我從來不明白為什麼人們來聽我演講。這個問題我永遠無法擺脫。一次又一次,我站在建築前面街道,看到男女大批大批地進我要演講的聽眾廳,我感到羞愧,我居然成為使人(依我看)浪費寶貴一個小時的原因。幾年前,我要在威斯康星麥迪遜一個文學會發表演說。我定了演講時間前一個小時,一場猛烈暴風雪開始,持續幾個小時。我決定不會有聽眾,我不用演講,不過出於責任,我去了教堂,發現擠滿人。這個驚訝使我震驚,整晚都沒恢復。

passages.original: People often ask me if I feel nervous before speaking, or else they suggest that, since I speak often, they suppose that I get used to it. In answer to this question I have to say that I always suffer intensely from nervousness before speaking. More than once, just before I was to make an important address, this nervous strain has been so great that I have resolved never again to speak in public. I not only feel nervous before speaking, but after I have finished I usually feel a sense of regret, because it seems to me as if I had left out of my address the main thing and the best thing that I had meant to say.
passages.vernacular: 人們經常問我演講前緊唔緊張,或者建議,既然我經常演講,佢哋估我習慣咗。回答呢個問題,我要講,我演講前總係極度緊張。不止一次,喺我要發表重要演說前,呢種神經緊張咁大,我決心永不再公開演講。我唔單止演講前緊張,完咗之後我通常感到後悔,因為似乎我遺漏咗我本來想講嘅最主要最好嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人們經常問我演講前緊不緊張,或建議,既然我經常演講,他們猜我習慣了。回答這個問題,我要說,我演講前總是極度緊張。不止一次,在我要發表重要演說前,這種神經緊張那麼大,我決心永不再公開演講。我不僅演講前緊張,完了之後我通常感到後悔,因為似乎我遺漏了我本來想說的最主要最好的東西。

passages.original: There is a great compensation, though, for this preliminary nervous suffering, that comes to me after I have been speaking for about ten minutes, and have come to feel that I have really mastered my audience, and that we have gotten into full and complete sympathy with each other. It seems to me that there is rarely such a combination of mental and physical delight in any effort as that which comes to a public speaker when he feels that he has a great audience completely within his control. There is a thread of sympathy and oneness that connects a public speaker with his audience, that is just as strong as though it was something tangible and visible. If in an audience of a thousand people there is one person who is not in sympathy with my views, or is inclined to be doubtful, cold, or critical, I can pick him out. When I have found him I usually go straight at him, and it is a great satisfaction to watch the process of his thawing out. I find that the most effective medicine for such individuals is administered at first in the form of a story, although I never tell an anecdote simply for the sake of telling one. That kind of thing, I think, is empty and hollow, and an audience soon finds it out.
passages.vernacular: 不過,呢種預先神經痛苦有一個大補償,就係我講咗大約十分鐘、覺得我真正掌握咗聽眾、我哋已經完全互相同情之後。我覺得,好少努力有公眾演說者覺得佢完全控制一大批聽眾時嗰種心智同身體喜悅嘅結合。連接公眾演說者同佢聽眾嘅同情同一體嘅線,同有形可見嘅嘢一樣強。如果喺一千人嘅聽眾中有一個唔同情我觀點、傾向懷疑、冷淡或批評嘅人,我可以揀出佢。搵到佢之後,我通常直接對住佢,睇住佢解凍嘅過程係極大滿足。我發現對呢類人最有效嘅藥,起初係以故事形式給予,雖然我從來唔會僅僅為咗講軼事而講。我諗呢種事空洞虛假,聽眾好快發現。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,這種預先神經痛苦有一個大補償,就是我講了大約十分鐘、覺得我真正掌握了聽眾、我們已經完全互相同情之後。我覺得,很少努力有公眾演說者覺得他完全控制一大批聽眾時那種心智和身體喜悅的結合。連接公眾演說者和他聽眾的同情和一體的線,與有形可見的東西一樣強。如果在一千人的聽眾中有一個不同情我觀點、傾向懷疑、冷淡或批評的人,我可以挑出他。找到他之後,我通常直接對著他,看著他解凍的過程是極大滿足。我發現對這類人最有效的藥,起初是以故事形式給予,雖然我從來不會僅僅為了講軼事而講。我想這種事空洞虛假,聽眾很快發現。

passages.original: I believe that one always does himself and his audience an injustice when he speaks merely for the sake of speaking. I do not believe that one should speak unless, deep down in his heart, he feels convinced that he has a message to deliver. When one feels, from the bottom of his feet to the top of his head, that he has something to say that is going to help some individual or some cause, then let him say it; and in delivering his message I do not believe that many of the artificial rules of elocution can, under such circumstances, help him very much. Although there are certain things, such as pauses, breathing, and pitch of voice, that are very important, none of these can take the place of soul in an address. When I have an address to deliver, I like to forget all about the rules for the proper use of the English language, and all about rhetoric and that sort of thing, and I like to make the audience forget all about these things, too.
passages.vernacular: 我相信一個人僅僅為咗講而講,總係對自己同聽眾不公。我唔相信一個人應該講,除非佢心裡面深深確信自己有信息要傳達。當一個人從腳底到頭頂覺得佢有嘢要講,會幫助某個人或某個事業,就讓佢講;傳達信息時,我唔相信許多人為嘅演說規則喺咁嘅情況下可以幫到佢好多。雖然有些嘢,例如停頓、呼吸同聲音音高,係非常重要,但冇一樣可以取代演說中嘅靈魂。當我有演說要發表,我鍾意忘記所有關於正確使用英語嘅規則,同所有修辭同類似嘅嘢,我亦鍾意令聽眾忘記所有呢啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我相信一個人僅僅為了講而講,總是對自己和聽眾不公。我不相信一個人應該講,除非他心裡深深確信自己有信息要傳達。當一個人從腳底到頭頂覺得他有話要說,會幫助某個人或某個事業,就讓他說;傳達信息時,我不相信許多人為的演說規則在這樣的情況下可以幫到他很多。雖然有些東西,例如停頓、呼吸和聲音音高,是非常重要,但沒一樣可以取代演說中的靈魂。當我有演說要發表,我喜歡忘記所有關於正確使用英語的規則,和所有修辭和類似的東西,我也喜歡使聽眾忘記所有這些。

passages.original: Nothing tends to throw me off my balance so quickly, when I am speaking, as to have some one leave the room. To prevent this, I make up my mind, as a rule, that I will try to make my address so interesting, will try to state so many interesting facts one after another, that no one can leave. The average audience, I have come to believe, wants facts rather than generalities or sermonizing. Most people, I think, are able to draw proper conclusions if they are given the facts in an interesting form on which to base them.
passages.vernacular: 我演講時,冇咩比有人離開房間更快令我失去平衡。為咗防止,我通常決心嘗試令我嘅演說咁有趣,嘗試一個接一個咁陳述咁多有趣事實,令冇人可以離開。我開始相信,普通聽眾想要事實多過籠統或說教。我諗大部分人,如果畀佢哋有趣形式嘅事實作為基礎,都有能力得出正確結論。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我演講時,沒什麼比有人離開房間更快使我失去平衡。為了防止,我通常決心嘗試使我的演說那麼有趣,嘗試一個接一個地陳述那麼多有趣事實,使沒人可以離開。我開始相信,普通聽眾想要事實多過籠統或說教。我想大部分人,如果給他們有趣形式的事實作為基礎,都有能力得出正確結論。

passages.original: As to the kind of audience that I like best to talk to, I would put at the top of the list an organization of strong, wide-awake, business men, such, for example, as is found in Boston, New York, Chicago, and Buffalo. I have found no other audience so quick to see a point, and so responsive. Within the last few years I have had the privilege of speaking before most of the leading organizations of this kind in the large cities of the United States. The best time to get hold of an organization of business men is after a good dinner, although I think that one of the worst instruments of torture that was ever invented is the custom which makes it necessary for a speaker to sit through a fourteen-course dinner, every minute of the time feeling sure that his speech is going to prove a dismal failure and disappointment.
passages.vernacular: 至於我最鍾意向邊類聽眾講話,我會將一個強壯、清醒嘅商人組織放喺榜首,例如波士頓、紐約、芝加哥同水牛城嘅。我發現冇其他聽眾咁快睇到重點,咁有回應。過去幾年,我有幸向美國大城市大部分主要此類組織演講。爭取商人組織嘅最佳時間係一頓好晚餐之後,雖然我認為被發明嘅最糟糕刑具之一,就係令演講者必須坐完十四道菜晚餐嘅習慣,每分鐘都肯定自己嘅演說會證明係悲慘失敗同令人失望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於我最喜歡向哪類聽眾說話,我會將一個強壯、清醒的商人組織放在榜首,例如波士頓、紐約、芝加哥和水牛城的。我發現沒其他聽眾那麼快看到重點,那麼有回應。過去幾年,我有幸向美國大城市大部分主要此類組織演講。爭取商人組織的最佳時間是一頓好晚餐之後,雖然我認為被發明的最糟糕刑具之一,就是使演講者必須坐完十四道菜晚餐的習慣,每分鐘都肯定自己的演說會證明是悲慘失敗和令人失望。

passages.original: I rarely take part in one of these long dinners that I do not wish that I could put myself back in the little cabin where I was a slave boy, and again go through the experience there—one that I shall never forget—of getting molasses to eat once a week from the “big house.” Our usual diet on the plantation was corn bread and pork, but on Sunday morning my mother was permitted to bring down a little molasses from the “big house” for her three children, and when it was received how I did wish that every day was Sunday! I would get my tin plate and hold it up for the sweet morsel, but I would always shut my eyes while the molasses was being poured out into the plate, with the hope that when I opened them I would be surprised to see how much I had got. When I opened my eyes I would tip the plate in one direction and another, so as to make the molasses spread all over it, in the full belief that there would be more of it and that it would last longer if spread out in this way. So strong are my childish impressions of those Sunday morning feasts that it would be pretty hard for any one to convince me that there is not more molasses on a plate when it is spread all over the plate than when it occupies a little corner—if there is a corner in a plate. At any rate, I have never believed in “cornering” syrup. My share of the syrup was usually about two tablespoonfuls, and those two spoonfuls of molasses were much more enjoyable to me than is a fourteen-course dinner after which I am to speak.
passages.vernacular: 我好少參加其中一個咁長嘅晚餐而唔希望可以將自己放返喺我做奴隸男孩嘅細小屋,再經歷嗰度我永不忘記嘅經驗——每星期一次從「大屋」得到糖蜜食。我哋喺種植園通常嘅飲食係玉米麵包同豬肉,不過星期日朝早,我媽媽獲准從「大屋」帶少少糖蜜畀佢三個子女,收到時我幾希望每日都係星期日!我會拎我嘅錫碟,舉起等甜食,不過糖蜜倒入碟時我總係閉上眼睛,希望打開時會驚訝地見到我得到幾多。打開眼睛時,我會向一個方向、另一個方向傾斜碟,令糖蜜散佈整個碟,完全相信咁散開會有更多、更耐食。我對嗰啲星期日朝早盛宴嘅童年印象咁強烈,以致好難有人說服我,糖蜜散開喺整個碟,唔比佔一個細角落(如果碟有角落)更多。無論如何,我從來唔相信「壟斷」糖漿。我嘅糖漿份額通常大約兩湯匙,呢兩匙糖蜜,對我嚟講比我之後要演講嘅十四道菜晚餐更令人享受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很少參加其中一個那麼長的晚餐而不希望可以將自己放回在我做奴隸男孩的小屋,再經歷那裡我永不忘記的經驗——每星期一次從「大屋」得到糖蜜吃。我們在種植園通常的飲食是玉米麵包和豬肉,不過星期日早上,我母親獲准從「大屋」帶一點糖蜜給她三個子女,收到時我多希望每天都是星期日!我會拿我的錫碟,舉起等甜食,不過糖蜜倒入碟時我總是閉上眼睛,希望打開時會驚訝地看到我得到多少。打開眼睛時,我會向一個方向、另一個方向傾斜碟,使糖蜜散佈整個碟,完全相信這樣散開會有更多、更久吃。我對那些星期日早上盛宴的童年印象那麼強烈,以致很難有人說服我,糖蜜散開在整個碟,不比佔一個小角落(如果碟有角落)更多。無論如何,我從來不相信「壟斷」糖漿。我的糖漿份額通常大約兩湯匙,這兩匙糖蜜,對我來說比我之後要演講的十四道菜晚餐更令人享受。

passages.original: Next to a company of business men, I prefer to speak to an audience of Southern people, of either race, together or taken separately. Their enthusiasm and responsiveness are a constant delight. The “amens” and “dat’s de truf” that come spontaneously from the coloured individuals are calculated to spur any speaker on to his best efforts. I think that next in order of preference I would place a college audience. It has been my privilege to deliver addresses at many of our leading colleges including Harvard, Yale, Williams, Amherst, Fisk University, the University of Pennsylvania, Wellesley, the University of Michigan, Trinity College in North Carolina, and many others.
passages.vernacular: 僅次於商人公司,我鍾意向南方人聽眾(無論兩個種族一齊或分開)演講。佢哋嘅熱情同回應不斷令人喜悅。有色人種自發嘅「阿們」同「嗰個係真理」,足以鞭策任何演說者盡最大努力。我諗我順序嘅偏好,下一個會係學院聽眾。我有幸向我哋好多主要學院演講,包括哈佛、耶魯、威廉姆斯、阿默斯特、菲斯克大學、賓夕法尼亞大學、衛斯理、密歇根大學、北卡羅來納三一學院,同好多其他。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 僅次於商人公司,我喜歡向南方人聽眾(無論兩個種族一起或分開)演講。他們的熱情和回應不斷令人喜悅。有色人種自發的「阿們」和「那是真理」,足以鞭策任何演說者盡最大努力。我想我順序的偏好,下一個會是學院聽眾。我有幸向我們很多主要學院演講,包括哈佛、耶魯、威廉斯、阿默斯特、菲斯克大學、賓夕法尼亞大學、衛斯理、密歇根大學、北卡羅來納三一學院,和很多其他。

passages.original: It has been a matter of deep interest to me to note the number of people who have come to shake hands with me after an address, who say that this is the first time they have ever called a Negro “Mister.”
passages.vernacular: 我深感興趣地留意到,演說後有好多人來同我握手,話呢係佢哋第一次稱一個黑人做「先生」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我深感興趣地留意到,演說後有很多人來與我握手,說這是他們第一次稱一個黑人做「先生」。

passages.original: When speaking directly in the interests of the Tuskegee Institute, I usually arrange, some time in advance, a series of meetings in important centres. This takes me before churches, Sunday-schools, Christian Endeavour Societies, and men’s and women’s clubs. When doing this I sometimes speak before as many as four organizations in a single day.
passages.vernacular: 直接為塔斯基吉學院利益演講時,我通常提前一段時間,喺重要中心安排一系列聚會。呢個帶我到教堂、主日學、基督徒奮進會,同男士同女士俱樂部。咁做時,我有時一日向多達四個組織演講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 直接為塔斯基吉學院利益演講時,我通常提前一段時間,在重要中心安排一系列聚會。這帶我到教堂、主日學、基督徒奮進會,和男士和女士俱樂部。這樣做時,我有時一天向多達四個組織演講。

passages.original: Three years ago, at the suggestion of Mr. Morris K. Jessup, of New York, and Dr. J.L.M. Curry, the general agent of the fund, the trustees of the John F. Slater Fund voted a sum of money to be used in paying the expenses of Mrs. Washington and myself while holding a series of meetings among the coloured people in the large centres of Negro population, especially in the large cities of the ex-slaveholding states. Each year during the last three years we have devoted some weeks to this work. The plan that we have followed has been for me to speak in the morning to the ministers, teachers, and professional men. In the afternoon Mrs. Washington would speak to the women alone, and in the evening I spoke to a large mass-meeting. In almost every case the meetings have been attended not only by the coloured people in large numbers, but by the white people. In Chattanooga, Tenn., for example, there was present at the mass-meeting an audience of not less than three thousand persons, and I was informed that eight hundred of these were white. I have done no work that I really enjoyed more than this, or that I think has accomplished more good.
passages.vernacular: 三年前,應紐約莫里斯·K·傑瑟普先生同基金總代理人J·L·M·柯里博士嘅建議,約翰·F·斯萊特基金受託人投票撥一筆款,用於支付華盛頓太太同我喺黑人人口大中心(尤其係前奴隸主各州大城市)有色人種當中舉行一系列聚會嘅開支。過去三年每年,我哋花咗幾個星期做呢項工作。我哋遵循嘅計劃係,我朝早向牧師、老師同專業人士演講。下午華盛頓太太單獨向婦女演講,晚上我向大型群眾大會演講。幾乎每個情況下,出席聚會嘅唔單止有大批有色人種,亦有白人。例如田納西查塔努加嘅群眾大會,出席聽眾不少於三千人,我被告知其中八百係白人。我冇做過比呢個更享受、或者我認為成就更多好處嘅工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三年前,應紐約莫里斯·K·傑瑟普先生和基金總代理人J·L·M·柯里博士的建議,約翰·F·斯萊特基金受託人投票撥一筆款,用於支付華盛頓太太和我在黑人人口大中心(尤其是前奴隸主各州大城市)有色人種當中舉行一系列聚會的開支。過去三年每年,我們花了幾個星期做這項工作。我們遵循的計劃是,我早上向牧師、老師和專業人士演講。下午華盛頓太太單獨向婦女演講,晚上我向大型群眾大會演講。幾乎每個情況下,出席聚會的不僅有大批有色人種,也有白人。例如田納西查塔努加的群眾大會,出席聽眾不少於三千人,我被告知其中八百是白人。我沒做過比這個更享受、或我認為成就更多好處的工作。

passages.original: These meetings have given Mrs. Washington and myself an opportunity to get first-hand, accurate information as to the real condition of the race, by seeing the people in their homes, their churches, their Sunday-schools, and their places of work, as well as in the prisons and dens of crime. These meetings also gave us an opportunity to see the relations that exist between the races. I never feel so hopeful about the race as I do after being engaged in a series of these meetings. I know that on such occasions there is much that comes to the surface that is superficial and deceptive, but I have had experience enough not to be deceived by mere signs and fleeting enthusiasms. I have taken pains to go to the bottom of things and get facts, in a cold, business-like manner.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲聚會畀華盛頓太太同我機會,透過見到人民喺佢哋嘅家、教堂、主日學同工作地方,以及監獄同罪惡窩,得到關於種族真實狀況嘅第一手準確資料。呢啲聚會亦畀我哋機會見到兩個種族之間存在嘅關係。我從未對種族感到咁有希望,似參加一系列呢啲聚會之後。我知道喺呢類場合有好多膚淺同欺騙性嘅嘢浮現,不過我有足夠經驗唔被單純跡象同短暫熱情欺騙。我費心深入事物底層,以冷靜、商業嘅方式搵事實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些聚會給華盛頓太太和我機會,透過看到人民在他們的家、教堂、主日學和工作地方,以及監獄和罪惡窩,得到關於種族真實狀況的第一手準確資料。這些聚會也給我們機會看到兩個種族之間存在的關係。我從未對種族感到那麼有希望,像參加一系列這些聚會之後。我知道在這類場合有很多膚淺和欺騙性的東西浮現,不過我有足夠經驗不被單純跡象和短暫熱情欺騙。我費心深入事物底層,以冷靜、商業的方式找事實。

passages.original: I have seen the statement made lately, by one who claims to know what he is talking about, that, taking the whole Negro race into account, ninety per cent of the Negro women are not virtuous. There never was a baser falsehood uttered concerning a race, or a statement made that was less capable of being proved by actual facts.
passages.vernacular: 我最近見到一個聲稱知道自己講咩嘅人作出嘅說法:考慮整個黑人種族,百分之九十嘅黑人女性唔貞潔。從未有過比咁卑鄙嘅關於一個種族嘅謊言,或者更唔能被實際事實證明嘅說法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我最近看到一個聲稱知道自己說什麼的人作出的說法:考慮整個黑人種族,百分之九十的黑人女性不貞潔。從未有過比這更卑鄙的關於一個種族的謊言,或更不能被實際事實證明的說法。

passages.original: No one can come into contact with the race for twenty years, as I have done in the heart of the South, without being convinced that the race is constantly making slow but sure progress materially, educationally, and morally. One might take up the life of the worst element in New York City, for example, and prove almost anything he wanted to prove concerning the white man, but all will agree that this is not a fair test.
passages.vernacular: 冇人可以像我二十年喺南方中心接觸種族,而唔確信種族喺物質、教育同道德上不斷取得緩慢但確實嘅進步。一個人可能以紐約市最差階層嘅生活為例,證明關於白人嘅幾乎任何佢想證明嘅,不過所有人都會同意呢個唔係公平測試。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒人可以像我二十年在南方中心接觸種族,而不確信種族在物質、教育和道德上不斷取得緩慢但確實的進步。一個人可能以紐約市最差階層的生活為例,證明關於白人的幾乎任何他想證明的,不過所有人都會同意這不是公平測試。

passages.original: Early in the year 1897 I received a letter inviting me to deliver an address at the dedication of the Robert Gould Shaw monument in Boston. I accepted the invitation. It is not necessary for me, I am sure, to explain who Robert Gould Shaw was, and what he did. The monument to his memory stands near the head of the Boston Common, facing the State House. It is counted to be the most perfect piece of art of the kind to be found in the country.
passages.vernacular: 1897年初,我收到一封信,邀請我喺波士頓羅伯特·古爾德·肖紀念碑揭幕禮發表演說。我接受邀請。我肯定我唔需要解釋羅伯特·古爾德·肖係邊個,佢做過咩。紀念佢嘅碑企喺波士頓公園頂部附近,面向州議會大廈。被認為係國內同類中最完美嘅藝術品。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 1897年初,我收到一封信,邀請我在波士頓羅伯特·古爾德·肖紀念碑揭幕禮發表演說。我接受邀請。我肯定我不需要解釋羅伯特·古爾德·肖是誰,他做過什麼。紀念他的碑站在波士頓公園頂部附近,面向州議會大廈。被認為是國內同類中最完美的藝術品。

passages.original: The exercises connected with the dedication were held in Music Hall, in Boston, and the great hall was packed from top to bottom with one of the most distinguished audiences that ever assembled in the city. Among those present were more persons representing the famous old anti-slavery element that it is likely will ever be brought together in the country again. The late Hon. Roger Wolcott, then Governor of Massachusetts, was the presiding officer, and on the platform with him were many other officials and hundreds of distinguished men. A report of the meeting which appeared in the Boston Transcript will describe it better than any words of mine could do:—
passages.vernacular: 揭幕相關儀式喺波士頓音樂廳舉行,大廳由上到下擠滿咗有史以來喺該市聚集嘅最傑出聽眾之一。在場人士當中,代表著名舊廢奴元素嘅人,比國內可能再次聚集嘅更多。已故嘅羅傑·沃爾科特先生,當時係麻薩諸塞州長,擔任主席,同佢一齊喺講台上有好多其他官員同幾百位傑出人士。《波士頓抄本報》刊登嘅會議報告,比我任何說話都更好咁描述:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 揭幕相關儀式在波士頓音樂廳舉行,大廳由上到下擠滿了有史以來在該市聚集的最傑出聽眾之一。在場人士當中,代表著名舊廢奴元素的人,比國內可能再次聚集的更多。已故的羅傑·沃爾科特先生,當時是麻薩諸塞州長,擔任主席,和他一起在講台上有很多其他官員和幾百位傑出人士。《波士頓抄本報》刊登的會議報告,比我任何話都更好地描述:

passages.original: The core and kernel of yesterday’s great noon meeting, in honour of the Brotherhood of Man, in Music Hall, was the superb address of the Negro President of Tuskegee. “Booker T. Washington received his Harvard A.M. last June, the first of his race,” said Governor Wolcott, “to receive an honorary degree from the oldest university in the land, and this for the wise leadership of his people.” When Mr. Washington rose in the flag-filled, enthusiasm-warmed, patriotic, and glowing atmosphere of Music Hall, people felt keenly that here was the civic justification of the old abolition spirit of Massachusetts; in his person the proof of her ancient and indomitable faith; in his strong thought and rich oratory, the crown and glory of the old war days of suffering and strife. The scene was full of historic beauty and deep significance. “Cold” Boston was alive with the fire that is always hot in her heart for righteousness and truth. Rows and rows of people who are seldom seen at any public function, whole families of those who are certain to be out of town on a holiday, crowded the place to overflowing. The city was at her birthright fête in the persons of hundreds of her best citizens, men and women whose names and lives stand for the virtues that make for honourable civic pride.
passages.vernacular: 昨日喺音樂廳舉行、紀念人類兄弟情誼嘅大中午聚會,核心同精髓係塔斯基吉黑人校長嘅卓越演說。沃爾科特州長講:「布克·T·華盛頓去年6月得到哈佛文學碩士學位,係佢種族第一個從國內最古老大學得到榮譽學位,因為佢對人民嘅智慧領導。」當華盛頓先生喺音樂廳旗幟滿佈、熱情洋溢、愛國同光輝嘅氣氛中起身,人們深切覺得,呢度係麻薩諸塞舊廢奴精神嘅公民證明;喺佢身上,係佢古老不屈信仰嘅證明;喺佢強烈思想同豐富演說中,係舊戰爭日子苦難同鬥爭嘅冠冕同榮耀。場景充滿歷史之美同深遠意義。「冷」嘅波士頓充滿佢心中對公義同真理一直熱嘅火焰。好少出現喺任何公眾場合嘅一排排人,假期必定出城嘅整個家庭,擠滿地方,人滿為患。城市以幾百位最好嘅市民身份出席佢嘅與生俱來嘅慶典,佢哋嘅名同生命代表締造光榮公民驕傲嘅美德。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 昨天在音樂廳舉行、紀念人類兄弟情誼的大中午聚會,核心和精髓是塔斯基吉黑人校長的卓越演說。沃爾科特州長說:「布克·T·華盛頓去年6月得到哈佛文學碩士學位,是他種族第一個從國內最古老大學得到榮譽學位,因為他對人民的智慧領導。」當華盛頓先生在音樂廳旗幟滿佈、熱情洋溢、愛國和光輝的氣氛中起身,人們深切覺得,這裡是麻薩諸塞舊廢奴精神的公民證明;在他身上,是她古老不屈信仰的證明;在他強烈思想和豐富演說中,是舊戰爭日子苦難和鬥爭的冠冕和榮耀。場景充滿歷史之美和深遠意義。「冷」的波士頓充滿她心中對公義和真理一直熱的火焰。很少出現在任何公眾場合的一排排人,假期必定出城的整個家庭,擠滿地方,人滿為患。城市以幾百位最好的市民身分出席她的與生俱來的慶典,他們的名字和生命代表締造光榮公民驕傲的美德。

passages.original: Battle-music had filled the air. Ovation after ovation, applause warm and prolonged, had greeted the officers and friends of Colonel Shaw, the sculptor, St. Gaudens, the memorial Committee, the Governor and his staff, and the Negro soldiers of the Fifty-fourth Massachusetts as they came upon the platform or entered the hall. Colonel Henry Lee, of Governor Andrew’s old staff, had made a noble, simple presentation speech for the committee, paying tribute to Mr. John M. Forbes, in whose stead he served. Governor Wolcott had made his short, memorable speech, saying, “Fort Wagner marked an epoch in the history of a race, and called it into manhood.” Mayor Quincy had received the monument for the city of Boston. The story of Colonel Shaw and his black regiment had been told in gallant words, and then, after the singing of
passages.vernacular: 戰鬥音樂充滿空氣。一次又一次嘅歡呼,熱烈而持久嘅掌聲,迎接肖上校嘅官員同朋友、雕塑家聖高登斯、紀念委員會、州長同佢嘅隨員,以及麻薩諸塞第五十四團嘅黑人士兵登上講台或入場。安德魯州長舊隨員亨利·李上校,為委員會作咗高貴簡單嘅呈獻演說,向約翰·M·福布斯先生致敬(佢代佢發言)。沃爾科特州長發表咗佢簡短難忘嘅演說,講:「瓦格納堡標誌一個種族歷史嘅一個紀元,喚起佢成為男子漢。」奎因西市長代表波士頓市接受紀念碑。肖上校同佢嘅黑人團嘅故事以英勇嘅說話講述,然後,喺唱完之後
passages.vernacularMandarin: 戰鬥音樂充滿空氣。一次又一次的歡呼,熱烈而持久的掌聲,迎接肖上校的官員和朋友、雕塑家聖高登斯、紀念委員會、州長和他的隨員,以及麻薩諸塞第五十四團的黑人士兵登上講台或入場。安德魯州長舊隨員亨利·李上校,為委員會作了高貴簡單的呈獻演說,向約翰·M·福布斯先生致敬(他代他發言)。沃爾科特州長發表了他簡短難忘的演說,說:「瓦格納堡標誌一個種族歷史的一個紀元,喚起它成為男子漢。」奎因西市長代表波士頓市接受紀念碑。肖上校和他的黑人團的故事以英勇的話講述,然後,在唱完之後

passages.original: Mine eyes have seen the glory Of the coming of the Lord,
passages.vernacular: 「我雙眼已見主降臨嘅榮耀,」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我雙眼已見主降臨的榮耀,」

passages.original: Booker Washington arose. It was, of course, just the moment for him. The multitude, shaken out of its usual symphony-concert calm, quivered with an excitement that was not suppressed. A dozen times it had sprung to its feet to cheer and wave and hurrah, as one person. When this man of culture and voice and power, as well as a dark skin, began, and uttered the names of Stearns and of Andrew, feeling began to mount. You could see tears glisten in the eyes of soldiers and civilians. When the orator turned to the coloured soldiers on the platform, to the colour-bearer of Fort Wagner, who smilingly bore still the flag he had never lowered even when wounded, and said, “To you, to the scarred and scattered remnants of the Fifty-fourth, who, with empty sleeve and wanting leg, have honoured this occasion with your presence, to you, your commander is not dead. Though Boston erected no monument and history recorded no story, in you and in the loyal race which you represent, Robert Gould Shaw would have a monument which time could not wear away,” then came the climax of the emotion of the day and the hour. It was Roger Wolcott, as well as the Governor of Massachusetts, the individual representative of the people’s sympathy as well as the chief magistrate, who had sprung first to his feet and cried, “Three cheers to Booker T. Washington!”
passages.vernacular: 布克·華盛頓起身。當然,正係佢嘅時刻。大批人群,被搖出佢通常交響音樂會嘅平靜,以未被壓抑嘅激動顫抖。佢哋十幾次作為一個人跳起歡呼揮手呼喊。當呢位有文化、聲音同力量、同時有深色皮膚嘅人開始,講出斯特恩斯同安德魯嘅名,感情開始高漲。你可以見到士兵同平民眼中淚光閃爍。當演說家轉向講台上嘅有色人種士兵,向瓦格納堡嘅持旗手(仍然微笑咁拿住佢從未降下嘅旗,即使受傷時),講:「向你,向第五十四團有疤痕、散落嘅殘餘者,空袖管、缺腿,以你哋出席為呢個場合增光,向你,你嘅指揮官未死。雖然波士頓冇建碑,歷史冇記載故事,喺你同你所代表嘅忠誠種族身上,羅伯特·古爾德·肖會有一座時間無法磨損嘅紀念碑。」然後係當日當時情緒嘅高潮。係羅傑·沃爾科特,同時係麻薩諸塞州長,人民同情嘅個人代表同行政長官,第一個跳起,喊:「為布克·T·華盛頓三呼萬歲!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 布克·華盛頓起身。當然,正是他的時刻。大批人群,被搖出它通常交響音樂會的平靜,以未被壓抑的激動顫抖。他們十幾次作為一個人跳起歡呼揮手呼喊。當這位有文化、聲音和力量、同時有深色皮膚的人開始,說出斯特恩斯和安德魯的名字,感情開始高漲。你可以看到士兵和平民眼中淚光閃爍。當演說家轉向講台上的有色人種士兵,向瓦格納堡的持旗手(仍然微笑地拿著他從未降下的旗,即使受傷時),說:「向你,向第五十四團有疤痕、散落的殘餘者,空袖管、缺腿,以你們出席為這個場合增光,向你,你的指揮官未死。雖然波士頓沒建碑,歷史沒記載故事,在你和你所代表的忠誠種族身上,羅伯特·古爾德·肖會有一座時間無法磨損的紀念碑。」然後是當天當時情緒的高潮。是羅傑·沃爾科特,同時是麻薩諸塞州長,人民同情的個人代表和行政長官,第一個跳起,喊:「為布克·T·華盛頓三呼萬歲!」

passages.original: Among those on the platform was Sergeant William H. Carney, of New Bedford, Mass., the brave coloured officer who was the colour-bearer at Fort Wagner and held the American flag. In spite of the fact that a large part of his regiment was killed, he escaped, and exclaimed, after the battle was over, “The old flag never touched the ground.”
passages.vernacular: 講台上有麻薩諸塞新貝德福德嘅威廉·H·卡尼中士,勇敢嘅有色人種軍官,係瓦格納堡嘅持旗手,拿住美國旗。儘管佢團大部分被殺,佢逃脫,戰鬥結束後大喊:「舊旗從未觸地。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 講台上有麻薩諸塞新貝德福德的威廉·H·卡尼中士,勇敢的有色人種軍官,是瓦格納堡的持旗手,拿著美國旗。儘管他團大部分被殺,他逃脫,戰鬥結束後大喊:「舊旗從未觸地。」

passages.original: This flag Sergeant Carney held in his hands as he sat on the platform, and when I turned to address the survivors of the coloured regiment who were present, and referred to Sergeant Carney, he rose, as if by instinct, and raised the flag. It has been my privilege to witness a good many satisfactory and rather sensational demonstrations in connection with some of my public addresses, but in dramatic effect I have never seen or experienced anything which equalled this. For a number of minutes the audience seemed to entirely lose control of itself.
passages.vernacular: 卡尼中士坐喺講台上雙手拿住呢面旗,當我轉向在場嘅有色人種團倖存者演說,並提到卡尼中士時,佢似乎本能地站起,舉起旗。我有幸見證過好多令人滿意同相當轟動嘅示範,同我一些公眾演說有關,不過戲劇效果上,我從未見過或者經歷過任何比呢個更勝。有好幾分鐘,聽眾似乎完全失去自控。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 卡尼中士坐在講台上雙手拿著這面旗,當我轉向在場的有色人種團倖存者演說,並提到卡尼中士時,他似乎本能地站起,舉起旗。我有幸見證過很多令人滿意和相當轟動的示範,與我一些公眾演說有關,不過戲劇效果上,我從未見過或經歷過任何比這個更勝。有好幾分鐘,聽眾似乎完全失去自控。

passages.original: In the general rejoicing throughout the country which followed the close of the Spanish-American war, peace celebrations were arranged in several of the large cities. I was asked by President William R. Harper, of the University of Chicago, who was chairman of the committee of invitations for the celebration to be held in the city of Chicago, to deliver one of the addresses at the celebration there. I accepted the invitation, and delivered two addresses there during the Jubilee week. The first of these, and the principal one, was given in the Auditorium, on the evening of Sunday, October 16. This was the largest audience that I have ever addressed, in any part of the country; and besides speaking in the main Auditorium, I also addressed, that same evening, two overflow audiences in other parts of the city.
passages.vernacular: 美西戰爭結束後全國普遍歡欣,幾個大城市安排和平慶典。芝加哥大學校長威廉·R·哈珀(芝加哥市慶典邀請委員會主席)請我喺嗰度慶典發表其中一個演說。我接受邀請,喺禧年週期間喺嗰度發表兩個演說。其中第一個,亦係主要嘅,喺10月16日星期日晚,喺禮堂發表。呢個係我喺全國任何地方向佢演說過最大嘅聽眾;除咗喺主禮堂演說,同一晚我亦向城市其他地方兩個溢出聽眾演說。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 美西戰爭結束後全國普遍歡欣,幾個大城市安排和平慶典。芝加哥大學校長威廉·R·哈珀(芝加哥市慶典邀請委員會主席)請我在那裡慶典發表其中一個演說。我接受邀請,在禧年週期間在那裡發表兩個演說。其中第一個,也是主要的,在10月16日星期日晚,在禮堂發表。這是我在全國任何地方向他演說過最大的聽眾;除了在主禮堂演說,同一晚我也向城市其他地方兩個溢出聽眾演說。

passages.original: It was said that there were sixteen thousand persons in the Auditorium, and it seemed to me as if there were as many more on the outside trying to get in. It was impossible for any one to get near the entrance without the aid of a policeman. President William McKinley attended this meeting, as did also the members of his Cabinet, many foreign ministers, and a large number of army and navy officers, many of whom had distinguished themselves in the war which had just closed. The speakers, besides myself, on Sunday evening, were Rabbi Emil G. Hirsch, Father Thomas P. Hodnett, and Dr. John H. Barrows.
passages.vernacular: 據講禮堂有一萬六千人,我覺得外面同樣多人試圖入。冇警察幫助,冇人可以接近入口。威廉·麥金萊總統出席呢次會議,佢嘅內閣成員、好多外國公使、大批陸海軍官員(好多喺剛結束嘅戰爭中表現出色)亦出席。星期日晚除咗我之外嘅演講者,係拉比埃米爾·G·赫希、托馬斯·P·霍德尼特神父同約翰·H·巴羅斯博士。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 據說禮堂有一萬六千人,我覺得外面同樣多人試圖進。沒警察幫助,沒人可以接近入口。威廉·麥金萊總統出席這次會議,他的內閣成員、很多外國公使、大批陸海軍官員(很多在剛結束的戰爭中表現出色)也出席。星期日晚除了我之外的演講者,是拉比埃米爾·G·赫希、托馬斯·P·霍德尼特神父和約翰·H·巴羅斯博士。

passages.original: The Chicago Times-Herald, in describing the meeting, said of my address:—
passages.vernacular: 《芝加哥時報先驅報》描述會議時,講我嘅演說:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 《芝加哥時報先驅報》描述會議時,說我的演說:

passages.original: He pictured the Negro choosing slavery rather than extinction; recalled Crispus Attucks shedding his blood at the beginning of the American Revolution, that white Americans might be free, while black Americans remained in slavery; rehearsed the conduct of the Negroes with Jackson at New Orleans; drew a vivid and pathetic picture of the Southern slaves protecting and supporting the families of their masters while the latter were fighting to perpetuate black slavery; recounted the bravery of coloured troops at Port Hudson and Forts Wagner and Pillow, and praised the heroism of the black regiments that stormed El Caney and Santiago to give freedom to the enslaved people of Cuba, forgetting, for the time being, the unjust discrimination that law and custom make against them in their own country.
passages.vernacular: 佢描繪黑人選擇奴役而唔係滅絕;回憶克里斯普斯·阿塔克斯喺美國革命開始時流血,令白人美國人自由,而黑人美國人仍然做奴隸;複述黑人同傑克遜喺新奧爾良嘅行為;畫出一幅生動而悲愴嘅圖畫:南方奴隸保護同支持主人嘅家庭,而主人正為永續黑人奴隸制而戰;講述有色人種部隊喺哈德遜港、瓦格納堡同皮洛堡嘅英勇,讚揚衝鋒埃爾卡內同聖地牙哥、令古巴被奴役人民得到自由嘅黑人團嘅英雄氣概,暫時忘記法律同習俗對佢哋喺自己國家造成嘅不公歧視。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他描繪黑人選擇奴役而不是滅絕;回憶克里斯普斯·阿塔克斯在美國革命開始時流血,使白人美國人自由,而黑人美國人仍然做奴隸;複述黑人與傑克遜在新奧爾良的行為;畫出一幅生動而悲愴的圖畫:南方奴隸保護和支持主人的家庭,而主人正為永續黑人奴隸制而戰;講述有色人種部隊在哈德遜港、瓦格納堡和皮洛堡的英勇,讚揚衝鋒埃爾卡內和聖地牙哥、使古巴被奴役人民得到自由的黑人團的英雄氣概,暫時忘記法律和習俗對他們在自己國家造成的不公歧視。

passages.original: In all of these things, the speaker declared, his race had chosen the better part. And then he made his eloquent appeal to the consciences of the white Americans: “When you have gotten the full story of the heroic conduct of the Negro in the Spanish-American war, have heard it from the lips of Northern soldier and Southern soldier, from ex-abolitionist and ex-masters, then decide within yourselves whether a race that is thus willing to die for its country should not be given the highest opportunity to live for its country.”
passages.vernacular: 演講者宣布,喺所有呢啲事情上,佢嘅種族選擇咗更好嘅部分。然後佢向白人美國人嘅良心作出雄辯嘅呼籲:「當你得到黑人喺美西戰爭中英勇行為嘅完整故事,從北方士兵同南方士兵、從前廢奴者同前主人口中聽到,然後你自己內心決定,一個咁願意為國家而死嘅種族,是否應該得到為國家而活嘅最高機會。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 演講者宣布,在所有這些事情上,他的種族選擇了更好的部分。然後他向白人美國人的良心作出雄辯的呼籲:「當你得到黑人在美西戰爭中英勇行為的完整故事,從北方士兵和南方士兵、從前廢奴者和前主人口中聽到,然後你自己內心決定,一個這麼願意為國家而死的種族,是否應該得到為國家而活的最高機會。」

passages.original: The part of the speech which seems to arouse the wildest and most sensational enthusiasm was that in which I thanked the President for his recognition of the Negro in his appointments during the Spanish-American war. The President was sitting in a box at the right of the stage. When I addressed him I turned toward the box, and as I finished the sentence thanking him for his generosity, the whole audience rose and cheered again and again, waving handkerchiefs and hats and canes, until the President arose in the box and bowed his acknowledgements. At that the enthusiasm broke out again, and the demonstration was almost indescribable.
passages.vernacular: 演說中似乎引起最瘋狂、最轟動熱情嘅部分,係我多謝總統喺美西戰爭期間嘅任命中認可黑人。總統坐喺舞台右邊嘅包廂。我向佢說話時,轉向包廂,當我講完多謝佢慷慨嘅一句,全場聽眾起立歡呼,一次又一次,揮動手帕、帽同手杖,直到總統喺包廂起身鞠躬致謝。熱情隨即再次爆發,示範幾乎無法形容。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 演說中似乎引起最瘋狂、最轟動熱情的部分,是我感謝總統在美西戰爭期間的任命中認可黑人。總統坐在舞台右邊的包廂。我向他說話時,轉向包廂,當我說完感謝他慷慨的一句,全場聽眾起立歡呼,一次又一次,揮動手帕、帽子和手杖,直到總統在包廂起身鞠躬致謝。熱情隨即再次爆發,示範幾乎無法形容。

passages.original: One portion of my address at Chicago seemed to have been misunderstood by the Southern press, and some of the Southern papers took occasion to criticise me rather strongly. These criticisms continued for several weeks, until I finally received a letter from the editor of the Age-Herald, published in Birmingham, Ala., asking me if I would say just what I meant by this part of the address. I replied to him in a letter which seemed to satisfy my critics. In this letter I said that I had made it a rule never to say before a Northern audience anything that I would not say before an audience in the South. I said that I did not think it was necessary for me to go into extended explanations; if my seventeen years of work in the heart of the South had not been explanation enough, I did not see how words could explain. I said that I made the same plea that I had made in my address at Atlanta, for the blotting out of race prejudice in “commercial and civil relations.” I said that what is termed social recognition was a question which I never discussed, and then I quoted from my Atlanta address what I had said there in regard to that subject.
passages.vernacular: 我喺芝加哥演說嘅一部分似乎被南方報界誤解,一些南方報紙藉機相當強烈咁批評我。呢啲批評持續咗幾個星期,直到我最終收到阿拉巴馬伯明翰出版嘅《時代先驅報》編輯嘅信,問我可唔可以講明我演說呢部分嘅意思。我用一封似乎令我批評者滿意嘅信回覆佢。喺呢封信我講,我定下規矩,從不向北方聽眾講我唔會向南方聽眾講嘅嘢。我講我認為唔需要作長篇解釋;如果我喺南方中心十七年嘅工作都唔夠解釋,我睇唔到說話點樣解釋。我講我作出同我喺亞特蘭大演說相同嘅呼籲,消除「商業同公民關係」中嘅種族偏見。我講所謂社會認可係我從未討論嘅問題,然後我引用我亞特蘭大演說對呢個題目所講嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在芝加哥演說的一部分似乎被南方報界誤解,一些南方報紙藉機相當強烈地批評我。這些批評持續了幾個星期,直到我最終收到阿拉巴馬伯明翰出版的《時代先驅報》編輯的信,問我可不可以說明我演說這部分的意思。我用一封似乎使我批評者滿意的信回覆他。在這封信我說,我定下規矩,從不向北方聽眾講我不會向南方聽眾講的話。我說我認為不需要作長篇解釋;如果我在南方中心十七年的工作都不夠解釋,我看不到話語怎樣解釋。我說我作出與我在亞特蘭大演說相同的呼籲,消除「商業和公民關係」中的種族偏見。我說所謂社會認可是我從未討論的問題,然後我引用我亞特蘭大演說對這個題目所說的。

passages.original: In meeting crowds of people at public gatherings, there is one type of individual that I dread. I mean the crank. I have become so accustomed to these people now that I can pick them out at a distance when I see them elbowing their way up to me. The average crank has a long beard, poorly cared for, a lean, narrow face, and wears a black coat. The front of his vest and coat are slick with grease, and his trousers bag at the knees.
passages.vernacular: 喺公眾聚會遇到人群時,有一類人我好怕。我係指怪人。我而家咁習慣呢啲人,可以喺遠處見到佢哋用手肘擠向我時認出佢哋。普通怪人有長鬍鬚,打理得差,瘦窄嘅面,穿黑色外套。佢背心同外套前面油膩,褲子膝蓋鬆垮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在公眾聚會遇到人群時,有一類人我很怕。我是指怪人。我現在那麼習慣這些人,可以在遠處看到他們用手肘擠向我時認出他們。普通怪人有長鬍鬚,打理得差,瘦窄的臉,穿黑色外套。他背心和外套前面油膩,褲子膝蓋鬆垮。

passages.original: In Chicago, after I had spoken at a meeting, I met one of these fellows. They usually have some process for curing all of the ills of the world at once. This Chicago specimen had a patent process by which he said Indian corn could be kept through a period of three or four years, and he felt sure that if the Negro race in the South would, as a whole, adopt his process, it would settle the whole race question. It mattered nothing that I tried to convince him that our present problem was to teach the Negroes how to produce enough corn to last them through one year. Another Chicago crank had a scheme by which he wanted me to join him in an effort to close up all the National banks in the country. If that was done, he felt sure it would put the Negro on his feet.
passages.vernacular: 喺芝加哥,我喺一個會議演講後,遇到其中一個。佢哋通常有某種方法一次過治好世界所有疾病。呢個芝加哥樣本有一個專利方法,話可以令玉米保存三四年,佢肯定如果南方黑人種族整體採用佢嘅方法,會解決整個種族問題。我試圖說服佢,我哋當前嘅問題係教黑人點樣生產足夠玉米食一年,都冇關係。另一個芝加哥怪人有個計劃,想我同佢一齊努力關閉國內所有國家銀行。如果做到,佢肯定會令黑人站穩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在芝加哥,我在一個會議演講後,遇到其中一個。他們通常有某種方法一次過治好世界所有疾病。這個芝加哥樣本有一個專利方法,說可以使玉米保存三四年,他肯定如果南方黑人種族整體採用他的方法,會解決整個種族問題。我試圖說服他,我們當前的問題是教黑人怎樣生產足夠玉米吃一年,都沒關係。另一個芝加哥怪人有個計劃,想我與他一起努力關閉國內所有國家銀行。如果做到,他肯定會使黑人站穩。

passages.original: The number of people who stand ready to consume one’s time, to no purpose, is almost countless. At one time I spoke before a large audience in Boston in the evening. The next morning I was awakened by having a card brought to my room, and with it a message that some one was anxious to see me. Thinking that it must be something very important, I dressed hastily and went down. When I reached the hotel office I found a blank and innocent-looking individual waiting for me, who coolly remarked: “I heard you talk at a meeting last night. I rather liked your talk, and so I came in this morning to hear you talk some more.”
passages.vernacular: 準備好無目的消耗一個人時間嘅人,數量幾乎無法計算。有一次,我喺波士頓晚上向一大批聽眾演說。第二朝,我被送入我房間嘅一張名片吵醒,連同一個信息,話有人想見我。以為一定係非常重要嘅事,我匆忙著衫落去。我到酒店辦公室,發現一個空白而天真樣子嘅人等我,冷靜咁講:「我昨晚喺一個會議聽過你講嘢。我相當鍾意你嘅演講,所以今朝來多聽你講。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 準備好無目的消耗一個人時間的人,數量幾乎無法計算。有一次,我在波士頓晚上向一大批聽眾演說。第二天早上,我被送入我房間的一張名片吵醒,連同一個信息,說有人想見我。以為一定是非常重要的事,我匆忙穿衣下去。我到酒店辦公室,發現一個空白而天真樣子的人等我,冷靜地說:「我昨晚在一個會議聽過你說話。我相當喜歡你的演講,所以今天早上來多聽你說。」

passages.original: I am often asked how it is possible for me to superintend the work at Tuskegee and at the same time be so much away from the school. In partial answer to this I would say that I think I have learned, in some degree at least, to disregard the old maxim which says, “Do not get others to do that which you can do yourself.” My motto, on the other hand, is, “Do not do that which others can do as well.”
passages.vernacular: 我經常被問,點樣可以一方面管理塔斯基吉嘅工作,同時又咁多時間離開學校。部分回答係,我認為我已經學會,至少某程度上,不理會舊格言:「唔好叫其他人做你自己可以做嘅事。」相反,我嘅座右銘係:「唔好做其他人可以同樣做好嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我經常被問,怎樣可以一方面管理塔斯基吉的工作,同時又那麼多時間離開學校。部分回答是,我認為我已經學會,至少某種程度上,不理會舊格言:「不要叫其他人做你自己可以做的事。」相反,我的座右銘是:「不要做其他人可以同樣做好的事。」

passages.original: One of the most encouraging signs in connection with the Tuskegee school is found in the fact that the organization is so thorough that the daily work of the school is not dependent upon the presence of any one individual. The whole executive force, including instructors and clerks, now numbers eighty-six. This force is so organized and subdivided that the machinery of the school goes on day by day like clockwork. Most of our teachers have been connected with the institutions for a number of years, and are as much interested in it as I am. In my absence, Mr. Warren Logan, the treasurer, who has been at the school seventeen years, is the executive. He is efficiently supported by Mrs. Washington, and by my faithful secretary, Mr. Emmett J. Scott, who handles the bulk of my correspondence and keeps me in daily touch with the life of the school, and who also keeps me informed of whatever takes place in the South that concerns the race. I owe more to his tact, wisdom, and hard work than I can describe.
passages.vernacular: 塔斯基吉學校最令人鼓舞嘅跡象之一,係組織咁徹底,學校嘅日常工作並唔倚靠任何一個人嘅在場。整個行政人員,包括導師同文員,而家有八十六人。呢班人組織同細分,令學校機器日復一日似時鐘咁運轉。我哋大部分老師已經喺學院好多年,同我一樣對佢感興趣。我不在期間,財務主管沃倫·洛根先生(喺學校十七年)係行政主管。佢得到華盛頓太太同我忠實嘅秘書埃米特·J·斯科特先生有效支持,佢處理我大部分通信,令我每日同學校生活保持聯繫,亦令我知道南方發生嘅任何關乎種族嘅事。我對佢嘅機智、智慧同辛勤工作,欠咗比我可以描述更多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 塔斯基吉學校最令人鼓舞的跡象之一,是組織那麼徹底,學校的日常工作並不倚靠任何一個人的在場。整個行政人員,包括導師和文員,現在有八十六人。這班人組織和細分,使學校機器日復一日像時鐘那樣運轉。我們大部分老師已經在學院很多年,與我一樣對它感興趣。我不在期間,財務主管沃倫·洛根先生(在學校十七年)是行政主管。他得到華盛頓太太和我忠實的秘書埃米特·J·斯科特先生有效支持,他處理我大部分通信,使我每天與學校生活保持聯繫,也使我知道南方發生的任何關乎種族的事。我對他的機智、智慧和辛勤工作,欠了比我可以描述更多。

passages.original: The main executive work of the school, whether I am at Tuskegee or not, centres in what we call the executive council. This council meets twice a week, and is composed of the nine persons who are at the head of the nine departments of the school. For example: Mrs. B.K. Bruce, the Lady Principal, the widow of the late ex-senator Bruce, is a member of the council, and represents in it all that pertains to the life of the girls at the school. In addition to the executive council there is a financial committee of six, that meets every week and decides upon the expenditures for the week. Once a month, and sometimes oftener, there is a general meeting of all the instructors. Aside from these there are innumerable smaller meetings, such as that of the instructors in the Phelps Hall Bible Training School, or of the instructors in the agricultural department.
passages.vernacular: 無論我喺唔喺塔斯基吉,學校嘅主要行政工作都集中喺我哋所謂嘅行政委員會。呢個委員會每星期開會兩次,由學校九個部門嘅九位負責人組成。例如:女主任B·K·布魯斯夫人,已故前參議員布魯斯嘅遺孀,係委員會成員,代表佢處理所有關於學校女孩生活嘅事務。除咗行政委員會,仲有一個六人財務委員會,每星期開會,決定當週開支。每個月一次,有時更多,所有導師開全體會議。除此之外有無數較小嘅會議,例如費爾普斯樓聖經培訓學校導師嘅會議,或農業部門導師嘅會議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論我在不在塔斯基吉,學校的主要行政工作都集中在我們所謂的行政委員會。這個委員會每星期開會兩次,由學校九個部門的九位負責人組成。例如:女主任B·K·布魯斯夫人,已故前參議員布魯斯的遺孀,是委員會成員,代表她處理所有關於學校女孩生活的事務。除了行政委員會,還有一個六人財務委員會,每星期開會,決定當週開支。每個月一次,有時更多,所有導師開全體會議。除此之外有無數較小的會議,例如費爾普斯樓聖經培訓學校導師的會議,或農業部門導師的會議。

passages.original: In order that I may keep in constant touch with the life of the institution, I have a system of reports so arranged that a record of the school’s work reaches me every day of the year, no matter in what part of the country I am. I know by these reports even what students are excused from school, and why they are excused—whether for reasons of ill health or otherwise. Through the medium of these reports I know each day what the income of the school in money is; I know how many gallons of milk and how many pounds of butter come from the dairy; what the bill of fare for the teachers and students is; whether a certain kind of meat was boiled or baked, and whether certain vegetables served in the dining room were bought from a store or procured from our own farm. Human nature I find to be very much the same the world over, and it is sometimes not hard to yield to the temptation to go to a barrel of rice that has come from the store—with the grain all prepared to go in the pot—rather than to take the time and trouble to go to the field and dig and wash one’s own sweet potatoes, which might be prepared in a manner to take the place of the rice.
passages.vernacular: 為咗令我同學院生活保持不斷聯繫,我有個報告制度,安排成無論我喺全國邊個地方,學校工作嘅記錄一年每日都送到我手。憑呢啲報告,我甚至知道邊啲學生被豁免上學,以及點解被豁免——係因為健康不佳或其他原因。透過呢啲報告,我每日知道學校嘅金錢收入;我知道乳牛場出產幾多加侖牛奶同幾多磅牛油;老師同學生嘅菜單係咩;某種肉係煮定烤;飯廳供應嘅某些蔬菜係從舖頭買、定係從我哋自己農場得到。我發現人性世界各地大致相同,有時唔難屈服於誘惑,去舖頭運來嘅一桶米(穀粒全部準備好落鍋),而唔係花時間同麻煩去田裡挖同洗自己嘅番薯(可以準備成代替米嘅嘢)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了使我與學院生活保持不斷聯繫,我有個報告制度,安排成無論我在全國哪個地方,學校工作的記錄一年每天都送到我手。憑這些報告,我甚至知道哪些學生被豁免上學,以及為什麼被豁免——是因為健康不佳或其他原因。透過這些報告,我每天知道學校的金錢收入;我知道乳牛場出產多少加侖牛奶和多少磅牛油;老師和學生的菜單是什麼;某種肉是煮還是烤;飯廳供應的某些蔬菜是從店鋪買、還是從我們自己農場得到。我發現人性世界各地大致相同,有時不難屈服於誘惑,去店鋪運來的一桶米(穀粒全部準備好下鍋),而不是花時間和麻煩去田裡挖和洗自己的番薯(可以準備成代替米的東西)。

passages.original: I am often asked how, in the midst of so much work, a large part of which is for the public, I can find time for any rest or recreation, and what kind of recreation or sports I am fond of. This is rather a difficult question to answer. I have a strong feeling that every individual owes it to himself, and to the cause which he is serving, to keep a vigorous, healthy body, with the nerves steady and strong, prepared for great efforts and prepared for disappointments and trying positions. As far as I can, I make it a rule to plan for each day’s work—not merely to go through with the same routine of daily duties, but to get rid of the routine work as early in the day as possible, and then to enter upon some new or advance work. I make it a rule to clear my desk every day, before leaving my office, of all correspondence and memoranda, so that on the morrow I can begin a new day of work. I make it a rule never to let my work drive me, but to so master it, and keep it in such complete control, and to keep so far ahead of it, that I will be the master instead of the servant. There is a physical and mental and spiritual enjoyment that comes from a consciousness of being the absolute master of one’s work, in all its details, that is very satisfactory and inspiring. My experience teaches me that, if one learns to follow this plan, he gets a freshness of body and vigour of mind out of work that goes a long way toward keeping him strong and healthy. I believe that when one can grow to the point where he loves his work, this gives him a kind of strength that is most valuable.
passages.vernacular: 我經常被問,喺咁多工作(大部分為公眾)之中,我點樣搵到時間休息或者娛樂,以及我鍾意咩種類嘅娛樂或者運動。呢個問題相當難回答。我強烈覺得,每個人對自己,以及對佢所服務嘅事業,有責任保持有活力、健康嘅身體,神經穩定強壯,準備好大努力同失望同艱難處境。我盡可能定下規矩為每日工作計劃——唔單止進行同樣嘅日常職責,而係盡早喺一日當中完成例行工作,然後開始一些新嘅或進階嘅工作。我定下規矩,每日離開辦公室前清理書桌上所有通信同備忘錄,令第二日可以開始新一日工作。我定下規矩,從不讓工作驅使我,而係掌握佢,完全控制佢,領先佢咁遠,令我成為主人而唔係僕人。意識到自己係工作所有細節嘅絕對主人,帶來一種身體、心智同靈性嘅享受,非常令人滿意同鼓舞。我嘅經驗教我,如果一個人學會遵循呢個計劃,佢從工作得到嘅身體清新同心智活力,對保持佢強壯健康好有幫助。我相信當一個人成長到愛佢嘅工作,呢個畀佢一種最有價值嘅力量。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我經常被問,在那麼多工作(大部分為公眾)之中,我怎樣找到時間休息或娛樂,以及我喜歡什麼種類的娛樂或運動。這個問題相當難回答。我強烈覺得,每個人對自己,以及對他所服務的事業,有責任保持有活力、健康的身體,神經穩定強壯,準備好大努力和失望和艱難處境。我盡可能定下規矩為每天工作計劃——不僅進行同樣的日常職責,而是盡早在一天當中完成例行工作,然後開始一些新的或進階的工作。我定下規矩,每天離開辦公室前清理書桌上所有通信和備忘錄,使第二天可以開始新一天工作。我定下規矩,從不讓工作驅使我,而是掌握它,完全控制它,領先它那麼遠,使我成為主人而不是僕人。意識到自己是工作所有細節的絕對主人,帶來一種身體、心智和靈性的享受,非常令人滿意和鼓舞。我的經驗教我,如果一個人學會遵循這個計劃,他從工作得到的身體清新和心智活力,對保持他強壯健康很有幫助。我相信當一個人成長到愛他的工作,這給他一種最有價值的力量。

passages.original: When I begin my work in the morning, I expect to have a successful and pleasant day of it, but at the same time I prepare myself for unpleasant and unexpected hard places. I prepared myself to hear that one of our school buildings is on fire, or has burned, or that some disagreeable accident has occurred, or that some one has abused me in a public address or printed article, for something that I have done or omitted to do, or for something that he had heard that I had said—probably something that I had never thought of saying.
passages.vernacular: 我朝早開始工作時,預期有成功愉快嘅一日,但同時為不愉快、意外嘅困難作準備。我準備好聽到我哋其中一座校舍著火或者已經燒毀,或者發生某種不愉快意外,或者有人因為我做過或冇做過嘅事,或者佢聽過我講過嘅嘢(大概係我從未想過要講嘅),喺公眾演說或印刷文章中辱罵我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我早上開始工作時,預期有成功愉快的一天,但同時為不愉快、意外的困難作準備。我準備好聽到我們其中一座校舍著火或已經燒毀,或發生某種不愉快意外,或有人因為我做過或沒做過的事,或他聽過我說過的話(大概是我從未想過要說的),在公眾演說或印刷文章中辱罵我。

passages.original: In nineteen years of continuous work I have taken but one vacation. That was two years ago, when some of my friends put the money into my hands and forced Mrs. Washington and myself to spend three months in Europe. I have said that I believe it is the duty of every one to keep his body in good condition. I try to look after the little ills, with the idea that if I take care of the little ills the big ones will not come. When I find myself unable to sleep well, I know that something is wrong. If I find any part of my system the least weak, and not performing its duty, I consult a good physician. The ability to sleep well, at any time and in any place, I find of great advantage. I have so trained myself that I can lie down for a nap of fifteen or twenty minutes, and get up refreshed in body and mind.
passages.vernacular: 十九年持續工作中,我只放過一次假。係兩年前,我一些朋友將錢放入我手,迫使華盛頓太太同我去歐洲三個月。我講過我相信每個人都有責任保持身體良好狀態。我嘗試照顧小病,認為如果我照顧小病,大病就唔會來。當我發現自己瞓唔好,我知道有嘢唔對。如果我發現我身體任何部分稍微虛弱、冇履行職責,我就去睇好醫生。我發現隨時隨地都可以好好瞓嘅能力有好大好處。我已經訓練自己,可以躺低小睡十五或二十分鐘,起身後身心清新。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 十九年持續工作中,我只放過一次假。是兩年前,我一些朋友將錢放入我手,迫使華盛頓太太和我去歐洲三個月。我說過我相信每個人都有責任保持身體良好狀態。我嘗試照顧小病,認為如果我照顧小病,大病就不會來。當我發現自己睡不好,我知道有東西不對。如果我發現我身體任何部分稍微虛弱、沒履行職責,我就去看好醫生。我發現隨時隨地都可以好好睡的能力有很大好處。我已經訓練自己,可以躺下小睡十五或二十分鐘,起身後身心清新。

passages.original: I have said that I make it a rule to finish up each day’s work before leaving it. There is, perhaps, one exception to this. When I have an unusually difficult question to decide—one that appeals strongly to the emotions—I find it a safe rule to sleep over it for a night, or to wait until I have had an opportunity to talk it over with my wife and friends.
passages.vernacular: 我講過我定下規矩,離開前完成每日工作。也許有一個例外。當我有一個異常困難嘅問題要決定——一個強烈訴諸情感嘅——我發現安全嘅規則係瞓一晚再決定,或者等到我有機會同太太同朋友傾過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說過我定下規矩,離開前完成每天工作。也許有一個例外。當我有一個異常困難的問題要決定——一個強烈訴諸情感的——我發現安全的規則是睡一晚再決定,或等到我有機會與妻子和朋友談過。

passages.original: As to my reading; the most time I get for solid reading is when I am on the cars. Newspapers are to me a constant source of delight and recreation. The only trouble is that I read too many of them. Fiction I care little for. Frequently I have to almost force myself to read a novel that is on every one’s lips. The kind of reading that I have the greatest fondness for is biography. I like to be sure that I am reading about a real man or a real thing. I think I do not go too far when I say that I have read nearly every book and magazine article that has been written about Abraham Lincoln. In literature he is my patron saint.
passages.vernacular: 至於我嘅閱讀;我得到最多時間做紮實閱讀,係喺火車上。報紙對我係不斷嘅樂趣同消遣。唯一嘅麻煩係我讀太多。小說我好少關心。我經常要幾乎強迫自己讀一本人人都講嘅小說。我最鍾意嘅閱讀類型係傳記。我鍾意肯定我讀緊嘅係真實嘅人或真實嘅事。我諗我講我已經讀過幾乎每一本、每一篇關於亞伯拉罕·林肯嘅書同雜誌文章,並唔過分。喺文學上,佢係我嘅守護聖人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於我的閱讀;我得到最多時間做紮實閱讀,是在火車上。報紙對我是不斷的樂趣和消遣。唯一的麻煩是我讀太多。小說我很少關心。我經常要幾乎強迫自己讀一本人人都說的小說。我最喜歡的閱讀類型是傳記。我喜歡肯定我讀著的是真實的人或真實的事。我想我說我已經讀過幾乎每一本、每一篇關於亞伯拉罕·林肯的書和雜誌文章,並不過分。在文學上,他是我的守護聖人。

passages.original: Out of the twelve months in a year I suppose that, on an average, I spend six months away from Tuskegee. While my being absent from the school so much unquestionably has its disadvantages, yet there are at the same time some compensations. The change of work brings a certain kind of rest. I enjoy a ride of a long distance on the cars, when I am permitted to ride where I can be comfortable. I get rest on the cars, except when the inevitable individual who seems to be on every train approaches me with the now familiar phrase: “Isn’t this Booker Washington? I want to introduce myself to you.” Absence from the school enables me to lose sight of the unimportant details of the work, and study it in a broader and more comprehensive manner than I could do on the grounds. This absence also brings me into contact with the best work being done in educational lines, and into contact with the best educators in the land.
passages.vernacular: 一年十二個月,我估平均有六個月離開塔斯基吉。雖然我咁多時間離開學校無疑有缺點,同時亦有些補償。工作嘅改變帶來某種休息。我享受喺火車上坐長途,當我獲准坐得舒服嘅地方。我喺火車上休息,除咗每班火車似乎都有嘅不可避免嘅人走近我,用而家熟悉嘅話:「呢位唔係布克·華盛頓嗎?我想向你介紹自己。」離開學校令我可以忽略工作嘅不重要細節,以比喺校園更廣泛、更全面嘅方式研究佢。呢種離開亦令我接觸到教育方面正在做嘅最好工作,同國內最好嘅教育家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一年十二個月,我猜平均有六個月離開塔斯基吉。雖然我那麼多時間離開學校無疑有缺點,同時也有些補償。工作的改變帶來某種休息。我享受在火車上坐長途,當我獲准坐得舒服的地方。我在火車上休息,除了每班火車似乎都有的不可避免的人走近我,用現在熟悉的話:「這位不是布克·華盛頓嗎?我想向你介紹自己。」離開學校使我可以忽略工作的不重要細節,以比在校園更廣泛、更全面的方式研究它。這種離開也使我接觸到教育方面正在做的最好工作,和國內最好的教育家。

passages.original: But, after all this is said, the time when I get the most solid rest and recreation is when I can be at Tuskegee, and, after our evening meal is over, can sit down, as is our custom, with my wife and Portia and Baker and Davidson, my three children, and read a story, or each take turns in telling a story. To me there is nothing on earth equal to that, although what is nearly equal to it is to go with them for an hour or more, as we like to do on Sunday afternoons, into the woods, where we can live for a while near the heart of nature, where no one can disturb or vex us, surrounded by pure air, the trees, the shrubbery, the flowers, and the sweet fragrance that springs from a hundred plants, enjoying the chirp of the crickets and the songs of the birds. This is solid rest.
passages.vernacular: 不過,講咗所有呢啲之後,我得到最紮實休息同娛樂嘅時間,係我喺塔斯基吉,晚餐之後,如我哋慣例,同我太太同波西婭、貝克同戴維森(我三個孩子)坐低,讀一個故事,或者輪流講故事。對我嚟講,世上冇咩比呢個更好,雖然差唔多一樣好嘅係同佢哋去樹林一個鐘或更多,如我哋喺星期日下午鍾意咁做,我哋可以喺嗰度接近大自然嘅心生活一陣,冇人可以打擾或煩擾我哋,被清新空氣、樹木、灌木、花朵,以及從一百種植物散發嘅甜美香氣包圍,享受蟋蟀嘅叫聲同鳥嘅歌聲。呢個係紮實休息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,說了所有這些之後,我得到最紮實休息和娛樂的時間,是我在塔斯基吉,晚飯之後,如我們慣例,與我妻子和波西婭、貝克和戴維森(我三個孩子)坐下,讀一個故事,或輪流講故事。對我來說,世上沒什麼比這個更好,雖然差不多一樣好的是與他們去樹林一個小時或更多,如我們在星期日下午喜歡這樣做,我們可以在那裡接近大自然的心生活一陣,沒人可以打擾或煩擾我們,被清新空氣、樹木、灌木、花朵,以及從一百種植物散發的甜美香氣包圍,享受蟋蟀的叫聲和鳥的歌聲。這是紮實休息。

passages.original: My garden, also, what little time I can be at Tuskegee, is another source of rest and enjoyment. Somehow I like, as often as possible, to touch nature, not something that is artificial or an imitation, but the real thing. When I can leave my office in time so that I can spend thirty or forty minutes in spading the ground, in planting seeds, in digging about the plants, I feel that I am coming into contact with something that is giving me strength for the many duties and hard places that await me out in the big world. I pity the man or woman who has never learned to enjoy nature and to get strength and inspiration out of it.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅花園,亦係我喺塔斯基吉嗰少少時間另一個休息同享受嘅來源。不知點解,我鍾意盡可能經常接觸大自然,唔係人為或模仿嘅嘢,而係真嘅。當我可以及時離開辦公室,花三四十分鐘鋤地、播種、挖植物周圍,我覺得我接觸緊某種嘢,畀我力量去面對外面大世界等我嘅許多職責同艱難處境。我同情從未學會享受大自然並從中得到力量同靈感嘅男女。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的花園,也是我在塔斯基吉那一點時間另一個休息和享受的來源。不知怎的,我喜歡盡可能經常接觸大自然,不是人為或模仿的東西,而是真的。當我可以及時離開辦公室,花三四十分鐘鋤地、播種、挖植物周圍,我覺得我接觸著某種東西,給我力量去面對外面大世界等我的許多職責和艱難處境。我同情從未學會享受大自然並從中得到力量和靈感的男女。

passages.original: Aside from the large number of fowls and animals kept by the school, I keep individually a number of pigs and fowls of the best grades, and in raising these I take a great deal of pleasure. I think the pig is my favourite animal. Few things are more satisfactory to me than a high-grade Berkshire or Poland China pig.
passages.vernacular: 除咗學校養嘅大量家禽同動物,我個人養一些最優品種嘅豬同家禽,養呢啲我得到好大樂趣。我諗豬係我最鍾意嘅動物。冇幾樣嘢比一隻優質嘅伯克夏或波蘭中國豬更令我滿意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了學校養的大量家禽和動物,我個人養一些最優品種的豬和家禽,養這些我得到很大樂趣。我想豬是我最喜歡的動物。沒幾樣東西比一隻優質的伯克夏或波蘭中國豬更使我滿意。

passages.original: Games I care little for. I have never seen a game of football. In cards I do not know one card from another. A game of old-fashioned marbles with my two boys, once in a while, is all I care for in this direction. I suppose I would care for games now if I had had any time in my youth to give to them, but that was not possible.
passages.vernacular: 遊戲我好少關心。我從未見過一場足球比賽。紙牌我唔識分辨每張。偶爾同我兩個兒子玩一場舊式彈珠,係我喺呢方面唯一關心嘅。我估如果我年輕時有時間投入,我而家會關心遊戲,不過係不可能嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 遊戲我很少關心。我從未見過一場足球比賽。紙牌我不會分辨每張。偶爾與我兩個兒子玩一場舊式彈珠,是我在這方面唯一關心的。我猜如果我年輕時有時間投入,我現在會關心遊戲,不過是不可能的。

passages.original: In 1893 I was married to Miss Margaret James Murray, a native of Mississippi, and a graduate of Fisk University, in Nashville, Tenn., who had come to Tuskegee as a teacher several years before, and at the time we were married was filling the position of Lady Principal. Not only is Mrs. Washington completely one with me in the work directly connected with the school, relieving me of many burdens and perplexities, but aside from her work on the school grounds, she carries on a mothers’ meeting in the town of Tuskegee, and a plantation work among the women, children, and men who live in a settlement connected with a large plantation about eight miles from Tuskegee. Both the mothers’ meeting and the plantation work are carried on, not only with a view to helping those who are directly reached, but also for the purpose of furnishing object-lessons in these two kinds of work that may be followed by our students when they go out into the world for their own life-work.
passages.vernacular: 1893年,我同瑪格麗特·詹姆斯·默里小姐結婚,佢係密西西比人,納什維爾菲斯克大學畢業生,幾年前來塔斯基吉做老師,我哋結婚時擔任女主任。華盛頓太太唔單止喺同學校直接有關嘅工作上完全同我一致,為我減輕好多負擔同困惑,除咗校園工作之外,佢喺塔斯基吉鎮辦母親聚會,並喺距離塔斯基吉大約八英里、一個大種植園相連嘅定居點,為居住嗰度嘅婦女、兒童同男人做種植園工作。母親聚會同種植園工作進行,唔單止為幫助直接接觸到嘅人,亦為提供呢兩類工作嘅示範,可以被我哋學生出到社會做自己終身事業時跟從。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 1893年,我與瑪格麗特·詹姆斯·默里小姐結婚,她是密西西比人,納什維爾菲斯克大學畢業生,幾年前來塔斯基吉做老師,我們結婚時擔任女主任。華盛頓太太不僅在與學校直接有關的工作上完全與我一致,為我減輕很多負擔和困惑,除了校園工作之外,她在塔斯基吉鎮辦母親聚會,並在距離塔斯基吉大約八英里、一個大種植園相連的定居點,為居住那裡的婦女、兒童和男人做種植園工作。母親聚會和種植園工作進行,不僅為幫助直接接觸到的人,也為提供這兩類工作的示範,可以被我們學生出到社會做自己終身事業時跟從。

passages.original: Aside from these two enterprises, Mrs. Washington is also largely responsible for a woman’s club at the school which brings together, twice a month, the women who live on the school grounds and those who live near, for the discussion of some important topic.
