She is also the President of what is known as the Federation of Southern Coloured Women’s Clubs, and is Chairman of the Executive Committee of the National Federation of Coloured Women’s Clubs.
passages.vernacular: 除咗呢兩項事業,華盛頓太太亦主要負責學校嘅婦女俱樂部,每月兩次召集住喺校園同附近嘅婦女,討論某個重要題目。佢亦係所謂南方有色人種婦女俱樂部聯合會嘅會長,同全國有色人種婦女俱樂部聯合會行政委員會主席。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了這兩項事業,華盛頓太太也主要負責學校的婦女俱樂部,每月兩次召集住在校園和附近的婦女,討論某個重要題目。她也是所謂南方有色人種婦女俱樂部聯合會的會長,和全國有色人種婦女俱樂部聯合會行政委員會主席。

passages.original: Portia, the oldest of my three children, has learned dressmaking. She has unusual ability in instrumental music. Aside from her studies at Tuskegee, she has already begun to teach there.
passages.vernacular: 波西婭,我三個孩子中最大,已經學識縫紉。佢有不尋常嘅器樂才能。除咗喺塔斯基吉嘅學習,佢已經開始喺嗰度教學。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波西婭,我三個孩子中最大,已經學會縫紉。她有不尋常的器樂才能。除了在塔斯基吉的學習,她已經開始在那裡教學。

passages.original: Booker Taliaferro is my next oldest child. Young as he is, he has already nearly mastered the brickmason’s trade. He began working at this trade when he was quite small, dividing his time between this and class work; and he has developed great skill in the trade and a fondness for it. He says that he is going to be an architect and brickmason. One of the most satisfactory letters that I have ever received from any one came to me from Booker last summer. When I left home for the summer, I told him that he must work at his trade half of each day, and that the other half of the day he could spend as he pleased. When I had been away from home two weeks, I received the following letter from him:
passages.vernacular: 布克·塔利亞費羅係我下一個最大嘅孩子。雖然佢咁細,已經幾乎掌握磚匠手藝。佢好細個就開始做呢門手藝,時間分配喺呢個同課堂工作;佢發展出好高嘅手藝技能同對佢嘅喜愛。佢話佢將會做建築師同磚匠。我從任何人收到最令人滿意嘅信之一,係去年夏天布克寫嚟嘅。我離家過夏天時,我話畀佢知,佢要每日一半時間做佢嘅手藝,另外一半時間可以隨佢喜歡咁用。我離家兩個星期後,收到佢以下嘅信:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 布克·塔利亞費羅是我下一個最大的孩子。雖然他那麼小,已經幾乎掌握磚匠手藝。他很小就開始做這門手藝,時間分配在這個和課堂工作;他發展出很高的手藝技能和對它的喜愛。他說他將會做建築師和磚匠。我從任何人收到最令人滿意的信之一,是去年夏天布克寫來的。我離家過夏天時,我告訴他,他要每天一半時間做他的手藝,另外一半時間可以隨他喜歡地用。我離家兩個星期後,收到他以下的信:

passages.original: Tuskegee, Alabama.
passages.vernacular: 阿拉巴馬塔斯基吉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 阿拉巴馬塔斯基吉。

passages.original: My dear Papa: Before you left home you told me to work at my trade half of each day. I like my work so much that I want to work at my trade all day. Besides, I want to earn all the money I can, so that when I go to another school I shall have money to pay my expenses.
passages.vernacular: 親愛嘅爸爸:你離家前話我每日做一半時間手藝。我好鍾意我嘅工作,我想成日做我嘅手藝。此外,我想盡可能賺錢,令我去另一間學校時有錢支付開支。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 親愛的爸爸:你離家前說我每天做一半時間手藝。我很喜歡我的工作,我想整天做我的手藝。此外,我想盡可能賺錢,使我去另一間學校時有錢支付開支。

passages.original: Your son,
passages.vernacular: 你嘅兒子,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的兒子,

passages.original: Booker.
passages.vernacular: 布克。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 布克。

passages.original: My youngest child, Ernest Davidson Washington, says that he is going to be a physician. In addition to going to school, where he studies books and has manual training, he regularly spends a portion of his time in the office of our resident physician, and has already learned to do many of the duties which pertain to a doctor’s office.
passages.vernacular: 我最細嘅孩子,歐內斯特·戴維森·華盛頓,話佢將會做醫生。除咗上學(喺嗰度學書本同手工訓練),佢定期花一部分時間喺我哋駐校醫生嘅辦公室,已經學識做醫生辦公室好多職責。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我最小的孩子,歐內斯特·戴維森·華盛頓,說他將會做醫生。除了上學(在那裡學書本和手工訓練),他定期花一部分時間在我們駐校醫生的辦公室,已經學會做醫生辦公室很多職責。

passages.original: The thing in my life which brings me the keenest regret is that my work in connection with public affairs keeps me for so much of the time away from my family, where, of all places in the world, I delight to be. I always envy the individual whose life-work is so laid that he can spend his evenings at home. I have sometimes thought that people who have this rare privilege do not appreciate it as they should. It is such a rest and relief to get away from crowds of people, and handshaking, and travelling, to get home, even if it be for but a very brief while.
passages.vernacular: 我人生中最令我深切遺憾嘅事,係我嘅公共事務工作令我大部分時間離開家人,而喺世上所有地方中,我最喜歡喺度。我總係羨慕終身事業安排成可以夜晚留喺屋企嘅人。我有時諗,擁有呢種罕見特權嘅人,冇好似佢哋應有咁欣賞。離開人群、握手同旅行,返屋企,即使只係好短時間,都係咁休息同解脫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我人生中最使我深切遺憾的事,是我的公共事務工作使我大部分時間離開家人,而在世上所有地方中,我最喜歡在這裡。我總是羨慕終身事業安排成可以夜晚留在家的人。我有時想,擁有這種罕見特權的人,沒像他們應有那樣欣賞。離開人群、握手和旅行,回家,即使只是很短時間,都是那麼休息和解脫。

passages.original: Another thing at Tuskegee out of which I get a great deal of pleasure and satisfaction is in the meeting with our students, and teachers, and their families, in the chapel for devotional exercises every evening at half-past eight, the last thing before retiring for the night. It is an inspiring sight when one stands on the platform there and sees before him eleven or twelve hundred earnest young men and women; and one cannot but feel that it is a privilege to help to guide them to a higher and more useful life.
passages.vernacular: 塔斯基吉另一件令我得到好大樂趣同滿足嘅事,係每晚八點半(就寢前最後一件事),喺禮拜堂同我哋學生、老師同佢哋嘅家人聚會進行靈修。企喺嗰度講台上見到面前一千一二百位認真嘅青年男女,係令人鼓舞嘅景象;一個人忍不住覺得,幫助引導佢哋過更高尚更有用嘅生活係特權。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 塔斯基吉另一件使我得到很大樂趣和滿足的事,是每晚八點半(就寢前最後一件事),在禮拜堂與我們學生、老師和他們的家人聚會進行靈修。站在那裡講台上看到面前一千一二百位認真的青年男女,是令人鼓舞的景象;一個人忍不住覺得,幫助引導他們過更高尚更有用的生活是特權。

passages.original: In the spring of 1899 there came to me what I might describe as almost the greatest surprise of my life. Some good ladies in Boston arranged a public meeting in the interests of Tuskegee, to be held in the Hollis Street Theatre. This meeting was attended by large numbers of the best people of Boston, of both races. Bishop Lawrence presided. In addition to an address made by myself, Mr. Paul Lawrence Dunbar read from his poems, and Dr. W.E.B. Du Bois read an original sketch.
passages.vernacular: 1899年春天,我得到一個可以形容為我一生最大驚喜之一嘅事。波士頓一些好心女士,為塔斯基吉嘅利益安排咗一個公眾聚會,喺霍利斯街戲院舉行。呢次聚會有波士頓兩個種族嘅最好人士大批出席。勞倫斯主教主持。除咗我自己嘅演說,保羅·勞倫斯·鄧巴朗讀佢嘅詩,W·E·B·杜波依斯博士朗讀一篇原創小品。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 1899年春天,我得到一個可以形容為我一生最大驚喜之一的事。波士頓一些好心女士,為塔斯基吉的利益安排了一個公眾聚會,在霍利斯街戲院舉行。這次聚會有波士頓兩個種族的最好人士大批出席。勞倫斯主教主持。除了我自己的演說,保羅·勞倫斯·鄧巴朗讀他的詩,W·E·B·杜波依斯博士朗讀一篇原創小品。

passages.original: Some of those who attended this meeting noticed that I seemed unusually tired, and some little time after the close of the meeting, one of the ladies who had been interested in it asked me in a casual way if I had ever been to Europe. I replied that I never had. She asked me if I had ever thought of going, and I told her no; that it was something entirely beyond me. This conversation soon passed out of my mind, but a few days afterward I was informed that some friends in Boston, including Mr. Francis J. Garrison, had raised a sum of money sufficient to pay all the expenses of Mrs. Washington and myself during a three or four months’ trip to Europe. It was added with emphasis that we must go. A year previous to this Mr. Garrison had attempted to get me to promise to go to Europe for a summer’s rest, with the understanding that he would be responsible for raising the money among his friends for the expenses of the trip. At that time such a journey seemed so entirely foreign to anything that I should ever be able to undertake that I did confess I did not give the matter very serious attention; but later Mr. Garrison joined his efforts to those of the ladies whom I have mentioned, and when their plans were made known to me Mr. Garrison not only had the route mapped out, but had, I believe, selected the steamer upon which we were to sail.
passages.vernacular: 一些出席呢次聚會嘅人留意到我似乎異常疲倦,聚會結束後一段時間,一位對聚會感興趣嘅女士隨意問我有冇去過歐洲。我答我從來冇有。佢問我有冇諗過去,我話冇;完全超出我能力。呢段對話好快從我腦海消失,不過幾日後我被告知,波士頓一些朋友(包括弗朗西斯·J·加里森先生)籌到一筆足夠支付華盛頓太太同我三四個月歐洲之行所有開支嘅錢。有人強調補充,我哋必須去。一年前,加里森先生曾嘗試令我承諾去歐洲夏季休息,條件係佢負責喺佢朋友當中籌集旅行開支。當時,呢種旅程似乎完全超出我可以承擔嘅任何事,我承認我冇認真留意;不過之後加里森先生連同我提過嘅女士一齊努力,當佢哋嘅計劃被告知我,加里森先生唔單止規劃好路線,我相信仲揀咗我哋要搭嘅輪船。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一些出席這次聚會的人留意到我似乎異常疲倦,聚會結束後一段時間,一位對聚會感興趣的女士隨意問我有沒有去過歐洲。我答我從來沒有。她問我有沒有想過去,我說沒有;完全超出我能力。這段對話很快從我腦海消失,不過幾天後我被告知,波士頓一些朋友(包括弗朗西斯·J·加里森先生)籌到一筆足夠支付華盛頓太太和我三四個月歐洲之行所有開支的錢。有人強調補充,我們必須去。一年前,加里森先生曾嘗試使我承諾去歐洲夏季休息,條件是他負責在他朋友當中籌集旅行開支。當時,這種旅程似乎完全超出我可以承擔的任何事,我承認我沒認真留意;不過之後加里森先生連同我提過的女士一起努力,當他們的計劃被告知我,加里森先生不僅規劃好路線,我相信還挑了我們要搭的輪船。

passages.original: The whole thing was so sudden and so unexpected that I was completely taken off my feet. I had been at work steadily for eighteen years in connection with Tuskegee, and I had never thought of anything else but ending my life in that way. Each day the school seemed to depend upon me more largely for its daily expenses, and I told these Boston friends that, while I thanked them sincerely for their thoughtfulness and generosity, I could not go to Europe, for the reason that the school could not live financially while I was absent. They then informed me that Mr. Henry L. Higginson, and some other good friends who I know do not want their names made public, were then raising a sum of money which would be sufficient to keep the school in operation while I was away. At this point I was compelled to surrender. Every avenue of escape had been closed.
passages.vernacular: 整件事咁突然咁出乎意料,令我完全站唔穩。我已經為塔斯基吉不斷工作十八年,從未諗過除咗咁結束我嘅生命之外嘅任何事。學校每日似乎越來越倚靠我支付日常開支,我話畀呢啲波士頓朋友知,雖然我真誠多謝佢哋嘅體貼同慷慨,我唔可以去歐洲,因為我不在期間學校財政上無法生存。佢哋然後告訴我,亨利·L·希金森先生,同一些我知道唔想公開名字嘅其他好朋友,正籌集足夠嘅錢,令學校喺我不在期間繼續運作。呢個時候我被迫投降。每條逃避嘅路都被封閉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整件事那麼突然那麼出乎意料,使我完全站不穩。我已經為塔斯基吉不斷工作十八年,從未想過除了這樣結束我的生命之外的任何事。學校每天似乎越來越倚靠我支付日常開支,我告訴這些波士頓朋友,雖然我真誠感謝他們的體貼和慷慨,我不可以去歐洲,因為我不在期間學校財政上無法生存。他們然後告訴我,亨利·L·希金森先生,和一些我知道不想公開名字的其他好朋友,正籌集足夠的錢,使學校在我不在期間繼續運作。這個時候我被迫投降。每條逃避的路都被封閉。

passages.original: Deep down in my heart the whole thing seemed more like a dream than like reality, and for a long time it was difficult for me to make myself believe that I was actually going to Europe. I had been born and largely reared in the lowest depths of slavery, ignorance, and poverty. In my childhood I had suffered for want of a place to sleep, for lack of food, clothing, and shelter. I had not had the privilege of sitting down to a dining-table until I was quite well grown. Luxuries had always seemed to me to be something meant for white people, not for my race. I had always regarded Europe, and London, and Paris, much as I regarded heaven. And now could it be that I was actually going to Europe? Such thoughts as these were constantly with me.
passages.vernacular: 內心深處,整件事似乎更似夢而唔係現實,好耐我好難令自己相信我真係去歐洲。我喺奴隸制、無知同貧窮嘅最底層出世並大部分成長。童年時,我因為冇地方瞓、冇食物、衣服同住所而受苦。我直到長大相當大,先有特權坐低食飯枱。奢侈品對我嚟講,一直似乎係為白人而設,唔係我種族。我一直視歐洲、倫敦同巴黎,同視天堂差唔多。而家真係我真係去歐洲?呢啲想法不斷伴隨我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 內心深處,整件事似乎更像夢而不是現實,很久我很難使自己相信我真是去歐洲。我在奴隸制、無知和貧窮的最底層出生並大部分成長。童年時,我因為沒地方睡、沒食物、衣服和住所而受苦。我直到長大相當大,才有特權坐下吃飯桌。奢侈品對我來說,一直似乎是為白人而設,不是我種族。我一直視歐洲、倫敦和巴黎,和視天堂差不多。現在真是我真是去歐洲?這些想法不斷伴隨我。

passages.original: Two other thoughts troubled me a good deal. I feared that people who heard that Mrs. Washington and I were going to Europe might not know all the circumstances, and might get the idea that we had become, as some might say, “stuck up,” and were trying to “show off.” I recalled that from my youth I had heard it said that too often, when people of my race reached any degree of success, they were inclined to unduly exalt themselves; to try and ape the wealthy, and in so doing to lose their heads. The fear that people might think this of us haunted me a good deal. Then, too, I could not see how my conscience would permit me to spare the time from my work and be happy. It seemed mean and selfish in me to be taking a vacation while others were at work, and while there was so much that needed to be done. From the time I could remember, I had always been at work, and I did not see how I could spend three or four months in doing nothing. The fact was that I did not know how to take a vacation.
passages.vernacular: 另外兩個想法令我好困擾。我擔心聽到華盛頓太太同我去歐洲嘅人,可能唔知道所有情況,可能以為我哋變得,如有人會講,「自大」,試圖「炫耀」。我記得從年輕時我就聽過,太多時候,我種族嘅人達到某種成功時,傾向過分抬高自己;試圖模仿富人,咁做令佢哋失去理智。人們可能咁諗我哋嘅恐懼,好困擾我。此外,我睇唔到我嘅良心點樣容許我從工作抽出時間而快樂。其他人工作、而且有咁多嘢需要做時,我放假似乎刻薄自私。從我記得開始,我一直工作,我睇唔到我點樣可以花三四個月咩都唔做。事實係我唔知道點樣放假。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 另外兩個想法使我很困擾。我擔心聽到華盛頓太太和我去歐洲的人,可能不知道所有情況,可能以為我們變得,如有人會說,「自大」,試圖「炫耀」。我記得從年輕時我就聽過,太多時候,我種族的人達到某種成功時,傾向過分抬高自己;試圖模仿富人,這樣做使他們失去理智。人們可能這樣想我們的恐懼,很困擾我。此外,我看不到我的良心怎樣容許我從工作抽出時間而快樂。其他人工作、而且有那麼多事需要做時,我放假似乎刻薄自私。從我記得開始,我一直工作,我看不到我怎樣可以花三四個月什麼都不做。事實是我不知道怎樣放假。

passages.original: Mrs. Washington had much the same difficulty in getting away, but she was anxious to go because she thought that I needed the rest. There were many important National questions bearing upon the life of the race which were being agitated at that time, and this made it all the harder for us to decide to go. We finally gave our Boston friends our promise that we would go, and then they insisted that the date of our departure be set as soon as possible. So we decided upon May 10. My good friend Mr. Garrison kindly took charge of all the details necessary for the success of the trip, and he, as well as other friends, gave us a great number of letters of introduction to people in France and England, and made other arrangements for our comfort and convenience abroad. Good-bys were said at Tuskegee, and we were in New York May 9, ready to sail the next day. Our daughter Portia, who was then studying in South Framingham, Mass., came to New York to see us off. Mr. Scott, my secretary, came with me to New York, in order that I might clear up the last bit of business before I left. Other friends also came to New York to see us off. Just before we went on board the steamer another pleasant surprise came to us in the form of a letter from two generous ladies, stating that they had decided to give us the money with which to erect a new building to be used in properly housing all our industries for girls at Tuskegee.
passages.vernacular: 華盛頓太太離開都有同樣困難,不過佢渴望去,因為佢認為我需要休息。當時有好多關乎種族生活嘅重要全國問題正被鼓動,令我哋更難決定去。我哋最終向波士頓朋友承諾去,然後佢哋堅持我哋嘅出發日期盡快定。於是我哋決定5月10日。我嘅好朋友加里森先生好心咁負責旅行成功所需嘅所有細節,佢同其他朋友畀咗我哋大批畀法國同英國人嘅介紹信,並安排我哋喺外國嘅舒適同方便。喺塔斯基吉道別後,我哋5月9日喺紐約,準備第二日開船。我哋嘅女兒波西婭,當時喺麻薩諸塞南弗雷明漢讀書,來紐約送我哋。我嘅秘書斯科特先生同我去紐約,令我可以在離開前清理最後一點事務。其他朋友亦來紐約送我哋。就喺我哋上船前,另一個愉快驚喜以兩位慷慨女士一封信嘅形式來到,話佢哋決定畀我哋錢,興建一座新建築,用於適當安置我哋塔斯基吉所有女孩工業。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 華盛頓太太離開也有同樣困難,不過她渴望去,因為她認為我需要休息。當時有很多關乎種族生活的重要全國問題正被鼓動,使我們更難決定去。我們最終向波士頓朋友承諾去,然後他們堅持我們的出發日期盡快定。於是我們決定5月10日。我的好朋友加里森先生好心地負責旅行成功所需的所有細節,他和其他朋友給了我們大批給法國和英國人的介紹信,並安排我們在外國的舒適和方便。在塔斯基吉道別後,我們5月9日在紐約,準備第二天開船。我們的女兒波西婭,當時在麻薩諸塞南弗雷明漢讀書,來紐約送我們。我的秘書斯科特先生與我去紐約,使我可以在離開前清理最後一點事務。其他朋友也來紐約送我們。就在我們上船前,另一個愉快驚喜以兩位慷慨女士一封信的形式來到,說她們決定給我們錢,興建一座新建築,用於適當安置我們塔斯基吉所有女孩工業。

passages.original: We were to sail on the Friesland, of the Red Star Line, and a beautiful vessel she was. We went on board just before noon, the hour of sailing. I had never before been on board a large ocean steamer, and the feeling which took possession of me when I found myself there is rather hard to describe. It was a feeling, I think, of awe mingled with delight. We were agreeably surprised to find that the captain, as well as several of the other officers, not only knew who we were, but was expecting us and gave us a pleasant greeting. There were several passengers whom we knew, including Senator Sewell, of New Jersey, and Edward Marshall, the newspaper correspondent. I had just a little fear that we would not be treated civilly by some of the passengers. This fear was based upon what I had heard other people of my race, who had crossed the ocean, say about unpleasant experiences in crossing the ocean in American vessels. But in our case, from the captain down to the most humble servant, we were treated with the greatest kindness. Nor was this kindness confined to those who were connected with the steamer; it was shown by all the passengers also. There were not a few Southern men and women on board, and they were as cordial as those from other parts of the country.
passages.vernacular: 我哋要搭紅星航線嘅「弗里斯蘭號」,係一艘漂亮嘅船。我哋喺開船時間正午前上船。我從未喺大型遠洋輪船上,發現自己喺嗰度時佔據我嘅感覺好難描述。我諗係敬畏混合喜悅嘅感覺。我哋愉快驚訝地發現,船長同其他幾位官員,唔單止知道我哋係邊個,仲預期我哋,友好咁問候我哋。有幾位我哋認識嘅乘客,包括新澤西嘅休厄爾參議員同報紙記者愛德華·馬歇爾。我有少少擔心,一些乘客唔會禮貌咁對待我哋。呢個擔心基於我聽過其他橫渡大洋嘅我種族人,講喺美國船隻橫渡大洋嘅不愉快經歷。不過就我哋而言,從船長到最卑微嘅僕人,我哋都受到最大嘅善意對待。呢種善意唔限於同輪船有關嘅人;所有乘客亦表現出。船上有不少南方男女,佢哋同國內其他地方嘅人一樣熱情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們要搭紅星航線的「弗里斯蘭號」,是一艘漂亮的船。我們在開船時間正午前上船。我從未在大型遠洋輪船上,發現自己在那裡時佔據我的感覺很難描述。我想是敬畏混合喜悅的感覺。我們愉快驚訝地發現,船長和其他幾位官員,不僅知道我們是誰,還預期我們,友好地問候我們。有幾位我們認識的乘客,包括新澤西的休厄爾參議員和報紙記者愛德華·馬歇爾。我有一點擔心,一些乘客不會禮貌地對待我們。這個擔心基於我聽過其他橫渡大洋的我種族人,講在美國船隻橫渡大洋的不愉快經歷。不過就我們而言,從船長到最卑微的僕人,我們都受到最大的善意對待。這種善意不限於與輪船有關的人;所有乘客也表現出。船上有不少南方男女,他們與國內其他地方的人一樣熱情。

passages.original: As soon as the last good-bys were said, and the steamer had cut loose from the wharf, the load of care, anxiety, and responsibility which I had carried for eighteen years began to lift itself from my shoulders at the rate, it seemed to me, of a pound a minute. It was the first time in all those years that I had felt, even in a measure, free from care; and my feeling of relief it is hard to describe on paper. Added to this was the delightful anticipation of being in Europe soon. It all seemed more like a dream than like a reality.
passages.vernacular: 最後嘅告別一說完,輪船離開碼頭,我背咗十八年嘅憂慮、焦慮同責任嘅重擔,開始以我覺得每分鐘一磅嘅速度從我肩膀上升起。呢十八年嚟,我第一次覺得,甚至某程度上,擺脫憂慮;我嘅解脫感好難用文字描述。加上就快到歐洲嘅愉快期待。全部似乎更似夢而唔係現實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後的告別一說完,輪船離開碼頭,我背了十八年的憂慮、焦慮和責任的重擔,開始以我覺得每分鐘一磅的速度從我肩膀上升起。這十八年來,我第一次覺得,甚至某種程度上,擺脫憂慮;我的解脫感很難用文字描述。加上就快到歐洲的愉快期待。全部似乎更像夢而不是現實。

passages.original: Mr. Garrison had thoughtfully arranged to have us have one of the most comfortable rooms on the ship. The second or third day out I began to sleep, and I think that I slept at the rate of fifteen hours a day during the remainder of the ten days’ passage. Then it was that I began to understand how tired I really was. These long sleeps I kept up for a month after we landed on the other side. It was such an unusual feeling to wake up in the morning and realize that I had no engagements; did not have to take a train at a certain hour; did not have an appointment to meet some one, or to make an address, at a certain hour. How different all this was from the experiences that I have been through when travelling, when I have sometimes slept in three different beds in a single night!
passages.vernacular: 加里森先生貼心咁安排我哋有船上最舒適嘅房間之一。出海第二三日,我開始瞓,我諗十日航程餘下時間我每日瞓十五個鐘。嗰時我先開始明白我真係幾疲倦。呢啲長覺我哋上岸後保持咗一個月。朝早起身,意識到冇約會;唔使喺某個鐘數搭火車;冇約定喺某個鐘數見某人或發表演說,係咁不尋常嘅感覺。同我旅行時經歷過嘅,有時一晚瞓三張唔同嘅床,係幾唔同!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 加里森先生貼心地安排我們有船上最舒適的房間之一。出海第二三天,我開始睡,我想十天航程餘下時間我每天睡十五個小時。那時我才開始明白我真是多疲倦。這些長覺我們上岸後保持了一個月。早上起身,意識到沒約會;不用在某個鐘數搭火車;沒約定在某個鐘數見某人或發表演說,是那麼不尋常的感覺。與我旅行時經歷過的,有時一晚睡三張不同的床,是多不同!

passages.original: When Sunday came, the captain invited me to conduct the religious services, but, not being a minister, I declined. The passengers, however, began making requests that I deliver an address to them in the dining-saloon some time during the voyage, and this I consented to do. Senator Sewell presided at this meeting. After ten days of delightful weather, during which I was not seasick for a day, we landed at the interesting old city of Antwerp, in Belgium.
passages.vernacular: 星期日到咗,船長邀請我主持宗教禮拜,不過我唔係牧師,婉拒。不過,乘客開始要求我喺航程中某個時間,喺飯廳向佢哋演講,我同意咗。休厄爾參議員主持呢次聚會。十日愉快天氣之後,期間我冇一日暈船,我哋登陸有趣嘅比利時古城安特衛普。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期日到了,船長邀請我主持宗教禮拜,不過我不是牧師,婉拒。不過,乘客開始要求我在航程中某個時間,在飯廳向他們演講,我同意了。休厄爾參議員主持這次聚會。十天愉快天氣之後,期間我沒一天暈船,我們登陸有趣的比利時古城安特衛普。

passages.original: The next day after we landed happened to be one of those numberless holidays which the people of those countries are in the habit of observing. It was a bright, beautiful day. Our room in the hotel faced the main public square, and the sights there—the people coming in from the country with all kinds of beautiful flowers to sell, the women coming in with their dogs drawing large, brightly polished cans filled with milk, the people streaming into the cathedral—filled me with a sense of newness that I had never before experienced.
passages.vernacular: 我哋登陸第二日,碰巧係嗰啲國家人民習慣慶祝嘅無數假日之一。係晴朗美麗嘅日子。我哋酒店嘅房間面向主要公共廣場,嗰度嘅景象——人們從鄉下來賣各種美麗嘅花,婦女帶住狗拉住大而閃亮擦亮嘅牛奶罐,人們湧入大教堂——令我充滿一種我從未經歷過嘅新鮮感。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們登陸第二天,碰巧是那些國家人民習慣慶祝的無數假日之一。是晴朗美麗的日子。我們酒店的房間面向主要公共廣場,那裡的景象——人們從鄉下來賣各種美麗的花,婦女帶著狗拉著大而閃亮擦亮的牛奶罐,人們湧入大教堂——使我充滿一種我從未經歷過的新鮮感。

passages.original: After spending some time in Antwerp, we were invited to go with a part of a half-dozen persons on a trip through Holland. This party included Edward Marshall and some American artists who had come over on the same steamer with us. We accepted the invitation, and enjoyed the trip greatly. I think it was all the more interesting and instructive because we went for most of the way on one of the slow, old-fashioned canal-boats. This gave us an opportunity of seeing and studying the real life of the people in the country districts. We went in this way as far as Rotterdam, and later went to The Hague, where the Peace Conference was then in session, and where we were kindly received by the American representatives.
passages.vernacular: 喺安特衛普花咗一些時間後,我哋被邀請同一批大約六個人嘅隊伍去荷蘭旅行。呢個隊伍包括愛德華·馬歇爾同一些同我哋搭同一艘輪船嚟嘅美國藝術家。我哋接受邀請,非常享受旅行。我諗佢更有趣更有教益,因為我哋大部分路程搭慢速舊式運河船。呢個畀我哋機會見到同研究鄉村地區人民嘅真實生活。我哋咁去到鹿特丹,之後去海牙,和平會議當時正在舉行,我哋受到美國代表好心接待。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在安特衛普花了一些時間後,我們被邀請與一批大約六個人的隊伍去荷蘭旅行。這個隊伍包括愛德華·馬歇爾和一些與我們搭同一艘輪船來的美國藝術家。我們接受邀請,非常享受旅行。我想它更有趣更有教益,因為我們大部分路程搭慢速舊式運河船。這給我們機會看到和研究鄉村地區人民的真實生活。我們這樣去到鹿特丹,之後去海牙,和平會議當時正在舉行,我們受到美國代表好心接待。

passages.original: The thing that impressed itself most on me in Holland was the thoroughness of the agriculture and the excellence of the Holstein cattle. I never knew, before visiting Holland, how much it was possible for people to get out of a small plot of ground. It seemed to me that absolutely no land was wasted. It was worth a trip to Holland, too, just to get a sight of three or four hundred fine Holstein cows grazing in one of those intensely green fields.
passages.vernacular: 喺荷蘭令我印象最深嘅,係農業嘅徹底同荷斯坦牛嘅優秀。我去荷蘭之前,從未知道人們可以從一小塊土地得到幾多。我覺得絕對冇土地被浪費。去荷蘭一趟都值得,單單睇到三四百頭優質荷斯坦牛喺一片極度翠綠嘅田野吃草。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在荷蘭使我印象最深的,是農業的徹底和荷斯坦牛的優秀。我去荷蘭之前,從未知道人們可以從一小塊土地得到多少。我覺得絕對沒土地被浪費。去荷蘭一趟都值得,單單看到三四百頭優質荷斯坦牛在一片極度翠綠的田野吃草。

passages.original: From Holland we went to Belgium, and made a hasty trip through that country, stopping at Brussels, where we visited the battlefield of Waterloo. From Belgium we went direct to Paris, where we found that Mr. Theodore Stanton, the son of Mrs. Elizabeth Cady Stanton, had kindly provided accommodations for us. We had barely got settled in Paris before an invitation came to me from the University Club of Paris to be its guest at a banquet which was soon to be given. The other guests were ex-President Benjamin Harrison and Archbishop Ireland, who were in Paris at the time. The American Ambassador, General Horace Porter, presided at the banquet. My address on this occasion seemed to give satisfaction to those who heard it. General Harrison kindly devoted a large portion of his remarks at dinner to myself and to the influence of the work at Tuskegee on the American race question. After my address at this banquet other invitations came to me, but I declined the most of them, knowing that if I accepted them all, the object of my visit would be defeated. I did, however, consent to deliver an address in the American chapel the following Sunday morning, and at this meeting General Harrison, General Porter, and other distinguished Americans were present.
passages.vernacular: 從荷蘭我哋去比利時,匆忙穿越該國,喺布魯塞爾停留,我哋喺嗰度參觀滑鐵盧戰場。從比利時我哋直接去巴黎,我哋發現伊麗莎白·卡迪·斯坦頓夫人嘅兒子西奧多·斯坦頓先生,好心為我哋提供咗住宿。我哋剛喺巴黎安頓好,巴黎大學俱樂部就邀請我做佢哋即將舉行嘅宴會嘅客人。其他客人係前總統本傑明·哈里森同愛爾蘭大主教,佢哋當時喺巴黎。美國大使霍勒斯·波特將軍主持宴會。我喺呢個場合嘅演說似乎令聽眾滿意。哈里森將軍好心喺晚餐中將佢好大部分講話用於我同塔斯基吉工作對美國種族問題嘅影響。我喺呢次宴會演說後,有其他邀請來到,不過我婉拒大部分,知道如果我全部接受,我探訪嘅目的就會落空。不過我確實同意第二個星期日朝早喺美國禮拜堂發表演說,哈里森將軍、波特將軍同其他傑出美國人在場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從荷蘭我們去比利時,匆忙穿越該國,在布魯塞爾停留,我們在那裡參觀滑鐵盧戰場。從比利時我們直接去巴黎,我們發現伊麗莎白·卡迪·斯坦頓夫人的兒子西奧多·斯坦頓先生,好心為我們提供了住宿。我們剛在巴黎安頓好,巴黎大學俱樂部就邀請我做他們即將舉行的宴會的客人。其他客人是前總統本傑明·哈里森和愛爾蘭大主教,他們當時在巴黎。美國大使霍勒斯·波特將軍主持宴會。我在這個場合的演說似乎使聽眾滿意。哈里森將軍好心在晚餐中將他很大部分講話用於我和塔斯基吉工作對美國種族問題的影響。我在這次宴會演說後,有其他邀請來到,不過我婉拒大部分,知道如果我全部接受,我探訪的目的就會落空。不過我確實同意第二個星期日早上在美國禮拜堂發表演說,哈里森將軍、波特將軍和其他傑出美國人在場。

passages.original: Later we received a formal call from the American Ambassador, and were invited to attend a reception at his residence. At this reception we met many Americans, among them Justices Fuller and Harlan, of the United States Supreme Court. During our entire stay of a month in Paris, both the American Ambassador and his wife, as well as several other Americans, were very kind to us.
passages.vernacular: 之後我哋收到美國大使嘅正式拜訪,被邀請出席佢住所嘅招待會。喺呢個招待會,我哋見到好多美國人,包括美國最高法院嘅富勒大法官同哈倫大法官。我哋喺巴黎整整一個月逗留期間,美國大使同佢太太,以及其他幾位美國人,都對我哋好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 之後我們收到美國大使的正式拜訪,被邀請出席他住所的招待會。在這個招待會,我們見到很多美國人,包括美國最高法院的富勒大法官和哈倫大法官。我們在巴黎整整一個月逗留期間,美國大使和他太太,以及其他幾位美國人,都對我們很好。

passages.original: While in Paris we saw a good deal of the now famous American Negro painter, Mr. Henry O. Tanner, whom we had formerly known in America. It was very satisfactory to find how well known Mr. Tanner was in the field of art, and to note the high standing which all classes accorded to him. When we told some Americans that we were going to the Luxembourg Palace to see a painting by an American Negro, it was hard to convince them that a Negro had been thus honoured. I do not believe that they were really convinced of the fact until they saw the picture for themselves. My acquaintance with Mr. Tanner reenforced in my mind the truth which I am constantly trying to impress upon our students at Tuskegee—and on our people throughout the country, as far as I can reach them with my voice—that any man, regardless of colour, will be recognized and rewarded just in proportion as he learns to do something well—learns to do it better than some one else—however humble the thing may be. As I have said, I believe that my race will succeed in proportion as it learns to do a common thing in an uncommon manner; learns to do a thing so thoroughly that no one can improve upon what it has done; learns to make its services of indispensable value. This was the spirit that inspired me in my first effort at Hampton, when I was given the opportunity to sweep and dust that schoolroom. In a degree I felt that my whole future life depended upon the thoroughness with which I cleaned that room, and I was determined to do it so well that no one could find any fault with the job. Few people ever stopped, I found, when looking at his pictures, to inquire whether Mr. Tanner was a Negro painter, a French painter, or a German painter. They simply knew that he was able to produce something which the world wanted—a great painting—and the matter of his colour did not enter into their minds. When a Negro girl learns to cook, to wash dishes, to sew, or write a book, or a Negro boy learns to groom horses, or to grow sweet potatoes, or to produce butter, or to build a house, or to be able to practise medicine, as well or better than some one else, they will be rewarded regardless of race or colour. In the long run, the world is going to have the best, and any difference in race, religion, or previous history will not long keep the world from what it wants.
passages.vernacular: 喺巴黎期間,我哋同而家著名嘅美國黑人畫家亨利·O·坦納先生見過好多面,我哋之前喺美國認識佢。發現坦納先生喺藝術界咁出名,留意到各階層對佢嘅高度評價,令人好滿意。當我哋話畀一些美國人聽,我哋要去盧森堡宮睇一位美國黑人嘅畫,好難令佢哋相信一個黑人受到咁嘅榮譽。我唔相信佢哋真係被說服,直到佢哋自己見到畫。我同坦納先生嘅相識,加強咗我思想中我不斷試圖令塔斯基吉學生印象深刻——以及我嘅聲音可以到達之處全國我哋人民——嘅真理:任何人,無論膚色,都會按佢學會做好某事、做得比別人更好(無論幾卑微)嘅程度而被認可同獎賞。正如我所講,我相信我嘅種族會按佢學會以不尋常嘅方式做普通事、學會徹底做事令冇人可以改進佢所做嘅、學會令其服務有不可或缺嘅價值嘅程度而成功。呢個係我喺漢普頓第一次努力(被畀機會掃同抹嗰間課室)時啟發我嘅精神。某程度上,我覺得我整個將來人生,取決於我清潔嗰間房間嘅徹底程度,我決心做到好到冇人可以挑剔。我發現,好少人睇佢嘅畫時,停低問坦納先生係黑人畫家、法國畫家或者德國畫家。佢哋只係知道佢能夠生產世界想要嘅嘢——一幅偉大嘅畫——而佢嘅膚色問題冇進入佢哋腦海。當一個黑人女孩學會煮食、洗碟、縫紉、或寫書,或一個黑人男孩學會餵馬、種番薯、生產牛油、建屋、或行醫,同別人一樣好或更好,佢哋會被獎賞,無論種族或膚色。長遠嚟講,世界會得到最好,任何種族、宗教或之前歷史嘅差別,唔會長時間令世界得不到佢想要嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在巴黎期間,我們與現在著名的美國黑人畫家亨利·O·坦納先生見過很多面,我們之前在美國認識他。發現坦納先生在藝術界那麼出名,留意到各階層對他的高度評價,令人很滿意。當我們告訴一些美國人,我們要去盧森堡宮看一位美國黑人的畫,很難使他們相信一個黑人受到這樣的榮譽。我不相信他們真是被說服,直到他們自己看到畫。我與坦納先生的相識,加強了我思想中我不斷試圖使塔斯基吉學生印象深刻——以及我的聲音可以到達之處全國我們人民——的真理:任何人,無論膚色,都會按他學會做好某事、做得比別人更好(無論多卑微)的程度而被認可和獎賞。正如我所說,我相信我的種族會按它學會以不尋常的方式做普通事、學會徹底做事使沒人可以改進它所做的、學會使其服務有不可或缺的價值的程度而成功。這是我在漢普頓第一次努力(被給機會掃和抹那間課室)時啟發我的精神。某種程度上,我覺得我整個將來人生,取決於我清潔那間房間的徹底程度,我決心做到好到沒人可以挑剔。我發現,很少人看他的畫時,停下問坦納先生是黑人畫家、法國畫家或德國畫家。他們只是知道他能夠生產世界想要的東西——一幅偉大的畫——而他的膚色問題沒進入他們腦海。當一個黑人女孩學會煮食、洗碟、縫紉、或寫書,或一個黑人男孩學會餵馬、種番薯、生產牛油、建屋、或行醫,與別人一樣好或更好,他們會被獎賞,無論種族或膚色。長遠來說,世界會得到最好,任何種族、宗教或之前歷史的差別,不會長時間使世界得不到它想要的。

passages.original: I think that the whole future of my race hinges on the question as to whether or not it can make itself of such indispensable value that the people in the town and the state where we reside will feel that our presence is necessary to the happiness and well-being of the community. No man who continues to add something to the material, intellectual, and moral well-being of the place in which he lives is long left without proper reward. This is a great human law which cannot be permanently nullified.
passages.vernacular: 我諗我種族嘅整個將來取決於,可唔可以令自己有不可或缺嘅價值,令我哋居住嘅鎮同州嘅人覺得,我哋嘅存在對社區嘅快樂同福祉係必要嘅。冇人不斷為佢所住地方嘅物質、智力同道德福祉增添嘢,而長時間得不到適當獎賞。呢個係偉大嘅人類法則,無法永久廢除。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我種族的整個將來取決於,可不可以使自己有不可或缺的價值,使我們居住的鎮和州的人覺得,我們的存在對社區的快樂和福祉是必要的。沒人不斷為他所住地方的物質、智力和道德福祉增添東西,而長時間得不到適當獎賞。這是偉大的人類法則,無法永久廢除。

passages.original: The love of pleasure and excitement which seems in a large measure to possess the French people impressed itself upon me. I think they are more noted in this respect than is true of the people of my own race. In point of morality and moral earnestness I do not believe that the French are ahead of my own race in America. Severe competition and the great stress of life have led them to learn to do things more thoroughly and to exercise greater economy; but time, I think, will bring my race to the same point. In the matter of truth and high honour I do not believe that the average Frenchman is ahead of the American Negro; while so far as mercy and kindness to dumb animals go, I believe that my race is far ahead. In fact, when I left France, I had more faith in the future of the black man in America than I had ever possessed.
passages.vernacular: 法國人民似乎好大程度被擁有嘅愛享樂同激動令我印象深刻。我諗佢哋喺呢方面比我自己種族嘅人更出名。就道德同道德誠摯而言,我唔相信法國人領先我喺美國嘅種族。激烈競爭同生活大壓力令佢哋學會更徹底做事同運用更大節儉;不過我諗時間會令我種族達到同一點。就真誠同高尚榮譽而言,我唔相信普通法國人領先美國黑人;至於對啞巴動物嘅仁慈同善意,我相信我嘅種族遠遠領先。事實上,我離開法國時,對美國黑人嘅將來比我曾經擁有嘅更有信心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 法國人民似乎很大程度被擁有的愛享樂和激動使我印象深刻。我想他們在這方面比我自己種族的人更出名。就道德和道德誠摯而言,我不相信法國人領先我在美國的種族。激烈競爭和生活大壓力使他們學會更徹底做事和運用更大節儉;不過我想時間會使我種族達到同一點。就真誠和高尚榮譽而言,我不相信普通法國人領先美國黑人;至於對啞巴動物的仁慈和善意,我相信我的種族遠遠領先。事實上,我離開法國時,對美國黑人的將來比我曾經擁有的更有信心。

passages.original: From Paris we went to London, and reached there early in July, just about the height of the London social season. Parliament was in session, and there was a great deal of gaiety. Mr. Garrison and other friends had provided us with a large number of letters of introduction, and they had also sent letters to other persons in different parts of the United Kingdom, apprising these people of our coming. Very soon after reaching London we were flooded with invitations to attend all manner of social functions, and a great many invitations came to me asking that I deliver public addresses. The most of these invitations I declined, for the reason that I wanted to rest. Neither were we able to accept more than a small proportion of the other invitations. The Rev. Dr. Brooke Herford and Mrs. Herford, whom I had known in Boston, consulted with the American Ambassador, the Hon. Joseph Choate, and arranged for me to speak at a public meeting to be held in Essex Hall. Mr. Choate kindly consented to preside. The meeting was largely attended. There were many distinguished persons present, among them several members of Parliament, including Mr. James Bryce, who spoke at the meeting. What the American Ambassador said in introducing me, as well as a synopsis of what I said, was widely published in England and in the American papers at the time. Dr. and Mrs. Herford gave Mrs. Washington and myself a reception, at which we had the privilege of meeting some of the best people in England. Throughout our stay in London Ambassador Choate was most kind and attentive to us. At the Ambassador’s reception I met, for the first time, Mark Twain.
passages.vernacular: 從巴黎我哋去倫敦,7月初到達,正係倫敦社交季節頂峰。議會在開會,有好多歡樂。加里森先生同其他朋友為我哋提供大量介紹信,亦寄信畀聯合王國不同地方嘅其他人,通知佢哋我哋嘅到來。到倫敦後好快,我哋被邀請出席各種社交場合嘅邀請淹沒,好多邀請要我發表公眾演說。大部分呢啲邀請我婉拒,因為我想休息。我哋亦只能夠接受其他邀請嘅一小部分。我喺波士頓認識嘅布魯克·赫福德牧師博士同赫福德夫人,同美國大使約瑟夫·喬特先生商量,安排我喺艾塞克斯廳舉行嘅公眾會議演說。喬特先生好心同意主持。會議出席人數好多。有好多傑出人士在場,包括幾位議員,包括詹姆斯·布萊斯先生,佢喺會議發言。美國大使介紹我時所講嘅,以及我所講嘅概要,當時喺英國同美國報紙廣泛發表。赫福德博士同夫人為華盛頓太太同我舉行招待會,我哋有幸喺嗰度認識英國一些最好嘅人。我哋喺倫敦整個逗留期間,喬特大使對我哋最好最留心。喺大使嘅招待會,我第一次見到馬克·吐溫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從巴黎我們去倫敦,7月初到達,正是倫敦社交季節頂峰。議會在開會,有很多歡樂。加里森先生和其他朋友為我們提供大量介紹信,也寄信給聯合王國不同地方的其他人,通知他們我們的到來。到倫敦後很快,我們被邀請出席各種社交場合的邀請淹沒,很多邀請要我發表公眾演說。大部分這些邀請我婉拒,因為我想休息。我們也只能夠接受其他邀請的一小部分。我在波士頓認識的布魯克·赫福德牧師博士和赫福德夫人,與美國大使約瑟夫·喬特先生商量,安排我在艾塞克斯廳舉行的公眾會議演說。喬特先生好心同意主持。會議出席人數很多。有很多傑出人士在場,包括幾位議員,包括詹姆斯·布萊斯先生,他在會議發言。美國大使介紹我時所說的,以及我所說的概要,當時在英國和美國報紙廣泛發表。赫福德博士和夫人為華盛頓太太和我舉行招待會,我們有幸在那裡認識英國一些最好的人。我們在倫敦整個逗留期間,喬特大使對我們最好最留心。在大使的招待會,我第一次見到馬克·吐溫。

passages.original: We were the guests several times of Mrs. T. Fisher Unwin, the daughter of the English statesman, Richard Cobden. It seemed as if both Mr. and Mrs. Unwin could not do enough for our comfort and happiness. Later, for nearly a week, we were the guests of the daughter of John Bright, now Mrs. Clark, of Street, England. Both Mr. and Mrs. Clark, with their daughter, visited us at Tuskegee the next year. In Birmingham, England, we were the guests for several days of Mr. Joseph Sturge, whose father was a great abolitionist and friend of Whittier and Garrison. It was a great privilege to meet throughout England those who had known and honoured the late William Lloyd Garrison, the Hon. Frederick Douglass, and other abolitionists. The English abolitionists with whom we came in contact never seemed to tire of talking about these two Americans. Before going to England I had had no proper conception of the deep interest displayed by the abolitionists of England in the cause of freedom, nor did I realize the amount of substantial help given by them.
passages.vernacular: 我哋幾次做英國政治家理查德·科布登嘅女兒T·費舍爾·安溫夫人嘅客人。似乎安溫先生同夫人為我哋嘅舒適同快樂做得唔夠。之後,近一個星期,我哋係約翰·布賴特嘅女兒(現為英國斯特里特嘅克拉克夫人)嘅客人。克拉克先生同夫人連同佢哋嘅女兒,第二年探訪我哋喺塔斯基吉。喺英國伯明翰,我哋做約瑟夫·斯特奇先生嘅客人幾日,佢爸爸係偉大廢奴者,同惠蒂埃同加里森嘅朋友。喺英國各地,能夠見到認識同尊敬已故威廉·勞埃德·加里森、尊敬嘅弗雷德里克·道格拉斯同其他廢奴者嘅人,係極大特權。我哋接觸到嘅英國廢奴者,似乎從不厭倦講呢兩位美國人。去英國之前,我對英國廢奴者對自由事業顯示嘅深切興趣冇適當概念,亦冇意識到佢哋給予嘅實質幫助數量。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們幾次做英國政治家理查德·科布登的女兒T·費舍爾·安溫夫人的客人。似乎安溫先生和夫人為我們的舒適和快樂做得不夠。之後,近一個星期,我們是約翰·布賴特的女兒(現為英國斯特里特的克拉克夫人)的客人。克拉克先生和夫人連同他們的女兒,第二年探訪我們在塔斯基吉。在英國伯明翰,我們做約瑟夫·斯特奇先生的客人幾天,他父親是偉大廢奴者,和惠蒂埃和加里森的朋友。在英國各地,能夠見到認識和尊敬已故威廉·勞埃德·加里森、尊敬的弗雷德里克·道格拉斯和其他廢奴者的人,是極大特權。我們接觸到的英國廢奴者,似乎從不厭倦說這兩位美國人。去英國之前,我對英國廢奴者對自由事業顯示的深切興趣沒適當概念,也沒意識到他們給予的實質幫助數量。

passages.original: In Bristol, England, both Mrs. Washington and I spoke at the Women’s Liberal Club. I was also the principal speaker at the Commencement exercises of the Royal College for the Blind. These exercises were held in the Crystal Palace, and the presiding officer was the late Duke of Westminster, who was said to be, I believe, the richest man in England, if not in the world. The Duke, as well as his wife and their daughter, seemed to be pleased with what I said, and thanked me heartily. Through the kindness of Lady Aberdeen, my wife and I were enabled to go with a party of those who were attending the International Congress of Women, then in session in London, to see Queen Victoria, at Windsor Castle, where, afterward, we were all the guests of her Majesty at tea. In our party was Miss Susan B. Anthony, and I was deeply impressed with the fact that one did not often get an opportunity to see, during the same hour, two women so remarkable in different ways as Susan B. Anthony and Queen Victoria.
passages.vernacular: 喺英國布里斯托,華盛頓太太同我都喺婦女自由俱樂部演說。我亦係皇家盲人學院畢業典禮嘅主要演講者。典禮喺水晶宮舉行,主持人係已故威斯敏斯特公爵,據講係英國甚至世上最富有嘅人。公爵同佢太太及女兒似乎對我所講嘅滿意,衷心多謝我。憑阿伯丁夫人嘅好意,我太太同我可以同一批出席當時喺倫敦舉行嘅國際婦女大會嘅人,去溫莎城堡見維多利亞女王,之後我哋全部係陛下嘅茶客。我哋隊伍中有蘇珊·B·安東尼小姐,令我深刻印象,同一個鐘頭內見到像蘇珊·B·安東尼同維多利亞女王咁以不同方式非凡嘅兩位女性,機會並不經常。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在英國布里斯托,華盛頓太太和我都在婦女自由俱樂部演說。我也是皇家盲人學院畢業典禮的主要演講者。典禮在水晶宮舉行,主持人是已故威斯敏斯特公爵,據說是英國甚至世上最富有的人。公爵和他太太及女兒似乎對我所說的滿意,衷心感謝我。憑阿伯丁夫人的好意,我妻子和我可以與一批出席當時在倫敦舉行的國際婦女大會的人,去溫莎城堡見維多利亞女王,之後我們全部是陛下的茶客。我們隊伍中有蘇珊·B·安東尼小姐,使我深刻印象,同一個小時內見到像蘇珊·B·安東尼和維多利亞女王那樣以不同方式非凡的兩位女性,機會並不經常。

passages.original: In the House of Commons, which we visited several times, we met Sir Henry M. Stanley. I talked with him about Africa and its relation to the American Negro, and after my interview with him I became more convinced than ever that there was no hope of the American Negro’s improving his condition by emigrating to Africa.
passages.vernacular: 喺下議院,我哋參觀幾次,見到亨利·M·斯坦利爵士。我同佢講非洲同佢同美國黑人嘅關係,同佢會面後,我比以往任何時候都更相信,美國黑人移民非洲改善處境冇希望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在下議院,我們參觀幾次,見到亨利·M·斯坦利爵士。我與他說非洲和它與美國黑人的關係,與他會面後,我比以往任何時候都更相信,美國黑人移民非洲改善處境沒希望。

passages.original: On various occasions Mrs. Washington and I were the guests of Englishmen in their country homes, where, I think, one sees the Englishman at his best. In one thing, at least, I feel sure that the English are ahead of Americans, and that is, that they have learned how to get more out of life. The home life of the English seems to me to be about as perfect as anything can be. Everything moves like clockwork. I was impressed, too, with the deference that the servants show to their “masters” and “mistresses,”—terms which I suppose would not be tolerated in America. The English servant expects, as a rule, to be nothing but a servant, and so he perfects himself in the art to a degree that no class of servants in America has yet reached. In our country the servant expects to become, in a few years, a “master” himself. Which system is preferable? I will not venture an answer.
passages.vernacular: 多個場合,華盛頓太太同我係英國人鄉村住所嘅客人,我諗喺嗰度見到英國人最好嘅一面。至少有一點我肯定英國人領先美國人,就係佢哋學會咗點樣從生活得到更多。英國人嘅家庭生活,對我嚟講似乎幾乎完美。一切像時鐘咁運轉。我亦對僕人對佢哋「主人」同「女主人」嘅恭敬留下深刻印象——我諗呢啲稱呼喺美國唔會被容忍。英國僕人通常預期只係做僕人,所以佢將呢門手藝完善到美國任何僕人階層都未達到嘅程度。喺我哋國家,僕人預期幾年內自己成為「主人」。邊個制度更可取?我唔敢冒險回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多個場合,華盛頓太太和我是英國人鄉村住所的客人,我想在那裡看到英國人最好的一面。至少有一點我肯定英國人領先美國人,就是他們學會了怎樣從生活得到更多。英國人的家庭生活,對我來說似乎幾乎完美。一切像時鐘那樣運轉。我也對僕人對他們「主人」和「女主人」的恭敬留下深刻印象——我想這些稱呼在美國不會被容忍。英國僕人通常預期只是做僕人,所以他將這門手藝完善到美國任何僕人階層都未達到的程度。在我們國家,僕人預期幾年內自己成為「主人」。哪個制度更可取?我不敢冒險回答。

passages.original: Another thing that impressed itself upon me throughout England was the high regard that all classes have for law and order, and the ease and thoroughness with which everything is done. The Englishmen, I found, took plenty of time for eating, as for everything else. I am not sure if, in the long run, they do not accomplish as much or more than rushing, nervous Americans do.
passages.vernacular: 喺整個英國另一件令我印象深刻嘅事,係所有階層對法律同秩序嘅高度尊重,以及做事嘅輕鬆同徹底。我發現英國人花好多時間食飯,正如做其他一切。我唔肯定長遠嚟講,佢哋成就嘅有冇比匆忙緊張嘅美國人少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在整個英國另一件使我印象深刻的事,是所有階層對法律和秩序的高度尊重,以及做事的輕鬆和徹底。我發現英國人花很多時間吃飯,正如做其他一切。我不肯定長遠來說,他們成就的有沒有比匆忙緊張的美國人少。

passages.original: My visit to England gave me a higher regard for the nobility than I had had. I had no idea that they were so generally loved and respected by the classes, nor had I any correct conception of how much time and money they spent in works of philanthropy, and how much real heart they put into this work. My impression had been that they merely spent money freely and had a “good time.”
passages.vernacular: 我探訪英國,令我對貴族比以前更尊重。我完全唔知道佢哋咁普遍被各階層愛戴同尊重,亦冇正確概念佢哋花幾多時間同金錢喺慈善工作,幾多真心放入呢項工作。我嘅印象係佢哋只係自由使錢、「玩得開心」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我探訪英國,使我對貴族比以前更尊重。我完全不知道他們那麼普遍被各階層愛戴和尊重,也沒正確概念他們花多少時間和金錢在慈善工作,多少真心放入這項工作。我的印象是他們只是自由使錢、「玩得開心」。

passages.original: It was hard for me to get accustomed to speaking to English audiences. The average Englishman is so serious, and is so tremendously in earnest about everything, that when I told a story that would have made an American audience roar with laughter, the Englishmen simply looked me straight in the face without even cracking a smile.
passages.vernacular: 我好難習慣向英國聽眾演講。普通英國人咁認真,對一切都咁極度認真,當我講一個會令美國聽眾大笑嘅故事,英國人只係直望我嘅面,連笑都冇笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很難習慣向英國聽眾演講。普通英國人那麼認真,對一切都那麼極度認真,當我說一個會使美國聽眾大笑的故事,英國人只是直望我的臉,連笑都沒笑。

passages.original: When the Englishman takes you into his heart and friendship, he binds you there as with cords of steel, and I do not believe that there are many other friendships that are so lasting or so satisfactory. Perhaps I can illustrate this point in no better way than by relating the following incident. Mrs. Washington and I were invited to attend a reception given by the Duke and Duchess of Sutherland, at Stafford House—said to be the finest house in London; I may add that I believe the Duchess of Sutherland is said to be the most beautiful woman in England. There must have been at least three hundred persons at this reception. Twice during the evening the Duchess sought us out for a conversation, and she asked me to write her when we got home, and tell her more about the work at Tuskegee. This I did. When Christmas came we were surprised and delighted to receive her photograph with her autograph on it. The correspondence has continued, and we now feel that in the Duchess of Sutherland we have one of our warmest friends.
passages.vernacular: 當英國人將你接納入佢心裡面同友誼,佢用鋼索咁將你綁住,我唔相信有好多其他友誼咁持久、咁令人滿意。也許我可以用以下事件,最好咁說明呢點。華盛頓太太同我被邀請出席薩瑟蘭公爵同公爵夫人喺斯塔福德府舉辦嘅招待會——據講係倫敦最好嘅屋;我可以補充,我相信薩瑟蘭公爵夫人據講係英國最美麗嘅女人。呢個招待會至少有三百人。晚間兩次,公爵夫人搵我哋傾偈,要求我返到屋企後寫信畀佢,講多啲塔斯基吉嘅工作。我照做。聖誕節到時,我哋驚訝高興地收到佢嘅相片,附有佢嘅親筆簽名。通信繼續,我哋而家覺得,薩瑟蘭公爵夫人係我哋最熱情嘅朋友之一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當英國人將你接納入他心裡和友誼,他用鋼索那樣將你綁住,我不相信有很多其他友誼那麼持久、那麼令人滿意。也許我可以用以下事件,最好地說明這點。華盛頓太太和我被邀請出席薩瑟蘭公爵和公爵夫人在斯塔福德府舉辦的招待會——據說是倫敦最好的屋子;我可以補充,我相信薩瑟蘭公爵夫人據說是英國最美麗的女人。這個招待會至少有三百人。晚間兩次,公爵夫人找我們交談,要求我回到家後寫信給她,講多一些塔斯基吉的工作。我照做。聖誕節到時,我們驚訝高興地收到她的相片,附有她的親筆簽名。通信繼續,我們現在覺得,薩瑟蘭公爵夫人是我們最熱情的朋友之一。

passages.original: After three months in Europe we sailed from Southampton in the steamship St. Louis. On this steamer there was a fine library that had been presented to the ship by the citizens of St. Louis, Mo. In this library I found a life of Frederick Douglass, which I began reading. I became especially interested in Mr. Douglass’s description of the way he was treated on shipboard during his first or second visit to England. In this description he told how he was not permitted to enter the cabin, but had to confine himself to the deck of the ship. A few minutes after I had finished reading this description I was waited on by a committee of ladies and gentlemen with the request that I deliver an address at a concert which was to begin the following evening. And yet there are people who are bold enough to say that race feeling in America is not growing less intense! At this concert the Hon. Benjamin B. Odell, Jr., the present governor of New York, presided. I was never given a more cordial hearing anywhere. A large proportion of the passengers were Southern people. After the concert some of the passengers proposed that a subscription be raised to help the work at Tuskegee, and the money to support several scholarships was the result.
passages.vernacular: 喺歐洲三個月後,我哋從南安普敦搭「聖路易斯號」輪船返航。呢艘輪船有個好圖書館,係密蘇里聖路易斯市民贈送畀船嘅。喺呢個圖書館,我發現一本弗雷德里克·道格拉斯嘅傳記,我開始讀。我尤其對道格拉斯先生描述佢第一或第二次去英國時喺船上點樣被對待感興趣。喺呢段描述,佢講佢點樣唔獲准入艙,要局限於船嘅甲板。我讀完呢段描述幾分鐘後,一個男女委員會來搵我,要求我喺第二晚開始嘅音樂會上發表演說。而仍然有人大膽到話美國種族情緒冇減輕!喺呢次音樂會,而家嘅紐約州長小本傑明·B·奧德爾主持。我喺任何地方都冇得到過更熱情嘅聆聽。乘客中好大部分係南方人。音樂會後,一些乘客提議籌集認捐幫助塔斯基吉嘅工作,結果籌到支持幾個獎學金嘅錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在歐洲三個月後,我們從南安普敦搭「聖路易斯號」輪船返航。這艘輪船有個好圖書館,是密蘇里聖路易斯市民贈送給船的。在這個圖書館,我發現一本弗雷德里克·道格拉斯的傳記,我開始讀。我尤其對道格拉斯先生描述他第一或第二次去英國時在船上怎樣被對待感興趣。在這段描述,他說他怎樣不獲准入艙,要局限於船的甲板。我讀完這段描述幾分鐘後,一個男女委員會來找我,要求我在第二晚開始的音樂會上發表演說。而仍然有人大膽到說美國種族情緒沒減輕!在這次音樂會,現在的紐約州長小本傑明·B·奧德爾主持。我在任何地方都沒得到過更熱情的聆聽。乘客中很大部分是南方人。音樂會後,一些乘客提議籌集認捐幫助塔斯基吉的工作,結果籌到支持幾個獎學金的錢。

passages.original: While we were in Paris I was very pleasantly surprised to receive the following invitation from the citizens of West Virginia and of the city near which I had spent my boyhood days:—
passages.vernacular: 我哋喺巴黎期間,我好愉快驚訝地收到以下邀請,來自西弗吉尼亞市民同我度過童年嘅城市附近:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們在巴黎期間,我很愉快驚訝地收到以下邀請,來自西弗吉尼亞市民和我度過童年的城市附近:

passages.original: Charleston, W. Va., May 16, 1899.
passages.vernacular: 西弗吉尼亞查爾斯頓,1899年5月16日。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 西弗吉尼亞查爾斯頓,1899年5月16日。

passages.original: Professor Booker T. Washington, Paris, France:
passages.vernacular: 法國巴黎,布克·T·華盛頓教授:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 法國巴黎,布克·T·華盛頓教授:

passages.original: Dear Sir: Many of the best citizens of West Virginia have united in liberal expressions of admiration and praise of your worth and work, and desire that on your return from Europe you should favour them with your presence and with the inspiration of your words. We must sincerely indorse this move, and on behalf of the citizens of Charleston extend to your our most cordial invitation to have you come to us, that we may honour you who have done so much by your life and work to honour us.
passages.vernacular: 親愛嘅先生:西弗吉尼亞好多最好嘅市民聯合慷慨表達對你價值同工作嘅欽佩同讚揚,希望你從歐洲返嚟時賞面出席,並以你嘅說話啟發佢哋。我哋必須真誠贊同呢個行動,代表查爾斯頓市民向你伸出我哋最熱情嘅邀請,請你來我哋度,令我哋可以榮耀你,你以你嘅生活同工作為我哋增光咁多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 親愛的先生:西弗吉尼亞很多最好的市民聯合慷慨表達對你價值和工作的欽佩和讚揚,希望你從歐洲回來時賞臉出席,並以你的話啟發他們。我們必須真誠贊同這個行動,代表查爾斯頓市民向你伸出我們最熱情的邀請,請你來我們這裡,使我們可以榮耀你,你以你的生活和工作為我們增光那麼多。

passages.original: We are,
passages.vernacular: 我哋係,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們是,

passages.original: Very truly yours,
passages.vernacular: 你非常真誠嘅,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你非常真誠的,

passages.original: The Common Council of the City of Charleston,
passages.vernacular: 查爾斯頓市議會,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 查爾斯頓市議會,

passages.original: By W. Herman Smith, Mayor.
passages.vernacular: 市長W·赫爾曼·史密斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 市長W·赫爾曼·史密斯。

passages.original: This invitation from the City Council of Charleston was accompanied by the following:—
passages.vernacular: 查爾斯頓市議會呢個邀請,附有以下:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 查爾斯頓市議會這個邀請,附有以下:

passages.original: Professor Booker T. Washington, Paris, France:
passages.vernacular: 法國巴黎,布克·T·華盛頓教授:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 法國巴黎,布克·T·華盛頓教授:

passages.original: Dear Sir: We, the citizens of Charleston and West Virginia, desire to express our pride in you and the splendid career that you have thus far accomplished, and ask that we be permitted to show our pride and interest in a substantial way.
passages.vernacular: 親愛嘅先生:我哋,查爾斯頓同西弗吉尼亞市民,希望表達我哋對你,以及你至今所成就嘅輝煌事業嘅驕傲,並請求我哋可以被容許以實質方式顯示我哋嘅驕傲同興趣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 親愛的先生:我們,查爾斯頓和西弗吉尼亞市民,希望表達我們對你,以及你至今所成就的輝煌事業的驕傲,並請求我們可以被容許以實質方式顯示我們的驕傲和興趣。

passages.original: Your recent visit to your old home in our midst awoke within us the keenest regret that we were not permitted to hear you and render some substantial aid to your work, before you left for Europe.
passages.vernacular: 你最近探訪你喺我哋當中嘅舊家,喚起我哋最強烈嘅遺憾:你去歐洲之前,我哋未獲准聽你講,並對你嘅工作提供一些實質幫助。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你最近探訪你在我們當中的舊家,喚起我們最強烈的遺憾:你去歐洲之前,我們未獲准聽你講,並對你的工作提供一些實質幫助。

passages.original: In view of the foregoing, we earnestly invite you to share the hospitality of our city upon your return from Europe, and give us the opportunity to hear you and put ourselves in touch with your work in a way that will be most gratifying to yourself, and that we may receive the inspiration of your words and presence.
passages.vernacular: 鑑於上述,我哋認真邀請你,從歐洲返嚟時分享我哋城市嘅款待,畀我哋機會聽你講,並以最令你滿意嘅方式,同你嘅工作接觸,令我哋可以得到你嘅說話同在場嘅啟發。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鑑於上述,我們認真邀請你,從歐洲回來時分享我們城市的款待,給我們機會聽你講,並以最使你滿意的方式,與你的工作接觸,使我們可以得到你的話和在場的啟發。

passages.original: An early reply to this invitation, with an indication of the time you may reach our city, will greatly oblige,
passages.vernacular: 及早回覆呢個邀請,說明你可能到達我哋城市嘅時間,會令我哋非常感激,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 及早回覆這個邀請,說明你可能到達我們城市的時間,會使我們非常感激,

passages.original: Yours very respectfully,
passages.vernacular: 你非常恭敬嘅,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你非常恭敬的,

passages.original: The Charleston Daily Gazette, The Daily Mail-Tribune; G.W. Atkinson, Governor; E.L. Boggs, Secretary to Governor; Wm. M.O. Dawson, Secretary of State; L.M. La Follette, Auditor; J.R. Trotter, Superintendent of Schools; E.W. Wilson, ex-Governor; W.A. MacCorkle, ex-Governor; John Q. Dickinson, President Kanawha Valley Bank; L. Prichard, President Charleston National Bank; Geo. S. Couch, President Kanawha National Bank; Ed. Reid, Cashier Kanawha National Bank; Geo. S. Laidley, Superintended City Schools; L.E. McWhorter, President Board of Education; Chas. K. Payne, wholesale merchant; and many others.
passages.vernacular: 《查爾斯頓每日公報》《每日郵報論壇》;G·W·阿特金森,州長;E·L·博格斯,州長秘書;威廉M·O·道森,國務卿;L·M·拉福萊特,審計長;J·R·特羅特,學校總監;E·W·威爾遜,前州長;W·A·麥科克爾,前州長;約翰·Q·迪金森,卡諾瓦山谷銀行行長;L·普里查德,查爾斯頓國家銀行行長;喬治S·庫奇,卡諾瓦國家銀行行長;埃德里德,卡諾瓦國家銀行出納;喬治S·萊德利,市學校總監;L·E·麥克沃特,教育委員會主席;查爾斯K·佩恩,批發商;以及許多其他人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 《查爾斯頓每日公報》《每日郵報論壇》;G·W·阿特金森,州長;E·L·博格斯,州長秘書;威廉M·O·道森,國務卿;L·M·拉福萊特,審計長;J·R·特羅特,學校總監;E·W·威爾遜,前州長;W·A·麥科克爾,前州長;約翰·Q·迪金森,卡諾瓦山谷銀行行長;L·普里查德,查爾斯頓國家銀行行長;喬治S·庫奇,卡諾瓦國家銀行行長;埃德里德,卡諾瓦國家銀行出納;喬治S·萊德利,市學校總監;L·E·麥克沃特,教育委員會主席;查爾斯K·佩恩,批發商;以及許多其他人。

passages.original: This invitation, coming as it did from the City Council, the state officers, and all the substantial citizens of both races of the community where I had spent my boyhood, and from which I had gone a few years before, unknown, in poverty and ignorance, in quest of an education, not only surprised me, but almost unmanned me. I could not understand what I had done to deserve it all.
passages.vernacular: 呢個邀請,來自市議會、州官員同我度過童年嘅社區兩個種族所有重要市民,而我幾年前從嗰度一無所知、貧窮無知咁出發尋求教育,令我唔單止驚訝,幾乎令我失去男子氣概。我唔明白我做咗咩值得呢一切。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個邀請,來自市議會、州官員和我度過童年的社區兩個種族所有重要市民,而我幾年前從那裡一無所知、貧窮無知地出發尋求教育,使我不僅驚訝,幾乎使我失去男子氣概。我不明白我做了什麼值得這一切。

passages.original: I accepted the invitation, and at the appointed day was met at the railway station at Charleston by a committee headed by ex-Governor W.A. MacCorkle, and composed of men of both races. The public reception was held in the Opera-House at Charleston. The Governor of the state, the Hon. George W. Atkinson, presided, and an address of welcome was made by ex-Governor MacCorkle. A prominent part in the reception was taken by the coloured citizens. The Opera-House was filled with citizens of both races, and among the white people were many for whom I had worked when I was a boy. The next day Governor and Mrs. Atkinson gave me a public reception at the State House, which was attended by all classes.
passages.vernacular: 我接受邀請,指定日子喺查爾斯頓火車站被前州長W·A·麥科克爾帶領、兩個種族男人組成嘅委員會迎接。公眾招待會喺查爾斯頓歌劇院舉行。州長喬治·W·阿特金森先生主持,前州長麥科克爾致歡迎辭。有色人種市民喺招待會扮演突出角色。歌劇院擠滿兩個種族嘅市民,白人當中有好多我做男孩時曾經為佢哋工作嘅。第二日阿特金森州長同太太喺州議會大廈為我舉行公眾招待會,各階層都出席。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我接受邀請,指定日子在查爾斯頓火車站被前州長W·A·麥科克爾帶領、兩個種族男人組成的委員會迎接。公眾招待會在查爾斯頓歌劇院舉行。州長喬治·W·阿特金森先生主持,前州長麥科克爾致歡迎辭。有色人種市民在招待會扮演突出角色。歌劇院擠滿兩個種族的市民,白人當中有很多我做男孩時曾經為他們工作的。第二天阿特金森州長和太太在州議會大廈為我舉行公眾招待會,各階層都出席。

passages.original: Not long after this the coloured people in Atlanta, Georgia, gave me a reception at which the Governor of the state presided, and a similar reception was given me in New Orleans, which was presided over by the Mayor of the city. Invitations came from many other places which I was not able to accept.
passages.vernacular: 不久之後,佐治亞亞特蘭大嘅有色人種為我舉行招待會,由州長主持,新奧爾良亦為我舉行類似招待會,由市長主持。好多其他地方嘅邀請來到,我無法接受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久之後,喬治亞亞特蘭大的有色人種為我舉行招待會,由州長主持,新奧爾良也為我舉行類似招待會,由市長主持。很多其他地方的邀請來到,我無法接受。

passages.original: Before going to Europe some events came into my life which were great surprises to me. In fact, my whole life has largely been one of surprises. I believe that any man’s life will be filled with constant, unexpected encouragements of this kind if he makes up his mind to do his level best each day of his life—that is, tries to make each day reach as nearly as possible the high-water mark of pure, unselfish, useful living. I pity the man, black or white, who has never experienced the joy and satisfaction that come to one by reason of an effort to assist in making some one else more useful and more happy.
passages.vernacular: 去歐洲之前,我人生中發生咗一些令我好驚訝嘅事。事實上,我整個人生好大程度都係驚訝。我相信任何人嘅生活,如果佢決心每日盡力做到最好——即係嘗試令每日盡可能接近純粹、無私、有用生活嘅高水位標記——就會充滿呢種不斷、意想不到嘅鼓勵。我同情無論黑人白人,從未經歷過因努力幫助令別人更有用更快樂而得到嘅喜悅同滿足嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去歐洲之前,我人生中發生了一些使我很驚訝的事。事實上,我整個人生很大程度都是驚訝。我相信任何人的生活,如果他決心每天盡力做到最好——即嘗試使每天盡可能接近純粹、無私、有用生活的高水位標記——就會充滿這種不斷、意想不到的鼓勵。我同情無論黑人白人,從未經歷過因努力幫助使別人更有用更快樂而得到的喜悅和滿足的人。

passages.original: Six months before he died, and nearly a year after he had been stricken with paralysis, General Armstrong expressed a wish to visit Tuskegee again before he passed away. Notwithstanding the fact that he had lost the use of his limbs to such an extent that he was practically helpless, his wish was gratified, and he was brought to Tuskegee. The owners of the Tuskegee Railroad, white men living in the town, offered to run a special train, without cost, out of the main station—Chehaw, five miles away—to meet him. He arrived on the school grounds about nine o’clock in the evening. Some one had suggested that we give the General a “pine-knot torchlight reception.” This plan was carried out, and the moment that his carriage entered the school grounds he began passing between two lines of lighted and waving “fat pine” wood knots held by over a thousand students and teachers. The whole thing was so novel and surprising that the General was completely overcome with happiness. He remained a guest in my home for nearly two months, and, although almost wholly without the use of voice or limb, he spent nearly every hour in devising ways and means to help the South. Time and time again he said to me, during this visit, that it was not only the duty of the country to assist in elevating the Negro of the South, but the poor white man as well. At the end of his visit I resolved anew to devote myself more earnestly than ever to the cause which was so near his heart. I said that if a man in his condition was willing to think, work, and act, I should not be wanting in furthering in every possible way the wish of his heart.
passages.vernacular: 阿姆斯特朗將軍去世前六個月,中風後近一年,表達咗想喺去世前再探訪塔斯基吉嘅願望。儘管佢四肢喪失到幾乎無助,佢嘅願望得到滿足,被帶到塔斯基吉。塔斯基吉鐵路嘅擁有人(住喺鎮上嘅白人),提出從主站——五英里外嘅切豪——免費開特別列車迎接佢。佢大約晚上九點到達校園。有人建議我哋為將軍舉行「松節火炬歡迎會」。呢個計劃得到執行,佢嘅馬車一入校園,佢就開始從一千多個學生同老師拿住嘅兩行點燃、揮動嘅「肥松」木節之間經過。整件事咁新穎令人驚訝,將軍完全被快樂淹沒。佢喺我屋做客近兩個月,雖然聲音同四肢幾乎完全失去作用,佢差唔多每個鐘頭都用於設計幫助南方嘅方法同手段。呢次探訪期間,佢一次又一次對我講,國家嘅責任唔單止係協助提升南方嘅黑人,亦包括窮白人。佢探訪結束時,我重新決心比以往更認真咁獻身於佢心愛嘅事業。我話,如果一個處於佢咁狀況嘅人願意思考、工作同行動,我唔會欠缺以一切可能方式促進佢心中嘅願望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 阿姆斯特朗將軍去世前六個月,中風後近一年,表達了想在去世前再探訪塔斯基吉的願望。儘管他四肢喪失到幾乎無助,他的願望得到滿足,被帶到塔斯基吉。塔斯基吉鐵路的擁有人(住在鎮上的白人),提出從主站——五英里外的切豪——免費開特別列車迎接他。他大約晚上九點到達校園。有人建議我們為將軍舉行「松節火炬歡迎會」。這個計劃得到執行,他的馬車一進校園,他就開始從一千多個學生和老師拿著的兩行點燃、揮動的「肥松」木節之間經過。整件事那麼新穎令人驚訝,將軍完全被快樂淹沒。他在我家做客近兩個月,雖然聲音和四肢幾乎完全失去作用,他差不多每個小時都用於設計幫助南方的方法和手段。這次探訪期間,他一次又一次對我說,國家的責任不僅是協助提升南方的黑人,也包括窮白人。他探訪結束時,我重新決心比以往更認真地獻身於他心愛的事業。我說,如果一個處於他這樣狀況的人願意思考、工作和行動,我不會欠缺以一切可能方式促進他心中的願望。

passages.original: The death of General Armstrong, a few weeks later, gave me the privilege of getting acquainted with one of the finest, most unselfish, and most attractive men that I have ever come in contact with. I refer to the Rev. Dr. Hollis B. Frissell, now the Principal of the Hampton Institute, and General Armstrong’s successor. Under the clear, strong, and almost perfect leadership of Dr. Frissell, Hampton has had a career of prosperity and usefulness that is all that the General could have wished for. It seems to be the constant effort of Dr. Frissell to hide his own great personality behind that of General Armstrong—to make himself of “no reputation” for the sake of the cause.
passages.vernacular: 幾個星期後,阿姆斯特朗將軍去世,令我有幸認識一位我接觸過最優秀、最無私、最有吸引力嘅人之一。我係指霍利斯·B·弗里塞爾牧師博士,而家漢普頓學院嘅校長,阿姆斯特朗將軍嘅繼任人。喺弗里塞爾博士清晰、強而幾乎完美嘅領導下,漢普頓經歷咗將軍所能希望嘅繁榮同有用嘅事業。似乎弗里塞爾博士不斷努力將自己偉大嘅個性隱藏喺阿姆斯特朗將軍背後——為咗事業令自己「冇名氣」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾個星期後,阿姆斯特朗將軍去世,使我有幸認識一位我接觸過最優秀、最無私、最有吸引力的人之一。我是指霍利斯·B·弗里塞爾牧師博士,現在漢普頓學院的校長,阿姆斯特朗將軍的繼任人。在弗里塞爾博士清晰、強而幾乎完美的領導下,漢普頓經歷了將軍所能希望的繁榮和有用的事業。似乎弗里塞爾博士不斷努力將自己偉大的個性隱藏在阿姆斯特朗將軍背後——為了事業使自己「沒名氣」。

passages.original: More than once I have been asked what was the greatest surprise that ever came to me. I have little hesitation in answering that question. It was the following letter, which came to me one Sunday morning when I was sitting on the veranda of my home at Tuskegee, surrounded by my wife and three children:—
passages.vernacular: 我不止一次被問,最大嘅驚訝係咩。我毫不猶豫咁回答呢個問題。係以下呢封信,有一個星期日朝早,我坐喺塔斯基吉嘅家嘅走廊,太太同三個孩子圍繞時收到:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不止一次被問,最大的驚訝是什麼。我毫不猶豫地回答這個問題。是以下這封信,有一個星期日早上,我坐在塔斯基吉的家的走廊,妻子和三個孩子圍繞時收到:

passages.original: Harvard University, Cambridge, May 28, 1896.
passages.vernacular: 哈佛大學,劍橋,1896年5月28日。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈佛大學,劍橋,1896年5月28日。

passages.original: President Booker T. Washington,
passages.vernacular: 布克·T·華盛頓校長:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 布克·T·華盛頓校長:

passages.original: My Dear Sir: Harvard University desired to confer on you at the approaching Commencement an honorary degree; but it is our custom to confer degrees only on gentlemen who are present. Our Commencement occurs this year on June 24, and your presence would be desirable from about noon till about five o’clock in the afternoon. Would it be possible for you to be in Cambridge on that day?
passages.vernacular: 親愛嘅先生:哈佛大學希望喺即將到來嘅畢業典禮授予你榮譽學位;不過我哋嘅習慣係只授予在場嘅紳士學位。我哋今年嘅畢業典禮係6月24日,你大約中午到下午五點在場為佳。你可唔可能嗰日喺劍橋?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 親愛的先生:哈佛大學希望在即將到來的畢業典禮授予你榮譽學位;不過我們的習慣是只授予在場的紳士學位。我們今年的畢業典禮是6月24日,你大約中午到下午五點在場為佳。你可不可能那天在劍橋?

passages.original: Believe me, with great regard,
passages.vernacular: 請相信我,懷住極大敬意,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請相信我,懷著極大敬意,

passages.original: Very truly yours,
passages.vernacular: 你非常真誠嘅,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你非常真誠的,

passages.original: Charles W. Eliot.
passages.vernacular: 查爾斯·W·艾略特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 查爾斯·W·艾略特。

passages.original: This was a recognition that had never in the slightest manner entered into my mind, and it was hard for me to realize that I was to be honoured by a degree from the oldest and most renowned university in America. As I sat upon my veranda, with this letter in my hand, tears came into my eyes. My whole former life—my life as a slave on the plantation, my work in the coal-mine, the times when I was without food and clothing, when I made my bed under a sidewalk, my struggles for an education, the trying days I had had at Tuskegee, days when I did not know where to turn for a dollar to continue the work there, the ostracism and sometimes oppression of my race,—all this passed before me and nearly overcame me.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係一個我從未絲毫想過嘅認可,我好難意識到我會被美國最古老、最著名大學嘅學位授予榮譽。我坐喺走廊,手執呢封信,眼淚湧入眼睛。我整個過去——我做奴隸喺種植園嘅生活,我喺煤礦嘅工作,我冇食物同衣服嘅時候,我喺人行道下面搭床,我爭取教育嘅奮鬥,我喺塔斯基吉嘅艱難日子,我唔知去邊度搵一美元繼續嗰度工作嘅日子,我種族被排斥有時被壓迫——所有呢啲喺我面前經過,幾乎淹沒我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是一個我從未絲毫想過的認可,我很難意識到我會被美國最古老、最著名大學的學位授予榮譽。我坐在走廊,手執這封信,眼淚湧入眼睛。我整個過去——我做奴隸在種植園的生活,我在煤礦的工作,我沒食物和衣服的時候,我在人行道下面搭床,我爭取教育的奮鬥,我在塔斯基吉的艱難日子,我不知去哪裡找一美元繼續那裡工作的日子,我種族被排斥有時被壓迫——所有這些在我面前經過,幾乎淹沒我。

passages.original: I had never sought or cared for what the world calls fame. I have always looked upon fame as something to be used in accomplishing good. I have often said to my friends that if I can use whatever prominence may have come to me as an instrument with which to do good, I am content to have it. I care for it only as a means to be used for doing good, just as wealth may be used. The more I come into contact with wealthy people, the more I believe that they are growing in the direction of looking upon their money simply as an instrument which God has placed in their hand for doing good with. I never go to the office of Mr. John D. Rockefeller, who more than once has been generous to Tuskegee, without being reminded of this. The close, careful, and minute investigation that he always makes in order to be sure that every dollar that he gives will do the most good—an investigation that is just as searching as if he were investing money in a business enterprise—convinces me that the growth in this direction is most encouraging.
passages.vernacular: 我從未尋求或關心世人所謂嘅名聲。我一直視名聲為用嚟成就好事嘅東西。我經常話畀朋友聽,如果我可以將任何可能到我身上嘅顯赫,用作做好事嘅工具,我就滿足有佢。我只關心佢作為做好事嘅手段,正如財富可以咁用。我同富人接觸越多,就越相信佢哋正朝向視佢哋嘅錢僅僅係上帝放喺佢哋手中用嚟做好事嘅工具嘅方向發展。我去約翰·D·洛克菲勒先生嘅辦公室(佢不止一次慷慨對待塔斯基吉),總係被提醒呢點。佢為咗確保佢所畀嘅每一美元都做最大好事而總係進行嘅密切、仔細、詳盡嘅調查——同佢投資喺商業事業一樣徹底——令我相信,喺呢個方向嘅增長最令人鼓舞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從未尋求或關心世人所謂的名聲。我一直視名聲為用來成就好事的東西。我經常告訴朋友,如果我可以將任何可能到我身上的顯赫,用作做好事的工具,我就滿足有它。我只關心它作為做好事的手段,正如財富可以這樣用。我與富人接觸越多,就越相信他們正朝向視他們的錢僅僅是上帝放在他們手中用來做好事的工具的方向發展。我去約翰·D·洛克菲勒先生的辦公室(他不止一次慷慨對待塔斯基吉),總是被提醒這點。他為了確保他所給的每一美元都做最大好事而總是進行的密切、仔細、詳盡的調查——與他投資在商業事業一樣徹底——使我相信,在這個方向的增長最令人鼓舞。

passages.original: At nine o’clock, on the morning of June 24, I met President Eliot, the Board of Overseers of Harvard University, and the other guests, at the designated place on the university grounds, for the purpose of being escorted to Sanders Theatre, where the Commencement exercises were to be held and degrees conferred. Among others invited to be present for the purpose of receiving a degree at this time were General Nelson A. Miles, Dr. Bell, the inventor of the Bell telephone, Bishop Vincent, and the Rev. Minot J. Savage. We were placed in line immediately behind the President and the Board of Overseers, and directly afterward the Governor of Massachusetts, escorted by the Lancers, arrived and took his place in the line of march by the side of President Eliot. In the line there were also various other officers and professors, clad in cap and gown. In this order we marched to Sanders Theatre, where, after the usual Commencement exercises, came the conferring of the honorary degrees. This, it seems, is always considered the most interesting feature at Harvard. It is not known, until the individuals appear, upon whom the honorary degrees are to be conferred, and those receiving these honours are cheered by the students and others in proportion to their popularity. During the conferring of the degrees excitement and enthusiasm are at the highest pitch.
passages.vernacular: 6月24日朝早九點,我同艾略特校長、哈佛大學監事會同其他客人,喺大學校園指定地點會合,被護送到桑德斯劇院,畢業典禮喺嗰度舉行,學位喺嗰度授予。當時被邀請在場接受學位嘅其他人包括內爾森·A·邁爾斯將軍、貝爾電話發明者貝爾博士、文森特主教同米諾特·J·薩維奇牧師。我哋被安排喺校長同監事會正後面嘅隊列,隨即麻薩諸塞州長由槍騎兵護送到達,同艾略特校長並排佔據行進隊列嘅位置。隊列中亦有穿帽同袍嘅各種其他官員同教授。咁樣我哋行去桑德斯劇院,通常畢業典禮儀式後就係授予榮譽學位。似乎呢個總係被視為哈佛最有趣嘅特點。直到人出現,先知道榮譽學位授予邊個,得到呢啲榮譽嘅人按佢哋嘅受歡迎程度被學生同其他人歡呼。授予學位期間,激動同熱情處於最高峰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 6月24日早上九點,我與艾略特校長、哈佛大學監事會和其他客人,在大學校園指定地點會合,被護送到桑德斯劇院,畢業典禮在那裡舉行,學位在那裡授予。當時被邀請在場接受學位的其他人包括內爾森·A·邁爾斯將軍、貝爾電話發明者貝爾博士、文森特主教和米諾特·J·薩維奇牧師。我們被安排在校長和監事會正後面的隊列,隨即麻薩諸塞州長由槍騎兵護送到達,與艾略特校長並排佔據行進隊列的位置。隊列中也有穿帽和袍的各種其他官員和教授。這樣我們走去桑德斯劇院,通常畢業典禮儀式後就是授予榮譽學位。似乎這個總是被視為哈佛最有趣的特點。直到人出現,才知道榮譽學位授予誰,得到這些榮譽的人按他們的受歡迎程度被學生和其他人歡呼。授予學位期間,激動和熱情處於最高峰。

passages.original: When my name was called, I rose, and President Eliot, in beautiful and strong English, conferred upon me the degree of Master of Arts. After these exercises were over, those who had received honorary degrees were invited to lunch with the President. After the lunch we were formed in line again, and were escorted by the Marshal of the day, who that year happened to be Bishop William Lawrence, through the grounds, where, at different points, those who had been honoured were called by name and received the Harvard yell. This march ended at Memorial Hall, where the alumni dinner was served. To see over a thousand strong men, representing all that is best in State, Church, business, and education, with the glow and enthusiasm of college loyalty and college pride,—which has, I think, a peculiar Harvard flavour,—is a sight that does not easily fade from memory.
passages.vernacular: 我名字被叫到時,我起身,艾略特校長以美麗有力嘅英語,授予我文學碩士學位。儀式結束後,獲榮譽學位嘅人被邀請同校長午餐。午餐後我哋再次排成隊列,由當日司儀(當年碰巧係威廉·勞倫斯主教)護送穿越校園,喺不同地點,被授予榮譽嘅人被叫名,並得到哈佛呼喊。行軍結束於紀念堂,校友晚宴喺嗰度供應。見到一千多位強壯嘅男人,代表州、教會、商業同教育所有最好嘅,帶住大學忠誠同大學驕傲嘅光輝同熱情——我諗帶有特別嘅哈佛味道——係一個唔容易從記憶中消退嘅景象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我名字被叫到時,我起身,艾略特校長以美麗有力的英語,授予我文學碩士學位。儀式結束後,獲榮譽學位的人被邀請與校長午餐。午餐後我們再次排成隊列,由當天司儀(當年碰巧是威廉·勞倫斯主教)護送穿越校園,在不同地點,被授予榮譽的人被叫名字,並得到哈佛呼喊。行軍結束於紀念堂,校友晚宴在那裡供應。看到一千多位強壯的男人,代表州、教會、商業和教育所有最好的,帶著大學忠誠和大學驕傲的光輝和熱情——我想帶有特別的哈佛味道——是一個不容易從記憶中消退的景象。

passages.original: Among the speakers after dinner were President Eliot, Governor Roger Wolcott, General Miles, Dr. Minot J. Savage, the Hon. Henry Cabot Lodge, and myself. When I was called upon, I said, among other things:—
passages.vernacular: 晚餐後嘅演講者包括艾略特校長、羅傑·沃爾科特州長、邁爾斯將軍、米諾特·J·薩維奇博士、尊敬嘅亨利·卡博特·洛奇同我自己。輪到我時,我講,除其他外:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 晚餐後的演講者包括艾略特校長、羅傑·沃爾科特州長、邁爾斯將軍、米諾特·J·薩維奇博士、尊敬的亨利·卡博特·洛奇和我自己。輪到我時,我說,除其他外:

passages.original: It would in some measure relieve my embarrassment if I could, even in a slight degree, feel myself worthy of the great honour which you do me to-day. Why you have called me from the Black Belt of the South, from among my humble people, to share in the honours of this occasion, is not for me to explain; and yet it may not be inappropriate for me to suggest that it seems to me that one of the most vital questions that touch our American life is how to bring the strong, wealthy, and learned into helpful touch with the poorest, most ignorant, and humblest, and at the same time make one appreciate the vitalizing, strengthening influence of the other. How shall we make the mansion on yon Beacon Street feel and see the need of the spirits in the lowliest cabin in Alabama cotton-fields or Louisiana sugar-bottoms? This problem Harvard University is solving, not by bringing itself down, but by bringing the masses up.
passages.vernacular: 如果我可以,即使略為,覺得自己配得你今日畀我嘅大榮譽,會某程度緩解我嘅尷尬。點解你從南方黑帶、從我卑微嘅人民當中叫我來分享今次場合嘅榮譽,唔係我解釋;不過我提出,或許並非不適當:接觸我哋美國生活最重要嘅問題之一,似乎係點樣令強大、富有、博學嘅人同最窮、最無知、最卑微嘅人有益接觸,同時令一方欣賞另一方嘅活力、強化影響。我哋點樣令彼端畢肯街嘅大宅,感覺同睇到阿拉巴馬棉田或路易斯安那糖田最卑微小屋入面靈魂嘅需要?哈佛大學正在解決呢個問題,唔係透過降低自己,而係透過提升大眾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我可以,即使略為,覺得自己配得你今天給我的大榮譽,會某種程度緩解我的尷尬。為什麼你從南方黑帶、從我卑微的人民當中叫我來分享這次場合的榮譽,不是我解釋;不過我提出,或許並非不適當:接觸我們美國生活最重要的問題之一,似乎是怎樣使強大、富有、博學的人和最窮、最無知、最卑微的人有益接觸,同時使一方欣賞另一方的活力、強化影響。我們怎樣使那端畢肯街的大宅,感覺和看到阿拉巴馬棉田或路易斯安那糖田最卑微小屋裡靈魂的需要?哈佛大學正在解決這個問題,不是透過降低自己,而是透過提升大眾。

passages.original: If my life in the past has meant anything in the lifting up of my people and the bringing about of better relations between your race and mine, I assure you from this day it will mean doubly more. In the economy of God there is but one standard by which an individual can succeed—there is but one for a race. This country demands that every race shall measure itself by the American standard. By it a race must rise or fall, succeed or fail, and in the last analysis mere sentiment counts for little. During the next half-century and more, my race must continue passing through the severe American crucible. We are to be tested in our patience, our forbearance, our perseverance, our power to endure wrong, to withstand temptations, to economize, to acquire and use skill; in our ability to compete, to succeed in commerce, to disregard the superficial for the real, the appearance for the substance, to be great and yet small, learned and yet simple, high and yet the servant of all.
passages.vernacular: 如果我過去嘅生命對提升我嘅人民、促成你嘅種族同我嘅種族之間更好嘅關係有任何意義,我向你保證,從今日起,佢會有雙倍意義。喺上帝嘅經濟中,一個人成功只有一個標準——一個種族亦只有一個。呢個國家要求每個種族以美國標準衡量自己。憑佢,一個種族必須上升或下降,成功或失敗,歸根結底單純情感幾乎冇分量。未來半個世紀以上,我嘅種族必須繼續通過嚴峻嘅美國熔爐。我哋要被考驗我哋嘅耐性、忍耐、堅毅、忍受錯誤嘅力量、抵擋誘惑、節儉、獲得同使用技能;考驗我哋競爭、在商業成功、捨棄表面求實質、捨棄外表求內涵、偉大而渺小、博學而單純、崇高而為所有人嘅僕人嘅能力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我過去的生命對提升我的人民、促成你的種族和我的種族之間更好的關係有任何意義,我向你保證,從今天起,它會有雙倍意義。在上帝的經濟中,一個人成功只有一個標準——一個種族也只有一個。這個國家要求每個種族以美國標準衡量自己。憑它,一個種族必須上升或下降,成功或失敗,歸根結底單純情感幾乎沒分量。未來半個世紀以上,我的種族必須繼續通過嚴峻的美國熔爐。我們要被考驗我們的耐性、忍耐、堅毅、忍受錯誤的力量、抵擋誘惑、節儉、獲得和使用技能;考驗我們競爭、在商業成功、捨棄表面求實質、捨棄外表求內涵、偉大而渺小、博學而單純、崇高而為所有人的僕人的能力。

passages.original: As this was the first time that a New England university had conferred an honorary degree upon a Negro, it was the occasion of much newspaper comment throughout the country. A correspondent of a New York paper said:—
passages.vernacular: 因為呢個係新英格蘭大學第一次授予黑人榮譽學位,全國報紙對此多有評論。一份紐約報紙嘅記者講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為這是新英格蘭大學第一次授予黑人榮譽學位,全國報紙對此多有評論。一份紐約報紙的記者說:

passages.original: When the name of Booker T. Washington was called, and he arose to acknowledge and accept, there was such an outburst of applause as greeted no other name except that of the popular soldier patriot, General Miles. The applause was not studied and stiff, sympathetic and condoling; it was enthusiasm and admiration. Every part of the audience from pit to gallery joined in, and a glow covered the cheeks of those around me, proving sincere appreciation of the rising struggle of an ex-slave and the work he has accomplished for his race.
passages.vernacular: 當布克·T·華盛頓嘅名被叫,佢起身致謝接受,爆發出除咗受歡迎士兵愛國者邁爾斯將軍之外,冇其他名字得到嘅掌聲。掌聲唔係經過研究同僵硬、同情同安慰嘅;而係熱情同欽佩。從池座到樓座,聽眾各部分都加入,我周圍人嘅面頰泛起光輝,證明真誠欣賞一個前奴隸奮起嘅鬥爭同佢為種族所做嘅工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當布克·T·華盛頓的名字被叫,他起身致謝接受,爆發出除了受歡迎士兵愛國者邁爾斯將軍之外,沒其他名字得到的掌聲。掌聲不是經過研究和僵硬、同情和安慰的;而是熱情和欽佩。從池座到樓座,聽眾各部分都加入,我周圍人的面頰泛起光輝,證明真誠欣賞一個前奴隸奮起的鬥爭和他為種族所做的工作。

passages.original: A Boston paper said, editorially:—
passages.vernacular: 一份波士頓報紙社論講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一份波士頓報紙社論說:

passages.original: In conferring the honorary degree of Master of Arts upon the Principal of Tuskegee Institute, Harvard University has honoured itself as well as the object of this distinction. The work which Professor Booker T. Washington has accomplished for the education, good citizenship, and popular enlightenment in his chosen field of labour in the South entitles him to rank with our national benefactors. The university which can claim him on its list of sons, whether in regular course or honoris causa, may be proud.
passages.vernacular: 哈佛大學授予塔斯基吉學院校長文學碩士榮譽學位,榮耀咗自己,亦榮耀咗呢個榮譽嘅對象。布克·T·華盛頓教授為教育、良好公民身份同民眾啟蒙所做嘅工作,喺佢所選擇嘅南方勞動領域,令佢有資格列入我哋國家恩人之列。可以聲稱佢列於其子之列(無論按正規課程或榮譽)嘅大學,可以感到驕傲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈佛大學授予塔斯基吉學院校長文學碩士榮譽學位,榮耀了自己,也榮耀了這個榮譽的對象。布克·T·華盛頓教授為教育、良好公民身分和民眾啟蒙所做的工作,在他所選擇的南方勞動領域,使他有資格列入我們國家恩人之列。可以聲稱他列於其子之列(無論按正規課程或榮譽)的大學,可以感到驕傲。

passages.original: It has been mentioned that Mr. Washington is the first of his race to receive an honorary degree from a New England university. This, in itself, is a distinction. But the degree was not conferred because Mr. Washington is a coloured man, or because he was born in slavery, but because he has shown, by his work for the elevation of the people of the Black Belt of the South, a genius and a broad humanity which count for greatness in any man, whether his skin be white or black.
passages.vernacular: 有人提到,華盛頓先生係佢種族第一個得到新英格蘭大學榮譽學位嘅人。呢個本身係一個榮譽。不過學位唔係因為華盛頓先生係有色人種,或者因為佢出世係奴隸而授予,而係因為佢為提升南方黑帶人民嘅工作,顯示咗一種天才同廣闊嘅人道,任何人(無論膚色白或黑)都因此偉大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有人提到,華盛頓先生是他種族第一個得到新英格蘭大學榮譽學位的人。這個本身是一個榮譽。不過學位不是因為華盛頓先生是有色人種,或因為他出生是奴隸而授予,而是因為他為提升南方黑帶人民的工作,顯示了一種天才和廣闊的人道,任何人(無論膚色白或黑)都因此偉大。

passages.original: Another Boston paper said:—
passages.vernacular: 另一份波士頓報紙講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 另一份波士頓報紙說:

passages.original: It is Harvard which, first among New England colleges, confers an honorary degree upon a black man. No one who has followed the history of Tuskegee and its work can fail to admire the courage, persistence, and splendid common sense of Booker T. Washington. Well may Harvard honour the ex-slave, the value of whose services, alike to his race and country, only the future can estimate.
passages.vernacular: 哈佛係新英格蘭學院中第一個授予黑人榮譽學位嘅。任何追蹤塔斯基吉歷史同工作嘅人,都唔會唔欣賞布克·T·華盛頓嘅勇氣、堅持同卓越常識。哈佛榮耀呢位前奴隸係應該嘅,佢嘅服務對佢種族同國家嘅價值,只有將來可以估計。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈佛是新英格蘭學院中第一個授予黑人榮譽學位的。任何追蹤塔斯基吉歷史和工作的人,都不會不欣賞布克·T·華盛頓的勇氣、堅持和卓越常識。哈佛榮耀這位前奴隸是應該的,他的服務對他種族和國家的價值,只有將來可以估計。

passages.original: The correspondent of the New York Times wrote:—
passages.vernacular: 《紐約時報》記者寫道:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 《紐約時報》記者寫道:

passages.original: All the speeches were enthusiastically received, but the coloured man carried off the oratorical honours, and the applause which broke out when he had finished was vociferous and long-continued.
passages.vernacular: 所有演說都受到熱烈歡迎,不過有色人種男人贏得演說榮譽,佢講完時爆發嘅掌聲吵鬧而持久。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所有演說都受到熱烈歡迎,不過有色人種男人贏得演說榮譽,他講完時爆發的掌聲吵鬧而持久。

passages.original: Soon after I began work at Tuskegee I formed a resolution, in the secret of my heart, that I would try to build up a school that would be of so much service to the country that the President of the United States would one day come to see it. This was, I confess, rather a bold resolution, and for a number of years I kept it hidden in my own thoughts, not daring to share it with any one.
passages.vernacular: 我開始喺塔斯基吉工作後不久,我心底下定一個決心:我會嘗試建立一間對國家非常有用嘅學校,令美國總統有一日來睇。我承認,呢個係相當大膽嘅決心,好多年我將佢隱藏喺自己嘅思想,唔敢同任何人分享。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我開始在塔斯基吉工作後不久,我心底下定一個決心:我會嘗試建立一間對國家非常有用的學校,使美國總統有一天來看。我承認,這是相當大膽的決心,很多年我將它隱藏在自己的思想,不敢與任何人分享。

passages.original: In November, 1897, I made the first move in this direction, and that was in securing a visit from a member of President McKinley’s Cabinet, the Hon. James Wilson, Secretary of Agriculture. He came to deliver an address at the formal opening of the Slater-Armstrong Agricultural Building, our first large building to be used for the purpose of giving training to our students in agriculture and kindred branches.
passages.vernacular: 1897年11月,我向呢個方向邁出第一步,就係得到麥金萊總統內閣一位成員、農業部長詹姆斯·威爾遜先生嘅探訪。佢來為斯萊特-阿姆斯特朗農業大樓(我哋第一座用於畀學生農業同相關分支培訓嘅大型建築)正式開幕發表演說。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 1897年11月,我向這個方向邁出第一步,就是得到麥金萊總統內閣一位成員、農業部長詹姆斯·威爾遜先生的探訪。他來為斯萊特-阿姆斯特朗農業大樓(我們第一座用於給學生農業和相關分支培訓的大型建築)正式開幕發表演說。

passages.original: In the fall of 1898 I heard that President McKinley was likely to visit Atlanta, Georgia, for the purpose of taking part in the Peace Jubilee exercises to be held there to commemorate the successful close of the Spanish-American war. At this time I had been hard at work, together with our teachers, for eighteen years, trying to build up a school that we thought would be of service to the Nation, and I determined to make a direct effort to secure a visit from the President and his Cabinet. I went to Washington, and I was not long in the city before I found my way to the White House. When I got there I found the waiting rooms full of people, and my heart began to sink, for I feared there would not be much chance of my seeing the President that day, if at all. But, at any rate, I got an opportunity to see Mr. J. Addison Porter, the secretary to the President, and explained to him my mission. Mr. Porter kindly sent my card directly to the President, and in a few minutes word came from Mr. McKinley that he would see me.
passages.vernacular: 1898年秋天,我聽聞麥金萊總統可能去佐治亞亞特蘭大,參加喺嗰度舉行嘅和平禧年儀式,紀念美西戰爭成功結束。當時我同老師一齊努力工作咗十八年,試圖建立一間我哋認為對國家有用嘅學校,我決心直接努力爭取總統同佢內閣探訪。我去咗華盛頓,冇耐就搵到去白宮嘅路。我到嗰度,發現等候室擠滿人,我嘅心開始下沉,因為我恐怕當日見到總統嘅機會唔大,如果有嘅話。不過,無論如何,我得到機會見總統秘書J·艾迪生·波特先生,向佢說明我嘅使命。波特先生好心將我嘅名片直接送畀總統,幾分鐘內麥金萊先生傳話話會見我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 1898年秋天,我聽聞麥金萊總統可能去喬治亞亞特蘭大,參加在那裡舉行的和平禧年儀式,紀念美西戰爭成功結束。當時我與老師一起努力工作了十八年,試圖建立一間我們認為對國家有用的學校,我決心直接努力爭取總統和他內閣探訪。我去了華盛頓,沒多久就找到去白宮的路。我到那裡,發現等候室擠滿人,我的心開始下沉,因為我恐怕當天見到總統的機會不大,如果有的話。不過,無論如何,我得到機會見總統秘書J·艾迪生·波特先生,向他說明我的使命。波特先生好心將我的名片直接送給總統,幾分鐘內麥金萊先生傳話說會見我。

passages.original: How any man can see so many people of all kinds, with all kinds of errands, and do so much hard work, and still keep himself calm, patient, and fresh for each visitor in the way that President McKinley does, I cannot understand. When I saw the President he kindly thanked me for the work which we were doing at Tuskegee for the interests of the country. I then told him, briefly, the object of my visit. I impressed upon him the fact that a visit from the Chief Executive of the Nation would not only encourage our students and teachers, but would help the entire race. He seemed interested, but did not make a promise to go to Tuskegee, for the reason that his plans about going to Atlanta were not then fully made; but he asked me to call the matter to his attention a few weeks later.
passages.vernacular: 我唔明白,點解任何人可以見咁多各類人、各種事務,做咁多辛苦工作,仍然像麥金萊總統咁,為每個訪客保持冷靜、耐性同清新。我見到總統時,佢好心多謝我哋喺塔斯基吉為國家利益所做嘅工作。我然後簡短地向佢講我來訪嘅目的。我令佢深刻印象:國家行政首長嘅探訪,唔單止會鼓勵我哋學生同老師,亦會幫助整個種族。佢似乎有興趣,不過冇承諾去塔斯基吉,因為佢去亞特蘭大嘅計劃當時未完全定好;不過佢叫我幾個星期後再向佢提起呢件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不明白,為什麼任何人可以見那麼多各類人、各種事務,做那麼多辛苦工作,仍然像麥金萊總統那樣,為每個訪客保持冷靜、耐性和清新。我見到總統時,他好心感謝我們在塔斯基吉為國家利益所做的工作。我然後簡短地向他說我來訪的目的。我使他深刻印象:國家行政首長的探訪,不僅會鼓勵我們學生和老師,也會幫助整個種族。他似乎有興趣,不過沒承諾去塔斯基吉,因為他去亞特蘭大的計劃當時未完全定好;不過他叫我幾個星期後再向他提起這件事。

passages.original: By the middle of the following month the President had definitely decided to attend the Peace Jubilee at Atlanta. I went to Washington again and saw him, with a view of getting him to extend his trip to Tuskegee. On this second visit Mr. Charles W. Hare, a prominent white citizen of Tuskegee, kindly volunteered to accompany me, to reenforce my invitation with one from the white people of Tuskegee and the vicinity.
passages.vernacular: 翌月中旬,總統已經確定決定出席亞特蘭大和平禧年。我再去華盛頓見佢,希望令佢將行程延伸到塔斯基吉。呢次第二次探訪,塔斯基吉一位知名白人市民查爾斯·W·黑爾先生好心自願陪我,用塔斯基吉同附近白人嘅邀請加強我嘅邀請。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 翌月中旬,總統已經確定決定出席亞特蘭大和平禧年。我再去華盛頓見他,希望使他將行程延伸到塔斯基吉。這次第二次探訪,塔斯基吉一位知名白人市民查爾斯·W·黑爾先生好心自願陪我,用塔斯基吉和附近白人的邀請加強我的邀請。

passages.original: Just previous to my going to Washington the second time, the country had been excited, and the coloured people greatly depressed, because of several severe race riots which had occurred at different points in the South. As soon as I saw the President, I perceived that his heart was greatly burdened by reason of these race disturbances. Although there were many people waiting to see him, he detained me for some time, discussing the condition and prospects of the race. He remarked several times that he was determined to show his interest and faith in the race, not merely in words, but by acts. When I told him that I thought that at that time scarcely anything would go farther in giving hope and encouragement to the race than the fact that the President of the Nation would be willing to travel one hundred and forty miles out of his way to spend a day at a Negro institution, he seemed deeply impressed.
passages.vernacular: 我第二次去華盛頓之前,全國因為南方不同地點發生幾場嚴重種族暴亂而激動,有色人種非常沮喪。我一見到總統,就察覺佢心因為呢啲種族騷亂而非常沉重。雖然有好多人等見佢,佢留住我一段時間,討論種族嘅狀況同前景。佢幾次講,佢決心唔單止以言語,而係以行動顯示對種族嘅興趣同信心。當我話畀佢知,我認為當時幾乎冇任何事比國家總統願意繞行一百四十英里、喺一間黑人機構度過一日,更能畀種族希望同鼓勵,佢似乎深受感動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我第二次去華盛頓之前,全國因為南方不同地點發生幾場嚴重種族暴亂而激動,有色人種非常沮喪。我一見到總統,就察覺他心因為這些種族騷亂而非常沉重。雖然有很多人等見他,他留住我一段時間,討論種族的狀況和前景。他幾次說,他決心不僅以言語,而是以行動顯示對種族的興趣和信心。當我告訴他,我認為當時幾乎沒任何事比國家總統願意繞行一百四十英里、在一間黑人機構度過一天,更能給種族希望和鼓勵,他似乎深受感動。

passages.original: While I was with the President, a white citizen of Atlanta, a Democrat and an ex-slaveholder, came into the room, and the President asked his opinion as to the wisdom of his going to Tuskegee. Without hesitation the Atlanta man replied that it was the proper thing for him to do. This opinion was reenforced by that friend of the race, Dr. J.L.M. Curry. The President promised that he would visit our school on the 16th of December.
passages.vernacular: 我同總統一齊時,一位亞特蘭大白人市民(民主黨人、前奴隸主)入房,總統問佢對去塔斯基吉嘅明智性嘅意見。亞特蘭大人毫不猶豫咁答,係佢應該做嘅適當事。呢個意見得到種族嘅朋友J·L·M·柯里博士加強。總統承諾12月16日探訪我哋嘅學校。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我與總統一起時,一位亞特蘭大白人市民(民主黨人、前奴隸主)進房,總統問他對去塔斯基吉的明智性的意見。亞特蘭大人毫不猶豫地答,是他應該做的適當事。這個意見得到種族的朋友J·L·M·柯里博士加強。總統承諾12月16日探訪我們的學校。

passages.original: When it became known that the President was going to visit our school, the white citizens of the town of Tuskegee—a mile distant from the school—were as much pleased as were our students and teachers. The white people of this town, including both men and women, began arranging to decorate the town, and to form themselves into committees for the purpose of cooperating with the officers of our school in order that the distinguished visitor might have a fitting reception. I think I never realized before this how much the white people of Tuskegee and vicinity thought of our institution. During the days when we were preparing for the President’s reception, dozens of these people came to me and said that, while they did not want to push themselves into prominence, if there was anything they could do to help, or to relieve me personally, I had but to intimate it and they would be only too glad to assist. In fact, the thing that touched me almost as deeply as the visit of the President itself was the deep pride which all classes of citizens in Alabama seemed to take in our work.
passages.vernacular: 當總統將探訪我哋學校嘅消息傳開,距離學校一英里嘅塔斯基吉鎮白人市民,同我哋學生同老師一樣高興。呢個鎮嘅白人(包括男女),開始安排裝飾鎮,並組成委員會,同我哋學校官員合作,令尊貴嘅訪客得到適當歡迎。我諗我之前從未意識到,塔斯基吉同附近嘅白人幾重視我哋嘅學院。我哋準備總統歡迎儀式嘅日子,幾十個呢啲人來搵我,話雖然佢哋唔想出風頭,但如果有任何佢哋可以幫忙、或者為我個人減輕負擔,我只需暗示,佢哋會非常樂意協助。事實上,幾乎同總統探訪本身一樣深深感動我嘅,係阿拉巴馬各階層市民對我哋工作所表現嘅深切驕傲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當總統將探訪我們學校的消息傳開,距離學校一英里的塔斯基吉鎮白人市民,與我們學生和老師一樣高興。這個鎮的白人(包括男女),開始安排裝飾鎮,並組成委員會,與我們學校官員合作,使尊貴的訪客得到適當歡迎。我想我之前從未意識到,塔斯基吉和附近的白人多重視我們的學院。我們準備總統歡迎儀式的日子,幾十個這些人來找我,說雖然他們不想出風頭,但如果有任何他們可以幫忙、或為我個人減輕負擔,我只需暗示,他們會非常樂意協助。事實上,幾乎與總統探訪本身一樣深深感動我的,是阿拉巴馬各階層市民對我們工作所表現的深切驕傲。

passages.original: The morning of December 16th brought to the little city of Tuskegee such a crowd as it had never seen before. With the President came Mrs. McKinley and all of the Cabinet officers but one; and most of them brought their wives or some members of their families.
